title: Q&A on being in the river of misery between « I can’t take care of people » and « I have value »
question:
Q : When you think, “Every anxious feeling is a step toward safety and ease,” how do you feel?

A : committed, willing, challenged

Q : when you think, “The more I feel anxiety, the more pleasure I’ll have in connection,” what does that make you want to do?

A : it makes me want to experiment discomfort : for exemple reappearing in a conversation I quitted long ago or answering to messages I would otherwise ignore.

Looking for the thought that keep me in the river of misery between « I can’t take care of people » and « I have value » :

Q : When you meet someone, how do you feel?

A : When I meet someone, I feel curious and warm but also childish and unworthy, I am trying to make them like me. Sometimes I compare myself to them and want to impress them.

If I had to summarize I would say the feeling is « evaluating » which is a lighter version of anxious Q :And what are the exact thoughts creating that feeling?

A : Can this person be a friend or is it an enemy ?

Q : When you tell someone you’re a coach, what comes up?

A : I think that they may not care. The feeling is mostly curiosity

And when you make an offer, what changes? I don’t make offers so often, but curiosity is the most felt emotion I would say

What are you making it mean in that moment?

Sometimes I make anxiety mean that I am on the right path and sometimes that there is something wrong with me.

Thank you coach for these helpful questions
answer:
Hey Coach,

I’m really glad you received the coaching and the questions so useful for you right now! Very powerful you brought this here and I want to start by reflecting something back to you because it matters.

The good news now is your awareness and now you’re not stuck. You’re actually very aware. That is powerful creating agency to decide how you respond to emotions like anxiety.

You can already see that the same feeling anxiety can mean two completely different things depending on the thought attached to it:

Sometimes it means “I’m on the right path.”
And sometimes it means “something is wrong with me.”

That right there is the work getting to decide what you make it mean.

So let me ask you this, and I’ll tell you why it matters, 
When you feel anxiety in a moment with someone, 
what do you decide it means about you? Why?

Because that meaning is what creates everything that follows.

If anxiety means “I’m doing something wrong,” of course your brain goes into evaluating, proving, comparing, trying to be liked. It’s like you step into the conversation already trying to fix yourself.

But if anxiety means “I’m stretching, I’m growing, I’m showing up,” notice what opens up. There’s more space. More willingness. Less urgency to perform. Same feeling and completely different experience.

When you said the feeling is “evaluating,” that’s actually such a clean awareness.

So I’m curious,  
Who are you evaluating in that moment,  them, or you? 
(This matters because it shows where your focus is going.)

From what you wrote, it sounds like the attention turns inward:
“Am I enough?” “Do they like me?” “Do I measure up?” And when your brain is there, it makes sense that offering, leading, or even staying present feels harder. You’ve left the room mentally and made yourself the project.

So here’s another question, and this one is directional—
What happens if you shift from “Am I valuable?” to “How can I create value here?” 
That shift is everything.

Because your work doesn’t live in proving your value it lives in using it. Right now, there’s a subtle loop happening:

You feel anxiety, you interpret it,  then you respond to yourself instead of the person in front of you.

And that’s what keeps you in that “river” you described between “I can’t take care of people” and “I have value.”

You’re not actually in the middle because you lack value.
You’re in the middle because you keep questioning it.

So instead of trying to get rid of anxiety, I’d add this to your “to-do list” in a very intentional way, Allow the anxiety and decide ahead of time what it means.

Something like:
“When I feel anxiety, it means I’m engaged, I care, and I’m in the room doing meaningful work.”

And from there, I’d anchor you back into what actually creates momentum in your business:

Who needs me right now?
What do they need to hear?
What do I have that could help them?

That’s high-value thinking! Value creates clients and money.

Because the truth is when your brain goes to “something is wrong with me,” that’s always your cue that you’ve drifted out of it.

You don’t become more valuable by solving your anxiety in away that avoids it distracts or reacts from it . 
You become more impactful by staying present 
with it
 and leading anyway.

Go listen to “Income Producing Beliefs” (Episode 382) again with this lens especially around how belief drives action.

You’re closer than you think Coach!

title: $ Goal
question:
Hi AAC!

Ok, so the good news is I am in SO much more belief! The last few weeks I am showing up more and really just more hopeful that I CAN do this. I signed a client a few weeks ago and I am excited about that. However, my goal was 4 clients in April. I don’t think I believed I really could sign 4, but I did believe I clients are coming. I realize that that is more of an “out there” belief though…as in I believe clients will come at some point, but maybe not soon.

I want to change this. I would honestly love to set a big goal like $10k for May…but that is hard to believe. I want that goal b/c I know I want the money. But even 4 clients in May would be pretty incredible. Can you please help me to set a goal that I can believe I can do, and help me create a belief plan to achieve it?

Oh, and a sneaky belief that I think I caught is that I’m thinking not a lot of people can afford coaching, or that it’s too expensive or I’m charging too much. This is in my mind quite frequently I realize b/c so often I am seeing prices and thinking money is hard right now, and I’m also hearing it from other people. I want to believe in abundance and I want to use that belief to grow my own abundance of clients/money/success and I want to have a track record to help others do the same.

Can’t wait to see where you take me with this! Thank you!
answer:
Hey there, Coach!

I love where you are right now. You can feel the shift in yourself, you’re showing up differently, you signed a client, and there’s more openness in your thinking. So amazing!

And – I want to be careful here because I don’t want to shrink that by immediately making this about a “more believable” goal. What I’m hearing isn’t that you need a “safer” goal. It’s that you don’t fully trust yourself 
(yet)
 to hit the one you actually want. You said you’d love to make $10k in May, and then immediately went to “but that’s hard to believe.” So instead of building belief for the goal you want, your brain is trying to negotiate you into something that feels more comfortable.

What if we didn’t do that? Or if instead found the happy medium that you feel empowered by? A way to stretch yourself 
but
 keep it fun, unattached, and showing up as your “best self-concept” as a coach?

We don’t build self-trust by only choosing goals we already believe. We build it by deciding what we want and then becoming the person 
who
 learns 
how
 to create it. So you can absolutely keep $10k as your goal but tell the truth alongside it: you don’t fully believe it (yet). That’s okay… That’s where the work is.

Now let’s look at what’s actually in the way. You already caught one of the biggest thoughts:
 people can’t afford coaching, money is tight, I might be charging too much. 
If that belief is running, it doesn’t matter what number or monthly goal you pick. You will unconsciously soften your offers, hesitate in your messaging, and relate to people as if they 
can’t
 buy – and people feel that.

Here’s what I want you to see: You’re trying to create $10k while holding a belief that people don’t have money. Those two things don’t coexist well. Your work isn’t just “believe more” but it’s deciding what you want to believe on purpose. In a grounded and practiced way. For example, instead of trying to jump all the way to “everyone has money,” it may be starting with some thoughts more approachable:

There are people who value this work and are willing to invest in it.

People are already spending money every day on things that matter to them.

I don’t need everyone to say yes. I need the right people to see themselves in this.

A bit easier to practice and more of a “bridge thought” that still supports your goal. From there, think about your result from April. You signed one client and your brain wants to make that mean “I’m not at 4 yet.” What if instead you make it mean: 
I know how to sign clients. 
Because that is the skill you’re really building and from there, we can get a lot more specific.

If you want 4 clients, or $10k, how many conversations are you having 
(or do you think you need to have)
?

How many invitations to buy are you making?

How consistently are you showing up in places where people can actually find you 
(whether in person, in emails, or in socials?)

Belief grows faster when it’s paired with evidence that you’re creating on purpose. So to anchor this down, figure out and keep the goal you actually want. Don’t negotiate it down just to feel better. Tell the truth that your belief isn’t fully there yet, and let 
that
 be the work. The work is how you would STILL show up in May, daily/weekly, believing 4 clients or 10k is a done deal – even when humanness comes into play and the belief feels a bit shaky.

Clean up the money story so you’re not selling from “people can’t afford this” and then focus on the actions that create clients, not just the number of clients itself or the monetary piece. What is most important here is that you need to believe that if you keep showing up, keep inviting, and keep refining, you will learn how to create the result you ultimately want. You’ve already started that process. If you can sign one client, you can absolutely sign more in a shorter period of time! That’s what you’re working towards and it’s absolutely possible.

Great work, coach. See how this lands and feel free to come back with any thoughts or further coaching you would like!

title: Strategic Doubt or Exhaustion?
question:
I have a goal to make $100K in 2026 by signing 20 clients into my six-month private coaching program, The Exhale, for couples who want their relationship to stay alive, embodied and deeply connected over time. So far, I have 0 clients in this offer and have made $3K total from coaching, which was last year. I am a mindset and somatic coach with 8 years of experience in the intimacy industry. I have a clear bigger vision: to hold in-person workshops for couples at luxury eco resorts and hotels across Australia and eventually globally, then invite couples from those workshops into complimentary consultations for private coaching.

The problem is that I am exhausted. I have been going through perimenopause and have had about 6 months of poor sleep, which has deeply affected my confidence, energy and clarity. I am a single mother and I also work on commission in sales, so my nervous system feels stretched. Because I am so tired, I am questioning everything. My offer, my capacity, whether I can coach couples, whether it matters that I don’t currently have a romantic partner, whether my reels are working, whether I am making good decisions. I don’t want to keep changing my offer because I have already changed it many times. I want to commit and build something properly. I know the next practical steps are probably to contact more potential workshop collaborators, refine my consultation process, and keep speaking to my audience. But my thinking is messy and I keep slipping into confusion, doubt and shame.

My current thoughts are: “It’s not going to happen. I don’t know how to coach couples. It’s embarrassing that I have not signed a client. My reels are not working. No one likes them. I don’t know if I can do this. My life is a mess, so how can I coach others? I don’t have a romantic partner, so how can I coach couples? I feel tired. I need a break. Maybe I am burnt out. Maybe I am not cut out for this. I don’t know what I am doing. I don’t make good decisions. I don’t move fast enough. I am not productive enough, yet I feel like I work too hard.”

My specific question is: How do I discern the difference between genuine strategic information I should respond to, such as needing to refine my offer, consultation process or outreach strategy, and exhaustion-based doubt that I should not make business decisions from?
answer:
Hi Coach!

Thanks for bringing this here. Happy to coach you on this and offer some insight.

First I just want to say, your first paragraph landed powerfully as the reader of it. Your goal and vision felt clear, grounded, and like you knew exactly what you were building and why. It came across very confident. Nothing about it felt confused or scattered. As I kept reading, I never questioned your vision for your business, but I noticed the shift in your energy. Your vision didn’t disappear, but your belief in your capacity to hold it felt a little wobbly (so let’s focus on that).

You’re navigating real fatigue which can be a lot on a nervous system – so it makes sense that your brain is trying to solve for safety by questioning everything. When you read your thoughts back, 
do they feel like clean, useful direction or do they feel like overwhelm trying to find certainty?
 There’s a difference between strategic refinement and exhaustion based self-doubt. 
Strategic thoughts tend to be specific and actionable.
 Doubt tends to sound like “I don’t know what I’m doing” or “maybe this isn’t going to work.”

One leads to movement. The other keeps you spinning.

I also want to gently bring your attention to how your brain is using your current relationship status against you. You have 8 years in the intimacy space. That doesn’t disappear because you’re single right now.
 What do you actually believe makes someone effective at coaching couples? Is it their current relationship status, or their ability to see patterns, hold space, and guide people through dynamics they may not be able to see themselves?
 There are people who would deeply benefit from what you know. It would be a shame to keep that quiet because of a potentially temporary circumstance of being single. It doesn’t erase all of the knowledge, expertise, and value you can bring to the table for couples who are in a position to use what you can teach them.

When it comes to discerning what to do next, I would anchor you back into 
execution as your source of clarity.
 You already named the next steps: Reaching out to collaborators. Refining your consult process. Speaking to your audience.

What if you decided on a timeline that feels supportive, not punishing? Maybe it’s six weeks, eight weeks, maybe twelve. During that time, 
you commit to specific actions and let the data come from doing, not from thinking.
 
Then you evaluate. What worked? What didn’t? What needs to shift? That’s very different from trying to solve everything from your head while you’re exhausted. And you can bring that data back here to AAC so we can coach you and help you stay in a clean, clear headspace.

At the same time, your exhaustion isn’t something to override. It’s something to work with.

What do you need right now to feel even slightly more supported?

Where can you give yourself a little more space, a little more care, without abandoning your business?

This doesn’t have to be “all or nothing.” You can build something meaningful AND honor where you are. The goal isn’t perfect consistency, but honest, sustainable movement forward. 
What do you think?

Feel free to come back with your answers or any thoughts you would like further coaching on. We are happy to help.

title: Day 22 / 30 – Instagram fears pt.2
question:
What am I afraid they will find out about me?

I think there’s a fear there that people will figure out I’m not as put together as they thought I was, not as inspiring. I’ve always been known as the one who is constantly having an adventure, traveling the world, living out her dreams. The last time I was posting consistently to Instagram was when I was living in Bali. Some people still think I live there. Now I spend 90% of my time in my bedroom at my brother’s house.

Stories like, “they’ll think I’m pathetic now or that my life looks sad” come up. That feels like shit and I can see very clearly that they aren’t serving me. But even when my life looked great and I was living in Bali I had a hard time showing up so I feel like it runs deeper than worrying about those specific stories.

I also feel a dualistic story come up that says “if they see me showing up and teaching, sharing wisdom, guiding others to success, then they’ll expect that from me too. I’ll have pressure to perform, to BE the person in those videos.” I know in Bali I felt like an imposter. Like I looked one way on camera but I wasn’t actually her in real life.

I’ve been feeling rather depressed recently and uncomfortable with where I am, unsure how to change my circumstances and gain back my sovereignty and independence. But even when I had it I struggled to show up. I think I actually do a very good job of allowing myself to be uncomfortable, taking action within that, but this feels deeper somehow. Like it’s more than just feeling uncomfortable.

I know I have to show up as a coach with value to offer who believes that people are waiting to hear from me, but a big part of me worries that I don’t have what it takes to actually be that person. I know I am meant for it, I have never once considered quitting, but I still feel that other story nonetheless. Lots of duality in me if you can’t tell.

Also, I feel like I’m noticing that I’m lacking what I believe is the correct level of motivation. In the past I had these visions for my future that I would chase after, it was my motivation to work through the discomfort because “the future I want” is past this discomfort. I don’t feel that same sense of inspiration anymore. Like the future I want feels clear but I don’t believe in it like I used to, in a way that made the discomfort worth it.
answer:
Hey coach,

First, let’s start with offering yourself some very sincere compassion. That is vitally important here. And I also want to say this clearly, if what you’re calling feeling depressed feels heavy or persistent, please get support. Don’t wait, don’t hesitate. Take that seriously.

Now, here’s what I notice.

You mention being afraid that people will “figure you out.” And what that’s doing is having you shrink and scan your life for anything that looks opposite of who you think you’ve portrayed or who you think people believe you are. Of course that feels terrible.

But I want to challenge something gently.

If you were actually an imposter, there would be something real to be found out. What exactly are you afraid of if they would find that live with brother, would be so bad? Fear of being found out is creating suffering. If you are not an imposter then what they think is not yours to deal with and if you feel like you are then how can you solve that?

I’m asking because your brain is treating that as dangerous, and that’s what’s keeping you from showing up.

And then this  if you want to be in integrity, solve for that. Because if you know you’re not an imposter, then what other people think actually can’t do anything to you. It only feels powerful if you’re agreeing with it somewhere.

It also makes sense that you’re seeing what you’re looking for. You’re in a season that looks different than Bali, so now your brain is using that as evidence against you.

But I want to offer you a different perspective.

There are coaches who have helped so many people from very simple, very real circumstances. Living in small spaces, doing calls from bedrooms, figuring things out as they go. And the people they helped did not care about their living situation they cared that they were helped. Stacey is the best example and she shares her story about running calls in motels and not knowing where her next meals coming from.  What do you think she was thinking?  I think she believed she had the tools to help people and people just want help.

So what does that tell you about what actually matters?

Now, I also hear this second layer  the fear that if you do show up and teach and lead, then you’ll have to be that person all the time. That there will be pressure to perform.

What if it just means you’re willing to be her today? And show yourself it’s ok to feel pressure it’s not a problem and you can do it. Not shrink and give your power away.

I’m asking that because right now you’re avoiding the action because of a future expectation you’re placing on yourself that isn’t actually required.

And then this deeper piece you named the lack of motivation, the disconnection from the future you used to feel so driven by. You used to believe the future you wanted was on the other side of discomfort. And that belief made the discomfort worth it.

What would you need to believe about your future for this to feel worth it again?

And if that belief isn’t there yet, then we don’t fake it. We start simpler.

Start with desire, and that will be enough to get going not waiting for motivation.

“I want to share this.”
“I want to help someone today.”
“I want to practice being the coach I know I can be.”

And I want to ask you something that might shift this for you.

What would it look like to be the person who no longer has this obstacle?

To be bigger than it? What if you decided to be a different version of you  one who doesn’t have this fear of being found out,  your current identity is holding onto?

If you had  people waiting to hear from you how would you handle this?

The coaches creating the results you want aren’t doing it because they feel perfectly aligned all the time. They’re doing it because they’re willing to show up beyond what their current thinking says is possible.

What do you need to believe in order to do the next thing?

And if you were coaching yourself through this, what would you tell yourself to do next?

You got this Coach, Stay with it.

title: Feeling like a fraud
question:
I sent a message in but I don’t think it went through as it said my link had expired? Please disregard if you receive this twice.

I realized I am really feeling like a fraud. I teach my clients all these tools in business and life and the model and using God’s word and how powerful they are…but I have only made an embarrassing amount of money the last 2 years. I keep holding onto this dream, showing up in service, and I LOVE coaching and helping clients, but it is really hard to shake the fact that it feels like it just isn’t working. I have only signed ONE new client since last July…and although I am doing my best to be in belief…I keep landing back here. My belief has been so much stronger since the end of March when Stacey coached me, and I signed a client in April…but now it’s been such a stretch of nothing again. So that cycle of believing and showing up and hoping…to get maybe something, or nothing…and then it’s really really hard to keep it up. And now add in this thought that I am a fraud to share that this all works when I have been on the struggle bus for 2 years.

I am speaking for 2 networking groups next month and I do not want these beliefs to get in the way…can you help?
answer:
Hi Coach,

First, thank you for heads up will disregard if we see it twice. I want to start with what is working for obvious reasons it’s the 2k way! and  also because where we direct our brain matters. Your brain will always search for evidence for whatever story you keep rehearsing. So if you only rehearse “it’s not working,” “I’m a fraud,” “nothing is happening,” your brain will continue strengthening that identity on default unmanaged mind way.

But when you intentionally look at what has worked, what you have created, the clients you have helped, the ways your life and thinking have changed through this work, you begin reinforcing a different identity not someone pretending to teach something she’s never lived, but someone actively practicing and using the tools she teaches. That adds value to your tools.

I also think it’s important to separate what fraud actually means. A fraud is claiming something that isn’t true. So I’d ask yourself: where specifically are you believing you’re being dishonest?

Are you promising results you haven’t created?

Or are you teaching tools that genuinely help people think differently, take action, create awareness, strengthen faith, and change their lives? Those are two very different things.

If you were claiming, “I can help anyone make 100k in six months,” while never having done that yourself, your brain may push back hard on that. But if you’re teaching women how to manage their mind, deepen belief, take action, grow in faith, create networking speaking opportunities, or move through fear you already have evidence of those things in your own life.

Your brain right now is discounting everything that is true because it’s hyper-focused on one measurement: money and client volume.

And I understand why. Results matter. But I also want you to notice something important here about your belief in action.

You are still here.

You are still showing up.

You are still serving.

You are still speaking at 2 networking events next month.

You are still coaching.

You are still pursuing this.

That tells me a part of you deeply believes in this work, even while another part feels discouraged. Both can exist.

I’m also curious why the thought “I’m a fraud” feels so dangerous to you.

Not because I want you to believe it  but because thoughts themselves are not the problem. Thoughts are involuntary. Your brain offers thoughts all day long. The suffering usually comes from attaching to them, arguing with them, resisting them, or treating them like absolute truth.

What if instead you noticed:

“Oh, there’s that fraud thought again.” Without making it mean anything. Without spiraling into proving or disproving yourself.

Just because your brain offers a thought does not mean you have to build an identity around it or listen to it at all.

I think sometimes coaches accidentally become afraid of their own thinking. But the goal isn’t to never have negative thoughts. The goal is to become someone who can hear them without obeying them.

You mentioned after Stacey coached you, your belief strengthened and you signed a client in April! YOu created that it’s working! I would study that thought and find and make a strong case for that belief. How did that new thought create your result?

What specifically shifted?

What were you believing then?

How did you feel?

How did you show up differently, exactly?

What actions did you take specifically?

What did you stop doing intentionally?

Because belief changes behavior. And behavior reinforces results.

Sometimes when people shift into discouragement, they unknowingly stop doing the very things that created momentum. They withdraw. They hesitate. They conserve energy. They stop inviting. They stop selling with conviction. They start showing up cautiously instead of powerfully. And then you keep looking for ” I am a fraud ” evidence.

I also think there’s something important here around emotional capacity. Can you build the capacity to keep showing up without immediate evidence?

Because entrepreneurship and coaching often require that, like  faith often requires that. Not blind delusion but the ability to tolerate uncertainty without collapsing your identity every time results slow down.

Right now your brain wants certainty before commitment:

“I’ll believe when it works consistently.” But most people who create something meaningful had to believe before the evidence fully arrived.

And finally, I would decide ahead of time who you want to be when these thoughts come up.

When your brain says, “You’re a fraud,” how do you want to respond? Maybe it becomes:

“My brain is offering fear because this matters to me.”

“I don’t need to listen to every thought my brain thinks.”

“I can feel discouraged and still keep moving.”

You do not need to be fearless to speak next month.

You do not need perfect belief.

You just need willingness to keep leading even while your brain has opinions about it.

You got this coach! Let us Know how it goes and how you respond to the unintentional thoughts.

title: 04/19/2026 | beliefs around my $8k offer
question:
After sitting with the questions you gave me around my $8k offer and how I can become the woman who fully believes in $8k before all the proof exists, I came up with these thoughts:

”$8k is a really reasonable price when it promises to change a person’s life for the better. $8k is an easy yes when I truly believe it will get me where I want to go, where I’ve been struggling to get to for years. I would do anything in my power to come up with that $8k if I knew it would help me become the person who is living the life I desperately want for myself.”

By choosing this $8k offer I am believing that the client holds the power to get the $8k result, my job is to show them that and to believe in their ability to accomplish it. $8k is a small price to pay to completely change a person’s life, and $8k isn’t even the thing that changes their life – it’s THEIR belief that changes their life, their thoughts, their feelings, their actions. & people will find a way to create that money when they really believe in themselves and the results they will get.
answer:
YES COACH!!! I can feel the energy shift here.

This last paragraph,
 “By choosing this $8k offer I am believing that the client holds the power to get the $8k result, my job is to show them that and to believe in their ability to accomplish it. $8k is a small price to pay to completely change a person’s life, and $8k isn’t even the thing that changes their life – it’s THEIR belief that changes their life, their thoughts, their feelings, their actions. & people will find a way to create that money when they really believe in themselves and the results they will get.”

title: Reconnecting with my why
question:
I watched Stacey’s facebook live today and it made me realize I’ve lost touch with the why behind my coaching. Somewhere in the grind of building my coaching business I lost touch with my passion, with how I want to help and serve, and things started to feel mechanical and like neverending work.

I want to feel emotionally invested in the way I did in the beginning.

There is one thought I want to work on:

It can’t be as exciting as it was in the beginning.

I just realized I have been thinking this thought constantly over and over as if it’s true, and it’s not serving me. Feeling excited about my business is how I signed clients in the beginning.
answer:
Hi Coach,

Thanks for bringing this here. You said the primary thought is, 
“It can’t be as exciting as it was in the beginning.”

Let’s dive deeper into that.

1. Why can’t it be? Why does it feel inaccessible to you right now?

2. What made you feel excited when you first started your business? What thoughts did you have back then?

Come back with your answers and we will continue to help you!

title: I feel like quitting
question: I haven’t sold anyone into my program this year. I’ve been selling htis progrma for over a year and raised my prices this year from $3K-5K. I’ve sold people into my program at $3K, but not any this year. I write emails 1-2 times per week, social media posts at least 3 times per week, go live 1-2 per week, run ads, get on sales calls and just get objections after obejctions and nos and many times it’s not on the call even though i ask. I schedule follow up calls cuz they want talk with their husband about big purchases and they cancel. They tell me afterwards they found someone in person or its too expensive or just ghost me. I review my sales calls and get help on them and i feel like just crying because i know other people sell programs so its possible but I just get objections like why did you book this call knowing its not an in-person program to go with someone in person? It just all seem like smoke-screens and I’m frustrated. i guess its not really a question but i don’t know how to change things. LIke do i just keep doing what i’m doing hoping things change. I don’t want to quit and i don’t want to stay where i’m at. I know my program helps people and i try to set up things so that when they come on the call they already know about me and what i do, but doesn’t seem like it’s working.
answer:
Hey coach,

I’m really glad you reached out. I want to start by saying this is the hard part of entrepreneurship. This is the part where nothing looks like it’s working, even when you’re doing a lot of the right things. And I hear how much effort you’re putting in… emails, posts, lives, ads, calls. That matters.

And also we want to look at what’s underneath all of that, because what you’re describing doesn’t sound like a strategy problem at the core. It sounds like a belief and energy problem that’s now showing up through your strategy.

This is exactly the work Stacey has been coaching on inside ECM. If you’re not in there yet, I really want to point you there, not as “more information,” but as support for this exact moment. Learning how to lead your brain when results aren’t coming yet, how to stay out of the spiral, and how to sell from clean belief instead of pressure… that’s the work and that is why she created the membership for this part of entrepreneurship.

You said you know this works because you’ve sold it before. That’s important. So something changed.

I want to understand what you think that is not from judgment, but from awareness.
What are your top three theories for why you’re not selling right now? Get specific and give this some reflection.

I’m asking this because your brain is already offering answers… but right now they might sound like frustration or confusion. When we slow them down and actually name them, we can work with them.

You mentioned raising your price from 3K to 5K.
What happened for you when you made that decision? Why did you make the increase ?

What did you start thinking about your membership, your clients, and your ability to sell it after the increase? Why?

Because often it’s not the price itself it’s what we make the price mean and the change in sales mean. 
Sometimes a higher price quietly introduces thoughts like:
“People won’t pay this.”
“I have to prove more.”
“This has to go perfectly.”

And those thoughts don’t just stay in your head they show up in how you market, how you lead calls, how you handle objections.

You also said it feels like people are giving you smoke screens.  Some of that may be true. And some of it may be that people are feeling your uncertainty and responding to that.

This is a big concept we work on in ECM: your thinking creates your emotional state, your emotional state drives how you show up, and your clients respond to that often without either of you realizing it. So it can look like “their objections,” but it’s actually an interaction between your belief and their decision-making.

So I want to explore this with you:

What are you making all of these “no’s” mean about you?

This matters because if every no is reinforcing “it’s not working” or “I can’t sell at this level,” that belief will start driving everything your tone, your confidence, your patience, your follow-up, even how you interpret objections.

You also said you don’t want to quit. I love that and I want you to connect to it more deeply.

Why don’t you want to quit? Take your time with this too.

Not the surface answer the real one.
Because that reason is what will anchor you when your brain wants to pull back or look for relief. This is also part of the work in ECM recommitting on purpose instead of reacting to how things feel in the moment.

Right now, you’re in the part of the process where you don’t want this to be happening. And I get that. But this is the work learning how to stay, adjust, and lead yourself through it.

If you were already consistently selling this program at 5K
What would be different about how you think, feel, and show up?

Be specific.
How would you talk about your offer?
How would you handle objections?
How would you feel going into a sales call?

I’m asking because that version of you isn’t created after the results it’s what creates the results. That’s a core principle becoming the version of you who can hold the result before it shows up.

Right now, “hoping things change” feels exhausting because it puts you in a passive position. And you can feel that there’s no power in it.

If nothing changes, nothing changes.

So instead of asking, “Do I keep going?”
The better question is:
“How do I need to think and show up differently to create a different result?” This is where we bring it back to your thoughts.

I’d love for you to actually write these out:

What are your current thoughts about selling at 3K?
And what are your current thoughts about selling at 5K?

No filtering just awareness.

Because we don’t fix this by doing more.
We shift this by seeing clearly what’s driving everything you’re already doing and then deliberately choosing thoughts that create steadiness, belief, and leadership. That’s the deeper work you’ll keep building.

You’re not stuck you’re in the middle of learning how to sell at a new level. And that requires a new level of thinking, belief, and emotional steadiness.

I’m here with you in this. Let’s keep working it.

title: I feel like quitting- III
question:
So when you think that what do you notice about how you sell? Are you believing the price matters more than the value and the transformation they receive? Do you lean in with certainty, or do you start explaining, adding, justifying?

I notice I go more into explaining, justifying & getting defensive. I’m thinking the price matters more than the value/transformation they receive.

Where are you already demonstrating the value clearly? Through testimonials. Maybe emails. I think i need to define value lol

.And where are you assuming they won’t see it? Why? That they will be stuck on the price tag, like what am I getting for this price, & not necessarily the transformation.

How do you provide the value ahead for them to see it? With things like testimonials, emails, social media, but maybe I’m not addressing the value they want to see

“Why is this 5K?” would your answer feel compelling to them? Hmm, maybe.

Or does it mostly make sense to you? I guess it mostly makes sense to me.

So the real question becomes what created the “no-brainer” feeling before? Was it clients signing up and then deciding it was a no brainer or clients getting results and value? I think it was both.

Was it actually the price or was it your belief and you decided the value? I think again it was both.

What do you need to believe about your offer now to show up that way before the evidence comes? Yes, I just noticed I am waiting for sales to create belief. I would need to go back to how I was believing about it before, like this is the best deal ever. This is so valuable. This is such a steal at this price. I notice, though I’m still not fully believing that. Hmmm, maybe an intermediate thought I could believe like I know this will help. Or I know i can make a difference for them. This has helped many women before this. I know I can help. I know this works. It doesn’t feel as strong but I believe it.

What is the actual transformation I help people create—and why is that worth 5K? Where have I already seen this work? How do I communicate that more clearly, more specifically, more tangibly? I have my past clients & their testimonials. I’m having a hard time thinking about how to communicate more clearly

Who is that version of you? How does she think about her clients, her offer, and her role in the process?

She thinks her clients are happy to pay this price & excited for the results. Confident. She is so happy for this offer & all the people it can help.
answer:
Hey Coach,

Great catch noticing the shift into explaining, justifying, and defending. That awareness matters, because that is the moment everything changes in how you sell.

I want to slow one piece down, because it’s sitting underneath almost all of your answers:
You’re treating price like the problem to solve instead of belief.

So I’m curious why does your brain think price matters more than value or transformation?
I’m asking that because wherever you decided that is likely where you started selling from doubt instead of certainty. And when you sell from there, your actions follow you explain more, you justify more, you try to “prove” instead of lead.

What if, instead, you anchored into this:
My ideal client already wants this. She’s looking for this level of support.

How would you show up if you truly believed your clients were already in the room, ready and wanting to hire you? Notice how different that version of you speaks she’s not convincing, she’s guiding.

You also said something really important: “Maybe I’m not addressing the value they want to see.”
That’s a useful hypothesis.

But I want to understand do you feel unclear on your value, or is it that you haven’t practiced articulating it enough yet?

I’m asking because those are two very different problems.
If it’s unclear, we define it.
If it’s a skill gap, we practice it.

Right now, it sounds more like the second. This is a skill. And skill-building requires being willing to say it imperfectly, evaluate how it lands, and refine. Your brain will want to avoid that and stay in vague language but this is the “heavy lift” part of the work.

When you said your answer to “Why is this 5K?” mostly makes sense to you that’s honest, and it’s key.

So what would you need to think and feel for it to feel compelling to them?
I’m asking because compelling communication doesn’t come from better wording it comes from deeper belief and willing to practice articulating it when it feels unclear.

This is where your note about waiting for sales to create belief is really important. Of course you feel shaky you’re asking results to create certainty, instead of creating certainty first. This never works, clients want you to be certain first not the other way around.

This is exactly where ITC comes in. Building belief on purpose is what is happening inside ECM right now.

Not just “this is valuable,” but why, specifically. Tangible and intangible. Over and over, until your brain stops debating whether it is or isn’t you decide and keep directing your mind back on purpose.

You mentioned an intermediate thought: “I know this will help. I know I can make a difference.”
That’s a solid place to stand. You don’t need to jump to “this is the best deal ever” if your brain isn’t there yet but you do need to keep building from what feels true.

And yes, of course it feels hard to communicate clearly right now. This is the work. Your brain will resist going deep and specific because it takes effort. But this is how you rewire it by thinking more intentionally, not less.

So instead of trying to “sound better,” I’d guide you here:

When you create content or speak about your offer, are you:
– Naming the specific problem your client is in?
– Helping her understand why it’s happening?
– Showing her what’s possible on the other side?
– Letting her experience your thinking before she ever gets on a call?

If not, what are you doing instead and what thoughts are driving that?

That question matters because your results in selling are always coming from how you’re thinking when you show up.

Lastly, I want you to look at everything you wrote and ask yourself:
What is the actual problem I’m solving right now? 
Is it price? Or is it clarity, belief, and communication?

So what does “getting clear” actually look like for you this week? More specificity? Practicing out loud? Writing it in multiple ways until it clicks?

Where do you want to take this now?

Great work here coach! Feel free to come back if you need anything further or coaching on anything else.

title: How times are changing
question:
The last time I came to AAC, I was reflecting on how I only come here when I’m at the same spot – desperate despair. Well, today is different! I have had 3 consults in the last 11 days – I CAN NOT tell you when the last time I had 3 consults, let alone in 11 days (probably never for the latter!). The first 2 said yes on the call, the 3rd one – oh gosh – the call was amazing, but he was interviewing one other coach, so I respected his decision to have that call (but I am manifesting hearing from him today/tomorrow with a YES!).

What a difference 3 calls and 2 yes’ makes to my belief. I am jubilant in seeing my bank account, I enjoy spending money for things, I am showing up relaxed online (helping people) – today has felt amazing.

I am starting to believe that this is my new normal. I would love coaching from you in staying in this feeling if 3rd consult says no, if I have no consults for the next week, if if if – my brain is already focusing on the lack. What can I do to continue focusing on the energy of this past 11 days? Thank you
answer:
Hi Coach,

First, so much to celebrate here!

Thank you for sharing your wins. I also want to acknowledge something important: you’re not only coming to Ask a Coach when you’re in despair. You’re here sharing success, recognizing your growth, and allowing yourself to see evidence of what’s working. That matters.

What strikes me most is that in just 11 days, nothing about who you are fundamentally changed. You didn’t suddenly become more capable, more valuable, or a better coach. What changed was your brain’s interpretation of the evidence in front of you.

You mentioned that three consults and two yeses have created a huge shift in your belief. That’s wonderful to notice. But I would get curious about this question:

What are you making those yeses mean?

I’m asking because the meaning you attach to those consults is creating the feeling you’re experiencing right now. The consults themselves don’t create confidence, certainty, or abundance. Your thoughts about them do.

And if that’s true, then the opposite is also true.

If the third consult says no, what will you make that mean?

If no consults come in next week, what will you make that mean?

Notice how quickly your brain wants to move from abundance back to scarcity. Not because scarcity is true, but because your brain is practiced at looking for evidence of what’s missing.

The work isn’t making yourself stay in this feeling forever. The work is noticing when your brain starts directing you toward lack and consciously redirecting yourself.

Simple? Yes.

Easy? Not always unfortunately.

But it gets easier with practice.

I also wouldn’t spend too much energy fearing that you’ll lose this feeling. Why? Because you’ve already shown yourself that you can create it. If you drift out of it, you can come back. The goal isn’t to never leave confidence; it’s to trust yourself enough to return to it.

Another question I’d explore: Answer as specifically as possible, create the success identity road map for yourself to see who you were being that created the how you showed up.

Who were you being on those consult calls?

How were you thinking about yourself, what were you not thinking about?

How were you thinking about the people you were helping?

What energy were you bringing into those conversations?

Sometimes we focus so much on the result that we miss the process that created it. If you can identify the thoughts, beliefs, and way of showing up that helped you serve those clients so powerfully, you can intentionally cultivate that regardless of whether the next consult says yes or no.

To me, the most powerful part is that you said you’re showing up more relaxed online and focused on helping people. That’s where I’d place my attention.

How can you stay connected to helping people rather than measuring your worth by the next consult, the next yes, or the next number in your bank account?

Think of it like driving a car. Your brain will naturally drift toward old familiar roads scarcity, doubt, lack. Your job isn’t to panic when you notice it. Your job is simply to put your hands back on the wheel and redirect your thinking in the new direction. Eventually the new route will become new normal.

You’re already proving you know how to do that.

Keep celebrating. Keep noticing what’s working. Keep practicing the thoughts and beliefs that helped you show up as your highest self. 
Everything you’re doing both in mindset and in action is creating momentum.

And remember, one consult, one yes, or one no never defines what’s possible for you. Great work Coach!

title: Day 23 / 30 – the most important skill for $100k
question:
I recently listened to Stacey’s podcast episode about creating a 3-year plan, I know it’s meant mostly for her $200k / $2M masterminds but I was super inspired by the concept of creating that 3 year plan so you can reverse engineer the process and see what skills you need in order to accomplish those later goals.

I was thinking about what skills I need in order to reach $100k in my business. At my current offer I would need 12 people to say yes to my $8k coaching package.

& in order to get 12 people to say yes, I need consults, enough consults to leave room for yeses, room for noes, and I also need to get really good at closing on those consults.

It’s so funny to see it written out as plainly as this – “to reach my goal I need to close on 12 consults in a year.”

& to reverse engineer that more I need:

– to get really good at making offers

– to get really good at generating consults

– to get really good at closing those consults

I just thought this would be fun to share here and to also ask – am I utilizing this “reverse engineering” process correctly? Because what I’m noticing more than anything is that, the most important thing for me to learn in order to scale to $100k in my business is to get really good at generating consults (& frankly I’m not good at this at all yet lol)

& I do see the obvious tie back to Stacey’s framework:

Meet new people,

tell them you’re a life coach

make offers to help them

That is a pretty clear formula to creating consults in my opinion lol but I’d love to hear your thoughts and receive any coaching on this that you think I may need.
answer:
Hey coach,

This is really good work. You are using the 200k concept correctly! Great work applying an advanced concept to yourself now. That is exactly how to become your future version, show up as that version making business plans now and acting from the the math of the goal not the drama.

What you’ve done is lay out the math for your goal simple, clean and doable : 12 clients = $100k.
And from there, getting consults, making offers, closing.

But here’s where I want to refine it a bit, because this is the actual gap, It’s not just a skill gap, It’s also an identity + thinking gap that’s showing up in the skills.

You’ve already named the three simple steps:

meet people → tell them you’re a coach → make offers

That is the process. What is in the way? Who do you need to be?  So the question isn’t really “am I doing the reverse engineering right?” You are. The question is who do you need to become?

The more useful question is:
Why aren’t these three steps happening at the level they need to? Not to judge yourself but to make a plan.

And this is where I want to slow it down and look at what’s underneath, because that’s what will actually move you.

How do you feel when you meet people?
I’m asking this because that feeling will either create connection… or hesitation.

What are the thoughts creating that feeling?
That’s what’s driving your behavior in those moments.

How do you feel when you tell people you’re a coach?
Do you feel grounded and clear… or a little unsure, maybe bracing?Again what are the thoughts there?

And then how do you feel when you make an offer to help someone?
This is a big one, because most people pull back right here.

Are you fully in belief that you can help them?
Or are you kind of waiting to see if they believe it first?

I’m asking you these questions very intentionally, because this is the work. The “skills” of generating consults and closing are built inside of how you’re thinking and feeling in each of these moments.

The person who signs 12 clients isn’t doing something wildly different. She’s thinking differently while doing the exact same steps.

She’s meeting people as someone who expects to connect.
She’s telling people she’s a coach like it’s just true not something to justify. She’s making offers from belief, not from hoping it lands.

That’s the identity piece.

Right now, you’re seeing “I need to get better at generating consults.”
Yes but consults come from you consistently doing those three things.

Don’t wait for clients to find you.
Don’t sit back and hope people reach out.

Take responsibility for going out into the world, finding people you can help, letting them know you can help them, and making them an offer. And to do that, this is what it actually requires (not perfectly—but consistently)

The good news is you can master these skills, review the training Five Vital Steps to making money as a life coach!

Willingness to fail and feel uncomfortable
Resilience to keep going when it’s not working yet
Commitment to the process
A real desire to get excellent at both coaching and selling (they are the same—helping people believe)
And the discipline to keep doing it even when it doesn’t feel good

The bar to start is low.
The bar to succeed is doing this over and over again.

And finally this is the shift I’d offer you: To get really good, you have to be willing to not be really good yet. What if you were willing to be good enough?

What would you do differently this week if “good enough” was enough to show up?
Who would you talk to?
What offers would you make?

That’s where your growth is. You’ve already mapped the path.
Now it’s about becoming the person who walks it.

title: My offer
question:
Im having thoughts about my offer: Right now my offer is:

“I help women who have spent their whole lives being the caretaker stop saying yes when they mean no and finally make time for themselves consistently in 90 days even if guilt has stopped them from choosing themselves before.”

My question is: does this kind of offer require a certain level of self-awareness for someone to buy into it?

Part of me wonders if I should position it more around tangible outcomes like healthier relationships, , or professional since women often invest faster in things connected to relationships, health, or income than simply “choosing themselves.

At the same time, I don’t want to lose the heart of what I actually help women with.

Do you think I’m overthinking this, or do you think there’s a way to tweak the positioning so the transformation feels more urgent and irresistible while still staying aligned with my niche?
answer:
Hi Coach!

Let’s begin here: 
what evidence do you currently have that the offer itself is the issue?

What I mean by that is, have you had conversations with women who hear the offer and say, 
“I don’t want that,”
 or
 “I don’t understand that,”
 or
 are you noticing your brain wondering if it could be better before you’ve gathered enough data to know?

Have you made money so far communicating who you help and selling your offer?

Let’s also get curious about the distinction you’re making between “choosing themselves” and outcomes like healthier relationships, improved health, or greater success at work. Are those actually different results, or are they often downstream effects of the same work?

For example, if a woman learns to stop saying yes when she means no, sets healthier boundaries, and consistently creates space for herself, what happens to her relationships? What happens to her stress levels? What happens to the way she shows up at work? What happens to her confidence?

I’m wondering if your offer and those outcomes may not be competing with each other as much as your brain thinks they are.

When women come to you, what problem are they saying they have? What words are they using?

Are they saying, “I need help choosing myself,” or are they saying, “I’m exhausted,” “I’m resentful,” “My relationships feel one-sided,” “I’m overwhelmed,” etc.?

The reason is because sometimes the transformation we provide and the problem clients are actively trying to solve are not described in the same language. Before possibly changing the offer, I’d get very curious about what your ideal clients already know they want help with and whether your current messaging is connecting those dots clearly enough.

Lastly, 
how many times have you presented this offer to potential clients, and what feedback have you received so far?

Bring your answers back for more coaching or any other thoughts arising that you could use some help teasing out. Thanks, Coach!

title: New Program
question:
Thank you for this. I love the simplicity of you’re not overwhelmed, you just need to make decisions.

I also like the focus in on the workshop vs. the entire program. I do know what I want the workshop to be.

It’s called “Release Your Body Story.” Every woman has a story about themself and their body. For many, it’s laced in negativity. The belief it’s not good enough. It needs to be smaller to be worthy. It needs to be ‘perfect’. I want to walk the participants through uncovering what that story is, understanding where it came from (where it was learned…. because that’s innate), I want to then walk them through how to create a new story that feels true and powerful RIGHT NOW and I think it would be fun to do some sort of simple ritual to release the old one and step into the new.

I want them to walk away with a new perspective on their bodies that they’ve never had before. I want them to feel a connection with their bodies and to walk away with this powerful knowing (even if it’s just a part of them) that feels like wow, maybe my body is enough right as it is in this moment.

Who are you when you sit down and map this out anyway? — I love this. I am the coach I want to be when I do this. I’m focused. I’m in belief. I know what I’m doing. I’m confident. I’m inspired. I feel in control. In the drivers seat.

I’m going to take this into focus too… really paying attention when my brain goes to overwhlem… is it just that I’m asking my brain to decide? And what if I just sit down and make a decision… I don’t know why but that makes things feel so much easier for me and I tend to get into overwhelm a lot. Into that freeze mode.
answer:
Hey coach,

You are so welcome and I love seeing the shift happening in real time. That perspective really does change everything. Sometimes also just asking how can this be simple? how can this be easy? is enough to redirect your brain. Not because it magically removes the work, but because it stops your brain from running its very practiced story of “this is too much.” Gently forcing a decision create movement and information, power move.

And that’s what I want you noticing your brain will default to overwhelm because it’s familiar, not because it’s true. So when you catch it, it’s less about fixing it and more about gently redirecting it. Of course my brain is looking for everything at once… and I’m going to decide where to focus instead. That’s the shift.

What I really want to highlight here is this, you made a decision and look what happened.

You have a clear, thoughtful, compelling workshop. The moment you decided, your knowing showed up. That’s not just a little part of this it’s how this works. Decision creates direction, and direction focuses your energy. It’s like taking a flashlight that’s been scattered everywhere and pointing it in one place. Of course everything becomes clearer.

When you sit down to map this out, if  you still notice leaving things open that actually need a decision to, now you know how to get into action.

Because those open loops are usually where overwhelm sneaks back in. It sounds like “I’m still figuring it out,” but what it often means is “I haven’t decided yet.” And you already know what happens when you do.

I also love who you said you are when you’re in this, focused, In belief,  Confident and  In control.

That’s not something you’re trying to become that’s who you are when you’re deciding. So it’s less about finding that version of you and more about practicing staying there.

What are you believing about yourself when you’re in that energy? Cultivate those high quality thought about yourself and notice the shift.

I’m asking because that belief is what sustains it. It’s what keeps you out of the freeze and in the driver’s seat. The workshop you’re creating is about helping them rewrite their body story but you’re doing the exact same thing here with your identity as a coach.

And I want to say this to highlight for you,  your workshop already sounds incredibly powerful. You’re not just giving them information you’re giving them an experience. Uncovering the story, seeing where it came from, choosing a new one, and then releasing the old that’s meaningful work. That’s the kind of shift people remember, can’t wait to hear more about it.

So when you feel that pull back into overwhelm or freeze, just come back to this: What decision am I avoiding right now? Why? 

How can I make this decision simple and easy too?

Because every time you do that, you’re reinforcing something new
that you don’t have to spin, you can lead. And you’re already doing that, great work coach!

title: Day 24 / 30 – who do I need to be to generate consults?
question:
This was genuinely invaluable coaching.

When creating my plan I also tried to draw out who I would need to become in order to have the result I desire – 12 clients who signed my year long coaching package.

I would need to believe that:

generating consults is normal

I am skilled at generating consults

I know why my coaching is worth $8k and why it’s a year long process

when people say no it’s because I either need to get better at selling or they just aren’t a good fit

I am an experienced entrepreneur

I know what it means to be an entrepreneur

To answer your questions:

When I meet people I feel hesitation, I think mainly because I don’t know what to share with them. My go to things to share lately is: “it’s been a hard couple years but I’m on the upswing.” Some of my thoughts are, “I don’t know what to share, I don’t want them to know what’s been going on.” I felt very avoidant of people for a while because of these thoughts. Again that fear of people finding out that I’m not doing well or “I’m not successful anymore.”

When I tell people I’m a coach I feel a little flustered which is frustrating to me because I used to be so good at talking about it with confidence and being taken seriously because of that. Now I am constantly telling the story that my business has been struggling, that I’ve been struggling, that I’m trying to get back on my feet again within my business. It’s all true but not exactly making it sound like I’m open or ready for clients.

When I’m alone in my room, doing my work, I do feel like I can help people but I definitely don’t feel like I can help the average person while I’m talking to them in my everyday life. It’s so frustrating to admit but I am often worrying that people will think I’m sad or pathetic when I interact with them. Ugh that’s so unhelpful! I guess I am seeing very clearly why I am currently stuck in the results I have. I’m not thinking supportive thoughts to create change.

It’s so odd to me that I feel like things are getting better in the safety and confines of my working environment but the second I go out into the world and interact with people I feel differently. I can sense that when I tell people I’m a coach I am telling them from a place where I am like wincing. Like “ugh yeah I have a business, I’m a coach, but it’s been really hard the last couple years and life hasn’t been that good because of it.”

I’m having a really hard time seeing how to untangle all of this and change it.
answer:
Hey coach,

I’m really glad you are receiving the coaching so well. What you shared all of this shows us you’re actually seeing the real issue very clearly. You’re not confused you’re aware. And that’s what makes this so workable. You are aware of where you are and how to get where you want to go.

You’ve done something powerful already,  you mapped out who you need to become and what she believes. That’s the work. But what you’re noticing now is the gap between seeing it on paper and embodying it in real life especially in moments that feel exposed, like talking to people.

Right now, it’s less about figuring out what to believe you’ve already done that and more about noticing which version of you is leading in the moment.

When you’re alone, in your room, doing your work you said you feel like you can help people. When you’re out in the world you feel hesitant, flustered, almost like you’re bracing. When you’re talking to someone and you feel that hesitation what are you making that moment mean about you?

I’m asking because that meaning is what’s driving the feeling. Not the person, not the conversation not the words you are saying or what their response it.

Right now it sounds like the meaning is something like:
“They might see I’m struggling”  and “That means I’m not successful” and therefore  “That makes me less credible.” That is not the truth.  Of course you’d feel hesitant if that’s the story running.

So instead of trying to “fix” the hesitation, I want you to look at the lens you’re using. Nothing has gone wrong here except the way you’re interpreting where you are.

You’ve been through a hard couple of years. That’s real.
But the part that’s keeping you stuck is what you’re making that mean about your identity your ability to help them.

Why do you think you have had a hard couple years? look with COMPASSION. And what if that does not have anything to do with your ability to help them with their struggle? How is it true that it could help you and them that you struggled?  Why is it that what you have been through makes you the perfect person to share coaching tools?

If this season of your business wasn’t evidence of failure what else could it be?

Right now, when you say “I’m a coach,” it sounds like you’re immediately buffering it with explanation almost softening it before anyone can judge it. How is that a self protection you don’t need to perpetuate now?

It’s also the  thing disconnecting you from the version of you who naturally creates clients. Instead of trying to “feel confident,” I want you to get intentional about what you’re choosing to think on purpose in those moments.

When you tell someone you’re a coach, what do you actually believe about coaching?

What do you know to be true about what it does for people?

I’m asking because when your focus shifts from “how am I being perceived?” to “this is something that genuinely helps people” your energy changes. You move from self-conscious to service. And that’s a completely different conversation.

What do most people misunderstand about coaching that you actually see clearly?

You said it feels “odd” that you feel strong in your work environment but not out in the world.

In your room, there’s no risk of judgment so your brain relaxes.
Out in the world, there is perceived risk so your brain offers protection. The goal isn’t to eliminate that. The goal is to lead anyway.

This is where the identity work becomes real: You don’t become her once you feel confident in every room. You become her by deciding who you are before the room reflects it back.

What would it look like to tell a cleaner story? Something like:
“I’m a life coach. I help people create real change in how they think and show up in their lives.”

And then stop. No apology. No backstory. No softening.

Let the silence be there.

That’s where you start building self-trust.

You don’t untangle this by fixing everything at once.
You untangle it by catching the moment you start making your current circumstances mean something about your worth and interrupting it.

You can accept where you are 
and
 actively create more.
You can acknowledge it’s been hard 
and
 not make that your identity.
You can be in process 
and
 be someone who leads.

You’re not trying to become someone new from scratch.
You’re practicing staying with her especially when it feels uncomfortable.

title: Haven’t Created Demand
question:
Ok, so I’m relaunching my group for July start— and a decision I made and then “unmade” was that I was going to keep it open. People could join at anytime, which I guess technically made it a “membership” in a way.

And then, because I was trying to push for sales, I decided I was going to go back to closed launches… 3 months in.

Oops.

So, now I’m wondering if I want to open this as a cohort or recommit to my vision of year round ability to join.

I notice that I keep wanting to change the C to avoid my own discomfort. The fear of doing it wrong, the idea that I’m not selling enough or needing to sell constantly, in a way that drains me.

I know that I haven’t been showing up to new places, growing my audience, so I don’t suspect that right now people are going to be lined up for this reopening of my program.

The offer is weekly group coaching, 6 months, $2500.

And even still, with the group currently at 3, I’m noticing my own relationship to when attendance is low, that the commitment is low. Because previously, I sold the group at 5k and even 6k— and when it was 6k, attendance was consistent.

So I guess I’m waffling not only on the demand re: cohort vs. membership, but also the price— woof.

The other thing is that I changed my audience from multi hyphenate performers to creatives. And even though that is just a more all encompassing category, I’m noticing that the work feels different/diluted, bc I’m no longer focused on creating a specific outcome. I started selling an emotional experience/relationship with self at the core.

I am feeling uncertain, unsure, of who I am as a coach and who I want to help. Even though, I know I could help everyone.

It feels like I’m moving through an ego death and nothing feels the same as it did over the past few years. It’s all just ideas.
answer:
Hey Coach,

Thanks for sharing all of this. For a moment, let’s anchor into some play and just see what comes up. Stay with me here.

1. When you close your eyes and imagine what results you want to create in your business (from a place of fulfillment and joy) what do you see? Share anything and everything.

When you aren’t worried about doing it wrong, what lights you up?

Imagine you have 15 clients who are eager to log onto their coaching call with you tomorrow… 

What’s the dream structure for your business/programs?

Who are you serving and why?

What are you coaching on because you love it so much?

Lastly, imagine that your business is thriving… what does thriving mean?

How much money are you making? How many clients do you have?

What does your day-to-day life look like and what do you imagine doing/feeling then that you may not do/feel now?

Let’s start there since you feel you’re in an “ego death”. Really let yourself anchor into the vision of it all. Let’s just explore where your mind goes when you allow it to play without rules or expectations. Bring your answers back here for so we can keep coaching on how to apply your answers to what may need to happen next. Thanks Coach!

title: Part 3…
question:
I see that now, that my brain is very focused on what is wrong…and I want to keep focusing on the version of me that creates instead. And I want to focus on what I do have and on building the business I have been hoping to for years.

You are correct that part of the struggle is that I had an expectation that after this much time it should be easier, and ultimately, I shouldn’t still be failing like I am. Because ultimately I do feel like I am failing. And all of it creates discouragement, not something that will benefit me in any way.

It is hard to see that this stage isn’t a problem…because I hate my current results and the way I feel about them so much. But I do think I could use this stage to learn some powerful lessons (and I believe they will be very helpful in my own work with future clients).

It’s such a flip to look at what is easier…my brain has a hard time b/c it is SO focused on actually not just business…but truly a lot in life being harder right now. And again, I don’t want to focus on that.

I think I have definitely grown in my belief that I do want to do this no matter how hard…it is my calling and my purpose and I love it. I might need to do other work but I don’t want to stop coaching. Quitting is not an option.

I am growing in my consults skill, and my marketing too. I am also learning email. I am getting more diligent with my time…quite a ways to go there yet tho! 🙂

As far as what I know about creating consults…that one is still a big challenge for me. It is still hard for me to believe that I create them. I know we are always told that, but I can’t really figure that one out. I think something else at play is seeing many other business professionals that are struggling too. I want to not be one of them! I want to say, this is how I used coaching and grew my business when so many around me were not. Here, let me show you too! That is what I want so badly.

An idea I have been thinking about is doing a workshop or webinar to bring in 1 on 1 clients…and my brain immediately goes to “You always spend so much time on those and no one signs up.” See how mean my brain is!! So that makes it hard to move forward.

I meet people in person with friends, online, in networking groups. I genuinely love talking to people so conversation is easy…letting them know I can help them/inspiring them to set up a consult is where I am missing the mark.
answer:
Hi Coach,

The first thing I want to invite you to question is your expectation. Why shouldn’t you be failing like you are?

Take your time with that question. Not from judgment, but from a curious and compassionate place.

You mention several times that you feel like you’re failing. The definition of failure I love is simply the omission of necessary action. It’s incredibly neutral. If we looked at your situation through that lens, would you still call it failure? Or would you say there are simply actions you haven’t discovered, developed, or taken enough of yet?

Why do you think you shouldn’t be missing pieces of the puzzle?

If you’ve never created this result before, how would you know exactly what works? We don’t know what we don’t know. Building a business is often the scientific method in real life. You try things. Some work. Some don’t. You gather data. You adjust. You try again. What if this stage isn’t evidence that you’re failing, but evidence that you’re learning?

I also noticed you said the discouragement won’t benefit you in any way. I think it’s worth looking at that thought. Is the discouragement coming from where you are, or from what you’re making where you are mean?

You shared something powerful: “I hate my current results and the way I feel about them.”

This is where I would spend some time.

My number one recommendation is to clean up how you feel about your current results as quickly as possible. Not because you have to love them. Not because you have to pretend they’re okay. But because hating where you are won’t help you create where you want to go. It slows you down.

I have so much compassion for hating your current results. But can you find some acceptance for this stage? Can you find a way to make peace with being a learner here? You cannot create a positive outcome from constantly arguing with reality.

I would also spend time strengthening the thoughts that are already serving you. ITC on how these are true and who you are when you think them and take action from here.

“Quitting is not an option.”

“I am growing in my consult skills.”

“I am learning marketing.”

“I am learning email.”

“I am becoming more diligent with my time.”

These thoughts matter because they are true. Find evidence for them. Write it down. Do an ITC on them. Let your brain see the proof. These thoughts create inspiration, gratitude, and commitment. They connect you to the version of you who is becoming the coach and business owner you want to be.

And regarding consults, I don’t actually think your problem is that you don’t know how to create clients.

Look at what you’ve already shared.

You meet people.

You network.

You have conversations easily.

You connect with people.

You have ideas for workshops and webinars.

Those are all parts of creating clients.

The skill you’re developing is how to inspire someone to take the next step.

That’s different than not knowing how.

When your brain says, “I can’t figure out how to create consults,” it shuts down curiosity. But what if the truth is, “I’m learning how to inspire people to want the help I offer”?

Notice the difference.

The workshop example is a perfect illustration. Your brain immediately offers, “You always spend so much time on those and nobody signs up.”

Okay. Maybe that happened before. But what if that wasn’t failure? What if it was data?

Why didn’t they sign up?

What did they need to hear that they didn’t hear?

How could you explain the value differently?

What did you learn about your messaging?

Those questions keep you moving.

The only way to learn how to say it in a way that resonates is to keep saying it. To keep meeting people. To keep making offers. To keep evaluating. To stay in massive action while remaining curious.

After each conversation, instead of making it mean something about you, ask:

What was I thinking?

What was I feeling?

Did I make a clear offer?

What worked?

What didn’t?

What will I try next time?

That’s how businesses are built.

And I want to reflect back something you may not fully see yet. The most powerful thing in your entire post wasn’t your struggle. It was this:

“Quitting is not an option.”

That thought tells me you’re still in the game.

Now the work is helping your brain stop using your current results as evidence against yourself and start using them as information for your next move.

You absolutely can figure this out Coach!  
I’d also encourage you to revisit this episode if you haven’t recently.

Episode 17: How To Get Consults

Not because it contains a magic answer, but because right now your brain needs more evidence for possibility than it does evidence for why this is hard.

Keep bringing yourself back to the version of you that creates. She isn’t created after the results come. She’s created by how she thinks, feels, and shows up while she’s building them.

title: overcoming objections and beliefs
question:
The last coach was so right. My brain keeps predicting that the next 5–7 years will be failure and that I won’t make money because of the history I’ve had. Sometimes I look at the job market and social work jobs, and I genuinely don’t see anything else I want to do. I feel mentally drained from it all.
