One of my goals right now is to use Ask a Coach as much as possible while I work on consistently showing up for my business. The next thing I’m focused on is content. I’ve been slowly creating content, but I haven’t posted yet because I keep telling myself I need to become consistent first.

I’ve made organic offers before, but I still hold myself back from posting. I keep going back and forth about whether I should wait until I have a full week (or more) of content prepared before I start posting consistently. Part of me feels like it’s strategy, because I want something ready for the days I don’t feel confident or consistent. But another part of me wonders if this is just another way my brain is trying to keep me safe by avoiding posting altogether.
answer:
Hey Coach,

First, I want to celebrate you for deciding that one of your goals is to consistently show up for your business and use Ask a Coach while you build that. That matters. You are already practicing something different by bringing awareness to the pattern instead of just unconsciously living inside of it.

I also want to direct you to Episode 11 of the podcast: 
Creating Content vs. Creating Clients
, because I think it will really help you separate actual strategy from what your brain may be calling strategy in order to keep you safe.

You said, “I haven’t posted yet,” and this is where I want you to slow down and really study what happens in your mind around posting. 
This is so normal.

Your brain will offer excuse after excuse to avoid the thing that feels vulnerable. I know this from experience. Now I think about it as strengthening my consistency muscle. Going first. Going often. Showing up with purpose before I feel fully ready.

At the core, this is not really a content problem. It’s a relationship with discomfort problem.

Your brain is trying to solve for emotional safety before action:

“I should wait.”

“I want something ready.”

“I need to become consistent first.”

“I don’t feel confident.”

“I haven’t posted yet.” ( very sneaky one )

That last one is sneaky because your brain presents it like evidence. But “I haven’t posted yet” is just a circumstance from the past. 
Your brain is taking it and using it to predict the future too.

I want you to notice the model underneath what’s happening:

C — You want to create consistent content for your business.

T — “I need to become consistent first.”

F — Pressure. Doubt. Hesitation.

A — Waiting. Preparing. Overthinking. Not posting. Looking for the “right” plan first.

R — You stay inconsistent and create more evidence for the original thought.

The reason I want you to see this is because the problem is not actually your ability to post. The problem is the sentence your brain keeps offering you before the action. 
And this is important: 
The action you want cannot come from the identity of someone waiting to feel ready first.

So instead of asking:

“How do I finally become confident and consistent?” 
Try asking:

“What would the version of me who is building consistency do today?”

Even if it’s messy.

Even if it’s uncomfortable.

Even if the post is simple.

That question matters because people often try to figure out 
how
 to create results while still thinking like the version of themselves who avoids the discomfort required to create them.

I also want you to think about your 
why
 not in a just motivational way, but because service changes where your focus goes.

Who needs to hear what you have to say?

What are they struggling with right now that your perspective could genuinely help with?

What happens if they never hear it because you stayed focused on yourself long enough to avoid posting?

When your focus stays on you  how you look, whether you’re doing it right, whether people will judge you   your brain experiences posting as danger. But when you focus on helping, serving, adding value, and connecting, it shifts the emotional experience entirely. When we get out of our own way we get out there and really help others!

I also recommend deciding ahead of time what consistency means for you right now. 
Not ideal consistency realistic for you to create the habit and overcome your brains nonsense and resistance. 

Two times a week?

Three times a week?

Something doable enough that you can build trust with yourself.

Consistency is not built by waiting to become a naturally consistent person. It’s built through repeated evidence. Through showing yourself, over and over again, “I do what I say I’m going to do.” 
And let it be messy in the beginning.

People spend so much time trying to avoid inconsistency that they never build consistency. 
You are becoming the version of you who shows up for the business.

I also want you to notice this:

When you don’t follow your original plan, what tends to happen instead? 
This question matters because there is usually a replacement behavior running automatically: 
scrolling, 
researching, 
rewriting, 
planning, 
consuming, 
busy work,

overthinking? Catch this and redirect it.  You will be able to help your client when they share a pattern and it will be something you have experience ovecoming.

You can’t change a pattern you can’t see. 
Once you identify the replacement behavior, gently interrupt it. Not from shame. From awareness. 
“Ohhh… this is what my brain does when posting feels vulnerable.” 
And then the next question becomes:

How do I take the action in spite of the emotion? 
Not: 
“How do I remove the emotion first?” 
That shift changes everything.

I also want to offer you this:

Just because your brain says, “I don’t want to do it right now,” does not mean you won’t, can’t, or shouldn’t. 
It just means you are in the process of becoming someone new.

Keep showing yourself that you can do it Coach! 

Especially before you fully believe it. This is the work and it’s so worth it.

title: Believing They Are Ready Now Pt. 2
question:
I’m responding to the following coaching from my recent question entitled “Believing They Are Ready Now”:

So instead of asking, “How do I accept this belief?” I want to consider your current belief is causing the lack of safety.

My response:

When I sit with this, it feels true. I think there is a belief I have that if I do start to believe people are ready to buy now I will fall on my face and be humiliated. Like…I’ll take action from this place of believing they are ready and they won’t be ready and I’ll come off pushy and sales-y and I’ll alienate people who would have otherwise become clients if I had just let them become ready in their own time. So in this way it’s like…I’m feeling like I’m “forcing” them to be ready…which is still not the same as believing they are ready.

I’m realizing my brain is kind of going in a bit of a circle…like “it’s not safe to believe they are ready because they actually aren’t ready and if I believe that I’ll be believing a lie.” So the unwillingness to believe is being cited as the reason I don’t feel safe believing. LOL.

If I had to guess why this is happening, I would say:

1. there might have been a past version of me in my business who “pushed too hard” and sold too aggressively and then people distanced themselves from me (I also used to make someone unsubscribing from my email list after I started making more frequent offers a sign that I was being too pushy and if I had just done it perfectly I would have kept them on my email list and they would have become a client eventually)

2. I want everyone to like me and if I believe they are ready to buy I will behave in ways that make them not like me. This might sound really extreme but it’s kind of like if you believe someone wants to get married and you propose too early in the relationship and it comes off as creepy but if you had just waited they might have gotten there eventually…like, making an offer at the wrong time could be detrimental to the relationship and I will make more frequent offers if I believe they are ready

3. If I believe they are ready…like REALLY believe it…and I make offers…and they don’t take action…then it will be a failure on my part. I can’t just hide behind “they aren’t ready.” Like if you make mac & cheese and offer it to someone that you KNOW likes mac & cheese and they don’t take it it’s like…”what’s wrong with MY mac & cheese”…does that make sense?
answer:
Hey Coach,

You did a really good job here of actually seeing yourself in the cycle while you’re in it.  Most people don’t catch it this clearly and with this much clarity. Such a good example of the power of looking at what you are thinking. Watching your pattern repeating give you all the power.

Notice what you said with so much acceptance and compassion.
 (I’m realizing my brain is kind of going in a bit of a circle…like “it’s not safe to believe they are ready because they actually aren’t ready and if I believe that I’ll be believing a lie.” So the unwillingness to believe is being cited as the reason I don’t feel safe believing. LOL.)

“The unwillingness to believe is being cited as the reason I don’t feel safe believing.” You are onto yourself, that is how you become in charge of your results.

The truth is you have a lot of story keeping this cycle going. And now that you see it, this becomes less about figuring it out and more about what you’re willing to do with it.

Because right now, you’re choosing to stay in it.
Not wrong for this choice, it’s normal and now you get to chose what you make true not the story is just true.

And the reason you stay is not because you don’t have the right belie it’s because of what you would have to feel if you stepped out of it.

So let’s look at that.

If you did believe they are read and you showed up and made offers from that place What would you have to be willing to feel?

I’m asking this because this is the actual work. Not the belief itself but the emotional capacity behind it.

You named a few things already:
Humiliation.
Being seen as pushy.
People not liking you.
Being wrong.
People not choosing you.

So of course your brain offers you a “safer” option:
Stay in “they’re not ready yet.”

That way you believe don’t have to risk any of that.

Now let’s go into what you made this mean.

You talked about your past self being pushy.
But notice that’s not a fact. That’s a story you’re still using as evidence.

What are you making it mean about you if someone unsubscribes or doesn’t respond to an offer? Why?
Because that meaning is what’s driving the fear not the action itself. What do you want to believe that serves you?

Same thing with wanting everyone to like you.

How is that keeping you from actually showing up in service? Because those two things don’t coexist well you being liked and you leading. What do you want to believe ? How do you create that new belief?

If they don’t take it you up on your offer it becomes about you. Why do you think you make it mean anything about you? What else could it mean?  What belief would be better for you to practice believing ? What if it actually has nothing to do with you and everything to do with what they are thinking and feeling?

Are you willing to let people not choose you without making it mean something about your value?

Because if not, you will keep yourself in this cycle to avoid that feeling.

And then we come back to what you already said:

You’re unwilling to believe.
Yes and that is because you’re unwilling to feel.

So now the question becomes:

Are you willing to feel all of it?
The discomfort, the vulnerability, the possibility of being misunderstood, not chosen, not liked? Because when you are this cycle loses its power.

Who do you need to become to respond differently here?

What do you notice about how you’re talking about the cycle? Because even in your words, you can hear where you’re giving it authority.

You are one thought away from shifting this.
Not a perfect thought just one you’re willing to try on.

This is powerful work and entrepreneurship is all about choosing the hard work.  Why do you want to chose this path and break free from the cycle you are in now?

Now that you see it and you notice what your currently believing, what do you want to do? What do you want your response to be now?

title: 3 of 30 days of coaching
question:
Good thought about my skill, commitment, and self-trust. I think the first thing that comes up is doubt around whether I will get my clients the results they want. So if they aren’t getting them, they can easily leave…something like that. But here is an interesting piece: my therapy clients get results. They stay with me for a long time. I have had some for several YEARS. My clients, who are my ideal clients, love me. My coaching clients have gotten results, too. But with coaching feels like there is more at stake. There are more expectations. Coaching feels special, and clients who look for coaches want results. Sometimes I think people who are in therapy don’t really expect much. That is only a few of my clients; they just want to “talk.” I charge a good amount (for a therapist, anyway), so most of my clients are with me to do the work. But, still, maybe with coaching I feel more pressure??

How many sessions would you include in a “package” and why? Right now, my package is bi-weekly for 6 months. I feel like clients need at least this long to see a shift. Bi-weekly…honestly, I have no space to see someone weekly right now. And, I like the space in between calls for me and for my clients to digest our work. They do have access to me in between calls.

What might you learn about yourself as a coach if you trusted yourself to stay (when you feel challenged, or the client feels challenged), even when it’s not as easy to do so? I have definitely done this. There is always some sort of expansion involved in the end. I am def better at staying with a client when they are uncomfortable. But when I do stay with myself, I get better at what I do.

How might it serve you and your client to commit to several sessions without an easy “out”? What might you learn in that process? For me, it helps with financial stability and planning. I also get to know them better, which aids in the “getting results.” For the client, it proves to themselves that they are committed to themselves, very important. They have to learn to stay with the discomfort, and that is how they get results. They improve resiliency and emotional intelligence. They learn they can do hard things and feel hard emotions. All of which improves emotional and physical health.

Lots about getting results today…..hmmmm….
answer:
Hi again, Coach!

I want to start by reflecting something back to you. You are incredibly self-aware here. You can already see that a package supports your client, supports you, deepens the work, and creates better results. You’re not confused about the value. In fact, you’re noticing the exact place where your brain tightens, and that’s such clean work! Great job!

Let’s go right to the sentence that holds the charge for you.

“Coaching feels like there is more at stake. There are more expectations.”

I want you to really look at that, because that sentence is doing a lot of work for your brain.

More at stake than what, exactly?

A client paying you in any capacity is bringing expectation into the room. Your therapy clients expect something. Your coaching clients expect something. Even session by session clients expect something. The moment money and time are exchanged, there is an inherent desire for movement, relief, clarity, or change. That part is not unique to coaching. So when your brain says “coaching has more at stake,” it’s not pointing to something objective. It’s creating a category where the standard suddenly feels higher, heavier, and more risky for you to hold.

I want you to get curious about what that belief is protecting you from.

If coaching has “more at stake,” then it makes sense that you would feel pressure. It makes sense that you would hesitate to lock someone into a package. It gives you a reason to keep things a little more open, a little more flexible, and a little less “defined.” It creates space for you to exit if it ever feels like you might not meet that imagined standard. It’s a very subtle form of self-protection around your identity as a coach. Because if there isn’t actually more at stake, then what’s left is this: You are a coach who creates results, and you are asking clients to commit to the process required for those results. Now the only thing to stand on is your skill, your process, and your leadership. That’s a much more exposed place to stand.

I also want you to notice the evidence you gave yourself without even realizing it. You get your clients results. They stay. They trust you! That’s a huge deal and all the more reason to believe clients enjoy the consistency, the safety, the space to been seen over time. You already know how to stay in the discomfort with them and with yourself, and you become a better coach because of it.

The real work here isn’t figuring out if coaching holds more pressure. It’s deciding whether you’re willing to lead at the level you already know you’re capable of without softening it through that thought. 
What shifts for you if coaching doesn’t have more at stake, and it simply requires clearer leadership and deeper trust in yourself?

title: RE: Niche Decisions
question:
I am a Life Coach – and I have two main groups of people I want to serve and it’s now become SUPER CLEAR to me who they are..and I am feeling confused on how to best navigate bringing both types of clients in…like do I have one main IG account and post content for all of them or do I have two separate accounts…and then I have a main podcast, do I just share all the things there or I tried to have two separate podcasts and accounts in the past and it felt like to

I want to coach & have a couple clients right now:

1- overall high performing women & men to live their best lives…with 1:1 and a new group coaching offer I have.

2- NFL athletes & coaches – no clients yet. I have started to pursue on & off the last year, more off, and now I am ready to go ALL IN & be their NFL Mindset & Life Coach.

I have thoughts that go back and forth to what way to move forward.

1) Speaking to the NFL athletes feels like I could be very specific and speak to them in my marketing with that specific IG account. And that would be really effective and stand out….but then I’d have to have my main account to serve everyone else and that feels like a lot to manage, like two separate businesses. I tried that in the past and the NFL account did drop off.

But then,

2) I think I could speak about my life coaching & more general concepts how I help on my one main account, no separate niche account for the NFL athletes, and just make some specific posts for them under the main account. But question if that is enough to be seen by the NFL athletes, and question if the ‘regular’ people would also look away because there is NFL content.

How can I help decide which way to move forward with??

I did the work this weekend on why the NFL, it keeps calling me back and I have multiple reasons to pursue it, and I want to preserve my revenue and also love to do general life coaching for others & have a big vision to grow & expand life coaching as a whole & be an industry leader and see doing that with both angles.

Help me see what I am missing or to get clear! Thank you!
answer:
Hi Coach,

You shared that you’re now SUPER CLEAR on the two groups you want to serve! Amazing, and then you asked how to get clear on the way forward.

The first thing I want to explore is this: what makes you think you’re unclear?

I ask because everything you wrote sounds pretty clear. You know who you want to help. You know why the NFL keeps calling you back. You know you want to continue serving high-performing men and women. You even see a vision that includes both.

So what if the issue isn’t clarity?

It is not uncommon for our brains to tell us we’re confused right when it’s time to execute. Sometimes “I need more clarity” is really “I’m afraid of choosing wrong.”

As I read your question, I notice that you already see the options. One account or two. One podcast or two. General content with occasional NFL content, or separate brands. Those are business decisions, not clarity problems.

What I would get curious about is your belief that there is a right answer hiding somewhere that you haven’t found yet.

What if there isn’t?

What if there are simply two viable paths and your job is to choose one and start collecting data?

You mentioned trying separate accounts in the past and the NFL account dropped off. What do you make that experience mean? Is it evidence that it won’t work, or is it evidence that you stopped pursuing it consistently?

I ask because those are two very different conclusions.

You also mentioned wanting to preserve revenue while pursuing the NFL. That feels important. When you think about marketing, selling, and delivering to both groups, what concerns come up? Is the concern truly about the platform structure, or is it about dividing your attention?

If you had to form a theory today, without looking for the perfect answer, what would you do?

Let’s pretend I told you that you would be successful either way. One account or two accounts. One podcast or two podcasts. If success was guaranteed, which option would you choose?

That question matters because it often reveals preference underneath all the analysis. It can also reveal that confusion keeps you from putting the offer out into the world. This is normal we tend to want to be absolutely clear before taking action.

At the end of the day, the 2k process is still the same. Meet people. Tell them what you do. Make offers. Continue refining.

The NFL athletes, NFL coaches, high-performing men and women, your 1:1 clients, your group clients those are different audiences, but the bigger question is whether you’re willing to decide on a strategy and then commit long enough to see what happens.

You may not be missing clarity. You can run your offer through Irresistible Offer Protocol Worksheet and and then sell yourself on the reasons you have for choosing the platforms to sell instead of waiting to be certain.  It is making decisions and then doing the work to commit to believing in yourself to market and sell it the way you decide.

You may simply be at the place where clarity has done its job and now it’s time to make some decisions.  What if the you decided to be clear and uncertain while moving forward?

What are your thoughts about this coaching?

title: 0 sales so far
question:
Hello AAC! I am selling an in-person event, $500/ticket. I have up to 15 seats. And had early bird pricing for $400, no one took me up on this! After postponing the event by 2 weeks, due to scheduling— I am still sitting with 0 sales.

I have 3 weeks to sell out this event, and I’m noticing that I’m getting stuck. Because, the freaking selling work is the same, regardless of what the offer is. I thought about sending personal invites, but it feels salesy. There are about 60 people who are regularly opening the emails but not clicking.

And I can see that I’m being tentative about this, yet again.

And now my brain is spinning in pricing drama. Did I over price it? Do people actually want to spend a day with me to change their life? LOL (I mean obviously). But I’m want to get to the place of enjoying selling this.
answer:
Hi Coach,

You mentioned that you’re “getting stuck,” and I’m curious why you think you are stuck?

Because with three weeks left to sell, thats is not nothing,  notice where your brain keeps going. It’s going to the pricing, whether people want it, whether they want to spend a day with you, whether it’s worth it. Your brain is trying to solve for certainty before you continue taking action.

But what would be different if you truly believed there was already a line of people wanting to purchase tickets right now?

If you were already in the energy of the room being sold out… what would look different?

Would you be questioning the price?

Or would you be focused on the experience people are about to have?

Would you spend time thinking about who isn’t buying? Or who IS ?

Or would you be talking about the event in the most excited, confident, inviting way possible?

Those questions matter because they show you where your attention currently is. Your focus is shaping the energy you’re bringing into the selling. The thought ” I am stuck ” is driving your decisions here.

And I want you to think about something else.

What if Stacey had a special event and knew you opened every email, but decided not to personally invite you because she thought it might feel “salesy”?

Honestly… I’d be heartbroken.

Sometimes personal invitations are not pressure. Sometimes they are care. Sometimes they are leadership. Sometimes people are waiting to feel seen personally before they move. What if that is true? What changes in you if you believed that?

What makes something feel salesy is  the thought  behind it. If someone wants it is that salesy or are you thinking about the people that are not wanting it?

If you believed people genuinely wanted this experience, wanted transformation, wanted proximity to you, wanted the room… how would you invite them differently? Get specific here really flush out who you would be before the how you sell.

You also asked why your brain is spinning in pricing drama right now. I think that question matters because the brain always has a very good reason.

What is the pricing drama protecting you from?

Disappointment?

Rejection?

Expending a lot of energy without guaranteed results?

That would make sense.

Most humans want proof before effort. But creating something new does not work that way. There is always a period where you don’t yet know the value equation. You don’t know how many offers it will take. You don’t know how many no’s happen before the yeses. That’s part of building anything meaningful.

And what if you were willing to play with that instead of making it mean something about your ability to sell?

Because if you stopped telling yourself you were stuck… then what?

What ideas become available?

What actions open up?

What conversations could you have?

What would happen if you allowed yourself to be tentative and still move?

The sold-out event is not created by the person who feels no fear, no doubt, no discomfort. 
It’s usually created by the person willing to feel all of that and continue anyway.

The person willing to hear no without making it mean nobody wants it.

The person willing to keep reaching people.

The person willing to believe before there’s evidence.

You do not need to remove every emotion to sell this out.

You need willingness.

Willingness to invite.

Willingness to believe.

Willingness to be uncomfortable.

Willingness to let people decide.

You can do this, Coach!

title: Taking action pt 3
question:
I did make it mean they don’t want or need my help. I asked if burnout prevention was relevant for her team of teachers and then the head of the school said ‘no our sick leave is very low’ and I let the conversation end. Now that I’m considering this, I’m aware of believing this objection while in reality I also help with shortening grading time and navigating parent teacher conversations.

I love thinking about a problem worth solving and at the same time feel a familiar frustration and helplessness because when I was a teacher I tried to communicate and put into words how ‘heavy’ and all consuming the job was and felt that management kind of dismissed it as a ‘me’ problem instead of a by product of the job. The expectation piece is interesting because I just found the thought ‘I don’t really expect this to work. I’m only doing it to get me moving forward and face my fears of telling people I can help them.

When the teacher (male, tall) said I was too late I felt rejected and confused. I was able to ‘stick’ with confusion to ask some questions and had a short conversation with him but it was right in front of a lot of people (teachers and admin) and I felt very insecure and unsure. I saw the teachers’ faces and made it mean that they really didn’t want to hear about burnout prevention. The lady from admin asked about the flyer and she either laughed or scoffed, it was a noise of disbelief and that whole interaction gave me the unhelpful thought ‘see they don’t want need and believe in this’.

Next time I would want to be able to have a real conversation about it. I would ask if there was any support before during after the burnout and if he approached his job any differently than before the burnout. I would show up just as a curious person, interested in the topic.

My current interpretation is making me feel frustrated and worried, because I’m starting to consider if this is really possible for me.

Thinking about this that fuels me is a good idea.. it took me a while but came up with this: I’m considering how many teachers were quietly suffering..so meeting one who was open about the burnout may have been just the tip of the iceberg.
answer:
Hi Coach,

Thank you for such a deep and honest reflection on the previous coaching, it really shows me you understand teachers, their challenges, and what they’re experiencing goes far beyond just burnout. It also show me how much you care about this.

What I see here isn’t that they don’t need or want your help. The problem right now is that you’re waiting for them to believe in it before you fully do.  notice how you said, “I don’t really expect this to work.” When that thought is there, your brain will naturally look for evidence to confirm it like in the comment about sick leave or the reaction from admin and use it to make conclusions about your ability and what’s possible for you and who is wants help.

I want to bring you back to something you said, because I think this is the most valuable part of your story: when you were a teacher, you felt the job was heavy and all-consuming, and when you tried to communicate that, it felt dismissed as a “you” problem instead of something created by the job itself. When you think about that version of you, what do you feel? I’m asking because that feeling connects you to your why, and your why is what steadies you in these conversations. Why does this matter to you?

When you bring yourself back to that, what does it look like to be willing to put yourself out there, not from a place of needing it to work, but from a place of wanting to understand and serve? Who better than you to communicate the silent pain and frustration they are experiencing. What is the impact on their life with coaching tools that you can communicate from your own experience?

I also want you to consider, what would it have meant to you back then if someone was willing to truly listen and even help explain your problem in a way you couldn’t yet articulate, especially when you didn’t feel seen? That’s the role you’re stepping into now. So instead of making their reactions mean something about you or your offer, how can you stay in that service energy? How can you expect this part learning how to communicate what you do in a way others understand to be hard, and not make that mean anything has gone wrong?

Because when it gets hard, your brain will offer you an out. It will say, “Maybe this isn’t possible,” or “They don’t want this.” That’s not the moment to evaluate yourself that’s the moment to stay. So how can you allow the fear of rejection to be there without making it mean anything about your work or your ability? And when you think about how many teachers are quietly suffering, why do you want to do this even when you feel frustration, insecurity, or rejection?

Have you heard Stacey say it’s harder not to believe than to believe? How is that true for you here? Notice the difference in how you show up when you’re in doubt versus when you’re in service.

Who do you need to become to stay in the conversation, even when they don’t immediately get it? How can you practice this in other areas, how can you become that version as fast as possible, suffering teachers are waiting coach.

And what would it look like to have these conversations when you genuinely believe in coaching and the impact it can have on teachers who are struggling whether they see it yet or not?

title: Adding a high-ticket offer when I still need to grow my basic offer
question:
I have combined my 20+ years of teaching experience and my life coach certification into a small-group online tutoring business. My offer is: I help motivated but struggling 9th and 10th-grade students raise their language arts grades and gain confidence so that they can succeed in core classes, prepare for future SATs, and be on track for college.

At this point, I have two students in my group and am running paid ads alongside organic, and I’m learning from Stacey (who I have been following for years). I know that there is great value here, and alongside just teaching school skills, the MINDSET and coaching are everything! The group coaching is $1200 for 12 weeks (2, 45-minute sessions per week), and the transformation is: creating a student who is independently successful in language arts AND has the actual skills ready to implement.

Additionally, I would like to add a high-ticket offer: this package plus 1:1 weekly sessions that focus more strictly on coaching, and less on tutoring, for $3700 for 12 weeks. Unfortunately, I have been having the hardest time bringing in new clients and generating leads, so my brain is stuck on adding this offer.

I am in a large educator/ tutor business mentoring group, and one solution I have is to offer to do free coaching to some of the other tutors in the group and just “coach my face” off to at least get back in the practce… but ya know, fear…
answer:
Hey coach,

First, I want to start by grounding you in what’s already working. You have two students in your group. That matters. That tells me this isn’t theoretical you’ve already created something real, something valuable, something people are saying yes to. And with 20+ years of experience plus coaching, this isn’t you 
figuring out if you can help, 
 it’s you learning how to consistently get in front of the people you can help.

Now, I want to go right to the thought you shared, because this is really the center of it:

“I’ve been having the hardest time bringing in new clients… so my brain is stuck on adding this offer.”

Before we even touch the high-ticket idea, we need to understand that sentence. Why do you think you’ve been having the hardest time bringing in new clients? What does that mean ? Also what are you making that mean now?

I’m asking this because if we don’t clearly define the problem, your brain will keep trying to solve it in ways that don’t actually address it, potentially like creating new offers instead of strengthening demand for the one you already have.

What are your top three specific theories?

Not general be as specific as you can.  With the actual process you have been using.

For example:

Is it visibility?

Is it messaging?

Is it belief when you’re selling?

Is it consistency in outreach?

What else?

The more honest and precise you are here, the more solvable this becomes. Because adding a high-ticket offer doesn’t solve a lead generation problem. It just gives your brain something new to focus on.

So I also want to ask:

What do you believe about your current group offer right now? If this was selling out beyond what you expected, if there was demand right now would you be adding this new offer now?  How would sold out demand impact your new offer?

And I’m asking this because how you think about 
this
 offer will directly impact how you show up to sell it.

Do you believe it’s an easy yes for the right student?

Do you believe parents see the value immediately?

Or are there thoughts like “this is a harder sell” or “people might hesitate at the price”?

Now connect that to this:

How do you think adding a 1:1 offer would change your actions?

Would you market differently?

Show up more confidently?

Reach out more?

And if so, why would that only be available to you with a new offer?

This is important, because how we do one thing is often how we do another.

If your belief about your ability to generate leads feels shaky right now, that likely follows you into 
any
 offer.

Sometimes a new offer gives a temporary boost—new energy, new excitement but the moment it gets hard, your brain will likely return to: “This is hard for me.”

So instead of solving for 
offers
, we want to look at how you’re showing up in the process of creating clients.

Let’s make that really tangible.

How do you feel when you meet new people who could be a fit?

What are the exact thoughts creating that feeling?

How do you feel when you tell someone what you do?

Again, what are the thoughts underneath that?

And how do you feel when you actually make an offer or invite someone in?

I’m asking these not just to ask but because those moments are where clients are created.

If there’s hesitation, doubt, or holding back there, it won’t matter how good the offer is.

Now, I also want to touch the part where you said:

“I could coach my face off… but, you know, fear.”

Let’s slow that down.

“You know, fear” what does that mean to you?

Because experiencing fear doesn’t actually mean anything has gone wrong.

It doesn’t mean you shouldn’t do it.

It doesn’t mean you’re not ready.

It usually means you’re doing something that matters.

So I want to understand:

What are you making fear mean?

Are you using it as a reason to pause?

Or can it be a signal that you’re expanding?

If you weren’t afraid, what would you do right now?

And even more important:

What specifically are you afraid of?

Get really honest here what’s the worst-case scenario your brain is offering you, and why does that matter?

Because on the other side of that fear isn’t just “more practice.”

It’s evidence for yourself that you can show up, help people, and create results.

And that’s what builds belief not thinking about it, but doing it.

So when you consider offering free coaching inside your group, I don’t see that as “just practice.”

I see that as you putting yourself in the exact environment where your future clients already are, and showing them what’s possible.

And I want to leave you with this, because this is the shift:

Don’t depend on clients finding you and deciding on their own. Don’t wait for that it will seem practical even logical to your brain when you believe you are not in charge of creating the clients by helping them decide on their own. IF you believe you are 100 percent capable of creating teh demand what is different?

Take responsibility for going out, finding the people you can help, letting them know clearly how you help, and then making them an offer.

You already have something valuable Coach!

Now it’s about becoming the person who is willing to consistently put that in front of people fear and all.

title: moving into selling courses 5
question:
What do you believe about yourself in hard moments that allows you to keep showing up? I think the thing I keep coming back to is my brain is valuable even when I’m having a hard time. I think I’ve been getting stuck in the “I don’t feel good right now, how can I help someone?” But I can help, I just forgot. The fertility grief felt so separate from what I do, that it felt easier to hold onto that valuable brain – but now it’s true too.

This made me cry – You don’t need to push yourself into being some superhuman version of you to make this work. – I do think I’m believing that. And of course that’s making it hard to actually make this work. lol. It just feels hard to let go of it.

The hardest part of motherhood for me has been learning how to take care of myself at a deeper level so I totally resonate with -The work is learning how to support yourself inside of that, not override it.

So maybe the real question isn’t “how do I do more,” but: Why do I want this? And what fuels me when I remember that?

I want it because I know what I know can help people. Even if I’m still learning too (I think that’s the part I can forget – I can feel like I’m in kindergarten so I can’t help – when that’s actually okay – I can help the 3 year olds. I don’t have to worry about the high schoolers). And I want to be able to have an impact. I want to be able to help people. I want the things in my brain to not stop with me. It feels like a waste to just keep it inside for myself. And I want to be paid well. Honestly so I can have the things I want – and mostly, travel the world.
answer:
Hi Coach,

So great that you can see this that both can be true. You can be in the hard, and you can still direct yourself back to what you want and why it matters. That’s the power. When you keep bringing your brain back to why this matters to you and I know how to help people, you start to access yourself again.

That thought “I don’t feel good right now, how can I help someone?” just notice what happens when you believe that. It pulls you out. It makes the feeling mean you can’t help. I’m asking you to look at that because the feeling isn’t the problem it’s what you’re making it mean.

What if feeling off didn’t disqualify you?

When we get out of our own way gently,  and then powerfully you can still go help people. And when you do that, when you move through the hard and show up anyway, you’re actually putting yourself in the exact position to help others when they’re in it. Not from theory but from experience. They will feel that you get it. You will believe they can do it because you did. That’s not even something you have to try to explain it’s the energy you bring.

So how do you keep bringing yourself back to that?

This is where directing your brain matters. You keep creating belief on purpose. A well-managed brain is what creates the results you want not a perfect emotional state.

What are you choosing to tell yourself when it gets hard?

Because the story you keep telling will become the loudest one in the room.

And I love what you said about kindergarten you don’t need to be ahead of everyone. You help the people who are a few steps behind you. That’s enough. That’s more than enough.

Also notice this “superhuman” version of you. Of course it feels hard to let go of that belief will keep raising the bar and making it harder to show up. But you don’t need to override yourself to do this work. The work is learning how to support yourself inside of it.

We are coaches we go first. We create the energy, the desire, and the choice to show up, especially when it’s hard. Over and over again. Each time, a little stronger, a little cleaner.

And your why is clear you want to help people, you don’t want what’s in your brain to stop with you, you want impact, and you want to create a life you love.

Keep bringing yourself back to that.

It’s pretty amazing to think about what you’re building and who you’re becoming in the process. That version of you is going to serve in a big way.

Let’s go Coach!  Your clients are waiting and so are your dreams.

answer:
Hey Coach!

There’s something really important here to remind yourself of – the timer isn’t up
 yet. 
It sounds like your brain may already be emotionally moving into “this isn’t working” or “it won’t work” while there are still 
9 days left 
to fill seats! You can look at these 9 days as limited time, or ample time to meet your goal! I’d get curious what would happen if, instead of trying to predict the outcome right now, you stayed focused on simply 
continuing to invite people in.

What if
 one ideal client said yes 
each day?

What if 6 people ended up in the room because you didn’t take your foot off the gas emotionally before time runs out?

Let’s also gently challenge the comparison to Stacey. Her event selling out does not mean yours cannot sell (I know deep down you inherently know this). It also doesn’t automatically mean you’re overpriced. I think your brain is looking at someone with years of audience-building and using it as evidence 
against yourself
