 Do it from genuinely believing there are still ideal clients out there who may need exactly what you’ve created. Remember, they can’t find you to say “yes” unless you are staying “top of mind” by showing up & keeping your foot on the gas.

A powerful question to also ask yourself could be:

“If my ideal clients walked into this room, what transformation or experience would make this event 
undeniably valuable for them?”

Sometimes when our numbers feel quiet or slow, our brains start focusing almost entirely on enrollment volume instead of the
 
actual potency
 
of the work we do.

What would it look like to stay focused on the 
potency of your offer
 and to let yourself FULLY LEAN IN to showing up until “the clock strikes midnight”?

title: Regular money objection
question:
Hi! I submitted a sales call evaluation just now, and also wanted to get some coaching on an objection I’ve gotten on my last two sales calls. People saying they don’t have the money, and sometimes being willing to make a plan for getting the money, but wanting time to do that.

I know sometimes that the objections we get can be traced back to something going on with us, so I wanted to get some coaching on this to see if there’s something else going on with me that I’m not spotting. The objection under the money objection has been (I think): not believing in herself; uncomfortable spending money on herself; not wanting to ask others for help with money. And the area that I’m working on when it comes to these objections is figuring out how to view these potential clients in a more empowering way, as people who can solve their money challenges, whose dream of writing a novel is worth it.

– What could I ask myself to build my belief around these potential clients?

– What could I ask myself to probe deeper into whether these objections/hesitations are actually coming from me?

– What could I ask myself to dig deeper into why it’s worth investing money to write a novel? I can get stuck here because there isn’t an immediate monetary return with finishing writing a book, but I also know that my life has completely changed because I was able to finish that first book 5 years ago, after decades of unsuccessful attempts. But I think I’m not convicted enough around it?

Appreciate any coaching or perspective you can offer!
answer:
Hi Coach,

You’re asking really important questions here, and I actually think the biggest thing I notice is that you’re already aware this may not just be about “handling objections,” but about how you’re relating to the objection when it shows up.

I want to point you first toward the Objections module and the Client/Coach modules because there’s such a powerful way Stacey teaches seeing is often showing you the exact thought loop the client is trapped in. So when someone says, “I don’t have the money,” instead of hearing it as the end of the conversation, you can begin hearing it as the doorway into understanding them more deeply.

What are they actually believing in that moment?

What feeling is driving the hesitation? Because “I don’t have the money” can sometimes mean, “I don’t trust myself.” “What if I fail again?” “What if I spend this and still don’t become who I want to become?” “I don’t know if I’m worth this level of investment.”

That’s very different than simply “I can’t.”

And I think you’re onto something important when you said you’re trying to view your clients in a more empowering way. That matters because clients can feel when we subtly agree with their limitation. Not consciously but energetically, emotionally, in the way we respond, the way we pull back, the way we stop exploring.

One thing I would ask yourself is:

When they give me the objection, do I internally believe it sounds reasonable?

Because if part of your brain goes, “Yeah… I get it… this is a lot of money and maybe it won’t work for them,” you’ll naturally soften, retreat, or stop leading. You may unintentionally join their fear instead of helping them examine it. And this is where sales gets really nuanced.

If exploring objections feels manipulative  you’ll hesitate to fully coach through them. But if you truly believe the coaching could help change the trajectory of their life, then exploring the objection becomes an act of service, not pressure.

That’s why I love the questions you already came up with for yourself, Especially: Why is it worth investing money to write a novel? Sit with that deeply. Flush that out and come up with a robust list of reasons. Spend time ITC on that one so you feel the energy of the value that would create.

Who does someone become by finishing something they’ve spent decades believing they couldn’t do?

What identity shifts?

What self-trust gets built?

What discipline, courage, emotional resilience, or self-respect gets created in the process?

What are the byproducts of becoming a person who follows through on a dream?

Because often the value is not just “the book.” It’s the transformation that happens while becoming the person capable of writing it.

And when you become sold on the deeper value of the work, objections stop feeling like barriers and start feeling like thoughts to explore compassionately.n You can even practice this outside of consults.

Write down every objection you think someone might give you.

What might they actually be afraid of underneath this?

What belief would they need to shift to move forward?

How would I coach someone through this if I fully believed in their ability to succeed? That’s where your confidence gets built.

And during the consult itself, curiosity will serve you far more than trying to “overcome” anything.

“Are you open to exploring what ‘I don’t have the money’ means for you?”

“If the money were available, would this feel like something you’d want to say yes to?” Why ?

And then you can gently explore:

“What would need to happen for this to feel like the best decision you’ve made for yourself?”

“What do you think you’re really afraid might happen if you invest?” “When have you invested in yourself before and not gotten the value? What happened there?”

And also remember every consult is practice. Sales is much more art than script and science.  You’re learning how to read people, how to stay grounded when discomfort appears, how to stay connected instead of rushing to solve or convince.

The more deeply you believe they are capable of creating the result they want, the less afraid you’ll be of the objection itself.

Because objections are often just thoughts people are having in real time about what’s possible for them.

You got this Coach!

title: 05/20/2026 | a force to be reckoned with
question:
”I’d be curious whether your brain is approaching this from leader energy or “accommodate-everyone” energy.”

This was such a powerful question for me because it helped me see that my brain is absolutely approaching this from a state of accommodation rather than leadership. It also reminded me that I had a similar experience back in 2022 when I hosted a Mastermind and stressed about scheduling because I wanted to accommodate everyone.

I can see almost immediately how the action I take from leader energy will be very different from what my brain wants to ruminate on now. Thank you for that, I know what to do now.

I got chills through my entire body when I read that last paragraph and honestly, I have uncovered a fear of success many times through the years. I have known for a long time that this is my path, that I will succeed, that I am a force to be reckoned with. That’s why I have never truly quit or even entertained another path.

But there’s always a part of me that looks forward and sees it all accomplished and fears that something will happen to mess it all up. I have no doubt when I really get out of my own way that it will all happen, everything I want. But for some reason there’s a fear that it won’t last. Maybe that I won’t be able to maintain it or that it will become too big for me to manage.

I notice that my brain really likes to ruminate 10 steps ahead and uses that as a reason to stop moving all together and typically I’ll get stuck in a state of rumination, digesting / learning, or doing thought work that leads to no action or implementation.

Sometimes I worry that I want the life I envision TOO MUCH, & there’s a fear that it’ll be so devastating if I get it and lose it. Maybe that goes back to succeeding in Washington & Bali then losing it and having to come back to Indiana, where I still am now. Maybe it goes back to the things my ex would say to me that slowly ate away at my self-love and confidence that I’m finally getting back now.

Maybe it doesn’t even matter what it goes back to. Either way, you are right. I do feel like half of me is itching to be a force, while the other half is afraid of what will happen when I am. I don’t want to stall anymore.
answer:
Hey Coach,

So happy to hear that coaching resonated deeply. In what you shared today, I just want you to know that everything you’re feeling about fear of success is normal. Sometimes the reminder that “you are not a unicorn” in that arena can be helpful. Most everyone who is going for big dreams and success has fears that they will lose it, or not be able to maintain it. When we really think about it, why would ANYONE aim for success only to lose it all? No one would want that – so most all of us hold that fear in some way. You are not alone.

What I want to offer is that as you grow, your brain also gets better and better at problem solving. Think of Stacey for example. The challenges she faced making her first 50k in her business were different than challenges she faced at 200k, 2 million, etc., She has shared herself how there has (and sometimes still is) fear of “losing it all.” That is why she also has began teaching on capacity work… our capacity to feel, to process, to hold the hard.. To redirect ourselves when the brain works overtime to sabotage us.

We are human – those thoughts that make us want to overthink or stall are absolutely normal.

The bigger question is, do we succumb to our brain fighting THAT hard to protect us… so much so, it won’t even allow us
 to try?

At each level Stacey has grown, she has been able to hire people who are better at certain things than she is. Who hold a skill she may not have that helps her in her own journey to success. My point in sharing this is that if you can just allow your brain to focus on what is within your control TODAY, and do THOSE things, your brain will learn how to solve problems or challenges 
as they come up
.

You can trust yourself.
 You don’t have to try to predict everything ahead of time so much so that you stall and never get where you’re trying to go. As you take consistent, 
sometimes boring/mundane
 actions, there comes a tipping point where the success will come. And as that success comes,
 you can get support to make sure you feel confident in maintaining it.

In the earlier stages of this, it may just be coming here and using your 2k resources to get coaching support and guidance…

Then as you grow more monetarily, you may have more wiggle room in deciding what best supports you in being able to hold and continue the success the way you desire. Again,
 trust trust trust
 yourself coach!

So in working on this what actions can you take in your business today? Focus on this day in front of you.

If the focus was 
“Just for today, I will ______”
 … Do what comes up and then repeat this daily.

Each time your brain tries to stall you out or subconsciously “fail ahead of time” – have a process.

Sometimes that process can be 
as simple
 as saying out loud….

“Thank you brain… I see you’re doing your best to keep me safe, but I’ve got this. I can trust myself – and just for today, I am going to ______ while I simutaneously feel ____(nervous, scared, unsure, etc)”

I know you’ve got this coach. Let the fear, uncertainty, etc., be present while you do what needs to be done.

That’s what living in our leadership truly looks and feels like.

title: Day 29 / 30 – raise my belief about my offer
question:
So today I decided to watch Stacey’s training Interrupt which has been really fun because this is before she’d even made her first million dollars in her business and I’ve never watched it before. Where she is in this video doesn’t feel very far away from where I could be in the next year or two depending on my growing self-belief.

She talks about the amount that she charges to work 1:1 with her at this point in her business, which was about $13k a year while also preparing to raise it again to $20k or $25k per year.

I felt very inspired by her belief around the amount that she was charging: “if I’m charging $20k a year to coach my clients, and some of them are turning around and making $100k or a quarter of $1m from scratch, then $20k feels like a no-brainer price point.” This feels very similar to her mindset around $200K mastermind, if not the exact same belief.

And I felt really inspired by that, but it also helped me see that I’m having a hard time coming up with reasons why I believe that it’s worth spending $8k in a year to come and work with me.

I believe that I deserve to feel supported by the price that I charge, so I can live the life I desire to live and feel supported. That’s a great thought to have, but it’s not exactly supporting my client. I feel good about that price because it supports ME, now I wanna come up with some reasons why it’s worth the investment for my clients and I’m sort of coming up blank.

Stacey is helping people make money and so it makes sense logically that she can use their financial results as fuel around her prices, but I don’t necessarily help people make money.

I don’t have any desire to change my price, but I do wonder what thoughts and beliefs would support me in selling my offer, i.e. how to sell that price point to other people, to make it seem worth it to them to invest.

some of my thoughts right now that I know are working in opposition to this are:

“$8K is a lot of money to a lot of people, a lot of people are struggling financially right now, I know there are a lot of people who want to work with me but who can’t afford to, most people who have historically come to me ARE struggling to make money – maybe that’s something they want to work on but I haven’t successfully helped coach anybody to earning more money, & I struggle to make more money, so of course it’s hard to coach other people there.”

I wish I had as concrete and logical of a belief as Stacey does around her prices.
answer:
Hey coach,

So glad you took time to watch The Interrupt training  that really is such a good one. And honestly, I think your awareness here is powerful. Tapping to modules and when you feel the inspiration taking action from that fuels momentum.

What I hear most in your question is not actually “how do I justify 8k?” but “how do I become the woman who fully believes in 8k before all the proof exists?”

That is very normal when you’re growing into new identity. And also brain wants to know the how when what really makes the difference is who is marketing and selling and delivering.  That version of you approaches this different, how is that true? What is different?

Anytime we set a new standard, a new identity, or a new level in business, the brain will toggle between belief and disbelief for a while. That’s part of building something new. Your current identity and your future identity will both try to speak at the same time for a bit. The work becomes spending more time in the belief on purpose instead of treating the doubt like truth.

And I think it’s important you noticed Stacey had to sell herself on belief too. She didn’t arrive magically certain. She practiced believing. That’s why she’s so good at teaching it. She’s lived it over and over. She shared it took 4 months before she started selling 200k at 25k and was willing to work with less people because she had been delivering it at 25K value.

I actually want you to listen to the newer podcast on Creating New Beliefs from the lens of your offer specifically.

Because right now, I think you’re trying to solve “how do I justify the price?” from the identity of someone who is still waiting to feel fully convinced first.

But entrepreneurial maturity is often: 
“I chose this.”

And then doing the emotional work of standing behind the choice.

One thing I would spend time with is this: 
When you are fully sold out at 8k… what does that version of you think about her coaching?

What does she deeply believe ?

What feels obvious to her?

What does she no longer debate?

What does she stop making mean something?

And this matters because most people try to figure out “how” while still thinking like the version of themselves who doesn’t yet create the result. 
But identity comes first.

If you chose 8k, the work now becomes:

Can you emotionally carry yourself as an 8k coach? 
Can you stay in belief long enough for your brain to stop treating it like danger?

I also want you to notice something really important:

you’re looking at Stacey’s logic around money results and thinking, “I need something equally concrete.”

But transformation is not only valuable when it creates money.

What is it worth for someone to:

— stop living consumed by anxiety?

— trust themselves?

— stop abandoning themselves?

— create peace in their relationships?

— change how they experience their life every single day?

People spend money all the time trying to feel better, escape themselves, avoid discomfort, or create change. 
Your coaching is not valuable only if it increases income.

And honestly, I would stop waiting for future client proof to finally permit yourself to believe in your work. 
That becomes a trap: 
“I’ll believe once I see enough evidence.”

But belief is what often creates the consistency, energy, conviction, and leadership that produce the evidence. 
I would spend time every single day selling yourself on your reasons for why your work matters instead of trying to borrow certainty from future results.

Pay attention to the thoughts that create charge in your body — the ones that make you feel connected, grounded, convicted. Then notice the ideas and actions available from there.

Because destructive thoughts usually don’t just feel bad — they shut down action, leadership, creativity, and visibility.

And one last thing:

You do not need every person to think 8k is worth it. 
You only need the right people to decide it is and it starts with believing yourself. 
That’s very different.

I also think running your offer through IOP during offer week could be really helpful   especially focusing less on “how do I convince people?” and more on “how do I become deeply sold on my reasons for this offer every single day?”

That’s the real work here. Keep going Coach! you got this!

title: Networking question
question:
Hi AAC!

I was listening to one of Stacey’s trainings today and I’m confused on what she said about networking. She said the point of networking meeting isn’t to sell…it’s to build my belief that I am a coach. I understand this in the sense that it is a place for us to tell people we are a coach and build our belief (because she said we first become a coach in our mind and I see that helps).

But this information brings up 2 questions…first, if I believe in my ability as a coach, but my struggle is more in marketing, is it still important for me to keep going to these? In the past year and a half I have I joined several networking groups and meetings, and I will be honest, I would have thought I would meet clients there. (I did meet 2 from those efforts most likely). But I see that I have been going in the hopes of “getting” clients, and I want to change this energy if it isn’t right. Then my brain goes to asking if it is still “worth” all the time, money and energy I put into going to these though?

The other thing is if I am not going to networking meetings to meet potential clients, where am I finding them? As I have shared with you, I am on FB and LinkedIn and I have not gotten many clients from FB for the past 2 years, and no clients from LI yet (new in the last couple months)…I know I am there to SERVE, and I do that and I really do love it. However, I am struggling to make sense in my brain. 🙂 I’m not on FB to “get” clients, but to serve them….but ultimately I am really on FB (social media) to “get” clients right? I mean, I show up in service, but isn’t the end goal to obtain clients? I’m sure this is an easy fix but I can’t make sense of it in my brain right now. I know I want to attract and ultimately “get” new clients…but it seems like the main 2 ways to do it are not what I am supposed to be doing? Does this make sense?

I hope you can help and that you understand what I mean lol. Thank you!!
answer:
Hey Coach!

This makes complete sense, and I’m really glad you brought it here because your brain is just trying to organize it all. You’re not wrong that the end result of all of this is clients. That’s the point of having a business. Where your brain is getting tangled is in how you relate to the process of getting them!

There’s a big difference between showing up in “get” energy versus “give” energy. When you’re in get, you’re scanning every interaction for “is this going to turn into a client?” and it creates pressure, urgency, and often subtle disconnection. When you’re in give, you’re focused on being useful, sharing value, and letting people experience you. Ironically, that’s what actually leads to people becoming clients. So yes, you are on Facebook, LinkedIn, and even at networking events to ultimately sign clients. 
But
 the way you do that is by consistently giving people a real experience of your work. 
Does that help shift anything for you when you think about it that way?

With networking specifically, I’d get curious about how you want to use those spaces. They can absolutely be valuable, but not because you walk in expecting to leave with clients. They’re a place to practice being someone who talks about what she does. It’s a place to also be someone who connects with others and who shares her work naturally. Do you feel like those rooms help you show up more confidently as a coach? Or do they feel draining and misaligned? It’s okay to decide they’re not your primary strategy if they don’t feel like the best use of your energy. But that decision should come from clarity, not from disappointment that they didn’t produce immediate clients.

Stacey teaches that when we meet people from “give/service” energy, we want to focus on 
nurturing the relationship over time
… not being in a space where we expect them to become a client right away (or at all). In thinking of this, when you meet someone, how can you stay in touch with them so they are exposed to who you are over time? For example, maybe it’s making a connection and then “friending” them on socials… Maybe it’s exchanging numbers and keeping in touch with coffee.

Something else I like to keep in mind is that when you meet people, you’re not just meeting 
them
… 
you’re stepping into their world.
 Every person you connect with has relationships, conversations, communities, and opportunities you can’t see yet. When you approach it from that place, the interaction stops being about “does this person become my client?” and becomes “how do I genuinely connect here?” You may meet a woman or man who never buys from you, and that’s completely fine. What matters is that they understand what you do, they’ve experienced you as genuine, and they trust the way you show up. If there’s no pressure, no attachment, no sense that you’re trying to get something from them, they’re much more likely to remember you and talk about you.

That’s how referrals happen in a really clean way. Over time, those kinds of connections can become incredibly powerful. Someone with a large network, or even just a few really aligned relationships, may naturally send people your way simply because they respect what you do and how you do it. They didn’t ever feel pressure or an expectation that you “only met and got to know them” for them to be your client. When you’ve built connections in a clean way, it feels easy for someone to share you with their network too.

So when you think about networking or even social media, it can help to zoom out a bit. You’re not just looking for the next client in front of you. 
You’re building a reputation, a presence, and relationships that extend far beyond a single conversation.

And when you ask, “if not there, then where do I find clients?” I’d turn that back to you a bit. Where are the people you want to help already spending time? And how are you showing up there in a way that lets them actually see what you do? You mentioned you love serving on social media, which is huge. Now the question becomes, are you also letting that service lead somewhere?
 Are you inviting people into working with you, or are you stopping at value?
 Attraction happens when people can feel your work AND also know what to do next if they want more of it. That can be as simple as remembering to add a CTA to the value you share (like having them book a consult, join an email list, sign up for a free webinar, etc.)

What do you think? Does this help clarify a bit?

title: Staying present on sales call when personal circumstances are distracting
question:
Hi there, I had a sales call over the weekend that didn’t close, and I know why. There was a money objection, that likely was hiding an underlying fear about her confidence in her ability to get the result (enough to make it worth the investment), but I struggled to stay with her on the call because of some life circumstances that were happening at the same time. I’d like support on how to stay present even when other things are going on.

Circumstances: my husband and I had had a fight the day before, and I’d left the fight feeling like he wasn’t supportive of my business. We didn’t talk it through before the sales call (we ended up discussing later that day and moving through it), and so when the client brought up money, I felt discouraged because that keeps being an objection I’m getting, I was annoyed with my husband for not being supportive, and I definitely just started believing her objection. It was hard to rein myself in in the moment.

Additionally, right before the call, my son woke up from his nap with an ear infection. My husband was with him and ended up needing to take him to urgent care. My husband texted me a couple updates during the sales call, and so that was understandably distracting as I was trying to focus on this potential client. I’m confident in my husband’s ability to care for our son, so I didn’t feel the need to cut the call short, and I didn’t think I needed to be with my son right in that moment. But there was some guilt about staying on the call, wondering if I was doing something wrong, wondering how to balance business priorities with motherhood. But if I compare it to a day job, if I were in an important work meeting, I would likely trust my husband to handle things and stay in the meeting. But my son not being well also played into the situation with my husband and not feeling supported from him.

I’d love some coaching on staying present on a sales call when other urgent life things feel distracting, and also that balance of prioritizing the business when my son isn’t feeling well. I think there’s mom guilt getting in the way, so that feels like a different issue than the husband situation. Would love your thoughts!
answer:
Hello Coach,

Thank you for sharing this and being willing to bring it here. It sounds like there was a lot happening all at once, and I want to acknowledge that. You were then faced with an objection that has already been feeling charged for you lately. 
That is a lot.

And before we coach this, I want to offer you some compassion. We have all been there. Whether it’s a consult, a coaching call, or an important conversation, sometimes life is happening at the same time. Would you really expect yourself to be completely undistracted with everything you had going on?

I think the first place I would start is accepting that life will challenge us. Being a coach doesn’t mean you never get distracted. Being a coach doesn’t mean you never have emotions. Nothing has gone wrong here.

Sometimes we think the goal is to show up perfectly focused no matter what is happening in our lives. But what if the goal is simply learning how to bring yourself back when you notice you’ve left the room mentally?

One thing I’m curious about is this: 
If you expected yourself not to be distracted, why?

What are you making distraction mean?

I’m asking because sometimes we suffer more from the judgment of the distraction than the distraction itself.

What if you accepted that sometimes you might show up a little distracted? Or even a lot distracted? What would you want to make that mean about yourself and your ability to be present?

I think there is something powerful about giving yourself the same grace we encourage our clients to have. You can be a great coach and still be human. You can be present and still have emotions. You can be thinking about your child and still be a professional.

You mentioned that when the money objection came up, you started believing it. That stood out to me. 
You said: 
“I felt discouraged because that keeps being an objection I’m getting.”

So I would get curious there.

Why do money objections discourage you?

What thought is creating the discouragement?

Are you making money objections mean something about your offer?

Something about your business?

Something about you?

I’m asking because if we solve for the discouragement, we often solve for a lot of what happens on the consult.

When we believe the objection ourselves, it becomes harder to stay curious.

If you had been feeling completely grounded and present, what would you have wanted to ask her about the money objection?

What would you have been curious to understand?

Sometimes after a consult, it can be helpful to replay it and ask yourself, “Where would I have gotten more curious if I wasn’t believing the objection myself?”

The other piece that stood out to me was your husband.

You mentioned feeling unsupported by him and then feeling discouraged by the client’s objection.

I wonder if there is any connection there.

Why do you need your husband to believe in the business in order for you to believe in the business?

What happens if he doesn’t?

What are you making his lack of support mean?

I’m asking because many of us unintentionally borrow confidence from other people. We think their belief creates our belief. But ultimately, your belief has to come from you.

And then there is the mom guilt piece.

I noticed you said that if you were at a traditional job in an important meeting, you likely would have trusted your husband to handle it and stayed in the meeting.

That makes me wonder:

What makes this different because it’s your business or how you think about that?

What are you making it mean when you prioritize your business while your child is being cared for by someone you trust?

Sometimes guilt feels like evidence that we’re doing something wrong. 
But guilt is often just a feeling.

It doesn’t mean you’re doing something wrong.

It may simply mean you’re challenging an old belief about what a good mother is supposed to do.

And finally, I want to offer this:

You don’t have to become someone who never gets distracted. 
You simply practice noticing when your brain leaves the conversation and bringing it back.

“My brain is on my son.” 
Come back. 
“My brain is on my husband.” 
Come back. 
“My brain is believing the money objection.” 
Over and over. 
That is the skill.

And like any skill, you get better with practice.

I would spend less time trying not to get distracted and more time learning how to return.

What thoughts come up for you as you sit with these questions?  You got this Coach!

title: Consult #2 – 24/04/26
question:
Evaluation – Matthew Williams – 24/04/26

What Worked

– Referral via a coach WhatsApp group.

– Rapport; felt connected to his current self.

– Well-prepared with cards for steps/questions.

– I articulated his problem better than he did—identifying his normalized anxiety as a tolerated character trait.

– Identified key growth areas: decision-making for the future self vs. past experience, redirecting thoughts, and holding space for discomfort.

– Used “What’s been valuable for you today?” as an effective wrap-up.

What Didn’t Work

– I agreed with his need to “think about it” instead of probing further.

– Failed to create a compelling 12-month vision; felt like I was following a formula rather than anchoring impact.

– He declined a follow-up call and found the cost unfeasible.

– I struggled with the thought that his issues (anxiety) could be solved too quickly to justify a year of work.

– Intake hit 45 mins (planned 30). Energy dipped toward the end; he began clock-watching and got distracted by his cat.

– When I asked how much it felt like a “YES,” he stalled, and I felt I “lost him.”

What To Do Differently

– Develop non-confrontational questions for “I need to think,” such as: “How do you plan to walk yourself through that thought process?”

– If cost is an issue, practice leaning into the discomfort to ask: “Is there a cost to you of NOT doing this work now?”

– When I feel there “isn’t enough to work on,” pivot to imagining the client pursuing even bigger results beyond the initial problem.

– Strict 30-min intake (approx. 3.75 mins per section). Set expectations early: “We’re going to move quickly through this part.”

– Get more specific on the “Bridging the Gap” steps.

I’d appreciate coaching on this eval please!
answer:
Hi coach,

You’ve done a really great job with this evaluation. And first let’s not use names in evals here, just to protect privacy.

There is a lot here that worked, and it matters that you see that. You’re creating consults from the WhatsApp group that’s working! You built rapport, you were prepared, and you articulated his problem even better than he could. That’s strong coaching Coach, it is working!

One thing you can always add to your AAC evaluation submission is what you specifically want coaching on. That request helps direct the support so you get the most useful, targeted coaching each time.

And the beauty of an eval is exactly this it becomes a playbook for your next call. You’ve already laid out powerful next steps. Now we just want to understand your thinking inside the moments you didn’t like, because that’s what will shift how you show up.

When you said you agreed with his need to “think about it,” you noticed it and that’s key. Why do you think you agreed? What were you believing about his reason to think about it?

I’m asking because understanding the thought behind agreeing will show you what drove that response. If you believed his “thinking about it” meant stop, then of course you stopped. But what do you want to believe about that moment instead? What Stacey teaches in the consultation code is this is when the coaching begins. He just shared the though in his way of change.

And if you were to approach it with more curiosity, what would you want to understand about how he plans to think it through? Most clients haven’t actually thought about that.

On the 12-month vision you said it felt like you were following a formula instead of anchoring impact of why you chose the year long package. That’s great awareness.

Vision casting is a skill, and you can practice it outside the consult. You could write out what success looks like for your clients, use their actual words, or even say it out loud and hear how it feels. Which way feels most doable for you right now?

This isn’t about getting it perfect it’s about making it feel real enough that they can see themselves in it.

When he declined the follow-up and said cost was unfeasible what thought did you have right then?

If you anticipate this happening again, what would you want to believe about a client who says that?

Sometimes you can ask if they’re open to exploring what makes it feel unfeasible. Not to convince them, but to understand their thinking. Especially in the beginning, it can feel logical for a client to think that way if they’ve never experienced coaching.

What would you need to be thinking or feeling to stay in that conversation instead of moving away from it? What if you anticipated the client offering reasons to get off the call?What would be different if you saw this as part of the

You also mentioned you struggled with the thought that his anxiety could be solved too quickly to justify a year.

What do you want to believe about the length of time you offer? Why do you believe in a year of work what are your reasons?

If you were fully anchored in that, how would you respond when a client questions it?

And what changes if you don’t expect the client to understand right away but you’re still willing to share your reasons clearly?

On the intake going over time you noticed it, which is good. Why do you think it ran long? Was it underestimating time, or losing track during the call?

And how do you want to lead that differently? Even setting the expectation at the start “we’re going to move quickly through this part” can help you guide the pace while still being present. Did you feel unable to move him along or do you want to set up more time next consultation. What do you need to believe about the consult to decide the length that works best for you and the client.

You also noticed his energy dipped and he got distracted. How would you want to respond in that moment? Would you pause and say, “I notice your energy shifted—what’s going on?”

I’m asking because that moment isn’t a problem it’s information. If you stay curious instead of ignoring it, it can actually deepen the conversation. It can show them what it is like to be with a coach vs another human may not pay such attention or avoid questions about it.

And when you asked how much it felt like a “YES” and he stalled you said you felt like you lost him. What do you think you were believing right there? Why?

What are you sure happened in that moment and what might you be making it mean? Because a pause doesn’t always mean loss. Sometimes it just means they’re thinking.

If you didn’t make it mean anything had gone wrong, how might you have stayed with him in that moment?

You’ve got a solid plan here. Each consult is you stacking skills, and this is exactly how you build mastery by looking at what happened, understanding your thinking, and deciding how you want to show up next time.

Great work Coach, bring any further coaching back after you have reflected on the coaching .

title: Consult eval
question:
Hi AAC!

My most recent consult eval with some questions.

WWW: she reached out just having seen my instagram handle which had the word ‘coach’ in it, I felt like I could connect to her and create a good bridge, it helped me get clarity on a lot of things for myself

title: my own revenue challenge of $10k in 30 days for April.
question:
Evaluation of last 2 revenue challenges: Failed:

I believed that just by paying for the revenue challenge, Stacey was somehow going to make it happen for me.

I didn’t create a clear plan

I listened to the calls but from a learners/consumers mindset

I compared myself to others

I didn’t really take action, meaning I might have posted content but I never made actual offers. I hoped my content would make someone reach out to me.

I was scared of visibility, being bold and I let that get bigger than my desire to create my result

2 weeks in, nothing was happening so I gave up mentally & quit.

I made it mean that I was a failure and not capable of creating my results.

I didn’t evaluate or learn from it. I just hid for a while.

$6k win in 40 days:

I focused on who I would become in the challenge over the $ amount.

I kept the $ amount visible and noted everytime money came in.

I posted content more regularly.

I reached out to people personally, invited them to work with me

I allowed myself to believe it was possible for me the whole time.

Just a share: I am facilitating a challenge this month and I’ve been promoting it on social and in person and the way I’ve been showing up has been amazing to me. I’ve been sharing the why, who it’s for and making actual offers boldly. It felt a little uncomfortable but not so much that I’ve shut down. (It’s a free challenge). I have 15 people signed up for it (I’m a little nervous to lead 15 people but also excited) and I’ve realized I’ve created evidence that I can be bold, make offers and I’m still ok AND 15 people said yes. I’ve never had that many people say yest to anything I’ve put out there.

My plan to go “All In “ this time

Listen to the belief plan podcast and create my own beliefs for the challenge

Start each day getting into the version of me on May 1st who created the result.

Create content with my people’s needs, challenges, struggles, desires in mind vs focusing on me and my wants.

Post value content 5 days a week.

Make offers in my content 3 days a week.

Reach out to 3 people 5 days a week to build relationships and if it’s appropriate, make an offer to get on a consult.

Network at least 2x in April.

Evaluate my actions every evening (without judgement, just pure curiosity and look for where I can improve)

Evaluate each week to set myself up for the next week.

Stay open and adaptable.

Batch my content each week so I have room to see what’s working, not working and adapt.

Have fun.
answer:
Hey coach,

First, I want to slow this down for a second because what you did here is actually the work. You didn’t just “reflect,” you evaluated.  The reason to practice evaluation is to train your brain to look at what you’re doing instead of making it mean something about you. And you did that. You focused on actions, patterns, and decisions not just “I failed.” That’s how you get better.

And notice this when you evaluated what didn’t work vs what did, you got very specific about what you would do differently. That’s the gold. That’s the whole point of evaluation. It creates direction. Really nice job here. When you feel inspired or compelled to go again it means you are in a new belief about your challenge.

Now, I want to bring your attention to something important because this is where your result will actually come from. In the first challenge, you were waiting for the result to create belief. You shared you even thought Stacey would create them by signing up vs taking responsibility for your results, just like ROI teaches this is a common student consumer mentality. Emotional entrepreneurial maturity is taking full responsibility for your investment.  In the second, you brought belief with you and acted from it. So good to catch this now.

So the real question becomes how are you going to sustain that this time, especially when results are not immediate? How can you keep your belief, enthusiasm all the way to the finish line.  What would be the benefit this time having these two revenue challenges behind you?

What is the thought you are going to practice on purpose that allows you to keep showing up the way you just described?
(I’m asking this because your results will not come from your plan alone they will come from the thinking that fuels your plan.

What if you were operating from the place of true belief operating in possibility? What would be different?

You already proved something to yourself: you can be bold, you can make offers, and people will say yes. 15 people is evidence. But your brain will try to dismiss that or move the goalpost. So we don’t wait for more evidence we use what we have and build on it.

This is where the belief plan becomes foundational. Not just writing it, but using it. Love your plan to tap into the podcast to generate the energy to stay in it. This weeks call Stacey shared how she creates the energy the desire the belief, by listening in the shower or while doing tasks until she feels the inspiration and then gets to work.  What will be your plan to create beliefs to fuel your action plan?

What thought helps you feel that grounded, clean confidence even before the money shows up?
What thought makes you willing to keep going at day 14 when nothing has happened yet?

Because that’s the moment that matters. And then how are you going to practice it?

Finding evidence is one way.
Creating evidence is another.
But the most important piece is rehearsing the thought in a way that you actually feel it in your body, because that is what drives your actions.

Your thoughts are not passive here they are directly impacting how you show up, how you sell, how you lead those 15 people.

And I also want you to think about this how are you going to use coaching in real time? For example when you don’t believe when your brain offers you the past challenge or the past fails, lets make a plan for belief.

When you feel doubt, hesitation, or that pull to hide what will you do in that moment?
This might look like: You notice the thought → you interrupt it → you choose a more useful one → and you act immediately from it.

That “act immediately” part matters. Because the moment you feel that inspired, grounded thought that’s your cue to move. Make the offer. Send the message. Post the content.

You’re not just learning how to do the challenge you’re learning how to coach yourself through creating a result.  And that’s exactly what you’re doing here, great work coach!

title: 06/08/2026 – evaluation on the last 3 months
question:
Thank you so much again. I just want to take a moment to tell all of you how much your coaching has impacted my life over the past few months. I went back and looked at my first message to you back in March and I can see just how far I’ve come since then. To celebrate my progress I want to do an evaluation over the progress I’ve made in the past 3 months.

What’s working?

– My thoughts are a lot more productive. I feel confident, inspired, creative, and clear.

– Some of my most productive thoughts: “I could get a consult TODAY, I am a truly skilled coach, people will be inspired to watch me grow, I can serve & sign clients regardless of my circumstances, I genuinely have the secret to the universe.”

– I have been meeting more people and reconnecting with my existing network

– Attending virtual networking events & am creating my own NE

– Reconnecting with a lot of my existing network & getting my name back out there. Result: 3 referrals

– I have started initiating coffee dates with people I think are really inspiring in my communities with the intention of getting in the room with successful people

– I created 1 offer that I am focusing all of my attention on & have a clear path and plan to succeed with it

– I made it incredibly easy to connect with me through a discovery call link that’s on all my socials, website, and podcast (I also give it to my network when they refer someone to me)

– I have learned how to overcome my own money objections which is helping me overcome objections on consults

– This led me to start the process of FINALLY buying a car

What isn’t working

– Still unintentionally getting caught in the story that my circumstances need to change before I can show up fully. Feeling: embarrassed; Action: not showing up on social media and marketing as effectively as I could, “waiting” until things change.

– Reacting poorly to my brother giving me “unproductive” advice; “you should create a course, get listed on databases, put ads on your podcast.” & I think “you have no idea what you’re talking about” & then shut down.

– Worrying that my family will always see me as someone who needs help rather than someone who’s a competent adult

– Spinning in thought work and not taking productive action

What to do differently

– Define “productive action”

– Get coaching about my family

– Catch cycles of unproductive action & turn the wheel

– Ask myself “what is this action motivated by?” frequently

– Create thoughts that lead to productive action
answer:
Hi Coach,

First, thank you for sharing this. What a powerful exercise. Looking back at where you were in March and comparing it to where you are now really highlights the impact of coaching, but more importantly, the impact of the work you have been willing to do.

There is so much growth here!Your thinking is more productive. You are creating opportunities instead of waiting for them. You are reconnecting with people, putting yourself in rooms with successful people, creating offers, simplifying how people can work with you, and overcoming money objections that used to hold you back. These aren’t small wins. They are evidence of a different identity being built. You are showing up more and more as the coach and business owner you want to become.

Let’s look together at what isn’t working.

You mentioned still getting caught in the story that your circumstances need to change before you can show up fully. I want you to get curious about the word “story.” Stories can feel very convincing when we’re in them. The question isn’t whether the story exists. The question is what you want to do when it shows up.

When embarrassment comes up, what story do you want to tell yourself instead? What would showing up with embarrassment look like? Because confidence isn’t the absence of embarrassment. Often it’s the willingness to keep moving while embarrassment is present. How could you plan ahead for those moments instead of being surprised by them?

You also mentioned shutting down when your brother gives advice.

I think it would be useful to understand what thought happens between his advice and your shutdown. What are you making his advice mean? That he’s right? That he knows better? That you’re missing something? That you’re doing it wrong?

The reason I ask is because people don’t shut down because someone speaks. They shut down because of what they believe about what was said.

What if his advice didn’t mean anything about your capability? What if it was simply another opinion available in the world? You don’t have to agree with it. You don’t even have to use it. But you can notice the thought that creates the shutdown and decide whether it’s one you want to keep believing.

You also shared that you’re worried your family will always see you as someone who needs help rather than a competent adult.

I want you to consider this from the future version of yourself who has created the success she wants. What would she think about this concern?

More importantly, what makes someone a competent adult? Have you defined that for yourself, or are you letting other people define it for you?

There are always two places you can focus: evidence of what you’re not doing or evidence of what you are doing. Even if there is more growth ahead, focusing exclusively on what you’re not doing will never help you see yourself clearly.

Your family is allowed to have opinions. The question is whether you want to spend your energy trying to manage those opinions or building a life that reflects your own standards. You get to decide the criteria. You get to decide who you are.

Finally, let’s talk about spinning in thought work instead of taking productive action.

This is so common because spinning feels productive. Your brain is busy, analyzing, evaluating, thinking. But thinking about movement and moving are not the same thing. Your brain has a way of convincing you this is being smart or practical or something that feels logical to your brain the way mine might say keep learning or ask someone else, it’s what works to stop us.

I would get very specific about what productive action actually means. What actions directly create opportunities, conversations, clients, or growth? Those are probably your productive actions.

And what feeling do you think you need before you take them?

Inspired? Confident? Certain?

What if the real skill is becoming willing to feel uncertainty and take the action anyway?

The brain loves the known. It loves staying still. Every time you act while feeling uncomfortable, you teach yourself that discomfort isn’t dangerous. You become more emotionally resourceful. You build evidence that you can trust yourself.

That is where the real confidence comes from.

Overall, I see someone who has created tremendous momentum in three months! . Keep studying what is working, keep doing more of that, keep catching the places where your brain wants to pull you back into old patterns, and keep turning the wheel toward the version of yourself you’re becoming.

Great work, Coach!

Do you have any questions about this evaluation specifically, or is there one area you want to explore more deeply?

title: Consult Left Early
question:
I had a consult that left at the 30 min mark and I have explored the ways that this was in my control. She arrived late and immediately said that she might need to leave early or continue the call from the car. She said her schedule was initially free for this hour when she booked the consult a few days ago but something had come up. she also said that her schedule tends to be in flux a lot. I told her that if she needed to leave early she could and we could find a new time slot to do the remaining portions of the consult. I realize I would have rather used that moment to reschedule to a time that she could actually be there for the full hour.

It ended with us deciding to finish up next week, where I’ll start with bridging the gap.

Some theories for why I didn’t take that approach

1. I got in the pool with her about the craziness of her schedule

2. People pleasing – I wanted her to like me and I wanted to be agreeable more than I wanted to do the consultation justice and create the space for the consult to be the best it could be

3. I wasn’t in service energy, in that I wasn’t seeing the consult as a valuable service that needed to be provided all at once. For example, you wouldn’t get half of a teeth cleaning or half of a facial and just tell the person they could leave early if they wanted to because that’s not actually of highest service to the client

4. I wasn’t the strongest energy on the call. I let her energy (chaos) overpower my energy and it literally split the consult in half. This feels differential. Like I deferred to her, I let her set the tone.

I’d like to use this Ask A Coach space to coach through each of these so that I can resolve them for future consults.

I also want to have a plan for what to do on the rest of her consultation next week so that I’m not still in the pool with her/experiencing these issues that I described.
answer:
Hi Coach,

Let’s dig in to each of the 4 areas you shared just in case you haven’t had your consult with her yet.

1. I got in the pool with her about the craziness of her schedule

– When it feels tempting to jump in the pool, keep in mind one of your “superpowers” as a coach is to stay in curiosity and be neutral so you can see where her brain isn’t serving her. One of the ways I like to visualize this is imagining someone in a pool who is starting to struggle. If you jump jump in with the life raft on a rope, it’s much harder to pull them out when you are also in the water. If instead you stay on the edge and throw them the life-raft, you have more strength and power to pull the rope and get them out. The next time you notice yourself wanting to jump in the pool, what might you do instead?

2. People pleasing – I wanted her to like me and I wanted to be agreeable more than I wanted to do the consultation justice and create the space for the consult to be the best it could be

– This is very human! We of course want to be likable and lovable. When you think of WHO you want to be as a coach, how do you want to show up? How can you trust that who you are as a person is likeable while also able to say the hard things (or honest things) with love? Stacey often calls this “being willing to risk the relationship”. While that may seem like we may come off as harsh or bold, sometimes it simply means we show up ready to coach someone’s brain with honesty and love (even if it’s not the easiest thing to do). Service energy may be helpful to anchor into here. What best serves the client for her to get the most from the consult?

3. I wasn’t in service energy, in that I wasn’t seeing the consult as a valuable service that needed to be provided all at once. For example, you wouldn’t get half of a teeth cleaning or half of a facial and just tell the person they could leave early if they wanted to because that’s not actually of highest service to the client.

— Great awareness here coach! You are so right. Now you know what you can do better for next time if this ever comes up again!

4. I wasn’t the strongest energy on the call. I let her energy (chaos) overpower my energy and it literally split the consult in half. This feels differential. Like I deferred to her, I let her set the tone.

— What do you think kept you from staying strong in your own energy? Could it have been because you jumped in the pool or wanted her to like you? How do you want to show up to your next call with her (or on future consults) when someone’s energy feels strong? How might you take the energy back as best as you can?

Hope your consult goes well! Feel free to come back with any coaching you may need!

– I post on LinkedIn 4x a week, in my Facebook group 5x a week, on my Facebook wall 3x a week, and on IG 2x a week
