– I did a virtual workshop in Dec. (the total webinars in 2025 was 5)

– Each morning I write out my gratitude & my 3 intentional thoughts, I answer the question, “How am I feeling about my business right now?” and “What’s the story I’m telling myself that’s creating this feeling?”

– This month, I’m re-starting 2k for 2k study (I originally joined in Sep 2020 & haven’t revisited the material in a while)

– I participated in the Entrepreneur Series: ROI, Revenue Challenge & Behind the Scenes

– I joined Entrepreneur Coach

So, I believe I’m ‘doing’ enough, but I haven’t had a consult book since Aug. 2025 & she was a no.

My Models:

Unintentional

C: 0 consults in 5 months

T: I’m doing a lot with no results

F: powerless

A: freeze, do nothing, 2nd guess myself & my actions, spin in confusion, overthink, consume more

R: Stay stuck & confused, with no results

Intentional

C: 0 consults in 5 months

T: Every action is either bringing results, or bringing data

F: empowered

A: evaluate, ask for help, make offers, think about & speak directly to my ideal client, solve her problem

R: I solve for creating consults & clients

Thanks in advance for your coaching.
answer:
Hi coach,

You asked how to turn things around in your business and start creating consults and clients again. I want to start by naming something important: you 
are
 in the right place, and you’re doing one of the most powerful things available when momentum slows ,  you’re staying in the room. EC, Behind the Scenes, the Entrepreneur Series, returning to 2k,  this is what it looks like to support yourself instead of isolating. Support isn’t a side strategy; it’s how you keep your brain pointed in the direction you want it to go. It the first thing on our todo list and always lead with belief work.

You did a really solid job laying out your two models, and there are two areas I want to help you explore more deeply not to add more to your plate, but to sharpen what’s already there.

The first is this: when you look at your action plan, what are the 
thoughts
 you’re having about those actions before, during, and after you do them?
This matters because we often conflate “doing” with “creating,” and the difference lives entirely in our thinking. Actions don’t create results on their own. They’re fueled by belief. When belief is thin or inconsistent, the actions tend to feel flat even when there are a lot of them.

So when you tell yourself, “I’m doing enough,” and we treat that as factual — 
you are doing enough, and you haven’t booked a consult since August 2025
 , what comes up for you emotionally? That answer points directly to the belief system driving your results.

This is where belief planning matters. How do you need to be thinking  consistently, over time in order to take belief-fueled action long enough for it to compound? Not for a week. Not until you feel better. Long enough for value to land and clients to respond.

The second area I want you to look at is time. How long have you actually been operating from your intentional model? And what timeline are you expecting for consults and clients to appear?

We tend to underestimate how long it takes to build momentum 
and
 how long we need to stay in a high-value mindset for that momentum to show up. When we judge results by how much effort we feel we’re putting in, discouragement creeps in fast.

Effort doesn’t create clients. Skill does. Mastery does. Repetition does. And belief is what allows those things to compound.

Finally, when clients aren’t reaching out yet, evaluation becomes your highest-value work. Not judgment  evaluation. Turn everything into a road map hwo to go again and who you need to become when you go again?

How are you meeting people, exactly? What’s working? What’s unclear? Where are you asking for consults, and where are you holding back? And what are the thoughts you want to deliberately cultivate so your actions stay belief-led instead of fear-managed?

Bring all of this back into the room. We can work through it together. Keep tapping into the community and the spaces that help strengthen your belief that’s how you stay in motion long enough for things to turn.

You’re not stuck. You’re building the part most people quit before. This is the most valuable part of you plan, the belief work fuels highest value.

title: Ghosting consult
question: I had a consult that while I felt there are areas I could have improved, I did much better than the past. I clearly didn’t uncover an objection because she need to talk to her husband (I handled that well and set her up for the follow up) she never showed. I sent her a caring email because I always think something might have happened – I included a summary of our call, validated her discoveries and explained why the follow up is so important for her process not pressure to say yes to working together. That evening, she showed up in a series of workshops I am teaching. I noticed some icky feelings on my part and actively shifted to be 100% present to teach her. She has an injury which I was clear could be addressed but in a 1;1 situation and how to apply what I was teaching in group considering her current state. I’m writing to work through a few things. Being totally utterly ghosted and then she shows up in my workshop and “takes alot of time” with her personal situation was hard and I definetly had feelings which I redirected to my goal for the group as best I could. But I have had NO response from her. On one hand, she has no responsiblity to respond to me. But then it’s like common courtesy? I offer the consults free so I shouldn’t have any expectations they “should” do anything. And yet, if I’m honest I do feel like a “no i’m not intereted” would be nice. what I’m really focusing on is evaluation – what didn’t I uncover, what I didn’t address, what I could have done better in the evaluation is where my energy is best placed. Not on “she ghosted me!” I feel like not responding any more is “letting of the reins.” Or is it giving up on the person who is in need and I can help? When is it pushy and when is it abandoning myself (out of fear? failure?) when is a continued follow up until I get an answer is placing value on the work I do or just. hounding her… or am I letting the consult be – she might still be thinking….here’s the thing in follow ups I get ghosted more often than not. So would you just direct me to eval eval eval? I get so few consults I do feel urgency when I do have one that it “go well.” Did I have that intention at the start of our consult? I don’t think so but I do know she needs help and I can help her. okey, i’m running out of space here 🙂
answer:
Hi coach!

I love how honest you are here, and there’s a lot of self-awareness in the way you’re looking at this. We just want to clean up where your brain is making this heavier than it needs to be. When you zoom out, nothing has gone wrong. A consult where someone says they need to talk to their husband, doesn’t show up, and then disappears is one of the most common sales experiences you can have. It’s not a unique situation that needs solving per se, it’s part of the process sometimes. What stands out to me most is what you said at the beginning, which is that you did better than you have in the past. That’s a celebration – so yay you!

What’s actually bothering you isn’t just that she didn’t respond, it’s the meaning your brain is making about it. There’s a part of you that wants closure, a part that wants to feel respected, and a part that is making her silence mean you must have missed something or done something wrong. We want to separate those. Her not responding is about her. People avoid decisions all the time. They feel awkward saying no, they get overwhelmed, they change their mind, or they just don’t engage. It’s not clean or ideal for us as the entrepreneur, but it’s very common and it doesn’t require you to make it mean anything about your ability.

Where you’re getting stuck is trying to find the “right” way to follow up so your brain can feel in control of the outcome. That’s why your brain is bouncing between wondering if you’re being pushy or if you’re giving up. A cleaner way to think about this is 
why
 you would follow up again… Would it be clean and unattached energy on your part in service of her, or would it be from “get/attached” energy to get an answer for yourself?

You can choose to reach out again in a clean way, with something simple that leaves the door open like 
“I wanted to check back in and see where you’re at. If now isn’t the right time, that’s completely okay.”
 and then you 
let it be.
 This is a personal choice based on what you feel good about. If she didn’t answer that message either, how would you feel?

Right now it feels like continuing to follow up means you value your work, and stopping means you’re losing her, but your value isn’t proven by whether you can get this one person to respond. It’s shown in how you hold yourself regardless of what she does. And with the workshop, of course that felt uncomfortable. You’re human, but look at how you handled it! You stayed present, you served the room, and you didn’t make it about her. That’s true leadership. The only thing I would clean up is the quiet expectation that because she had a consult with you, she should maybe behave differently in that space. In the workshop, she’s simply a participant, and your role is to lead the room, which you did. It also shows that while she ghosted you for the consult, she still values what you bring to the table as a coach. Maybe she just isn’t quite ready for 1:1 and doesn’t feel comfortable in communicating it.

With evaluations, yes, you want to look at the consult, but keep it clean and neutral. Instead of asking what you did wrong, look at whether you clearly led her to see why one-on-one coaching was the best fit, whether you fully understood what she wants and what’s getting in the way, and whether you stayed in leadership or followed her energy. Then you take what’s useful and move forward. The urgency you’re feeling is really coming from the thought that you don’t get many consults, which makes this one feel like it “has to work.” That’s where the pressure is coming from. This isn’t about squeezing more out of this consult, it’s about becoming the coach who creates more opportunities so no single consult carries this much weight.

You did a lot right here and I think it’s worth celebrating. 
What are your thoughts?

If you trusted more consults were on their way and more clients were ready to work with you right now, how would you proceed from this situation?

What actions would you take next in your business?

title: Making money is as in my control as weight loss
question:
Things I notice when I work towards a result and don’t create the results I want in two weeks. This is good awareness.

I started EOC, Creating new beliefs. It’s going great. At the start of class, I set the intention that I would create 3 clients this month. I feel empowered, focused, creating desire.

I hold the desire and space well for 2 weeks, then my brain is like, “OK, where issss it?’

My brain expected I would sign at least one client within those two weeks. I noticed when that did not happen, my brain offered these UTS:

This isn’t working.

I must be doing it wrong.

I don’t have what it takes.

You’re a fool.

You’re embarrassing.

Why do you always try to do things you can’t create?

Rude. These are not thoughts I’m entertaining, but I did write the crap out after ITC to see what was causing the feelings of Disbelief. I evaluated my actual work and anchored back into what I am grateful for and the other results I’ve created during these two weeks. One is being invited to speak at a Women’s Conference this summer and being invited on a podcast that I wanted to speak on. Those are great things.

Things I DO believe I control over: my time, my schedule, my body – ex: to lose 15 pounds I know how to do that. I know that when I take those actions, I get the results. This is in process now and going great despite a couple unexpected results. I’ve lost 3 pounds.

I’m showing my brain, that’s what making money is like. Meet people, tell them I’m a life coach, make offers. That’s all it really takes. In my evaluation, I laid out the other tasks I’m taking from being the sold out coach.

Right now, what my brain is really craving is the reassurance that my work will pay off. I assured it that yes. However, just like with our health, we can’t go into this in disbelief, we have to make the plan based on the fact we have, make decisions as the athlete, weigh and checkin once a week to see where I’m at, and don’t make fluctuations means I can’t do it, I’m having setbacks, or that this is going slow.

Borrowing that is helpful. I’d love coaching on my control in making the money. I’ll do an ITC on that too. I’m asking: What do I control bringing in cash?
answer:
Hey Coach,

I want to slow this down and really meet you where you are because there’s a lot you’re doing well here. The awareness you have is not small. You’re noticing the pattern, catching the thoughts, and bringing yourself back to intention. There is proof here that part of you does see you control over making money and it needs some strengthening.

I also love the comparison you made with weight loss, and I want to build on it a little more because there’s something really useful there. Even with weight, you’re not actually in full control of the result, you’re in full control of the inputs, the outputs and the effort. You create a theory (calorie deficit), you execute, and then you evaluate. And sometimes, even when you do everything “right,” your body sometimes retains water, stress impacts you, hormones shift. You don’t make that mean it’s not working you adjust the theory and keep going. Part of you has made this mean you are in control and that impacts your efforts too.

Business is no different. Making money is also posing a Theory then  Execution and then Evaluation.

Right now, what I see is that you created a theory: “this level of action will create 3 clients in a month.” After two weeks, when the result didn’t match the expectation, your brain went to: “this isn’t working.”

What if nothing has gone wrong yet?

Not as a feel-good thought, but as a real possibility. If two weeks simply isn’t enough time for your current inputs to compound, then your brain is evaluating too early and calling the experiment a failure before it’s complete.

Now, let’s go to your actual question: what do you control in making money?

Before I answer that directly, I want to challenge the belief underneath it because you already named it: part of your brain thinks it’s not in your control.

Where in your life have you already created money?  At some point, you’ve exchanged value for money whether through a job, selling something, or even managing your finances. That’s evidence of control.

How much control do you have over how many people you meet?

How much control do you have over how often you show up as a coach?

How much control do you have to clearly you communicate someone’s problem and solution?

How much control over how many offers you make?

These questions matter because they bring your brain back to what is actually within your control the actions that create opportunity.

You don’t directly control “3 clients.”

You control the volume and quality of exposure, connection, and offers. Making money is a byproduct of those things you control.

So when you say your brain is craving reassurance that it will pay off, I get that. But reassurance isn’t actually what builds trust and sense of control.  What you get to control is how much value you create and VALUE creates MONEY and CLIENTS!

Right now, you ran one cycle of theory → execution → partial evaluation. That’s not enough data yet.

What would it look like to commit to this process long enough that the result becomes inevitable? That question matters because it shifts you from short-term validation to long-term creation.

Now, let’s explore your model a bit, because this is where you take your power back:

C: making money
T: it’s not in my control

F- what do you feel? Because that feeling will explain your actions.

A- Do you hesitate? Do you hold back energy? Do you show up halfway? Do you look for proof it’s not working?

R: you don’t create the money (yet), which reinforces the belief.

Now let’s shift it:

C: making money
T: I am in control of making money When you think that, what changes?

F-

A-

Do you initiate more conversations?

Do you make more direct offers?

Do you stay in the process longer?

Do you evaluate without drama? That’s the version of you I want you to study.

Who is the version of you that fully believes she creates money and how does she behave when results aren’t immediate?

Because that’s the moment that actually determines your success. Not the first two weeks when you feel energized but the moment after, when your brain says “where is it?” That’s where you either keep going… or subtly pull back.

The only reason you haven’t created the 3 clients yet is not because you can’t, it’s because you haven’t matched the necessary volume, clarity, and consstency for long enough.

Refine your theory. Increase your exposure. Keep evaluating doing thorough evaluation Coach!

You’re much closer than your brain is telling you you just have to outlast that two-week checkpoint it’s trying to impose.

title: 1:1 vs. group
question: Hi, I currently have 1:1 as my main offer, 10 sessions package ($1600). Result I want to give my clients is for them to get unstuck in their careers and create career success without stress or self-doubt. My clients are high-achievers who feel behind in their career. My issue with 1:1 has been that 10 sessions has felt very tight to take them from anxiety/burnout/career stagnation/low self worth, to creating calm, building confidence, and building career clarity. We get half way through and it’s the end, only a couple of ppl renew. I would have ideally liked to make that a 15-20 session package and then I would confidently deliver the result. However, given I am not converting even at $1600, I don’t want to increase my prices even more. (Not converting at $1600 because mainly money objection, my clients are based out of India). I tried doing a hybrid program last year at a bit lower cost which worked out well, and I was able to cover much more content in lesser investment because of that. I really am very tempted at creating a 20 week purely group coaching program (2 calls per week, so 40 calls in total), for $950, offer payment plan for $200/month for 5 months to make it even better. My confusion is whether I should just go ahead and do the group program or is this a circumstance change aimed at changing how I feel. My thoughts – 1) I haven’t been fully booked on 1-1, so am I running away from 1:1 to group because it grass looks greener there. 2) If I put same effort in selling my 1-1 package (not treat it like a hobby as I do), I’ll get success here too. 2) I have been coaching for 4 years now, and the idea of a group program actually gets me excited (nervous and scared as hell whether I can deliver as I would like to, but am excited to experiment) vs. just sitting on improving 1-1 business has started to feel a bit boring now. 3) I am not a social media savvy person, and hate posting etc, so while I feel this might be harder to pull together given the challenges of launching a program, at the same time I feel this might be the very challenge that gets me out of my comfort zone. 4) I have never paid for a 1-1 coach for myself to date, and I was in a similar situation as my clients, so I have a thought that more of my clients will want a monthly small payment too. Which thoughts do I believe? Thank you!
answer:
Hey there eCoach,

First, I just want to slow this down and acknowledge something important you are creating consults and you are closing clients. That matters. It tells me this isn’t a “nothing is working” problem… it’s a refinement problem. And those are very solvable.

You started by saying 10 sessions feels tight to deliver the result you really care about. I want to stay there for a moment, because that’s actually foundational.

If you don’t fully believe 10 sessions is enough, how do you think you’re showing up in those consults?

I’m asking that because clients don’t just buy the offer they buy your certainty in the result. If there’s even a small part of you thinking, “This really should be 15–20 sessions,” it can come through in subtle ways how you explain the process, how you handle objections, how grounded you feel when you say the price.

So one place to explore:

What would change if you were selling the length of coaching you actually believe creates the result?

Not from a pricing strategy but from clean belief. What if you changed to 15-20 weeks and kept the 1600?

Now, you mentioned not wanting to increase the price because of conversion. You said the main objection is money especially with clients in India.

But here’s the question that matters more:

Why do you think they’re offering that objection?

Because “money” is often just the surface-level reason. People find money for things they deeply believe in all the time. So when someone says it’s too expensive, I get curious about what’s underneath that.

Do they fully believe they’ll get the result?

Do they believe they can follow through and create the result?

Do they clearly see the value of what you’re offering?

I’m asking this because if the belief in the result isn’t solid, lowering the price or changing the structure won’t actually solve that problem it just changes the packaging.

And I noticed something else in what you shared. You said you’d feel more confident delivering the result in 15–20 sessions.

So I’m wondering:

Is it possible your current level of certainty is influencing both your conversions and your renewals?

Because if a client feels like they’re only halfway there at session 10, and you also feel that renewal becomes a much harder sell.

Now, let’s look at your question about group coaching versus 1:1.

You asked:

“Am I changing the circumstance to change how I feel?” You already have awareness here , what do you know here?

So let’s separate this cleanly:

There’s nothing wrong with wanting to create a group program because it excites you. And excitement alone doesn’t mean it’s the cleanest business decision.

So I’d explore it from both sides:

If you knew your 1:1 offer would convert consistently…

Would you still want to create the group program now?

And on the flip side:

If you knew the group program would be successful

Are you willing to learn the entirely new skill of selling and filling a group?

Because that’s the part I don’t want you to underestimate.

Sometimes group feels more attractive because it seems like:

lower price = easier yes

But in reality, people still buy for the same reason—belief in the result and belief in themselves.

So the real question becomes:

Do you want to solve the skill of selling 1:1 with deep conviction…

Or take on the additional challenge of building, selling, and delivering a group program?

Neither is wrong. But they are different paths with different skill sets.

I also hear you saying 1:1 is starting to feel a bit boring, and group feels exciting and like a stretch.

That’s honest and useful.

But I want to offer you this perspective:

New doesn’t equal better.

It often just feels better because it gives us a break from the discomfort of mastering what we’re currently in.

So I’d get really honest here:

Are you moving toward group because it’s aligned…

Or because it feels like relief?

And one more piece I want to reflect back to you—

When you list your thoughts:

“grass is greener”

“I just need to try harder at 1:1”

“group would be exciting”

“price is the issue”

There’s a common thread I see:

a bit of wavering belief.

Not in your ability as a coach but in the vehicle you’re using to get clients results.

And that matters, because whichever model you choose 1:1 or group you take that belief with you.

So before changing the model, I’d anchor into this:

If you fully believed your clients could create career success without stress or self-doubt through your work…

What would you sell?

How would you sell it?

How would you respond to a money objection?

And what would feel unnecessary to change?

You don’t need to rush this decision.

You can even decide intentionally:

“I’m going to keep selling 1:1 while I experiment with building a group program.”

Not from urgency but from strategy and willingness to learn.

So I’ll leave you with this to sit with:

What do you want to get really good at right now?

And which path supports that most?

What’s coming up for you as you look at it this way?

title: Jumping in with both feet
question:
I am getting the objection of “I want to wait to start til I can fully go all in” or “I want to wait to start til I finish setting up XYZ.” or “I want to wait to start because I’m visiting my mom next week & I want to be able to give this investment my full attention”

And I typically ask “What does “going all in” mean for you?”

They usually say some version of they just don’t want to let themselves down for not utilizing coaching and the investment.

But often times the delay is forever or their self trust about following through worries them enough to talk themselves out of the investment. Any advice for how I coach through this objection better?
answer:
Hi Coach!

First off, that’s a great question you ask them: 
“What does “going all in” mean for you?” 
This helps you gain understanding and find out each individual’s thought around “showing up” for themselves and get clear on what is stopping them.

When they say something like,
 “they don’t want to let themselves down for not utilizing coaching and the investment” 
what comes to mind immediately is that showing up is a choice. Letting themselves down would be from 
the choice
 their making. Not utilizing coaching would be a choice. Not showing up for their investment would be a choice…

Why 
they would make that choice is what I’d want to understand from them.

So maybe the process for the objection would be 
really hearing them
 
when they say this, then get curious as to why their brain is offering it, and repeat back what you hear in a loving way.

Let’s do an example scenario:

You:
 “What I’m hearing you say is you don’t think you will utilize the coaching if you start now… how so? or why?”

Them: 
 “Yes, I just think I’ll be too busy to give it my full attention. It would be easier when I’m done with xyz in a few weeks.”

You:
 “Interesting, can I share what I see? It’s what I would do as your coach.”

Them:
 “Sure!”

You:
 “Okay, our brain’s job is to protect us from discomfort and challenge — but we also know that growth usually comes from facing and moving through those challenges. Do you see how, right now, your brain is doing its job and trying to protect you? On one hand, you know coaching would be helpful for creating the results you want, and at the same time, your brain is telling you it would be safer to wait. But that’s actually the whole point of coaching – to build the skills to meet the challenges that are already in front of us.

From here, you can gauge how open and receptive they have been to this coaching.

If they are open, you may even give a
 silly visual example for them.

Something like,

“Think about a teenager that needs to learn how to drive so they can get to work. They know the benefits of learning.

But imagine they keep telling you they 
should wait
 
until school slows down, or they have less homework, or until summer break…

Stalling feels safer for
 
their brain
 — but through stalling, they also rob themselves of learning how to drive AND how to balance learning a new skill with school obligations. This is similar to what your brain is doing too. It’s just protecting and doing its job. There’s a very simple solution to utilize the coaching/your investment… and it’s as simple 
as choosing
 to show up. Do you trust yourself to show up one hour, once a week?”

This is just an example and not anything you’d have to do if it’s not your style. You can come up with your own style/coaching when you get objections like this. The main thing is remembering you can always show your consults their mind and what it’s doing. Ask if they are open to seeing it and then show them. Sometimes that helps them realize their brain is just protecting them and the outcome is that 
they act
 
rather than wait.

You just want to be sure you’re doing it from a calm, detached energy. Not a “get” energy, or a convincing energy where you’re attached to them signing up. It’s meant to be clean coaching to show them their mind and then release the reins and let them powerfully decide.

What are your thoughts? What is coming up?

Do you see some different ways you could address this objection now?

Bring anything you may still need back here for more coaching.

title: Consult Eval 1/26/26
question:
What worked:

I connected with the client and knew her problem well.

I focused on connecting with the client instead of making sure I stuck to the call format. This meant discussing her relationship in a bit more detail than I’ve done in the past.

I

What didn’t work:

I didn’t ask her about what comes up for her around the price. Time ran over and I got the feeling that she was a no. And once i felt like she was a no I let go of the process. I think moving forward I want to let go of the reins but not the process.

I felt nervous as soon as she said she was coach shopping. I felt pressure to perform and be the best even though I’m not trying to get a yes, I’m trying to get to an honest answer. I felt exposed.

I wasn’t able to coach her on shopping around for other coaches. I didn’t go very well last time I did this so I need to figure out what motivation is with this one so I feel really clean about it.

What to do next time:

Stick to the process even when I feel like the clients is a no.

Make sure to ask about price no matter what. The first person that says the elephant in the room wins the prize!

Get consent to coach on objections.

Please share any coaching you have on the above consult. Thanks!
answer:
Hey Coach!

Great consult eval! Let’s hone in on what you shared that “didn’t work.”

You shared that this person was shopping around for other coaches which brought up feeling like you had to be the best and to perform. You also shared that you felt exposed.

“I wasn’t able to coach her on shopping around for other coaches. It didn’t go very well last time I did this so I need to figure out what motivation is with this one so I feel really clean about it.”

1. What kept you from coaching her on shopping around? Was it simply because it “didn’t go well” on a previous consult?

2. What do you think might have happened if you coached her on it?

3. What didn’t go well in a previous consult where you tried coaching them on it?

4. When you say 
“I need to figure out what motivation is with this one so I can feel really clean”
 — share more on this if you don’t mind.
 What do you mean by this?

5. What might you try differently next time if on a consult they say they are shopping around?

title: Weight loss consult – bridging the gap
question:
hi there!

I just had a consult with a potential weight loss client. I felt a little stuck with the bridging the gap part. Her main issue is yoyo dieting. The pattern is she over-restricts and then over indulges. the way i would help her is by first addressing the over-restriction because that is the first domino of the cycle. i could tell she is afraid of not over-restricting (for her its mainly severely intermittent fasting where she eats one meal a day). i brought that up and she agreed she’s afraid of not over-restricting). i wasn’t really sure where to go from there. i started getting into the details of what we would do on our first call which would be to create a custom plan for her where she would pick it and i would help guide her using my guidelines that i would provide during our first session.

We ended the call saying that she would think about it and get back to me.

Would love your thoughts! not sure if i did the bridging the gap part correctly / overcoming objections. Thank you in advance!
answer:
Hey Coach! Creating a consult is always a time for a celebration. Any time you get on a consult, that’s a win. These calls are where the real learning happens. Every consult gives you more information, more awareness, and more skill for the next one.

You asked specifically about two things: 
bridging the gap
 and 
overcoming objections
. I think it’s useful to look at those separately so you can see more clearly what actually happened on the call.

There isn’t really a “correct” or “incorrect” bridge the gap. The goal is simply to help the client see the connection between 
their problem and the work you would do together
. From what you shared, it actually sounds like you did a nice job keeping it simple, and doable with clear steps,  which is exactly what Stacey teaches.

You said you explained that on the first call you would create a custom plan together, she would choose what felt right for her, and you would guide her using your guidelines. That’s clear and simple. You didn’t overcomplicate it, which is great.

So I’m curious what 
your
 thoughts are about that part now. When you look back, what specifically makes you feel like you didn’t bridge the gap well?

Sometimes what happens in the beginning is the consult feels like it’s moving faster than our brain can process. You even mentioned having the thought “I wasn’t sure where to go from there.” That’s very normal early on. With more practice, something interesting happens: the consult starts to feel slower, because you’ve seen the pattern so many times. You begin to anticipate where the client is going, and you develop a natural structure for how you bridge the gap.

Another thing you did well was getting specific about what would happen first and then next. One small distinction Stacey often makes is that we just don’t want to actually get into the  protocol during the consult. The bridge can be as simple as explaining the approach and then checking in with the client.

For example, after explaining the process you might ask something like: 
“How does that sound to you?” 
That question is powerful because it lets you see what’s happening in their mind before moving forward.

What were you thinking and feeling while you were bridging the gap?

If you felt confused on a consult, it’s often a signal that our brain is trying to figure something out in real time. One useful move in that moment is simply asking another question and giving yourself a moment to gather your thoughts. You can even say something like: 
“What’s coming up for you as I share this?”

This keeps the conversation moving and brings you back into curiosity instead of pressure.

Now let’s talk about the 
“I’ll think about it”
 response. When the client said she would think about it, what did you notice happening in your own mind?

Did it seem reasonable to you that she wanted to think about it?
Did you find yourself agreeing with her?
Did you feel a little in your head at that moment?

These questions matter because objections usually tell us as much about 
our thinking as the client’s thinking
.

One way I like to think about objections is that nothing has gone wrong. Objections are simply 
confusion
. The human brain is designed to say no to anything unknown. If something isn’t guaranteed, the brain will default to safety.

So when a client says they want to think about it, what they usually mean is that the reason they’re giving (think about it , time, money, uncertainty) currently feels more valuable than the result they want.

In the future, when someone says they want to think about it, you can gently explore what’s behind that. For example: 
“What are you thinking about specifically?” 
or 
“What do you feel like you need to know in order to make a decision?”

Questions like these help bring the hidden concern into the open. Another question could be: 
“What are you believing about coaching right now that has you wanting to think about it?” 
Again, the goal isn’t to push them. It’s simply to understand what their mind is doing.

I’m also curious about something related to you. If a client says they want to think about it, 
what emotion would you need to feel in order to stay curious instead of closing the conversation? 
For example, if you tried on curiosity in that moment, how might you respond differently?

Because the truth is this: the decision to stay where they are will often feel like the
 best decision
, simply because it’s the decision they’ve practiced making. It’s known. It’s comfortable. It’s familiar. But that doesn’t mean it’s actually the decision that serves them. how could you share this when they say they want to think about it?

The most important thing here is that you now have 
new information, data
. After every consult you can look back and ask:
What worked?
What would I try differently next time?

That reflection is where the real growth happens. Every time you go again you hav opportunity to figure out what what they need to hear to help themselves believe they can create the results.

And you already have everything you need to go into the next consult with a little more awareness and a little more skill.

Take some time to answers the questions and then bring back your answers here for more coaching.

title: Self-love week eval 2
question:
I took a long time because I didn’t plan ahead, I was clear on the topic and took notes in my notes app, but was wrapped in warming them up and didn’t think about the time. I want to warm them up but 5 min or so.

What planning will you implement specifically to create a clean start time?- I’ll say hellos, ask. questions about the training before, and share a thought about it and use that to ease into that days topic. I will have a timer. T- they are ready to go, I have great information to teach, we’re all ready. F- decisive, planned, clear.

What thoughts were behind the energy shift- It was a mix; disappointment when not as many people were there; not man consults booked. Next time I want to remind myself that I’m doing this for right now clients as well as those 3 years from now and in-between. I’m in this for the long haul. I’m always speaking to one person whether live or in person and this is content I’ll use over and over again.

I didn’t plan ahead because I didn’t really sit and think out the flow of this challenge. I did underestimate the time and energy it would take and didn’t think about the benefit of nurturing or having concise emails in place. For the next round, I want a daily email to market to everyone to join. Once started, I want a daily email to remind them of the live call in the morning and to wrap up and provide replay at the end. I also want to send an email to those that have not joined sharing screenshots of wins/shifts, etc and remind them to join. I’ll start emailing/marketing 7 days before go-time. and then selling 5 days after.

the 20 consults was just a hope. no date behind it. To create more consults next time, I’ll have a tighter marketing plan like above, tighter teaching live call with Q&A at the end of each call; continue the giveaways, etcl.

I am a 10/10 it will make a difference because I know it will make this a better teaching/learning/buying experience for them.
answer:
Hey Coach! This is such a strong evaluation. You didn’t just say “I’ll do better next time.” You slowed down enough to actually see 
why
 things happened and what specifically you’ll change. That’s where real growth lives. Great job answering each question specifically.

I want you to notice the shift in who you are being now versus who you were being going into this one.

When you say you’ll have a timer, plan your warm-up, create daily emails, and define the flow ahead of time that tells me you’re no longer relying on hope or instinct.  Structure ensures the value you worked so hard to prepare actually gets delivered cleanly. A clean start time isn’t about the clock it’s about leadership. It signals to your brain and to them: 
we’re here, we’re ready, this matters.

“I’m doing this for the clients now and the ones three years from now. I’m always speaking to one person.” Powerful thoughts to practice and keep leaning on.

When you anchor into serving one person, your power returns. One person listening deeply is enough.  Every room, every replay, every piece of content becomes an asset that compounds over time.

You mentioned disappointment when fewer people showed or fewer consults were booked. That’s honest. And it’s important to ask yourself this: what did you make that mean about you in the moment? Notice the meaning is optional and you can decide to believe anything you want.

What influences your energy? Identify what takes your energy and leadership and what gives it.  When the meaning shifts from 
this isn’t working
 to 
this is part of building something that lasts,
 your nervous system stays steady. You remain decisive. You keep leading.

What I see now is someone who is no longer guessing. You’re thinking ahead. You’re respecting the full cycle nurturing, the reminders, the follow-up, the selling window. That’s the difference between delivering information and building an experience.

And I want you to really see your 10/10 belief. That’s everything.

A 10/10 belief doesn’t come from perfect results. It comes from knowing you can trust yourself to evaluate, adjust, and go again. It means you’re no longer depending on this one launch to validate you. You’re using it to refine yourself.

This is how mastery is built.

Think of it like stacking bricks. Each launch isn’t separateit becomes part of the foundation. The timer, the clean start, the email flow, the emotional steadiness these are all skills you now own. And once you own them, they don’t disappear. They compound.

So the real question moving forward isn’t 
will this work?

It’s: can you continue showing up as the version of you who plans, leads, evaluates, and goes again without making any single result mean something about your capability? Keep practicing this energy: “I am a 10/10 it will make a difference because I know it will make this a better teaching/learning/buying experience for them”

Great work!

title: Can you help me with the evaluation step please?
question: I am working through the models and the workbooks. I feel myself stalling on the pages that say evaluation, and then the self-coaching after the sections. Can you give me some coaching on how to make better use for these sections and how to implement please?
answer:
Hey Coach,

This is such a great question! And I love that you’re noticing where you’re stalling out when you go to do them, that awareness alone is useful data.

Doing the exercises with the right intention will extract the best information from them. Doing them just to do them can keep you busy without actually moving you forward.

You’re asking how to make better use of the 
evaluation
 sections and the 
self-coaching
 sections, and how to actually implement what comes out of them. That’s such a smart place to pause and get clarity. When you understand 
why
 you’re doing something and what you want to get from it, the work becomes much more impactful than simply completing exercises for the sake of completing them.

One place I like to start is by looking at what’s happening in your mind 
when you think about doing those sections.
 The reason I ask that is because when we stall, it’s usually not about the exercise at all, itself it’s about the thoughts we’re having about the exercise.

You could even model that:

C:
 Doing the evaluation section
T:
 ?
F:
 ?
A:
 Stall out
R:
 Don’t complete the evaluation

Or

C:
 Self-coaching section
T:
 ?
F:
 ?
A:
 Stall out
R:
 Don’t use the tool

The purpose of these exercises is awareness. Both the evaluation and the self-coaching are designed to help you see your thinking and your process more clearly.

With 
evaluation
, the process Stacey teaches is simple but powerful:
What worked?
What didn’t work?
What will you do differently next time?

The real power of evaluation comes from that last question. When what you plan to do differently directly addresses what didn’t work, you create a clear path for the next attempt. That’s when people often feel motivated to go again  because now they have useful data instead of vague self-criticism.

Implementation is simply 
going again using what you learned.

Instead of repeating the same approach over and over, evaluation helps you identify what needs to change so you can keep improving.

I’m also curious what comes up for you when you think about doing the evaluation.

Is it that you’re not sure what to write?
Maybe you feel like you don’t have anything to evaluate?
Or maybe it’s uncomfortable to look at your work that closely?

All of those experiences are part of the process. Evaluation is a skill, and sometimes it takes practice to learn how to do it well.

Another possibility is that a thought like 
“this won’t make a difference”
 or 
“I’m not sure it matters”
 is coming up. When we think something like that, stalling makes a lot of sense.

So I’d love to know: What thoughts come up for you when you reach those sections?
Why do you think you’re stalling out?
And what are you hoping to gain from doing these exercises?

All of these exercises are powerful and very intentionally designed to support your growth. The key is figuring out how they can work 
best for you.

So let’s start there  with what you hope to gain from them and what you think might be getting in the way. Share what you’re noticing, and we can work through it together.

title: Three Consults This Week
question:
I have three consults on my calendar this week. I asked myself, how are you feeling about the three consults?

I have a bit of nervousness and what feels like graspy energy when I think, “This could it, I could make some money.” Then I also go to “they won’t say, “yes.”, and also telling myself not to get too excited to say cautious – I know this warning is to brace myself for discouragement if the consult cancels or if I am unable to convert them on the call.

I don’t know if I’m asking myself the write questions but I wanted to dump out what I’m thinking about this week in my self coaching. This month I’d like to sign 6 clients. I’ve done this in the past, however my belief in signing 6 clients this month feels like a 1 because I’m telling myself I have to get better at consults.

I’ve been noticing that I do a lot of “protection” of myself or what my brain thinks is protection. So, I fail ahead of time on goals I’ve set.

Going into this week, I do want to prepare for my consults by reviewing my last two consults that did not close and I also want to coach my brain on not choosing failure ahead of time.
answer:
Hi Coach,

First, let’s pause and acknowledge you! You created three consults. Your brain needs to register what’s working, not just scan for what could go wrong. Confidence is encouraged by letting accomplishments land.

Before we go into the nervousness and the “graspy” energy, I want to slow this down for a moment. What 
else
 are you feeling about these consults? I ask that intentionally, because when we only name fear or pressure, we accidentally train our brain to believe that’s the whole experience. It rarely is.  Do you notice positive emotions and can you choose to think some of those thoughts too?

What happens if you let yourself focus on the three people who 
chose
 to book time with you? “They’re curious.” “They’re hopeful.” “They’re coming because something in them wants help.” How is that true? 
When you place your attention there on service instead of outcome what do you notice shift in your body? In your energy?
 This is about choosing the lens you bring into the room.

You mentioned feeling like you’re bracing for discouragement telling yourself not to get too excited in case they cancel or say no. That makes sense. Your brain thinks it’s protecting you. But notice how it does that: it rehearses the worst-case scenario ahead of time. That’s the most practiced neural pathway, so of course it’s the default.

Here’s the key question: what if those thoughts aren’t warnings… but habits? And what if discouragement isn’t something you need protection from because you already know how to feel it and keep going? If you believed you could feel 
any
 emotion disappointment included how would that change how you show up on the call?

Instead of trying to eliminate nervousness, what if you normalized it? Of course this feels edgy. 
Of course your body reacts when something matters
. Nothing has gone wrong. In fact, this is often what alignment feels like before growth. And if a client feels nervous too because they’re saying something vulnerable or making a decision how would you support them? You’d probably say, 
“It’s okay to feel this. I’m here with you.”
 That’s leadership you can model, not something you need to hide.

You also shared that your belief in signing six clients this month feels like a one, because you’re telling “yourself you need to “get better at consults.”

Skill-building matters, yes AND notice this: a perfectly executed consult won’t land if you’re disconnected from yourself or the client. People don’t say yes to scripts; they say yes to presence.

So here’s a reframe I want you to sit with: what if the goal of the consult isn’t to convert, but to listen deeply and coach honestly? How would it feel to walk into the call with curiosity instead of an agenda? To trust your intuition instead of trying to perform the “right” process? That shift alone often changes the entire dynamic for you 
and
 for them.

Lastly, let’s talk about the “protection” you’re noticing , failing ahead of time on goals. Why is it a problem that your brain wants to keep you safe? What if the work isn’t to eliminate protection, but to respond to it differently?

Instead of arguing with it, what would it sound like to say, 
“I see you. I know you’re trying to help. And we’re okay.”
 This week, as you review past consults, choose thoughts that support that message: 
I’m capable. I can handle this. I believe in my clients, in coaching, and in my ability to feel whatever comes up and keep showing up anyway.

That’s not reckless confidence. That’s grounded self-trust.

And that version of you the one who doesn’t fail ahead of time, who leads with service, who allows emotions instead of bracing against them is already here. This week is just an opportunity to practice letting her lead. You got this!

title: Surprised by a follow up no show
question:
WHAT WORKED

I prepped before the call, refreshed on 2K, and came in service energy. This was a referral and she’d been watching me on IG for 6 months. Tech hiccup at the jump, but we moved right into the greet. She was looking off to the side, but I didn’t let it bother me.

I loved having the pre-qualifying questions. They helped guide where she is and where she wants to go. I inquired deeper throughout and held a strong standard: I only work with people ready to go all in on one product. She had multiple ideas.

She got emotional several times because I hit the nail on the head and she felt safe. I spoke the truth, even when uncomfortable. This is the best I’ve done at bridging the gap.I clearly saw what she needed. I identified her objection early: time.

I let her ask about price, stated it confidently, and held silence. When she said it was higher than expected, I agreed and asked what it’s costing her not to do it—she connected it to her health, mindset, and lifestyle. When she gave the time objection, I challenged it and she realized it’s already been 3 years.

She asked to start later, I said no and reinforced we start now. I gave two options: decide now or follow up in 2 days. She chose follow-up. Call felt natural, not rushed. I had fun, served, spoke truth, and saw her highest potential. I could feel she wanted to say yes.

WHAT DIDN’T WORK

I need to simplify how I bridge the gap:clear, concise, slower. I didn’t fully understand her vision or end goal. I rushed key moments.

I didn’t fully handle the time objection at a deeper level or inquire enough. She mentioned her husband and I didn’t address it. When she asked to start later, I said no instead of exploring it.

She lacked belief in herself, and I missed the chance to fully paint the vision and step her into possibility.

WHAT I’LL DO DIFFERENTLY

Rebalance the call: 25% where they are, 25% where they want to go, 15% gap, 15% vision, 15% objections, 5% next steps.

Practice simplifying the gap. Focus on mastering vision. Slow down.

When time objections come up, inquire deeper and uncover the real fear (uncertainty, doubt). Stay curious instead of assuming.

RESULT / HYPOTHESIS

No-show for follow-up.

I didn’t paint the vision strongly enough or fully resolve the time objection. My response to “starting later” may have created resistance. The no-show reflects indecision and unresolved fear.

Followed up with a video (gap + vision). Releasing attachment and calling in clients ready to commit.

title: Connection energy not coming across
question:
First- I just want to say the quality of ask a coach has been so amazing lately. Loving the depth in the Q&A, thank you.

Second- I had a consult recently she was a no and when I asked for feedback over email, this is what was said:

“Absolutely, I’m passionate about the coaching field so I’ll be honest. I didn’t feel an emotional connection with you. It felt more transactional than anything.”

I certainly didn’t mean for it to feel transactional but I did keep the call structured and professional.

But I think I need to work on the skill of “emotionally connecting” like she said. I am wondering what that could look like.

Part of me just comes up with logical answers like more small talk at the beginning of the call but I know that’s not what this is about.

Can you help me brainstorm how I might ground my energy in more emotional connection with the person on the call aside from active listening and coaching questions?
answer:
Hey Coach,

First, thank you for your kind words about Ask a Coach. The whole AAC team  really do put a lot of intention into these responses, and it means a lot that you’re feeling the depth of that.

Now, before we even touch the “how, to create connection ” I want to acknowledge you. You received that feedback with openness, curiosity, and zero defensiveness… and that is not common. That alone will accelerate your growth more than a “yes” ever could. You turned a “No”  into data and that’s GOLD!

And it was also courageous to ask for the feedback in the first place. This is exactly how you build something sustainable.

Now let’s look at the “emotional connection” piece. I love that your brain offered “more small talk,” but you’re right that’s not actually what creates connection. In fact, when small talk comes from the wrong energy, people can feel that.

You’ve probably experienced that before at a doctor’s office or on a sales call where someone is saying the “right” things, but it feels flat or transactional anyway. So the question isn’t:

“What should I do differently?” 
It’s: 
“Who am I being and what am I thinking that creates connection?”

Because connection is a feeling and all feelings are created by our thinking.

When you lean heavily into structure and professionalism, it’s not a problem in itself but it often comes from thoughts like:

“I need to get this right”

“I need to be effective”

“I need to show value”

Those thoughts tend to create a more transactional energy.

So let’s experiment with thoughts that naturally create connection:

“I genuinely care about this person.”

“I want to understand what it’s like to be them.”

“What is their life like without this work?”

“How is this problem impacting them emotionally?”

“I’m here to serve, not perform.”

Notice what happens in your body when you think those. Connection often comes when you allow yourself to feel them not fix them.

When you really think about her struggle…
do you feel something for her? Why or Why not?

You can even map this out:

C:
 Consult
T:
 “I want to truly understand and serve this person.”
F:
 Connection
A:
 You slow down, you listen differently, you reflect, you’re present
A (not):
 Rushing, performing, sticking rigidly to structure
R:
 I help the client feels seen, understood, and safe

And here’s the part that most people skip but I don’t want you to. Be willing to overcorrect.

Try going into a consult where you lean too far into connection:

Less structure

Less “professional”

More human

Not forever but as data too. That’s how you find your balance between art and process. Because this truly is an art. The most powerful part of this whole situation isn’t the feedback…It’s how you showed up to receive it and use it.

That tells me you’re deeply connected to your mission and your growth and that will translate into your consults as you keep refining.

title: I feel like quitting- IV
question:
So I’m curious why does your brain think price matters more than value or transformation?

I think because that is what my brain thinks they value. That they are not willing to pay for the transformation. They just want a low price. They want a transformation but want it where it doesn’t cost them. I think there is also a bit of unworthiness underneath as well. Like I’m not worthy to be charging the price I’m charging

How would you show up if you truly believed your clients were already in the room, ready and wanting to hire you? I would move out of convincing and more qualifying-like are you a good fit for the program, let’s get started now

But I want to understand do you feel unclear on your value, or is it that you haven’t practiced articulating it enough yet? I think it’s a bit of both. I started to get more clear on the value of my program and the problem it solves and it’s helped.

When you said your answer to “Why is this 5K?” mostly makes sense to you that’s honest, and it’s key. So what would you need to think and feel for it to feel compelling to them? That I’m 100% confident this works even if you’ve tried “everything”. Confident. Certain of the transformation I know they can achieve. Certain about my own skills and not doubting what i can do. Confident that my program works. Being able to guide them through their any challenge that comes up

Lastly, I want you to look at everything you wrote and ask yourself:

What is the actual problem I’m solving right now? Is it price? Or is it clarity, belief, and communication? It’s the clarity and belief that I am worthy to charge whatever price i want and know that i can deliver on it and more and transform lives. And communicating that to my dream clients I can help them solve their problem. Also not looking for outside validation to create certainty.

So what does “getting clear” actually look like for you this week? More specificity? Practicing out loud? Writing it in multiple ways until it clicks? I’ve been writing things down just to get my thoughts out and so i can see them on paper. Also answering the questions about the specific problem I solve, helping themm understand why its happening, what’s possible on the other side and practicing saying it out loud. I’m also practicing those new beliefs because I still recognize the old ones popping up but I don’t want that anymore. I want to breakthrough and create something new, new levels, and enroll a client!
answer:
Hi Coach,

You did a really great job answering these questions because this is actually where the work starts to become challenging. This is the part where you’re asking your brain to do the heavy lifting.

You’re asking it to access deeper clarity, stronger belief, and new ways to articulate value around something that is inherently intangible. Coaching is different because you’re not selling a physical object someone can hold in their hand. You’re helping someone bridge the gap between where they are and where they want to be  and being able to describe that clearly is part of the value.

What stood out to me is that you’re already noticing the shift. You can see that this isn’t really a “price problem.” It’s never a price problem it’s belief problem in the value. It’s a clarity, belief, and confident communication problem.

And that matters because when your brain believes people only care about price, you start showing up from convincing energy. But when you believe in the value and transformation, you naturally move into sharing the value not the cost. How is it true they want the result more than they want to keep 5k?  If they believe in the value and they understand the value why would it be worth investing 5k? What is the benefit if a 5k investment?  Notice how your brain wants to say I don’t know, maybe, like mine it doesn’t want to think hard and dig deep for the answers that are not on the surface. Brains want to take the easy more efficient way of thinking so you might have to direct it to answer.

I also want you to notice something important:

The more time you spend thinking deeply about your client’s problem, understanding why they’re stuck, learning how to explain it clearly, and helping them see what’s possible on the other side the more valuable your offer becomes.

Not you as a human.

Your worth is already whole and complete. 
This work does not add to or take away from your worthiness. 
But your ability to communicate transformation clearly? That absolutely grows with practice.

That’s why I loved seeing your plan for this week. Writing things down. Practicing out loud. Exploring different ways to explain the problem and solution. That is the work. 
You are training your brain to think more specifically and communicate more cleanly.

And honestly, part of becoming excellent at this is being willing to explain it 100 different ways until it clicks more and more. Every conversation gives feedback. Every time you speak it out loud, your clarity sharpens.

This is also why in-person conversations can be so valuable. They leave room for imperfection while helping you practice real-time communication. You get to see where people lean in, where they get confused, what resonates, and what creates connection.

You mentioned wanting certainty that your program works “even if they’ve tried everything,” and I think this is important too:

Part of building certainty is being willing to practice before you feel fully ready. Before you have all the proof. Before your brain gives you permission. 
Because that’s actually how confidence gets built. 
Not by waiting to feel certain first.

But by continuing to speak, coach, refine, think, and share anyway.

You’re already doing the right work here. Keep practicing the beliefs you want to create. Keep strengthening your ability to articulate the problem and transformation. Keep getting in the room and having conversations. Great work Coach!

title: Another no…part 3
question:
So much good stuff to think about here…

When she said she was going to do it on her own, I think instantly I felt disappointed. I was “trying” not to, but I know I was. I was also surprised, bc I knew I could help her, and wanted to, and genuinely thought she was a yes. I think I thought “I did it wrong” quite quickly. I judged myself I see now, and blamed it on me.

I think I thought it was too late, I didn’t want to convince, her, and so I only asked the one question and then was quite encouraging to her b/c I tell people they will get clarity from a consult…and she did. So I also knew that I had done my job well…maybe too well was the question.

I think it would have been helpful to get more curious about her response. I like some of the questions you offered that I could have asked and I see that would have been helpful, and also not convincing or pushy.

I think my brain just has this ingrained idea of if it isn’t working, I’m doing it wrong. For much of my life I was very black and white, right or wrong, enough or not enough….so I think what goes on autopilot is if it doesn’t work out, I messed up somewhere. I don’t love that conclusion!

As far as clients having the what and the how, MAYBE they could use it and be successful, but I know the what and how and I still need help from coaches. It is implementing and also seeing the little things that stop them that they can’t see for themselves.

To be genuinely curious, and not fear being pushy, I could think I am committed to helping her make an educated decision that is best for her.

I think pushy means convincing someone to do something that might not be right for them…and just saying that has me realize I would never do that. Ever. That is not me. Asking questions is so much more helpful for them and it feels better for me too.

When she mentioned $ being hard, I knew I agreed. I was feeling some fear rise up…it reminded me that $ being hard was one of the reasons I really wanted her to sign. Yes b/c I can help her…and b/c I would help me financially too. I was in the pool with her instead of staying in my coach brain. I slipped to thinking about me, I see that now.

I see I have a lot to learn, but I love thinking of this as a huge way to learn and get better at this skill.

Thank you!
answer:
Hey Coach,

You are so welcome.

I want to shine a big light on how much awareness is in this response because this is exactly where the gold is. The value isn’t just in what happened on the consult it’s in your willingness to slow down afterward and extract every lesson available to you. You did a beautiful job of getting specific about what was actually happening in your mind, and that level of awareness is what allows real growth.

I love how you took the coaching and then continued to dig deeper within yourself to see what was coming up. I can actually feel the energetic difference from how your response started, when your brain was still trying to make sense of what happened and looking for where you may have gone wrong, to where you ultimately landed by the end.

One thing that stood out to me was how quickly your brain went to, “I did it wrong.” That awareness is huge because now you can begin separating the result from your evaluation of yourself. Just because someone doesn’t sign up does not automatically mean you did something wrong. 
That’s a conclusion your brain has practiced for a long time,
 
but it doesn’t make it true.

What I find interesting is that in the very same consult, you were able to recognize that she got clarity and that you served her well. Yet another part of your brain was simultaneously making her decision mean you failed.

I also love what you uncovered around being pushy. It sounds like when you really examined that fear, you found that what you actually want is to help someone make an informed decision. That’s very different from convincing someone. Convincing is trying to get someone to do what is best for you. Coaching is helping someone see what is true for them.

And I think your insight about money is equally important. When she brought up that money was hard, you noticed yourself jump into the pool with her.  We all have places where our own fears get activated. The goal isn’t to never have those moments. The goal is to notice when we’ve left our coach brain and gently return to it.

What I see in all of this is not someone who did anything wrong. I see someone learning how to stay present when disappointment shows up, how to remain curious when objections arise..

That is a skill. And like any skill, it gets stronger through awareness, reflection, and repetition.

Keep doing exactly what you’re doing here. This level of self-coaching is what will make you a stronger coach, not because every consult will become a yes, but because you’ll become less reactive, more curious, and more available to serve the person in front of you.

There is so much gold in this reflection. Great Work Coach!

title: Meetup evaluation and feedback request
question:
Hi!

I went to an informal church ladies meetup yesterday. Picnic in the park with moms and kids. I was hoping to meet and connect and tell people I was a life coach and see what happened from there. I did go in curious but also with intent to meet people and tell them I was a life coach and offer to help, if the occasion arose.

My eval:

Ww- I showed up

One other family showed up

I brought food/water/toys

My boys enjoyed themselves

I brought my chair, had a nice time, good weather.

Wdw- No bathrooms and ants showed up

Only one other family showed up because the leader last minute change the venue didn’t alert anybody who had said they were going and didn’t show up.

The other lady and I talked about realty the whole time -why? That was her job. She didn’t ask about mine after I told her what I did.

It was really far away for me to drive.

Wdd- introduce myself and figure out where in the conversation I could insert that this is how I help the ladies that I coach.

Check the invite again last second?

Not bring sandwiches.

I really just feel like i don’t know how to naturally steer the conversation to, oh, that is what I help people with.

I don’t really even think any of our conversation was a lead-in to tie coaching in or how I help.

Do you have any suggestions or what else I could do differently? Or is that too salesy or creepy and because she didn’t ask, I shouldn’t push?

Thank you
answer:
Hey Coach,

Let’s start where we always like to start with what worked and how you showed up.

You showed up!
And I really believe that’s the first successful thing in business. Most people don’t even get themselves in the room. You did. You went with intention, curiosity, and willingness to connect.

Now let’s look at your “what didn’t work,” but clean it up so it actually helps you extract so much value from your showing up effort and energy.

You mentioned ants, no bathrooms, I’m going to lovingly say those aren’t as useful for your eval. Also are ants that just part of a picnic? lol  When you evaluate, stay with what you can control and where you may have been in your head or you didn’t lean in when you would have liked to.

You said the conversation stayed on real estate the whole time. My question is what were you thinking in that moment? What were you feeling and what did that lead you to say or not say?

I’m asking this because your thoughts in real time are what either open you up to share or keep you quiet. Were you thinking about her and what she was sharing? What if that was not a problem and you were being interested in her?

Did you think:

“There’s no natural way to bring this up”?
“I don’t want to be pushy”?
“She didn’t ask, so I shouldn’t say anything”?

Because if that’s what was happening, it makes sense you didn’t share.

If you felt there was an opportunity and didn’t take it, why not?
And if there truly wasn’t one, that’s okay too. Not every conversation is meant to go there.

But don’t just say “it didn’t happen” look at why and if you like the reason then go from there.

You said you don’t know how to naturally steer the conversation to “this is what I help people with.” So let’s look at that.

Was there actually something she said that you help people with?
Or were you trying to come up with something to fit it in?

Because sometimes when you’re telling yourself “there’s no natural way,” what’s really happening is you’re trying to force a connection that isn’t there and that’s when it feels salesy. Salesy because of your thought not because sharing is inherently salesy.

Now I want you to consider this: If you were fully booked…
and you showed up to that same picnic?

What would be different about how you approached that conversation?

Would you be thinking about how to bring up coaching?
Or would you just be present, asking about her, genuinely interested in her experience? Notice the difference in who you are being.

If you were coaching her in that moment, would your focus be on you and what you do or on her and understanding her?

Showing up as a coach isn’t something you wait to be invited into with a perfect line. It’s how you show up in the conversation.

What if you were interested and were in your coach indentity? Some thing you might ask next time are natural and if you are genuinely curious might sound like:

“What do you love about that?”
“What’s the hardest part?”
“How did you get into it?”

That’s you being in coach energy. And from there, sometimes it opens sometimes it doesn’t. And that’s okay.

I also want you to look at this piece:

You asked if it’s too salesy or creepy to bring it up if she didn’t ask. That’s a thought that either you or her would be having. It is a optional.

So what would you need to believe about sharing what you do… for it to feel clean instead of pushy? Because “salesy” is just a feeling created by what you’re thinking usually something like “I need to get a client” or “I’m forcing this.”

What if instead you believed:

“There are clients everywhere, and my job is just to show up as a coach.”

You can even run your own model here:

C: Picnic, conversation about real estate
T: “I don’t know how to naturally bring this up”
F: ?
A: What do you do or not do?
R: What result do you create?

That will show you everything. From there what do you want to believe instead?

Coach you did a great job with this eval. Now we just refine where you’re putting your focus so it actually helps you grow.

I want to direct you to this podcast episode so you can borrow Staceys thoughts and energy around networking in life, and at events in person and online

Episode 24: Networking for
 
Business

I have to ask what are you bringing instead of sandwiches next time? I’m curious what you’d do differently there too.

title: Consult Eval – JB – 06/02/26
question:
What went well

• I felt NO Stress. Some stage fright, sure but nothing debilitating

• I thought I would need a Thousand consults to reach this state of “oh yeah… A consult got booked in the evening for the following morning and it’s totally normal)

• The start of the consult felt natural, not scripted or rehearsed

• She felt seen / understood, especially after the bridging the gap

• I sensed that she wasn’t fully bought in and asked questions to understand what was going on instead of shying away from it

• I asked what was missing for her to make her decision

What didn’t go well

• I didn’t handle her objections well.

1. She had seen two therapists and didn’t follow through with them because it wasn’t concrete enough

2. I showed her how coaching WAS action / goal oriented and then she was afraid it would take up too much of her time and add to her mental load.

3. At the core, her objection was : I know what I want to do but I don’t want to do it AND I’m afraid I’m not going to be capable to do the work

• So i addressed some of it

– You’re already living in “what if it doesn’t work”

– You decide on the action plan and an action doesn’t have to require a ton of energy / effort

• But I think at the core, where I failed is on creating the vision. I was too much on the process and not enough on the results it would create for her or how she would feel.

So she did have the concrete part she was looking for but it must have still felt too brainy and not enough problem solving or relief bringing.

What to do differently

• Revisit the 2K for 2K material, listen and journal from it, especially the “Objection” module

• Actually say the words “it sounds like it’s a “no” for now”

• Remember to treat the consult like a coaching sessions with more questions than statements so it’s not received like judgements or assumptions
answer:
Hi Coach!

Great job on the consult and coming here with your eval! It sounds like you’re clear on WW, WDW, and WDD.

When bringing consult evals here, what is one thing in particular you would like coaching on related to this consult evaluation?

You can go back through your WDW and WDD sections and find one thing and bring it back here and ask about it specifically. Getting in the habit of being specific 
(on every consult eval you bring to AAC)
 lets you hone your skills at auditing what you’ve done and adapting what you’ll do going forward. It also helps you get the most targeted coaching and transformation.

This being said, if you’d like, find one specific area you’d like to focus on with this consult and bring it back here for more coaching.

If not, try to do so with any new consult evals going forward so we can best serve you! Thanks Coach!

title: Client wants to postpone start b/c pregnancy
question:
I had a consult in March with someone who wanted to begin May 1. I just got this email and I’m wondering how to respond:

“So… we set things up to begin my coaching on 5/1. Well, I just discovered I’m pregnant with my first babe!!

I’m so excited and also will want to postpone any investments to cover out of pocket maternity care.

Expected due date is 12/12… so I’d love to circle back potentially around new year.

I’m very appreciative of your work and will continue to plug in all the time.

Now, this woman is about to get pretty savage about transition to remote work 💫”
answer:
Hey coach,

I love this question, and I want to start where you started here, you created a consult, she said yes, she was ready to begin in two months. That matters. Don’t skip over that.  A very strong part of her wants to get started, and a part of her feels unsure and that is normal.

And now you’re asking, how do I respond to her wanting to postpone after her initial delay of coaching.

When you read her email, what actually came up for you? What did you notice you made her postpone email mean? Why ?

Was it “of course, that makes sense”?
Or was there a part of you that went, wait… WHY  postpone?

I’m asking because that thought is important. That’s the doorway into how you could chose to respond.  I might suggest the second one if it feel true, a big authentic response, WHY now, I’m confused now seems more like the time to get started asap?  What are your thoughts?

And I’m also curious what are you making her decision mean ? What are you believing about postponing now after delaying?

Is it about money? Timing? It never is the true reason to postpone, she is probably believing other things are more important.  I might ask her specifically what she thinks about coaching that has her put this off now? 
Or is there any part of you making it mean something about your offer or your ability to hold the value of what you do?

Just notice that, because if that’s in the background, it will either have you pull back or try to convince.

Now let’s look at her view point  for a second to understand a bit more.  She just found out she’s pregnant , big, emotional, exciting.
And at the same time, she’s about to navigate a pretty big transition into remote work. Her emotions are probably high, normal and not typically when we make the best decisions.

What if you asked her , what has you believing this is a time to postpone support instead of a time she might need it the most?

You could say, If you actually want this I am happy to talk about what you might be considering why or why not you want to put this off?

If you really believe postponing is best for her, you’ll feel clean just supporting that. But if there’s a part of you that’s like, this is exactly when coaching would help her… then are you willing to say that?
