Not to push. Not to override her.
But to offer her a perspective she may not be considering.

Because right now, she’s making a decision from her current thinking, in her big emotions with out your thoughts and beliefs and expert knowledge,  which makes sense.
But your role isn’t just to agree with her thinking it’s to help her see what she can’t see yet.

What do you think is the cost of her waiting?

Not financially but in how she navigates this next season of her life.

And are you willing to share that from a place of care?

Sometimes this is where it can feel a little uncomfortable, like, “am I being pushy?” But there’s a difference between being pushy and being honest. If you believe in what you do, then offering that truth is service.

And this is where I’d bring you back to the belief triad.

Where do you think the wobble is, if there is one?
Is it belief in the value of coaching?
Belief in her ?
Or belief in yourself delivering the result?

Because wherever that is will show up in your response.

And I also love the question “what if it’s not about the money?” If it’s not then what is it?
And how would you respond if you weren’t trying to protect her from discomfor or yourself from rejection?

People invest in things all the time when life is full especially when they see the value.

How do you want to communicate the value of starting now?
What would you say if you fully trusted that what you offer matters here?

This really isn’t about crafting the perfect response. It’s about who you are when you respond.

Are you someone who just agrees and moves on?
Or are you someone who can celebrate her, honor her decision  and also gently challenge her thinking if it’s not serving her?

You’ve got this coach!

title: Energy with consultations vs. Energy with clients
question:
I’ve been at a place where I’m not having scarcity thoughts like I used to with consultations that would cause a lot of “get” energy. I also know that I’m a great coach and my clients get amazing results.

The problem is, I will go a long time without a consultation and then when one schedules I feel like I’m not prepared. I’ll start questioning my prices and question things I’m doing, which makes me feel like a beginner again.

I think because I don’t get a lot of consults I haven’t been able to really work through this behavior, and it throws me off every time and makes me nervous for the call. And when I’m nervous, I don’t listen or feel like my full leadership energy. Now, when people become my clients, I’m never nervous. I feel confident, capable and like a full leader.

Can you help me with this confusion, I want to feel as confident with consults as I do with my clients.
answer:
Hey coach,

First, I want to slow this moment down and have you really acknowledge something important: you’ve already done meaningful work here. You’re no longer showing up to consults with that frantic, scarcity-driven 
get
 energy. That didn’t happen by accident. At one point, this is exactly where you wanted to be less urgency, more trust in yourself, more certainty in your value. Noticing that progress matters, because confidence grows faster when we allow ourselves to register what’s already changed.

Now let’s look at what’s actually throwing you off.

You said: 
“I’ll go a long time without a consultation, and then when one schedules I feel unprepared. I start questioning my prices and what I’m doing, and I feel like a beginner again.”
This is an important clue  because the discomfort isn’t coming from the gap between consults. It’s coming from what you’re making that gap mean
.

Time without consults is neutral. But when your brain interprets “a long time” as 
something is wrong
, 
I should be further along
, or 
maybe I don’t know what I’m doing
, of course your nervous system kicks in. Nervousness isn’t the problem it’s the signal that confidence-eroding thoughts are running the show.

So instead of asking, “Why am I nervous?” I want you to ask a more useful question:
What am I telling myself when a consult finally appears on my calendar?

Take a moment and actually list the thoughts that show up right before a consult:
What do you question about your pricing?
What do you doubt about your process?
What story do you tell yourself about being “out of practice”?

This matters because thoughts always create feelings — not the calendar, not the consult itself. When you see the pattern, the confusion starts to lift.

Here’s a perspective shift that often helps:
If you hadn’t had consults because you were fully booked… or intentionally paused… or chose not to open spots what would you be thinking about the absence of consults then?
Notice how different the feeling would be. Same circumstance. Completely different meaning.

That tells us something powerful: confidence isn’t missing  it’s conditional right now.

The next layer to explore is gently honest, not self-critical:
What do you think is happening with consult creation right now?
Have your actions shifted? Your visibility? Your consistency?

And when you notice that, what do you make 
that
 mean about you?

This isn’t about fixing anything it’s about removing unnecessary judgement so leadership energy can return.

Now let’s anchor into what 
already works
.

You said something crucial: once someone becomes your client, the nerves disappear. You feel capable. Present. Like a leader.

So ask yourself:
What are you thinking about yourself when you’re on a client call?
Who are you being in that space?
How do you view the person on the other side of the screen?

The skills are the same. The leadership is the same. The only thing that’s changing is the story your brain tells you about what’s at stake.

Confidence isn’t something you earn through repetition alone. It’s something you 
practice allowing
 by choosing thoughts that support the version of you who already knows how to lead.

Bring awareness to that  and you’ll start showing up to consults the same way you show up everywhere else.

And  bring your answers back. We can walk this through together and stabilize your confidence so it doesn’t depend on how full (or empty) your calendar looks.

title: Another no part 2…
question:
You are spot on about me overlooking the good. It was a big deal to serve her so well 2 times…and to do a great job! Before I go on, I did want to ask you if I did anything wrong with the fact that she had a plan and wanted to go it alone? Did I give too much info? I did not give the how…only the what…but did I do that wrong?

It’s also very helpful that you pointed out the skill isn’t about avoiding disappointment…but getting better at allowing it, and being careful about what I make it mean. I can see I’m not there yet.

You are also correct that I am feeling scarcity and that it’s been a long time of consults being rare, and that it might continue. I do not want it to be that way…but my brain now has TONS of evidence about them not happening much. I see my brain asking HOW are other people getting consults? That is also why I am still in here showing up…bc consistent consults is not a skill I have yet.

Eval…I think I handled the consult well. I think I bridged the gap, created the vision, and showed up in great energy. I do feel I am getting more clear there. And truthfully, I was also proud of myself for not offering any lower prices. I was committed to my price being very worth it before I even got on the call, and I held that belief easily, especially for where she was and where we were about to go.

Something came up that might be something though…a difference from the discounted 2 to this one is I think I felt going into the other 2 that they were not going to be able to pay full price and I was going to take whatever it took for them to be clients. And looking back, I remember thinking “Uh oh” when the last one said she was a 2 in her finances and was explaining why. I remember purposely trying to not focus on that fear when she talked about how life was so expensive and that she doesn’t make enough $ and that it’s always been hard. If I may be 100% truthful here…I think I also realized that I feel that way too! I hate to say that…but inside I know I was feeling it. I was also thinking how I don’t WANT to feel that way anymore..and I am working to stop it. I tried to be in belief for her and I really felt I did…guessing this means no though?

I also see I could have asked what she meant by tougher. I think I also fear being pushy or convincing b/c I don’t want to sway anyone to do something or come on too strong or be graspy. Overcoming objections is still tricky for me too!

Jeesh my list is long!
answer:
Hi Coach,

What you’re noticing about overlooking the good is such a normal human tendency. One of the reasons we do evaluations so deeply in 2k is because when you extract the value from a consult, you get to use that information the next time. The skill is training your brain to first look for what worked and what you did well. That puts you in a much better state to evaluate what didn’t work. When we only look at what’s missing or wrong, it becomes much harder to get clean information.

You asked a really good question: Did I give too much information? Did I do it wrong?

Let’s slow that down with a model.

C- consult says: “I am going to try it on my own”

T- What were you thinking in that moment?

F- How were you feeling?

A- What did that feeling have you do or not do? Be as specific as possible here. For example would you have shared the problem with them trying your process on their own and then judging the process as not working and they didn’t actually work the process?

A- What do you wish you had done differently?

R- Not help them see the impact of doing on own.

The reason I’m asking is because often what impacts our response isn’t the objection itself t’s our thinking about the objection.

I’m also curious: if you did do it “wrong,” what are you making that mean? Is it a problem? Or is it simply information that helps you learn how to respond to a similar situation in the future?

You mentioned wondering if you gave too much information. Even if you had given more of the “how,” what do you know about clients having the what and the how? Most people already know a lot of what to do. The challenge is usually implementation. It’s the fears, doubts, blind spots, habits, and obstacles that get in the way. Coaching isn’t just about information; it’s about helping someone do what they already know they want to do. What about the part of them that showed up to get help?

I also think this is a great opportunity to get curious about the objection itself. What would you need to think to feel genuinely curious instead of worried about being pushy? Curiosity might sound like:

“What do you mean by that?”

“What does your plan look like?”

“What will you do if that doesn’t create the result you want?”

“What would make working together worth it?”

” Why would you want to do this together even if you could do it alone?” what is the benefit?

Those questions aren’t about convincing someone. They’re about helping them get clarity on their own thinking.

You also mentioned fearing being pushy. I think that’s important to look at. What do you think being pushy means? How is it different from helping someone fully explore their decision? Sometimes we avoid asking the next question because we’re afraid of influencing them, when really we’re just helping them understand themselves better.

I also want to highlight something you noticed that feels important. You recognized some of her thoughts around money sounded familiar. That’s useful awareness. Not because it means that’s why she didn’t buy, but because it gives you something to explore. What was happening for you internally while she was talking about money being hard? What impact do you think that had on your energy, your questions, or your confidence in that moment?

And finally, I want to celebrate something. You held your price. You believed in the value. You didn’t discount. That’s a big win.

The way we find the “right” approach is by trying a lot of approaches that don’t work. That doesn’t mean you’re doing it wrong. It means you’re learning. Every objection gives you another opportunity to practice, evaluate, and refine your skill set.

You said overcoming objections is still tricky. No problem. What if you saw this consult as exactly how you get better at overcoming objections? One conversation at a time. One evaluation at a time. One lesson at a time.

That’s how the skill gets built. Great work on this part of the process, even though it’s tricky.

title: 0/15 sign ups // aac4
question:
I really considered the coaching! And was going all in… except in order to secure the space, I need to have the funds to book. And without the actual sales, the closer the event got, it felt like too much of a risk!

So I set the “strike of midnight” at midnight tonight and put out a few friends and fam invites. I got one person interested— which puts me back in the loop of offering discounts when I swore never again, lol.

I did however see my lack of commitment.

It’s interesting that I didn’t secure the space first. But I just assumed once I had the first few yeses, I could rent the space.

In hindsight, one thing that I am celebrating is that in past years, this would’ve devastated me. Now it feels more like, disappointing, but also ok that it wasn’t the time for this.

It feels like I’ve been in a shifting relationship with my business, who I want to be as a coach— bc my own thoughts haven’t been in love with my business and my offers.

Now, it feels like I’m back to square one; even though, I know that’s not anywhere near true! Bc I’ve gained so much experience over the years.

But ready to start feeling excited by my business and offers again.

Thanks for the coaching!
answer:
Hey Coach,

First, I want to celebrate how much growth is here! 
What stands out to me is not that the event didn’t happen. It’s how you handled it.

You allowed yourself to feel the disappointment without letting it become devastation. You’re able to look back honestly, see what happened, acknowledge what you did well, and keep moving forward. That is growth.

I also love that you’re able to see in hindsight that you weren’t fully committed. Not as a criticism, but as awareness. Awareness is always valuable because now you have information that is gold.

Notice that not securing the space first was likely a reflection of a belief. There was a part of you waiting for enough evidence before you went all in. You were waiting for others to commit before you committed.

What I find interesting is that as coaches and business owners, we are often leading people with our belief long before we’re leading them with our strategy. When we hesitate, they feel hesitation. When we’re waiting for proof, they’re often waiting for proof too.

It’s a bit like asking people to cross a bridge that we haven’t fully stepped onto ourselves. Yikes, feels scary to offer that.

The other thing I want to offer is around what you said about wanting to feel excited about your business and your offers again.

Do you really want the business or the offer to create the excitement? 
I ask because I think this distinction matters.

If the offer creates the excitement, then your emotional state becomes dependent on finding the right offer, the right launch, the right opportunity, or the right circumstances. But if you create the excitement, then you’re in charge.

An offer doesn’t actually create excitement. We do.

So I would get curious about this:

How do you want to think about your business regardless of the offer?

How could you fall in love with the process of serving people, creating value, and growing your business before the results arrive?

What would you need to believe about yourself, your offer, and the people you help in order to go all in first? 
Those questions matter because they shift the power back to you.

From everything you’ve shared, I don’t think you’re back at square one at all. Someone at square one wouldn’t have this level of awareness, honesty, experience, or self-trust.

You already know how to sell.

You already know how to create offers.

You already know how to go all in.

The question isn’t whether you can do those things. 
The question is: What do you need to think and believe to become the version of you who goes all in first and then leads others there? 
That feels like the work in front of you.

And from what you’ve shared, I think you’re much closer than you realize. Thank you for sharing and we are here for more coaching, you got this coach!

title: Consult Call Judgements
question:
Hi Coaches,

I just received a notification for a consult call booking, and on my booking page I have the question “Is there anything I should know prior to our call?” where I typically get basic info. However…. the person who booked this consult call left a verrrrryyyy long message (which is absolutely fine), and I am having a hard time not judging her based on what she says in this answer.

In her answer, she goes into a very in-depth story about her son and daughter-in-law, claiming that this DIL has ruined the relationship she had with her son. She claims the DIL has “torn our family apart.” She also writes about how the other sons don’t do enough for her, and it’s also because of their wives, and how it’s wrong of them to focus on their own little children and not her.

The coach in me can see what’s going on very clearly– victim mentality, her expectations, and the manual she has for her children and their wives, etc. But there is also a part of me that already dislikes her because she sounds exactly like my own mother-in-law. I keep having the thought that “someone like this will never change, no matter what.” I know our thoughts create our feelings and drive our actions, and are not truth… but this feels very true to me right now. I have a LOT of thoughts about her already, and I’m struggling to keep a clean mindset around this consult call.
answer:
Hi Coach,

Thanks for bringing this here and also for vulnerably sharing how you feel about it. First of all, of course this feels a bit sticky… You’re human and you are in a similar situation so your brain is sending off alarm bells. Your ego is just wanting to protect you. We want to acknowledge it, but not let it run the show. Let me help you consider how you can go into this consult clean and do your best to serve.

Some perspective shifts:

The first thing I recognized about this situation is the fact that she is actually showing up to get/ask for help. She may not know it 
(yet)
 that she is in victim mentality, blame, or her own manuals… but she 
is
 
someone willing to sign up for a consult, seek help, & learn. How admirable is it that she is 
actually willing
 to take steps that can better her as a person/MIL? Or to take actions that your own MIL maybe hasn’t/won’t? Can you imagine what might shift in your own life if your MIL was willing to be coached? Keep in mind this woman is at least trying to gain awareness
 (and how perfect that she’s coming to you for it?)

Next, she is trusting you. There is some level of comfort or trust she already feels to not only book a consult, but be that open and vulnerable right off the bat. That’s a compliment. She is obviously in “pain.” On the consult, how can you anchor into compassion to validate where she is, but also share how you can help her?
 Here’s what I mean:
 She listed out all of her thoughts about what she doesn’t like and feels victim to. For her this feels very real and valid. If your MIL also behaves this way, what it shows us is that 
this woman is “not alone”
 in her thoughts, fears, or struggles. She may not be RIGHT, but she isn’t alone in what she feels.

Being neutral and separating yourself from your own situation can help you offer compassion 
(even though you have different thoughts)
 so she knows 
“Oh, I am not alone in how I feel, but there is a different way to go about this and this coach can help me.”

Next, when you hop on the consult with this woman, try to anchor into the fact that you have two separate identities. You have who you are as a daughter-in-law 
(that may very much want to pick apart every word and judge this woman),
 
AND
 you have your professional, neutral coach self who can 
help this woman.
 There may be several times on the call where you have to remind yourself to be that professional, neutral coach-self. If it helps, put a sticky note on your laptop or nearby so you can look at it and 
anchor back into service
 when your mind ventures into your own story.

Lastly, keep in mind that by being neutral, you may actually learn that her situation is completely different than yours with your own MIL. You don’t yet know her dynamics with her kids or their spouses. You don’t know if they’ve done something terrible, or if they are truly just focused on their own families. At one point her sons were her entire life and if they’ve pulled away to focus on their own family, she’s likely just in grief. That grief has turned into whatever is happening in her mind.

Here’s something important — she’s asking for help 
with her mind
 and she needs someone she can trust and be open with. She has chosen you to potentially be that person in some way and that is an honor.

Imagine the ripple effect of you being able to be neutral for this woman.

1. She will feel safe to come to you authentically and honestly.

2. She will know she’s in safe hands to get help and be coached without judgement.

3. Though maybe uncomfortable at times, she will learn how to shift her mindset and feel better over time.

4. When she begins to learn and shift (because you 
cleanly
 coach her 
and don’t make her calls about you
), she may start behaving differently to her sons/DILs.

5. Her DILs may experience a totally different version of her and their relationship 
could
 get better.

6. They may all have a healthier family 
because of you being clean/in service
 and 
her
 being willing
 to do the work.

What do you think? How does this land/feel? Do you feel you can go into this consult ready to serve?

Feel free to bring back your thoughts or any further coaching you may need. Thanks Coach!

title: Seeing problems as “too big”
question:
Hi Coach,

I have a consult tomorrow, and I’m struggling to believe that I can help her, that her problems are “too big”. I know logically of course that this isn’t true, I know I can help. But I wanted to do a practice “bridging the gap” based on what I know about her so far, and I just keep thinking that this isn’t enough to help her. The only things I’ve really been able to come up with are to teach her how to identify the secondary level of pain that is piled on top of the already painful situation (clean pain vs. dirty pain). But even that doesn’t seem good enough to actually make a difference in her life.
answer:
Hi Coach,

Thanks for bringing this here, we are happy to help!

You said,
 “I’m struggling to believe that I can help her, that her problems are “too big”.

1. Why do you think your brain is telling you her problems are “too big” based on what you already know?

2. And why do you think your brain is struggling to believe you can actually help her?

Your brain is also offering, “
But even that doesn’t seem good enough to actually make a difference in her life.”

Anytime our brain believes something won’t be “good enough,” it often means it has an underlying, subconscious “manual” for what IS good enough… So currently your brain thinks what it has come up with isn’t good enough to bridge the gap – why?

What do you believe IS “good enough”?

Can you answer that if you really dig?

Something you may find helpful is revisiting the bridging the gap modules in 2k if you haven’t already.

Another way I personally like to think about “bridging the gap” is understanding where they are currently, where they want to be, and then recognizing how I can help them make that happen. Not by teaching them my process on the consult, but repeating back what they’ve told me they are struggling with, repeating back what they want in their life (the results they are hoping for), and then embodying that “expert, I can help you” energy.

For example
, if on a consult someone told me they need to have hard conversations with their partner but they shut down. They hate how they don’t feel confident and it leads to fights. Instead they want to be calm, but still speak up and allow the conversation to be productive.

To bridge the gap I might say,

“so what I’m hearing from you is you tend to shut down when difficult conversations take place and your goal for yourself is to be able to have those conversations but feel empowered doing so…. Okay, so what needs to happen is getting your nervous system more regulated. We need to figure out what causes you to want to shut down and then get to work on emotional regulation skills when you feel activated. So if we do work together, I am going to help you do that. I’ll help identify
 why
 this feels so challenging in those moments and
 teach you
 some different tools/concepts to help you stay regulated during difficult conversations so you don’t shut down. 
There’s a version of you that can feel really proud of yourself
 when stuff like this arises and
 the good news is I know exactly how to help you do it.
 So even though 
you aren’t there right now, you will be
 once we start coaching together and you learn my processes.”

This is of course just an example. You may have a different way you want to bridge the gap! What feels aligned based on what you do as a coach and how you know you can help?

You can bring any of your thoughts and responses back here and we will continue to help you before this consult! You’ve got this coach, trust yourself!

title: Meeting people and telling them I am a life coach – with flyers?
question:
I have been working through the 2k process for about 4 months now. I have had 0 clients but have definitely developed skills and confidence. I know my day will come!

I’m comfortable on social and video but have not figured out in person yet.

My biggest challenge is meeting people and telling them I am a life coach.

I coach moms and my kids’ activities are filled with other moms. I get out of my comfort zone (natural introvert) to meet them and talk to them but I don’t seem to find the space to mention what I do and how I can help them.

I have a ballgame coming up and I would like to share what I have to offer with others.

I chat, ask about their day, their life but coaching doesn’t seem to come up naturally. It makes me uncomfortable to try to force it so I don’t.

I had this idea to offer free coaching sessions for Mother’s Day. My tentative plan is to pass out flyers for this at the game to invite them to experience a coaching session. This may spark a conversation about how coaching can help them.

I was excited for this plan but then I got in my own head and now I have doubts.

My thought is if I don’t have the flyers or something to give them, I won’t be able to show them how I can help them.

I feel like I am using the flyers as a crutch but at the same time, I am super excited to share what I do and this will for sure help.

Any advice is greatly appreciated!
answer:
Hey coach!

I love how much intention is behind this. You’re not just trying to “get clients”- you’re actually thinking about how to connect, how to serve, how to do this in a way that feels like you. I can also feel the tension you’re in between wanting it to feel natural and also wanting something to lean on so you don’t miss the opportunity. So let’s slowly look at all of this together.

What actually feels like you when you picture yourself at that game?
 The version of you who genuinely enjoys talking to other moms and knows the value of what she does.
 Is she forcing coaching into the conversation, or is she letting conversations be conversations and trusting that the right openings will come?
 And if they don’t, is that actually a problem or just your brain telling you that you “should” have made something happen?

I don’t think the flyers are the issue. It’s the meaning you’re giving them. Could they be a crutch? Maybe. Could they also be a fun, light, low-pressure way to share something you’re excited about? Also yes. What if you had them, but only handed them out when it actually felt aligned? When a conversation naturally opens up or when you genuinely want to offer something to someone? Think of whatever you hand out as a “bridge” that still feels like you. Even something like a simple business card with a QR code to book a free Mother’s Day session could feel more natural. Or posting them somewhere if that’s allowed. Or even just saying, 
“Hey, I’m offering something special for moms this month, do you mind if I give you one of my cards in case you hear of any moms that could use some coaching support?”
 It can be as simple as you’d like it to be.

Another two questions to ask yourself are:

When you think about the value of what you do, how do you want to show up in that space?

Do you want to be someone who waits for the perfect moment, or someone who gently creates it? And if you want to gently create it from an unattached place, what comes to mind?

Also, there isn’t a right answer here. But I imagine there is a version of you who can feel grounded, proud, and open about what she offers without forcing it – it’s just a matter of asking yourself what that could potentially look like.

Feel free to come back with any of your thoughts or anything that surfaced from the questions. We are happy to help!

title: What’s working – the momentum is building
question:
Things that are working. I’m creating momentum. People are reaching out.

I have a consultation next week. I had several people this weekend talk to me after an event and say they need this work. I invited them to a consultation.

What I’d like to do now is pick a topic, write the emails, record the podcast, and do the class each month on that topic. These are the repeatable steps for me that create and maintain momentum.

The only snag in my thinking that I see pop up is when my brain is like,’I don’t know what to write.’ I’ve been answering that back with, ‘Let’s just write what worked last time.’ That redirects my brain.

I’m sticking with the topic from the event since it was so powerful and women shared so many experience.

THE MOMENTUM IS BUILT, and I’m so happy. Remember when I was thinking what I offer isn’t valuable? I have had SO many people over and over tell me how valuable the work is, and I know a big part of that is owning that and getting out there.
answer:
Hey Coach! You’re doing such great work! Awesome job on creating momentum and getting such great feedback.

So you’re noticing the thought,
’I don’t know what to write.’

It seems you’ve been able to course-correct really well but here are some other tips they may help.

What if you wrote down everything people are telling you and then build upon that?

As in, use their feedback to take each of your topics deeper and target what they are loving.

Or what if you wrote down 5 ideas for each topic and just see which one lights you up most?

Also, recycling anything that has worked in the past is also a great option to save time and re-use what has already worked or provided great value in between the moments where your brain feels a bit stuck!

Let us know if we can continue to help you in any way. Great work!

title: Follow up Believing I can help people / social anxiety
question:
Hi coach, thank you again for your answer.

My thoughts are :

I will never be able to make it

I am not learning (fast enough)

I am very negative today

lol

My feeling today is discouraged : so much effort for only one post !

But I did it and I think it’s quite good so I am glad.

I love the idea of willing to go first, it is always moving me forward. (Why do I need you to remind it to me ?)

I also love the idea that « I am practicing my social skills » because of course, I was afraid that my client would be disappointed by my answer (now I think he has a better reason to be disappointed because it took me so long to answer. It’s like I am disappointing him on purpose pffff)

To be kind and fair to myself, I could note that it is a specially explosive client who is having violence issues and the last time I coached him it was on « not killing people » :/ so maybe I am a little scared of an explosion.

Another thought is that you said both :

« The goal is to move your brain into a belief state that creates a slightly better feeling so you can take action from there. The minute you feel better you are in better energy to move better. »

And

« The work now is learning you can feel anxiety and still move. »

I am totally aware that two different things can be true at the same time and I see very well what you mean.

The problem is that I tend to force myself to move when I feel anxiety, because « it’s how we do it » and it creates pressure and paralyses me. I didn’t discover yet the place where I can first prepare myself to be able to do it with anxiety.

Nourish myself first.

And when I am too anxious I am also « not wanting » to self coach.

Well, I am learning.

I love when you are saying that I am closer than I think but it’s hard to believe.

I choose to trust you.

Thank you again.
answer:
Hey Coach,

The first thing I want to celebrate is how open you are to new perspectives.  
As I read your response, I notice how many times you say things like, “I love that idea,” “I love this perspective,” and “I choose to trust you.” What I see is someone operating from a growth mindset, not a fixed mindset.

The next step is learning how to find evidence for those new beliefs.

You mentioned that you love the thought, “I am closer than I think,” but you also shared several thoughts that pull you in the opposite direction. This is where your brain’s bias comes in. Right now, it seems very practiced at looking for evidence of how far you have to go, how much longer it will take, and what you’re not doing fast enough.

What would happen if you intentionally started looking for evidence that you are closer than you think? 
I’m asking because whatever your brain is trained to look for, it will find.

Let’s make the case for it:

You felt discouraged and still completed the post.

You were afraid your client might be disappointed and still answered him.

You offered yourself some compassion by acknowledging that this is a particularly challenging client.

What other evidence exists?

The goal isn’t to convince yourself of something that isn’t true. The goal is to become equally skilled at seeing what is already true but often overlooked.

You also asked why you need reminders about “willing to go first.” 
Because you’re human and learning and we all need reminders especially when training our brain to go in different direction.

Your clients need reminders too. They often know what to do, but knowing and practicing are two different things. Repetition is how we build new pathways. It isn’t evidence that you’re failing. It’s evidence that you’re human.

What we’re aiming for as coaches with ourselves and clients  is a little more understanding, a little more compassion, a little more willingness. 
I think you’re already practicing this more than you realize.

The fact that you completed the post despite feeling discouraged is evidence.

The fact that you answered this client despite being scared of his reaction is evidence.

The fact that you’re examining your mind with this much honesty is evidence.

One day, a client is going to sit across from you and say, “I’m putting in so much effort and getting so little return.” And you’ll know exactly how to help them because you’ve lived it.

You’ll be able to show them that in the beginning, effort is often high and results are small. Not because it isn’t working, but because they’re building the capacity required for future results. 
That’s what I see you doing.

Keep practicing being open, curious, patient, and kind with yourself. 
The better you get at doing that with you, the more naturally you’ll be able to do it with others.

And from where I sit, you really are closer than you think. How can you keep directing yourself to find evidence of that and not just trust us but truly trust you are on the right path Coach,  closer than you think!

title: 06/02/2026 – question about the CTA module
question:
Hi coaches,

I have a question today about the CTA module. Stacey talks about giving value first, waiting for them to “opt in,” then making a CTA.

Most of my CTA’s are currently made in my podcast at the end of each episode, just a friendly invitation to a consult if the episode resonated and they want more curated help, or I’ll make that same offer at networking events.

I’m wondering if I can uplevel that system somehow.

I know that some people talk about trust funnels; you start with a space where free value lives and there may be a CTA in that space to a free training, masterclass, or very low ticket offer (maybe less than $100), if they say yes then they have “opted in” and from there you can make CTA’s for a paid offer.

I don’t think I have a system like this at all.

As of right now I meet people organically in networking events or having coffee chats after meeting on the internet.

I will refer them to my podcast, or maybe my personal instagram account (which I haven’t really posted to in years), or my Linkedin (which is brand new and doesn’t have any posts), and that’s the end of the line.

& even if people are opting in to listen to my podcast I don’t necessarily feel like I’m “catching” them or giving them a space where they can come in and have conversations with me if they want to do that.

But I guess I don’t really know where to start. What do you suggest?
answer:
Hey Coach,

What stood out to me as I read your question is that you already have a CTA.

You mentioned that at the end of your podcast you invite listeners to book a consult ” just a friendly invitation to a consult if the episode resonated and they want more curated help, or I’ll make that same offer at networking events.”

So before assuming you need a completely different funnel or system, I would spend some time evaluating what is currently happening. Be as specific as possible.

What’s working?

What’s not working?

What specifically are you hoping an “upleveled” system would solve?

The reason I ask is because sometimes we jump to building something new before we’ve fully understood the problem we’re trying to solve.

I also noticed the thought, “I don’t really know where to start.”

Is that actually true?

Or does that thought keep you from taking the next obvious step?

Not in a judgmental way just from a place of curiosity.

Sometimes confusion can feel safer than testing. If we stay in “I don’t know,” we don’t have to risk finding out what works, what doesn’t work, or hearing feedback we weren’t expecting.

I’d also get curious about your consult offer itself. 
What are all the reasons someone would want to book a consult with you? What do they walk away with after spending that time with you? What problem does the consult solve for them?

The clearer you are about the value of that conversation, the easier it becomes to create invitations that feel compelling rather than simply informational. You can get better at doing the one thing vs trying a bunch of things and switching a bunch of things, what if it could be the one thing you are doing but clearer with more conviction.

I’m also curious about what happens after you meet people.

You mentioned directing them to your podcast, Instagram, or LinkedIn, but then described that as “the end of the line.”

What’s happening in those conversations that has you sending them there instead of inviting them to a call?

What are they saying?

What questions are they asking?

The answers to those questions will give you valuable information.

Are they interested but not ready?

Are they confused about what you do?

Are they unclear on how you can help?

Understanding where people are stopping is often more useful than immediately building another step in the funnel.

The other thing I’d offer is not to underestimate the power of repetition. Is it possible what you are doing is working it is just taking longer than you expect?

There are countless ways to create CTAs. The goal isn’t finding the perfect one. The goal is being willing to test, refine, learn, and improve.

You’re learning how to articulate the value of working with you. That’s a skill. 
And skills are developed through practice, not through thinking about them.

I actually think you already have several ideas what to do next what comes up for you when you think about taking the next steps to the ideas you have to focus on?

So if you believed you knew enough to take the next step, where would you start?

What would you test first?

What action would you take if you trusted that even if it didn’t work, it would teach you something valuable? 
I don’t think your challenge is a lack of ideas. 
I think your opportunity is becoming willing to test them.

You learn far more from doing than from trying to think your way to certainty.

And sometimes the best marketing strategy is simply deciding on a direction, taking action, gathering information, and adjusting as you go. 
What sounds easiest, most natural, and most fun for you to try next?

I’d suggest start there and be willing to figure out the rest along the way. Great job creating all these opportunities coach!

title: Help attracting consults
question:
I was thinking that it would be amazing to have three to five consultations a month.

And then I decided to look at my thoughts.

Business has been slow.

I just resigned 1 old client into my new offer for embodiment & Breathwork.

But I haven’t had a consult in months or a new client.

And tonight I wrote down my thoughts about consults.

No one wants to work with me.

People don’t understand what I do.

I’m not clear on what I do.

And these two thoughts below brought up feelings when I was listing out my thoughts.

T: Consults are hard to come by for me.

f: victim, like I’m being punished and signaled out by the universe.

action:, don’t make cta’s, waiver on my offer, change my messaging, change the name of my consult.

Results: no consults booked

T: i can’t get people interested in working with me anymore.

Feeling: defeated.

Action: is post then disappear, Post in half belief energy, worry about marketing instead of actually marketing, don’t have strong ctas, don’t email my list as much.

Result: no one is inquiring, no one is booking calls.

I would love help this month changing my thoughts and having consults booked.
answer:
Hey Coach!

Thanks for bringing such great models here. What I see is that you’re not confused about what’s happening in your mind. You see the direct line from thought to feeling to action to result and did a great job. What stands out to me first is how believable your current thoughts feel to you. 
“Consults are hard to come by” and “I can’t get people interested anymore”
 aren’t just thoughts you’re observing. They’re thoughts you’re 
currently living and taking action from
.
 So when you say you want more consults, but those are the sentences running in the background, your actions make complete sense. You soften your messaging, you hesitate on CTAs, you pull back.

In saying this, nothing has gone wrong here. You’re just being consistent with what you’re currently believing – so let’s coach on it.

Instead of jumping straight to “how do I get consults,” let’s slow it down. 
When you think about your work, your embodiment and breathwork, and the actual transformation you help people create… what do you genuinely believe about that?

Not what your fear is saying but what 
you
 know from your experience. I don’t see a lack of strategy here – 
I just see a disconnect between what you know is valuable and what you’re letting yourself stand behind consistently.

From there, I would get very intentional about how you want to show up this month. It doesn’t need to be perfect or in constant high belief. 
But consistently.

What would it look like to keep posting, keep inviting, keep making clear CTAs EVEN ON the days your brain is louder?

Can you decide ahead of time how often you’re going to email, how often you’re going to invite people into consults, and then follow through so you actually have data to work with?

I want to bring you back to something simple but important… Consults aren’t something that just “come to” you. They are created. Through your repetition, clarity, visibility, and invitations. 
So if you were to shift from “why aren’t they coming” to “how am I actively creating opportunities for them to book,” what changes in how you show up this week?

Take some time to sit with these questions, see what else comes up, and come back if we can further help coach you!

We are happy to do so. Thanks Coach!

title: Income producing belief (part one) Social anxiety
question:
Regarding social anxiety, I think it helps me if label it that way, because I make it mean that I can change it. I used to think it was my personality. Now it is just a problem I am busy resolving.

And you are right, accepting the anxiety as normal is the way to change it.

I can see the other side of it, since I already made offers and had clients, but I did sabotage some relations and opportunities, and it would be familiar to continue that way : I am in the middle, in the river of misery.

Learning to feel anxiety is my job right now. And it’s a solid one because I hate it and I am hyper sensitive, but I already did an amazing job at supporting my nervous system with posting on social media, I can bridge the rest of the gap.

Thoughts that will support me :

Every anxious feeling while interacting with a human is a step on the way to learn safety and ease

The more I am able to feel anxiety, the more pleasure I will get from interacting with humans
answer:
Hello Coach,

This is such great work. The shift from “this is my personality” to “this is something I’m learning to work through” is everything. That alone puts you back in the driver’s seat. And your willingness to feel anxiety instead of avoid it that’s the work.

You’re already onto something powerful with the thoughts you created. Now the next step is strengthening them so they don’t just sound good, but actually move you.

When you think, “Every anxious feeling is a step toward safety and ease,” how do you feel? I’m asking because the feeling that thought creates will determine what you do next. If it creates willingness or even a little courage, that’s what will get you to keep engaging instead of pulling back.

And when you think, “The more I feel anxiety, the more pleasure I’ll have in connection,” what does that make you want to do? we’re building thoughts that compel action. Thoughts that make you 
want
 to step into the very thing that used to feel like a threat.

You mentioned being in the “river of misery,” and I actually think that’s an honest place but it’s also a familiar one. So I want you to look at this: what thoughts keep you there? Not to judge them, but to see them clearly. Because once you can see them, you can decide if you want to keep practicing them.

Let’s  get specific, because this is where your power is.

When you meet someone, how do you feel?
And what are the exact thoughts creating that feeling?

When you tell someone you’re a coach, what comes up?
Again what are the thoughts driving that?

And when you make an offer, what changes?
What are you making it mean in that moment?

I’m asking you this because anxiety isn’t random. It’s coming from very practiced thinking. And when you map it out, you stop being at the mercy of it you start understanding it.

Also, we don’t wait for clients to come find you. That keeps you passive and reinforces the anxiety. Your job is to go into the world, have conversations, create value, and let people know you can help them. That’s where the growth is.

If you’re willing to feel anxiety while doing that, there is nothing you won’t be able to do.

This isn’t just about social anxiety. You’re building emotional resilience. The kind that will support you in every conversation, every offer, every part of your business and life.

You’re not just “in the middle” you’re in the practice. And the more you lean into it, the less power anxiety has, and the more freedom you create. Keep going your clients are waiting to see you do it so they can believe they can do scary things too!

title: Making Offers
question: What’s the most effective way to make a good offer to attract paying clients?
answer:
Hey Coach,

This is such a great question—and I’m really happy to help you solve this together.

First, let’s ground this in the formula Stacey teaches: 
Value creates clients.
So before we even get into “how to make a good offer,” I want to ask you a really thought-provoking question to get your brain working 
for
 you here:

What do you think your ideal clients truly value?
What do they believe would be worth paying you to solve?

I’m asking this on purpose, because your brain will want to jump to “what should I offer,” but the real work is understanding what 
they
 see as valuable. That’s where effective offers come from.

A “Good” offer starts with 
your belief
 and the compelling energy behind it.

Your belief in: yourself, your product, and your client.

So let’s look at that more closely:

What thoughts do you have about your offer?
What thoughts do you have about 
you
?
What thoughts do you have about your clients?

These questions matter because they will either strengthen or weaken your offer before you even say a word. If you’re not fully behind it, your client will feel that.

The offers that convert, the ones clients are willing to pay for, are the ones you believe in and present in a way where they can see the value 
ahead of time
. They don’t need to be convinced they already want it.

So when you think about your offer this way, what comes up for you?

Is there any hesitation, doubt, or “negative thoughts” showing up?
That’s useful awareness, because that’s the exact place to do the work.

I also want to point you back to the modules on 
Making Offers
 and 
Beliefs
, because this is where those concepts really come together. The skill of making offers isn’t just strategy it’s thinking + belief + communication. And there’s a great podcast I recommend you tap into here:

Episode 7: 4 Things You Are Always Selling

It will help you see that you’re always selling your offer, your belief, your energy and that’s what makes something compelling.

Offers themselves aren’t inherently good or effective. The way you think and demonstrate the vlaue.  And that’s a skill you’re in the right room to master it.

So I want to leave you with this to bring it all together:

What have you tried so far?
And what are you currently believing about your offer?

title: Day 25 / 30 – “he took it from me”
question:
When feeling hesitancy / flustered / bracing I’m making that mean I’m a mess, I’m an embarrassment, I don’t know what I’m doing, or I’m pathetic.

A lot of times I talk about how I need to stop feeling sorry for myself. & you’re right, it is true that I’ve had a hard couple years. I left a place that felt deeply safe and nurturing to me along with my sovereignty, I entered into a relationship that became coercively abusive and almost a year after leaving that relationship I still don’t feel like myself. It feels like he took something from me, like he sucked the spark out of me. & then I feel dramatic for thinking that at all. I think this relates to what you said about “you’re talking about confidence like it went somewhere without your permission.” I think I HAVE been believing that, that he took it from me.

I always try to remember that the thought line is typically verified in the result line. So if I’m really resonating with the thought that he took something from me, my spark, then I will find evidence to verify that.

& frankly a lot of the things I mentioned before, these are all things that my ex would say to me when we were together. He would tell me I wasn’t a good representation of my work, I didn’t have much to show for my efforts, that my concerns made me pathetic, all while spitting angry. Then the next day would become a completely different person who was supportive and encouraging.

I’m not trying to dump my traumas here I’m just seeing that this voice might not be my own. I think it’s his, even though I left him almost a year ago I am still letting him exist in my brain, controlling my actions and my belief in myself.

Before he and I got together I was the most confident I’d ever been. I would think things like, “I really like who I am, I’ve put in a lot of work, I’ve changed, I’ve become a better person, I like who I’ve become, I am more myself now than I’ve ever been before, I’ve lived a really cool and inspiring life so far, I have a lot to offer.” He would refute these things when I said them, even in front of other people.

I think I’m making my family’s thoughts mean I’m a burden, I’m not someone to be proud of anymore. When I interact with them I’m quiet, then I feel rejected, like I don’t belong. If I believed my audience was already here, I would show up happy to engage.

If I were showing up differently…. I’m struggling to answer that for some reason. Maybe I’ll have more when I sleep on it.
answer:
Hello coach,

Here is the truth and I want to start with both honesty and compassion. You are in the messy middle. The place where you 
do
 see yourself, you 
do
 believe in who you are at your core, and that’s exactly why this feels so uncomfortable. Part of you knows you’re capable, and another part of you is stuck in these well-practiced thought loops that don’t match that version of you.

That doesn’t mean anything has gone wrong. It means you’re in the work.

You shared something really important you’re starting to see that the way you’re talking to yourself now sounds a lot like what you were told in that relationship.

If you can see that these thoughts were learned and then you reinforced, you can also start to question them instead of automatically believing them.

Your brain is doing what brains do it’s replaying what it practiced. That relationship gave those thoughts repetition, emotion, intensity… so now they feel very true. But something feeling true doesn’t make it true. This is where your work becomes very clear, even if it’s not easy.

You’re going to have to start seeing your brain as unreliable in these moments, specifically when it’s offering you painful, disempowering stories that keep you stuck.

A thought you can try on Stacey shared this week is perfect to open this up a little.  “My brain is not a reliable source of truth especially when it feels like crap.” Not because your brain is broken, but because it’s trying to keep you in what it knows even if what it knows hurts you.

You said, “It feels like he took something from me.” I’m going to challenge that not to dismiss your experience, but to give you your power back.

He didn’t take it. You gave your power away in that dynamic. And that is actually the best news you could have… because if you gave it away, you can take it back. You don’t need him or anyone else to return it to you. But that requires a decision.

What would you need to believe about yourself to start taking your identity back?  Because identity isn’t something you go find again. It’s something you decide and then practice into.

You already showed me who you are. The version of you who thought: “I like who I am. I’ve done the work. I have a lot to offer.” That didn’t disappear. You stopped practicing those thoughts, and started practicing different ones.

So now the work is simple but it will require a level of mind management that feels uncomfortable at first. You will have to believe on purpose before you see evidence.

And again, I want to be really honest with you here self-pity will keep you stuck. You’ve had a hard couple of years. That’s real. And you can have compassion for that without using it as a reason to stay in a story that keeps you small.

Self-pity feels terrible, and it also keeps your focus on what happened to you instead of what you’re going to create now. And those lead to very different lives.

So instead of asking “Why do I feel this way?”
Start asking: What am I choosing to believe right now, and what is it creating? Because you already know what you look for is what you will find, and then create more of.

If you keep believing “he took my spark,” your brain will keep proving that true. So let’s redirect it.

Where is your spark already showing up, even just a little?
I’m asking because your brain needs direction. If you don’t give it one, it will default to the past.

Even you being here, what I see is someone asking to do this, doing this work that is evidence. That is not someone who has lost herself. That is someone who is actively fighting for herself.

The same thing is happening with your family. You’re quiet, and then you make that mean you’re a burden or you don’t belong.

But what if we questioned that? If you believed “I belong here, even when I’m quiet,” how would you show up? You stop letting your past define your identity, and you start deciding it on purpose.

Are you willing to decide who you are now, and practice believing it even before there’s evidence?

Because that’s the work. That’s what you will ask your clients to do too. You will ask them to believe in you , in coaching , in themselves without evidence.

You don’t need anyone to give your power back. You just have to stop leaving it in the past.

So I’ll leave you with this Coach, Who do you want to be now?
And what would she choose to think, starting today? What is different about her? Imagine how she shows up and start doing that today.

title: Support with Visibility Triggers on Social Media PART 2
question:
Here is my response:

To be seen on social media it means to be vulnerable and knowing there will be people who will not agree with you and will have their own comments/remarks. As I am writing this, I am noticing that it is definitely a fear of being seen. “If I stay small, people won’t notice me and they won’t make fun of me”

When I create videos, I find myself criticizing how I look. I’ll say let me put some makeup on. I am getting better at this though lol Also, with what I am communicating to my audience on what I do and my beliefs I tend to say “Ooh I know this will trigger people.”

Reason why I feel triggered when seen are:

1. People will judge me and say mean things to me.

When people disagree or challenge me, I get tense and I try to snap out of it and say “that’s their opinion.” But I notice I am trying too hard to think that. My brain tries to protect me.

As a child, I was bullied by other kids. So I know this has a lot to do with it.
answer:
Hey Coach,

Here’s something great – you’re already noticing that this isn’t really about makeup, lighting, social media strategy, or saying the “right” thing. What has happened is your brain has connected “visibility” with “emotional risk.” And that makes a lot of sense to me if you were bullied growing up 
(and I am sorry that happened to you).

When children are repeatedly criticized, judged, excluded, or made fun of, their nervous system learns that visibility can feel unsafe. So now as an adult, your brain tries to protect you the best way it knows how: 
“If I stay smaller, quieter, safer, less visible… maybe I can avoid being hurt.”

Another important observation from your submission is that your brain is treating disagreement almost as “danger”. You mentioned thinking, “I know this will trigger people,” and then feeling tense when people challenge or disagree with you. 
I’d get really curious there.
 What meaning is your brain making out of disagreement? Does disagreement mean you’re wrong? Rejected? Unsafe? Unlikeable? Just remember you may have to tell your adult brain (after childhood bullying) that people having opinions about your content does not automatically mean you are “in danger.”

If you are building a visible business, there is probably no version where every single person agrees with you, likes you, understands you, or resonates with your message. I am sure you know this logically but again, your brain is fighting hard to keep you safe. So I don’t know that the goal is becoming a person who “never gets triggered.” Being triggered is actually okay. I think the goal is becoming a woman who can stay
 connected to herself 
even when
 discomfort arises. Who creates safety inside of herself.
 That may also look like finding ways to nurture your inner child self each time these emotions pop up in your adult body.

I’d be curious if part of the work here is allowing yourself to stop viewing visibility only through the lens of potential criticism and starting to 
see the other side of it too
! Visibility also creates connection, opportunity, CLIENTS, impact, and resonance. The women who will feel deeply understood by you
 cannot find you
 if you are hiding from the possibility that someone else may not approve.

I think it’s important to remember your adult self does not have to remain emotionally governed by what happened to you as a child. Sometimes we as adults have to remind ourselves that we can give ourselves the love, support, and nurturing we craved when we were in those hard situations and big feelings as children. Don’t forget that is always available within you… but…. anytime it’s a struggle, we are happy to help you here in AAC as much as we can. You’re doing amazing things in building your coaching business! Keep going! There are clients who need exactly who you are and what you offer.

Thanks coach!

title: The Who / the how Q&A
question:
Q : What would working look like this week?

A : This is an excellent question, I rarely ask it, usually I just « do » without a plan. Working would be like sitting at a desk and writing, and for that I need to be able to feel boredom and anxiety and doubt. Working would be feeling the feelings and writing.  Q : What are the actions you believe create value?

A : First reflex : oh god, I have NO idea.  …Posting on social creates value. Making connections creates value. Sharing what I think creates value. Making offers creates value and possibly money.

Q : What are the things you can do that put that value in front of people?

A : I just made a procrastination bingo, I think it’s great I am gonna post it on socials. I am gonna offer some workshops too.

The Who that I want to be, the fool and the poet, the one who is open, curious, compassionate, and playful doesn’t seem to get what value is.

When I ask myself these questions : What value can I create? How can I communicate it? How can I get it in front of more people?

My brain goes directly to the How and forgets about The Who. We think there is a proper way to do business and I try to figure it out.

The Who is just writing inspiring poetry without making any offer. And specially not thinking about money.

But : I am shutting down a facebook group that was not « working » and I invited everybody from the group on my public page. I want to speak in front of more people. I’ll see if it works. One of my bingo thought is « What’s the point ? ». I noticed it and I did it anyway.  I find that this fight against my brain is exhausting. It was supposed to get easier and easier and I don’t think it is. After some years, posting is still challenging and hard. I think that coaching myself for half a day in order to write a post is not sustainable. Even if it is a bold move to close this group,( it is hard to let down 2500 people), I can hardly refrain myself to think « this should be easier ». Which is a super unproductive though, let’s face it. I know it shouldn’t, but I am still struggling to get out of « it’s not working ».

Can you help me again please ?
answer:
Hello Coach,

Yes, absolutely we can help you dismantle this sticky thought.

And remember, these thoughts are sticky for a reason. Your brain likes to keep you safe. In the moment, “What’s the point?” and “It’s not working” feel logical, safe, and predictable. Your primitive brain believes this is the best way to protect you.

The challenge is that if you keep starting from what you don’t believe, you will keep ending up feeling hopeless, discouraged, and stuck.

I want you to take yourself to a place of what you do believe first.From a more elevated place, changing your belief and problem solving coach identity. How do you help others change a negative thought loop?

What do you believe about yourself that explains why you have not quit?

I’m asking because I think your brain is overlooking some important evidence.
What do you agree is already working?

Ignoring the thoughts that say it isn’t working, where do you already have proof that you can do this?

You noticed the thought “What’s the point?” and did it anyway. That was brave.

I think sometimes we are so focused on what isn’t happening yet that we stop giving ourselves credit for what is.

You said working would look like sitting down, feeling boredom, anxiety, and doubt, and writing anyway. 
I think that’s exactly it!  
Working isn’t getting rid of boredom first.

Working isn’t coaching yourself for half a day until you feel motivated. 
Working is feeling boredom, anxiety, doubt, uncertainty, and writing anyway.

What if nothing has gone wrong?

What if this is what building a business looks like?

I also don’t know that posting is supposed to get easy. Why do you think is it supposed to get easy?  What makes it hard?  Overthinking maybe causing added suffering to the action.  But posting is nto inherently hard. What you tell yourself will make it hard.

I think we tell ourselves that if we’ve done something enough times it should stop feeling uncomfortable. 
But why?

Posting requires visibility. 
Visibility often creates vulnerability. 
Your brain may continue offering thoughts to protect you from that. Arguing with the reality will make you struggle.

Is the goal isn’t getting rid of those thoughts then what ?

The goal is learning not to obey them.

Instead of fighting “What’s the point?” or “It’s not working,” what if you got curious? 
What is the point?

What is the point of posting?

What is the point of sharing your work?

What is the point of helping people?

What is the point of becoming someone who keeps going before the results arrive?

Don’t leave the question unanswered. Decide the point you want to make otherwise brain will offer the path of least resistance , old stcky thoughts.

I also want to gently challenge this sentence:

“I am struggling to get out of it’s not working.” 
Maybe.

But you also don’t have to keep rehearsing that thought.

You can notice it and decide not to participate.

“I notice I’m thinking it’s not working.”

“I notice I’m thinking what’s the point.”

And then continue. 
No fighting with your brain today. 
Just noticing and continuing and not struggling.

You might even try thoughts like:

“I’m learning what works and what doesn’t, and I can adjust.”

“I am capable of taking small steps that add up.”

“I notice I’m thinking it’s not working, and that’s okay.”

“I can keep going even when I don’t have evidence yet.”

Then bring yourself back to useful questions:

How can I meet someone today?

How can I add value today?

How can I put my work in front of one more person today?

If I believed this was working, what would I do next?

Because at the end of the day, I think the real work is becoming the person who continues when their brain says stop.

Who are you when you do it even when you don’t feel like it?

Who are you when you keep showing up before the evidence arrives?

And when you figure that out, you’ll be able to help your clients do the exact same thing when their brain tells them, “It’s not working” and “What’s the point?”

Keep poking holes in the disbelief. 
And keep going coach!

title: My buyer confusion?
question: I teach how to attract high end clients – that’s my offer attract your first (or next) high end client. Where I meet people is based on who I can serve. Yes, I can serve everyone but this is the rub. I’ve chosen to meet entrepreneurs wanting to attract high end clients. I like this because it’s the work I do too! However, I’m noticing that my buyer are high end, but not particularly wanting to sell to high end clients. That’s fine but if my buyers are mostly not wanting to sell to high end clients, then it impacts how I talk to them on IG. My last two buyers do not know me from IG. But other consults I’ve created all know me from IG. I write my copy to those interested in what I offer (attract high end clients). But being that most of my all time buyers are not interested in this if I should change my copy to “make money” My clients come to me because I treat them all as the high end clients that they are and with white glove service. I love this level of hospitality. But maybe my buyers only come to me for this, but don’t want to learn how I do it for themselves. They come to me because how I make them feel. But my goal is 6 clients in 12 months (I’m at 2 clients on payments – so grateful for them!) Maybe I should change my result/offer to “feel luxurious and make money!” I treat my clients like royalty!
answer:
Hey Coach,

First, I want to acknowledge you for really thinking about who you help and how you help them. One thing I hear clearly is that you love treating your clients like royalty! I love this!  You love creating a white-glove experience, and I actually think that’s something worth talking about more in your marketing. For the right client, hearing that level of care and hospitality creates a feeling of, “Yes, she’s my coach.” That feeling matters.

As I was reading your question, what I became most curious about was not whether you should change your offer, but what is happening for you when you start thinking you should change it. When you think, “Maybe I should change my result” or “Maybe I should change my offer,” what feeling does that create for you? Does it create confusion, uncertainty, doubt, or something else? I ask because the feeling behind the thought often drives the actions we take next.  Does it create a desire to figure out what result you most want to deliver and figure out how to explain it in ways that call your best clients in?

When you’re thinking about changing your offer, how does that impact your messaging? What do you start saying? What do you stop saying? What becomes harder to communicate? Who are you being when you’re questioning the result you help people create? The reason I ask is because sometimes the issue isn’t the offer itself. Sometimes it’s our relationship with the offer. When we’re feeling certain, we show up very differently than when we’re questioning ourselves. Conviction, energy sells the offer, feeling inspired to coach on it all day long.

I’m also curious about what evidence you’re using to conclude that your messaging should change. Are clients actually telling you they want “feel luxurious and make money,” or are you noticing that some of the people who hire you aren’t specifically interested in learning how to attract high-end clients? Those are two very different things. Just because someone hires you for one reason doesn’t necessarily mean they aren’t interested in the result you help create.

Another thing I would explore is whether you’re making this decision based on who you’ve worked with in the past or based on who you most want to work with moving forward. Those are not always the same audience. Sometimes when we’re looking backward at past buyers, we unintentionally start building our future around them instead of around the people we most want to serve.

You mentioned that where you meet people is based on who you can serve. I agree with that. At the same time, I believe some of the strongest offers are built around what you genuinely love helping people do. If you could coach one topic every day for the next few years, what would you want it to be? Attracting high-end clients? Creating a luxury client experience? Making money? Something else? I think that answer is important because there is a difference between what attracts people to you and what you most love helping them create.

I’m also curious why it matters that clients come to you because of how you make them feel “but may not want to learn how to create that same experience themselves”

Is teaching hospitality and white-glove service important to you? Or is your real passion helping people attract and serve great clients, regardless of how they do it?

I ask because understanding what is most important to you helps clarify whether this is actually an offer issue or simply a marketing message issue.

As I read your question, I’m not yet convinced the problem is the offer. I think we may need to get more specific about the problem you’re trying to solve.

Is the issue that you’re not attracting enough consults? What do  you think is happening are you meeting people and they are not not interested?

Is it that consults aren’t converting? Why?

Is it that you’re attracting people who aren’t your ideal clients? What is your theory?

Is it that you’re questioning whether your offer is what people really want? Why? Those are very different problems, and each one would require a different solution.

Before making any changes, I’d love for you to explore your beliefs around this.

What are your top three thoughts about yourself as a coach right now?

What are your top three thoughts about the value of your work?

What are your top three thoughts about people’s desire to work with you?

And what are your top three thoughts about your offer?

Often when we think we have a messaging problem or an offer problem, what we discover underneath is a belief problem. The thoughts we’re thinking about ourselves, our work, and our clients will always influence how we market, sell, and show up. Lets dig into your current beliefs and then we can compare to what you need to be thinking to create the result you want.

Bring your answers back to AAC and we can coach more deeply on what’s coming up.

title: Day 17 / 30 – courageous action
question:
What does “I’m not ready yet” actually give me in this moment?

That thought actually gives me anxiety, it makes me feel restless but also frozen. It makes me feel like there is still something that needs to be done before I can push forward. & to solve for that my brain came up with the “wait until Monday then go all in” scenario as a solution which then causes relief. Because now I can plan all these other things my brain thinks I need to accomplish before I go all in.

Do I want to keep choosing relief, or do I want to start choosing expansion even when it feels uncomfortable? If I were already the version of me who is “ready” what would she do today?

I absolutely want to choose expansion, I am so tired of being in this place of “I’m almost there.” That is actually worth noting. The way I’ve respond when people ask me how things are going the last couple years has been “it’s been a really hard few years but I can feel that things are going to change soon.” & of course nothing really changes. I just keep spinning in that thought..

So if I don’t wait, if I overcome the noise, if I am already the version of me who is “ready,” I would record and hit post. I can feel my mind wanting to barter with that as well – “we’ll just post something simple, the way we’ve always done, better something than nothing.” I feel similar thoughts around making connections with new people or reconnecting with people from my past. I can make a list of people but the thought is “when we connect I won’t talk about what I do, I’ll just enjoy human connection. Better something than nothing.” But I want to challenge myself on those thoughts too because I know the resistance is coming from the idea of trying something different and potentially feeling awkward or icky.

& to do something different I would need to believe that I can handle whatever comes after I take that action, whether that’s getting more attention / sales or realizing I need to tweak my efforts and try something different in the future.
answer:
Hey coach,

You’re not just in this cycle you’re actually watching it happen in real time, and that matters more than you think. What you’re noticing is that the thought 
“I’m not ready yet”, 
 It’s creating anxiety, and then that anxiety becomes the reason you use to give yourself permission that you don’t move forward. So it turns into a loop: you feel anxiety, your brain interprets that as “something isn’t done,” you delay, you create a plan like “Monday I’ll go all in,” and that gives you relief. But that relief is temporary and it keeps you in the same place. So it also gives you a way to avoid feeling.

So the real issue here isn’t the anxiety itself it’s the resistance to it. When you treat anxiety like something that has to go away before you act, you reinforce the belief that you can’t handle it. And I want to gently challenge that, because you’re already onto yourself here. You can see the pattern, which means you can choose differently within it. It also tells me you parts of you do believe you can handle it. That is why you keep coming back you know you could.

Let’s lay out what’s happening in a simple model so you can really see it clearly:

Unintentional Model:
C: “I’ll start Monday” / preparing to go all in
T: “I’m not ready yet” / “I can’t handle this”
F: Anxiety
A: Spinning, overplanning, perfecting, avoiding, staying in preparation mode, not fully putting yourself out there, keeping things safe or surface-level. avoid feeling,
R: You reinforce the belief that you can’t handle it and you stay in “almost there”

Now compare that to what it could look like if you shift the thought not to eliminate anxiety, but to change your relationship to it:

Intentional Model:
C: Same circumstance “I’ll start Monday” or the opportunity to show up now
T: “I can handle this”
F: Maybe still anxiety but also willingness or courage
A: You post, you share, you reach out, you allow it to be imperfect, you stop overpreparing, you feel the anxiety without letting it stop you
R: You build evidence that you can handle it and you start moving forward now not later

Notice the difference isn’t that anxiety disappears. It’s that you stop making it mean you have to wait.

So I want to ask you a question here, and this is important because it shifts where your power sits, what if the goal isn’t to get rid of the anxiety, but to become someone who can feel it and still move? Because if you can do that, then “ready” is no longer required.

You also said something really important this pattern of “I feel like things are going to change soon.” it keeps you in that “almost there” identity.

Let’s take it one step further. If you were already the version of you who is “ready” and not the version who feels no fear, but the version who trusts herself to handle what comes after what would she believe about anxiety? I’m asking this because your actions will always follow that belief. Would she see anxiety as a stop sign, or as part of the process? And from that place, what would she actually do today?  Would she still wait until Monday, or would she record and post anyway?
