What are you actually trying to avoid feeling if you show up differently? Awkwardness, exposure, judgment, maybe even success and visibility? Once you name the feeling, you can decide if you’re willing to feel it. Are you wiling ?

Expansion isn’t just about taking action, it’s about expanding your capacity to feel. You said it yourself,  to do something different, you would need to believe you can handle whatever comes after. So let’s ground that 
how is it already true that you can handle it?
 Not hypothetically, but based on your life. You’ve handled hard things before. This isn’t about capability, it’s about willingness.

Nothing has gone wrong here. You’re human, and anxiety is part of the experience. The real trap is the second layer the moment you interpret anxiety as a reason to stop.

So in real time, this can look like noticing the spiral without rushing to override it. You pause, take a breath, and remind yourself, “This is a fear loop.” And then you anchor into something like, 
“I can be uncomfortable and still move,” or “I can handle what comes after this
.” From there, you act not because you feel ready, but because you’ve decided readiness isn’t the requirement anymore.

Do you want to keep choosing relief, or do you want to start building evidence that you can handle expansion? Because courage doesn’t feel good it feels exposed, uncertain, and a little messy. But it also moves your life forward. And right now, you’re right at that edge.

F grounded/ supported / secure / held

A: Take care of myself in large and small ways (body/mind/spirit). Take a breath and pause when I’m stressed or get in my head. Remember what’s important. Connect daily with my dreams and take action to create them. Bold action. Inspired action. Kind action. Make offers to well-matched clients, and say no to those who aren’t well-matched. Say no to “busy and misaligned opportunities”. Work hard and watch my energy, when I’m tired, refill my cup. Coach my clients with love and caring (and a little sparkle). Be bold in my asks and celebrate my boldness. I allow myself to want what I want without apology

R: I parent and care for myself. I feel supported and resilient.
answer:
Hi Coach,

Yes. I agree the identity piece is where you want to start. The “who” before the “how.” 
Because before the strategy, the offers, the podcast, the clients, or the income, there’s the coach creating all of it. The deeper work is not just what you do, it’s who you are being while you do it.

That’s why I wouldn’t rush past these models. The most important part isn’t just the actions listed underneath them. It’s the identity underneath the actions.

“I am the coach who no longer abandons myself.” 
That sentence alone changes everything.

Because a woman abandoning herself and a woman parenting herself may technically do some of the same tasks, but the energy behind them is completely different.
 One is performing from pressure, fear, proving, and depletion. The other is creating from grounded belief, self-trust, care, and intention.

When I read your model, I noticed how much your future identity already understands energy management, alignment, and sustainability. She isn’t just working harder. She’s protecting herself differently. She remembers what matters. She refills her cup. She says no to misaligned opportunities. She allows herself to want what she wants without apology.

Because I imagine the version of you with the fully booked practice and waitlist spends far less time obsessing over what isn’t working and far more time getting her work into the world. There’s less hesitation and more “this matters, let’s share it.” Less energy drain. Less self-abandonment in the form of overthinking, second-guessing, and emotional exhaustion.

The identity of the $500k coach isn’t just someone making more money. She thinks differently, feels differently, and therefore acts differently.

And becoming that version of yourself is uncomfortable. Massive growth usually is, brain will want to pull back and find familiar feelings at the expense of your dreams and goals.

When you want a result you don’t yet have, it’s often because there’s a version of you that still needs to be developed emotionally, mentally, and energetically in order to hold it. Not because you’re incapable but because growth requires becoming someone new.

So I’d get really curious here:

What does the version of you who already has this business believe about herself?

What does she think when she sits down to record a podcast episode?

How does she think about the value of her work?

How does she respond when discomfort shows up?

Because those questions help expose the gap between your current conditioning and your future identity. Not to judge yourself  but to build awareness.

I also think it’s important to notice that your model already includes resilience.  
“The woman who shows up graciously even when things are uncomfortable.” 
That’s different than white-knuckling your way through growth.

You’re describing someone who can feel discomfort without making it mean she’s failing. Someone who can stay connected to herself while building something big. That’s powerful.

I’d spend time visualizing her. Not just the results she has, but the way she moves through an ordinary day.

How does she care for herself?

How does she make decisions?

What does she no longer waste energy on?

What thoughts does she practice repeatedly?

How does she recover when doubt shows up?

Because identity work is repetition. You become her by practicing her. 
And one of the fastest ways to create a new result is to stop rehearsing the identity that created the old one.

So if you fully believed this was possible not only possible, but inevitable  what would your actions look like?

What would you stop doing?

What would you finally allow yourself to do boldly in your podcast, offers, and celebrations?

I think your model already points to the answer. Great Job Coach!

title: Energy of 2k Today – separating the value I give from when the results arrive pt 3
question:
I recently wrote in and asked for help understanding the energy of 2k today, given that I have had a YT video that I posted in 2024 produce consultations in 2026. I am working on separating the idea of giving daily value from the idea of getting immediate results, without removing the possibility of being paid today.

Here, I’m responding to the question from Ask a Coach:

From here, let’s work on something else you said: “I do want to create results in the short term and I don’t want to feel like nothing I do today will create a short-term result.”

Something you could also evaluate (if you haven’t already) are your CTAs on what you put out into the world.

For example:

1. Do you give your audience a clear CTA so they know how to act on the value they see? 2. Do they see links to book consults, sign up for freebies, join an email list? 3. Do you make it easy for them to enter your world after they’ve received value?

I like to think of our CTAs as inviting them into our world as coaches… and remembering that people don’t often let themselves in without a clear invitation. If you’re already doing this well, we can explore more ways to create the results you’re seeking in the short term.

My Response:

1. Right now after delivering the main piece of value I say “this is the type of work I do with my clients” (and maybe I elaborate a bit) then I say “if you want to learn more about becoming a client your next step is to book a consultation at the link below. A consultation is a free hour long session where we get to know each other and decide whether working together is the right next step.”

2. Yes, so on my YouTube videos I always verbally mention a related freebie and say that I’ll link it in the description, and I give the consult invitation that I wrote out above. The freebies are being downloaded and consults are being booked even if not always in the timeframe I would like.

3. I do. I always cross-reference my other platforms (so on YT I always mention my podcast, on my podcast I frequently mention my YT channel), and I take the step above of always having a relevant freebie for each YT video. I also email my YT videos and podcast episodes out to my list whenever they come out.

These are all practices I put in place within the last 4-6 months so I am open to the idea that results will take time, but since we are talking about the idea of creating results in the short term I will say that I AM doing these things and I’m NOT seeing quick results.
answer:
Hi Coach,

Thanks for sharing what you are doing! It is great that you are cross-referencing ways for your audience to stay connected to you and offering CTAs any chance you get!

What I’d like to focus on from here is your final sentence:
 “I AM doing these things and I’m NOT seeing quick results.”

1. What does your brain make it mean when you put out a CTA and you do not see “quick” results?

2. On a scale of 1-10, what is your belief in making “2k today” … 10 being full belief it’ll happen today, 1 being not so confident it’ll happen? Where do you notice yourself falling
 most
 once you’ve posted & attached a CTA?

Lastly, in your CTA actions I noted that you do really well inviting them to a consult or to other freebies, do you also 
directly invite them to buy?
 How often would you say they have the opportunity 
to buy
 a service you offer? Do they have to do a consult with you first?

Take some time to answer these and then bring your answers back here so we can continue coaching! In the meantime, great work on showing up and being consistent with the CTAs!

title: 05/21/2026 | who will I be when I’m fully booked?
question:
Hi coaches,

It’s me again, obsessively stalking you all in AAC lol

I am here for the hard coaching today. The main result I have been focused on lately is becoming fully booked (signing 12 clients), and even smaller is just getting really good at generating consults. I’d say I’m making progress because this month I’ve had 3 consults even though they were 2 no’s and a no show.

This morning I felt so inspired, I recorded 2 podcast episodes back to back (have I mentioned I have a podcast?), & I made really powerful offers in both episodes, I was in full belief and was thinking “this is exactly the type of energy that would get me to book a consult with someone.”

Pre-recording these episodes felt productive in the moment toward my desired results, but I started second-guessing after that.

“Was this actually a client / consult generating activity? Should I have spent that time doing something different? These episodes don’t go out today, they go out on May 25 & June 1 so do they really count as creating consults / clients today?”

Then I started second-guessing the consults I got this month (2 people who seemed interested in my offer but also seemed more interested in selling ME their marketing services). “Did they actually book because they are interested or because they wanted to sell to me?”

Then I started ruminating on how I could be taking action to create my own networking event and immediately thought “it’s Thursday, I’ll just wait and go all in on creating the event and finding more consult generating activities on Monday,” which made me feel relief (but I know is really holding me in inaction).

I did a model where the result is “generating consults consistently with a fully booked practice,” and I know I will be feeling inspired, confident, and creative when that happens. I know I’ll be living in breakthrough and sharing from inspiration like I did this morning.

I just keep getting in my head about client generating activities. Is it networking events, social media, podcasting – my brain wants to say give up on socials entirely because it really hasn’t resulted in consults in the months I was consistent with it. But I also wasn’t in the state of inspiration I keep finding myself in now. I want to start posting on Instagram but feel hesitant. Is this all just about trial and error?

I feel myself getting in my own way. I feel periods of inspiration then I put out my own fire. I know what I feel inspired to do but then I just don’t do it.
answer:
Hey Coach,

Let’s do the “hard coaching” you said you are here for today.

First, let’s challenge the way your brain is defining “client-generating activities.” A client-generating activity is any action that has the potential to generate a client. It can truly be that simple. You recording 2 podcast episodes today absolutely counts. Especially because you said yourself that you were in belief, making powerful offers, and speaking from inspiration. Just because those episodes release on May 25th and June 1st does not suddenly make them “non-productive.” Those episodes now exist as assets that can generate interest, questions, consults, referrals, and clients long after today. The same goes for social media posts, networking, events, emails, conversations, consults, and relationships you build over time.

Your brain keeps wanting immediate proof that every action “worked” before it allows you to trust the action but entrepreneurship does not work that way. Much of business is cumulative. Every post, episode, consult, conversation, offer, and connection adds to the 
“value bank”
 over time. You do not always know which thing will lead someone to book. Sometimes it’s a podcast episode from 4 months ago. Sometimes it’s seeing you consistently show up. Sometimes it’s one consult after hearing you speak for weeks.

I’d like to lovingly point out how quickly your brain invalidates evidence. You had 3 consults this month and immediately started questioning whether they “counted” because two people wanted to sell you marketing services. But the fact remains… they booked consults. That is evidence that your actions ARE creating movement and visibility. Your brain keeps “moving the finish line” so it can play in rumination vs. commitment.

Now let’s address “Monday energy.” “I’ll start Monday.” “I’ll go all in Monday.”

This often comes from wanting relief… and sometimes that relief is sneakily disguised under avoidance of other uncomfortable emotions you’d feel by following through now vs. pushing it off.

What is actually happening is not really confusion about client-generating activities. I bet you often know exactly what you feel inspired to do. The harder part is 
tolerating the uncertainty that comes after taking the action.
 Your brain wants certainty that the effort will work before fully committing to it. But we as entrepreneurs cannot wait for guaranteed outcomes
 before
 showing up. That’s the challenging part about what we’ve committed to in our line of work.

Your job right now isn’t to perfectly identify the “magical activity” that guarantees clients but to consistently put yourself in rooms, conversations, content, offers, and spaces where clients can find you. Repeatedly. Long enough for momentum to build!

What do you think, coach?

title: Part 4…
question:
OK, I guess I think I “shouldn’t” be failing b/c I should be better, more skilled, by now. For the amount of time and money I have put in, the belief models, the actions, the dreams, the prayers…it is hard not to be sad and discouraged that I am where I am. Again, goes back to “I’m not good enough.” Is that a thought anyone can ever really be done with? My brain always goes to that.

If failure is omission of necessary action, it feels better. It focuses on the action instead of WHO I am…My brain goes to all the action I HAVE taken, but I can look and see that it must take way more than I thought. Which isn’t a problem I guess, unless I make it one. I could say that I could definitely do more action than I have. Truthfully, I think it has “felt” like I have taken more action than I have b/c I have wasted a lot of time overthinking and in confusion. If that time had been spent on activities that were to move my business forward, I definitely believe I would be further along.

I like the thought of “I’m learning” and I wish I was a faster learner too!! 🙂

I see you are right that hating where I am won’t help me create where I want to go…and I do need to clean up my thinking about my results.

So, something like this? I am learning what it takes to get to where I want to be? If I were to have compassion for my current stage, I could get there if I think that I haven’t figured out what was necessary to get my desired result yet…but I will. I am figuring it out. I am also building a stronger foundation, b/c I truly don’t believe I can get to where I want to go with some of the ways I was doing things before. I can say that truthfully.

As far as using past workshops as data, I can definitely do that too. I want to offer another workshop or webinar this month, even though I have past evidence that didn’t go how I wanted. I wanted to see about maybe doing a “launch” from it to get more clients. I am always offering a free consult call, but again, I am not getting takers on that as much as I hoped. I was thinking I should watch Stacey’s webinars to see how she runs hers and learn how to make a more powerful CTA? I think my whole thing needs improving, more notice ahead of time, and more selling afterward. Those are all things I could improve on.

One more thing for clarity…how do I know when it’s appropriate to make an offer? Any time someone shares something I help with? I have some fears around selling too hard in normal conversation…
answer:
Hey Coach,

First, I want to acknowledge the amount of awareness you’ve gained through exploring this. What I notice is that you’re starting to separate where you are from who you are, and that’s a really important shift. Not making this personal increases your ability to learn from everything!

When your brain goes to “I’m not good enough,” notice that there is nowhere useful to go from that thought. It doesn’t create clarity. It doesn’t create action. It doesn’t create learning. It just creates pain.

And your brain probably goes there because it’s an old story that has felt true for a long time and has successfully stopped you in the past. But just because a thought is familiar doesn’t mean it’s useful.

Sometimes when my brain offers me a thought like that, I don’t argue with it. I simply notice it.

“Oh, there’s that old story again.”

I think it’s worth asking: What does “not good enough” even mean? How would you measure it? Compared to whom?

The reason I ask is because most people never define it. They just feel it. And when we don’t define it, it becomes impossible to disprove.

I also want to speak to your expectation of how long this would take.

It is incredibly common to underestimate what it takes to build something you’ve never built before. But how could you accurately know what it would take if you’ve never done it?

I’m curious: What was your expectation based on?

If you told me you drive from Montana to Maine every year and it normally takes 20 hours but now it’s taking 40, we’d want to investigate. But building a business isn’t like following a route you’ve already driven. You’re creating the map as you go.

What I hear you recognizing now is that some of what felt like action was actually overthinking, confusion, and trying to figure everything out before moving.

That’s valuable data.

Not because it means you failed.

Because now you know something you didn’t know before.

In fact, imagine helping a future client avoid years of overthinking because you’ve lived through it yourself. That lesson may end up being part of the value you bring.

I really like the thoughts you came up with:

“I am learning what it takes to get where I want to go.”

“I haven’t figured out everything that is necessary yet, but I will.”

“I am building a stronger foundation.”

Those feel honest. They don’t deny reality, but they also don’t make your current results mean something about your worth.

Regarding the webinar and CTA, I think you’re asking some good questions.

Instead of immediately assuming your CTA is the problem, I’d get curious.

What else might people need to hear, know, understand, or believe before they are ready to take the next step?

What concerns or questions might they still have after attending?

What would make saying yes feel easier?

Sometimes the issue isn’t the CTA. Sometimes people simply need more exposure to the offer, more trust, more clarity, or more follow-up.

As for your question about when it’s appropriate to make an offer, I think we need to define what “appropriate” means to you.

When you say you’re afraid of selling too hard, what specifically are you afraid will happen?

What would an inappropriate offer look like?

And what would an appropriate offer look like?

The reason I ask is because many coaches have an unexamined belief that offering help is pushy. But offering help and pressuring someone are two very different things.

My best guess is that you already know the difference.

An offer is simply an invitation.

Pressure happens when we make it mean someone should say yes.

So tell me more about what “appropriate” means to you.

What is your best guess about when it is appropriate to make an offer? 
I think your answer to that question will tell us a lot.

Love your idea to watch Stacey sell on webinars also incredible time to watch how she selling in all the different platforms and how powerful, compelling and interesting the CTA’s are.  She is modeling it all for us everyday in every offer!

title: Income producing belief (part one) Models
question:
Dear coach,

Thank you very much for this substantial and so helpful feedback.

I didn’t realize I am only working on the intellectual part of beliefs, a little inefficiently. I am not (yet) working on them « in real time », not applying them nor confronting them with reality.

I was just writing some believable belief on a sheet of paper and asking myself why they were true, I was not trying to create reality from them. It is a step further and I love it.

I just realize, I am such a brainy and sensitive person, maybe I need to spend more time in the feelings and less in the thoughts. That’s a huge takeaway.  You asked why I think the value I’m listing isn’t fully clicking, and I think it is why. I am just thinking it and not feeling it enough. Not embodying and then not incorporating.

The two models you asked me to fill gave some surprising results today. They make sense though.

That’s what they gave me when I did one after the other :

C- Figuring out how to make money as a life coach

T- I don’t have value

F- Low

A- Hiding, staying at home with my cat, fearing contact with others, specially with messages, not showing up on socials, not meeting people, doing my stuff only for myself, not showing my work, feeling comfortable, indulging in low emotion, not challenging the belief, not trying to prove it wrong, being in my own world and not risking the judgement of others

R-I don’t see my value, people can’t see my value, I’m wasting my value

C- Same

T- I have value

F- Pressure

A- Telling myself « I have to » do something with it, remembering all the times people call me genius and ask « why don’t you do something with all your gifts ? », shouldn’t myself, being strict with myself, not being compassionate or loving toward myself, stepping into confusion « what does value even mean », doubting, blurring the message « I don’t even know what value is »

R- result is unclear because the thought « I have value » is not mine today…. I don’t think my value is enough ?

I make it hard to believe in my value ?

I devalue my value ?

Here again, I seems that not wanting to believe that I have value is protecting from interacting with others. Protecting me from the feeling of anxiety.

My brain doesn’t want to go (yet) to the thought « I have value » and imagine how I would behave.

It’s screaming « DON’T GO THERE ! IT IS DANGEROUS, don’t offer something ! People may want it and we don’t know how to deal with people ! »
answer:
Hey coach,

You’re very welcome, and we love hearing how you are not just receiving the coaching, notice how you are applying it! You’re not just understanding the coaching, you’re starting to catch yourself in the moment where it actually matters. You are very aware of what is actually getting in your way, always a negative thought or feeling you are unwilling to feel.

Right now, the real issue isn’t just the thought  “I don’t feel my value.” It’s that your brain is using that thought to protect you from something it believes is more dangerous interacting with people, being seen, and feeling anxiety. So of course “I have value” feels like pressure, because your brain immediately takes it to “now I have to go out there and deal with all of that.” Very different than desire to go out there and share from desire, want to vs pressure of have to.

So let’s go there on purpose.

What do you think is the worst-case scenario if you allow the anxiety to be there, you show up with your value, and people actually want it?

I’m asking this because your brain is yelling “this is dangerous,” but it’s being vague. When we slow it down and get specific, we can actually see what it thinks you won’t be able to handle.

What do you think you would need to “deal with” when it comes to people?

Let’s really flush that out. Is it judgment? Rejection? Not knowing what to say? Having expectations on you? Getting it wrong?
Your brain is acting like there’s something on the other side of this that you are not equipped for.

So then the more useful question becomes, who would you need to become to handle those things?

Because this is where your power is. If you believe you can handle anxiety, rejection, confusion, or even success then none of it is actually a problem. It’s just an experience.

Right now, anxiety isn’t the problem it’s the signal your brain is using to keep you in the familiar. The sentences sound like: “don’t go there,” “it’s dangerous,” “don’t offer.” That’s not truth. that’s protection. You are right, feeling on purpose is the work for you here.

So what would you need to tell yourself instead, on purpose?

Maybe it’s:
“I can handle any emotion.”
“Anxiety is not dangerous.”
“It’s safe to feel pressure.”
“I can figure out how to deal with people.”

Not to force belief but to give your brain somewhere new to go.

And I’m curious what comes up when you stop trying to control or avoid the anxiety, and instead allow it to be there?

Because the goal isn’t to feel confident first. The goal is to expand your capacity to feel what you’re currently avoiding.

What do you think is the best-case scenario if you feel the anxiety and you handle the people?

And zooming out for a moment what if you didn’t hide from the value you have to offer?

What if the focus wasn’t “how do I feel?” but “who could I help?”

Because one thing I know to be true when you step into serving, you step out of suffering. Not because the feelings disappear, but because your focus shifts from protecting yourself to contributing.

So I want you to notice this how much are you currently suffering by hiding, staying small, and indulging the low emotions your brain offers?

And the what if you allowed all of it? The anxiety, the pressure, the uncertainty.

Who would you become if you did that?

We’re here to support you in that process. You don’t have to get rid of anxiety you just have to stop making it mean you can’t move.

So if anxiety comes up (and it will), how do you want to plan for it?

title: This is what I want coaching on.
question:
Love your last coaching on part 2. That was great.

This is where I am: I’m at the crossroads of – I’m creating the momentum, and the scales are going to tip in value any moment. AND when will the scales tip?

Essentially, if I am in belief, addressing life at the higher level of thinking, at what point should I evaluate differently or make shift?

Here’s my reasoning: Nothing is going to stop me from creating new beliefs, choosing my responses, evaluating from a High value cycle, being the leader and the coach.

The actions that follow that formula under that mindset include: posting insights, making offers, emailing my list, providing trainings for free as value ahead of time, meeting people, and introducing self.

I believe the scales will tip, I’ve created momentum, and at the same time want to ensure I’m putting my efforts and actions that are most productive.

When I think that I feel empowerment and clear. I put value out and write my ideas and put in action.

At this level of mindset, I did believe I’d create 3-clients a month. Without entitlement, I’m curious when the consults will appear.

In the meantime, I’m going for the same outcome this month with what I learned and lived so far:

3-5 consults, 3 signed clients at $2000 for the package. Excellent classes presented with planning, rehearsal, in service to the entire audience, using those clips to share.

I’d like to believe I can create 5 clients a month, up to 15 a week.

Just now a thought came up, so we can address this to (I’ll also coach myself): What if I’m selfish to want that much, so I should only go for one client or lower my price.) Got it. I’ll get to work. I’d also love your coaching.
answer:
Hey Coach!

First off, I love how self-aware you are and how great you do at catching your brain. You’re thinking like a leader, you’re coaching yourself in real time, and your belief is clean. That matters more than you probably realize because this is the part most people don’t stay consistent in. I can feel that you’re all in on becoming the coach who creates the result, not just hoping for it, and that’s exactly the energy that builds momentum.

The piece I want to layer in is a little more structure around what you’re already doing so your belief has something tangible to build on. Keep everything you’re doing mentally, and alongside that, start tracking a few simple things each week. How many posts did you make, and how many of those actually included an offer? What were you offering? How many direct invitations to a consult did you make? How many emails went out with a clear opportunity to work with you?

This isn’t about pressure or proving anything… it’s just giving you some visibility into what’s actually happening behind the scenes. And my input would be 
not
 to check this every day or make it mean anything about you. Don’t let this be something your brain uses as a distraction or something to be hyper-focused on. Think of it as a 
weekly or every other week
 check-in where you step back and look at the numbers with the same grounded mindset you already have. You’re simply asking, is there enough volume and clarity here for the result I want, and if not, where do I want to gently increase or refine?
 Your belief work stays steady, this just helps direct your effort.

On the thought about wanting more clients being selfish, keep coaching yourself exactly like you are. You caught it quickly, you didn’t spiral, and you redirected. That’s the most important work we can do. When your brain says wanting more clients is selfish, 
what is it actually trying to protect you from? 
Is it that you’re worried about taking too much, being too much, being seen differently, or creating a level of responsibility that feels bigger than what you’ve held before?

There’s usually something underneath that thought that has nothing to do with money or clients and everything to do with identity and safety. If we look at this cleanly, wanting more clients means 
wanting to serve more people
, 
practice your craft more, and create more impact.
 The only way it becomes “selfish” is if your brain is tying your desire to something like greed, pressure, or losing connection to people. Get really honest about what you think changes about you if you actually have five clients, or ten, or more. Who do you become in your mind, and is that version of you someone you trust?

From there, you get to decide on purpose what you make it mean. You can make wanting more clients mean you’re building something meaningful, that you’re expanding your capacity to support others, and/or that you’re allowing your work to reach the people who need it. That’s a very different internal experience than quietly holding yourself back because a part of you thinks there’s a limit to how much you’re allowed to want. The fact that you caught that thought so quickly tells me your awareness is strong – and kudos to you for that! This is just about going one layer deeper and deciding intentionally what kind of woman you are as you grow,
 instead of letting this unintentional thought set the ceiling for you.

What do you think?

title: Belief Triangle
question: I’ve been diving into ITC, which has brought up some beliefs that are truly not helpful. I need to figure out if my conflict/struggle with my niche/people is because of my belief in them (or me) or a lack of desire to help them. Full transparency, I am in 200k and the peer coaching left me more frustrated, so I thought I’d bring it here under the belief triangle. I do have 100% belief in my modality. 100% belief I’m good at what I do. Less belief in my coaching abilities because it’s a newer skill. I’m 100% confident 1:1 has success and is most likely a necessary entry point, but I really love teaching to a group. My niche is sign language interpreters. I don’t have much interest in interpreting right now. I’m not “in” it. But I do believe I can still help interpreters- I have this belief that because I left the US, set up my work virtually before zoom was a thing that I can’t help terps who are still working in person and in the US. Also becaue I currently don’t love interpreting. I used to, it was my life but I burned out. In the past, I didn’t have many interpreter friends. I didn’t hang out with them. I don’t like going to our conventions. And some of this dislike of my community fires up when I’m marketing/offering/talking to them. I get annoyed. And then I meet such amazing humans who are these bad ass, incredibly smart people others don’t understand. I do. Sure, there are jerks in our field (there is a reputation of tearing each other down and being rabidly critical and mean) but do I want to work with them? Do I feel passionate about helping them( the bad ass one?)? Yes. Do I think they need what I teach and coach on? YES. Do I believe they want to change and will invest in themselves? This one, and thinking they are gonna come after me for doing something wrong, is a huge obstacle. I can find evidence to the contrary, but will this become a sustainable business on a few who pay me what they think is a huge amount, but isn’t enugh. . Oh, and there is another one that they aren’t interested in or believe in what I offer. I do have proof of the opposite. Today, I was told it sounded like it was a pragmatic choice to have this niche, and I’m not passionate. I’m not sure. Desire might be hiding under the negativity. Desire might be afraid to show herself fully cuz it might be crazy thinking. without getting past those beliefs it doesn’t matter what niche I have. I have to know how to move myself through this.
answer:
HI Coach,

I’m really glad you brought this here, this is exactly the kind of work that matters, because you’re not actually stuck on your niche, you’re in a relationship with your thoughts about your niche. And that’s what we want to look at. You are igniting your resourcefulness, ECM is the best place for the ITC work is on fire this month and so happy 200K is the place to learn the skills of scaling 1:1 to group.

For context are you creating consults and what is working there? The way Stacey teaches is the easiest way to fill group is with with your thinking like you share ” I love groups” AND with demand for consults, closing them and filling your spots, all what we work on here.

I want to start with what you said: “I need to figure out if this is belief or lack of desire.” I actually don’t think those are separate for you right now. I think your desire is there, but it’s getting covered up by the way you’re currently thinking about them.

You already showed me that. You can clearly see the “bad ass, incredibly smart humans” and you light up there. That matters. That tells me desire exists. But then your brain offers you a different story, about criticism, about being attacked, about them not investing and notice what that does. It pulls you out of connection and into protection.

So instead of asking, “Do I have desire?” I want to redirect you slightly:
What happens to your desire when you think those thoughts about them?
Because this helps you see that it’s not the niche removing desire it’s the thinking.

Let’s look at it from another angle.
You said you’re unsure if you really want to help them. I want to understand what actually compels you.

What do they struggle with that you deeply understand better than most?
I’m asking this because clarity here naturally builds desire. When you’re connected to their real problem, you stop focusing on whether they’ll judge you and start focusing on how you can help.

And then this:
Why do you want to help the “bad ass ones”?
That distinction you made is important. It shows you’re not trying to help everyone you’re drawn to a specific type of person. There’s something there. When your “why” is clean and specific, it becomes much easier to market, to invite, and to stay in the room.

Right now, your brain is also offering you a lot of future-based fear:
“They won’t invest.”
“They’ll come after me.”
“This won’t be sustainable.”

So I want to ground you back in something more useful to direct your focus.

What evidence do you already have that they do want this and will invest?
You mentioned you have proof of the opposite, your brain is currently filtering that out. We want to intentionally bring it back in so you can make decisions from a more complete picture, not just fear.

And I also want to gently challenge this thought about not being “in” interpreting anymore.

Why does not currently loving interpreting mean you can’t help interpreters?
Sometimes distance actually creates clarity. You’re no longer inside the noise, you can see patterns, problems, and solutions more cleanly. That could be a strength, not a disqualifier.

Another place to look:

What are you currently avoiding when it comes to showing up and meeting them?
Because often what we call a “niche problem” is actually an avoidance pattern driven by uncomfortable thoughts. This question helps you see where the real work is.

And finally, I want you to consider this, 
If you fully believed there were 100 interpreters already looking for exactly what you offer… how would you show up differently today?
This question matters because it exposes the gap between your current actions and the actions you’d take if belief felt solid. That gap is your work.

Right now, nothing is wrong with your niche. What’s creating the friction is the mix of admiration, judgment, fear, and doubt you’re holding about them, all at the same time. That’s exhausting, and it will always dampen desire.

Your work isn’t to find the “perfect” niche.
It’s to clean up your relationship with the one you’ve chosen so you can show up in belief, clarity, and leadership.

You don’t need to feel 100% certain.
But you do need to be willing to see that your thoughts are shaping your experience here and that’s something you can work with.

Bring back what you notice here Coach as you sit with these.

title: I feel like quitting- II
question:
First of all, thank you. That was very helpful.

What are your top three theories for why you’re not selling right now? I don’t fully believe that people will pay that price for my program. I’m focusing on whether or not they will see the value. I’m being really hard on myself.

What happened for you when you made that decision? Why did you make the increase? I increased it because I was looking at how much it cost to get a client with ads, running the program, and other things i added to the program and made that decision.

What did you start thinking about your membership, your clients, and your ability to sell it after the increase? Why? I started to think things like is this still a no-brainer? If I kept the old program and charged this amount, would I think that people would think this is the best deal ever? And i found myself answering i don’t know. And i felt like i had to add more things to justify the price. I went into selling thinking I had to convince people now. Whereas before I thought it was the best deal out there.

So I want to explore this with you:

What are you making all of these “no’s” mean about you? That they don’t want this, it’s not good, it’s too expensive, they don’t see the value, it’s not unique enough, I’m not doing enough, I don’t understand why they don’t want this, what am i doing wrong

Why don’t you want to quit?Because I really believe this is what I’m called to do and people really need this help!

If you were already consistently selling this program at 5K What would be different about how you think, feel, and show up? I would be more confident in sharing how my program can really transform their lives and be more curious about their objections like how can you not want this amazing thing tell me more. I wouldn’t have that feeling of needing to justify or convince anyone. I would feel like the prize. Like this is my very special private club, and there’s a long line and everyone is just so hyped to get in

What are your current thoughts about selling at 3K? This is a no-brainer; This is so good, this is a steal, this is the best deal, it’s your loss if you don’t join

And what are your current thoughts about selling at 5K? Am I providing enough to justify this price? Should I add more? Will people see the value? I think they see the value. I think people will buy. I think it’s still an amazing deal. seems like more doubt creeped it.
answer:
Hi Coach,

You’ve already done something really important here you didn’t just say “I’m not selling,” you actually looked at how you’re thinking when you sell. Posing your own theory is so useful and you get the benefit of training your brain to solution focused thinking.

I want to slow this down and look at what’s really happening underneath your top theory: “I don’t fully believe people will pay that price.”
Why this matters is because that thought  shapes how you show up in every sales conversation.

So when you think that what do you notice about how you sell? Are you believing the price matters more than the value and the transformation they receive?
Do you lean in with certainty, or do you start explaining, adding, justifying?

I’m asking because you also said you went from “this is a no-brainer” to “I have to convince people.”
That shift alone will change your results.

Let’s look at the value piece, because your brain is making “they might not see the value” the problem.

It’s true people need to see value and it is our job to demonstrate it, that is the skill that develops the more you sell it.  But notice where your brain went: doubt, adding more, questioning the offer.

Where are you already demonstrating the value clearly?
And where are you assuming they won’t see it? Why?

How do you provide the value ahead for them to see it?

That question matters because there’s a difference between a value problem and a belief problem. Right now, this seems much more like belief.

You also made your pricing decision based on costs ads, delivery, what you added. Those are valid business reasons. But I want you to really look at this: If a client asked, “Why is this 5K?” would your answer feel compelling to them?
Or does it mostly make sense to you?

That distinction matters, because clients don’t buy based on your cost they buy based on the transformation they believe they’ll get.

Now let’s look at what changed after the increase.

Before: “This is the best deal ever.”

After: “Is this still a no-brainer? Do I need to add more?”

Same offer but Different thinking and believing .

So the real question becomes what created the “no-brainer” feeling before? Was it clients signing up and then deciding it was a no brainer or clients getting results and value?

Was it actually the price or was it your belief and you decided the value?

When you make the no’s mean “they don’t want this, it’s not good, I’m doing something wrong,” it makes sense you’d pull back or try to fix yourself mid-sale. That energy creates hesitation, and hesitation doesn’t sell transformation.

Now I want to connect this to something you said that’s really powerful. You don’t want to quit because you believe in this work.

If you were already selling this at 5K consistently, you said you would feel confident, curious, unattached like the prize.

What do you need to believe about your offer now to show up that way before the evidence comes? Because right now you’re waiting for sales to create belief.
But selling at 5K will require belief to come first.

Not “I hope they see the value,” but
“I know exactly why this is valuable, and I can help them see it too.”

Think of it like this At 3K, you’re offering something you feel certain about. At 5K, you’re offering something you’re still negotiating with yourself about. Clients can feel that difference.

So instead of asking, “Should I add more?”
I’d shift you to:

What is the actual transformation I help people create—and why is that worth 5K?
Where have I already seen this work?
How do I communicate that more clearly, more specifically, more tangibly?

That’s how you solve for value without diluting your offer.

And lastly, I want you to really sit with this: You already know how to sell this. You’ve done it at 3K with conviction. So this isn’t about learning how to sell again.
It’s about becoming the version of you who believes it at 5K.

Who is that version of you?
How does she think about her clients, her offer, and her role in the process?

Because you don’t become her after you sell at 5K.
You become her to sell at 5K.You got this Coach!

title: Day 22 / 30 – entrepreneur identity vs. coaching identity
question:
What is Stacey’s ECM Identity Series? I am not familiar with it.

I see what you’re saying about my coaching identity vs. my entrepreneur identity. I think where I feel the biggest disconnect between them is in my coaching relationships it requires a large deal of listening, observing, reflecting, asking good questions, etc. In marketing and content it feels like creating something out of thin air, there is no person to listen to or to observe. I feel like I’m PERFORMING rather than serving.

So I WANT to show up in the same way, it’s just that my brain is convinced I have to perform. But if my thoughts are the problem then I want to believe that it’s easy to show up in the same way, that it’s possible to show up in the same way, that it’s possible for me to show up as myself and in service.

Actually I just had a bit of an epiphany. I draw inspiration for content based on what I’M currently struggling with, what I’M currently learning. So if I’m showing up in service to anyone it’s me, not my potential clients.

Like I’m using my content as a way to solve my own problems without having completely solved them yet. I’m usually sharing my own breakthroughs, my own moments of realization, even if I’m not outwardly using that language – that’s still where the inspiration is drawn from. But it’s always in the energy of “I haven’t fully figured this out yet.”

Does that make sense? I leave my own setbacks and struggles at the door with my coaching clients, I am clean, I’m never worrying about myself on those calls. But in marketing and content I am the one who is still trying to figure something out. I’m not a coach worth investing in, I don’t “have the answers,” I’m someone in their process.

& I’m attaching meaning to it, I let insecurity creep in, I’m not convinced anyone should listen to what I’m saying or buy what I’m selling. It’s so funny that those insecurities don’t come up in my client calls at all. Like of course I can serve them, but then why am I so detached from that in my marketing?
answer:
Hey Coach,

The Identity Series is one of the foundational courses inside Stacey’s Entrepreneur Coach Membership, and it’s incredibly helpful for exactly what you’re working through. It walks you through building your identity 
on purpose 
not just as a coach, but as an entrepreneur who sells, markets, and leads. You can try ECM month-to-month, and I really do recommend it because this is the work inside of it.

Now, what you’re seeing about yourself here is so important. The difference you’re feeling isn’t actually about 
what
you’re doing it’s about 
how you’re thinking
 when you’re doing it. That is where all your power is, how you chose to think, feel and act while taking action.

You said that when you’re coaching, you leave your own struggles at the door and fully focus on your client. That’s why you feel clean, grounded, and in service.

What if marketing is the exact same skill? What if you decided to approach it the same way and focus on the client. When you focus on them you stop struggling with your fear to perform right.

Because right now your brain is offering you, “This is performance. I have to create something out of thin air.” And that thought immediately disconnects you from service. It puts the spotlight back on you. But in reality, nothing about marketing requires you to perform. It requires you to 
focus on value and serving.

Stacey teaches this in all of her work, especially in things like the Served course, that you can always think of one person. One real human. One struggle. And speak directly to them. The marketing to one person will help them think you speaking to them directly.

That’s what takes you out of performing and puts you back into serving.

Now, I want to go to the insight you had, because it’s a good one, but I’m going to gently challenge the meaning you made from it.

You said you’re often creating content from what you’re currently learning or working through, and that it feels like you’re solving your own problems, not serving your clients. That’s not a problem. That’s actually 
normal.

But here’s the distinction that matters:

Are you sharing it from “I’m still figuring this out, so who am I to say anything?” Why?

Or are you sharing it from “I’m in this work, I see this clearly, and I know someone else needs to hear this too”?

Notice you can offer the same content with completely different identity.

One is self-focused and creates insecurity.
The other is service-focused and creates connection.

You’re not disqualified because you’re in the process. Your clients don’t need someone who has a perfect life they need someone who can 
see
 and 
lead. 
And you already do that beautifully on your calls.

So the real work isn’t becoming someone new it’s borrowing the exact same thoughts you already have as a coach and bringing them into your marketing. That’s how you close the gap between those two identities.

Let me ask you a few questions to help you see this more clearly  and I’ll tell you why each one matters.

When you’re on a consult or a coaching call, how do you feel about the person in front of you?
(I’m asking because that feeling is what creates your presence and your ability to serve so powerfully.) For example curious, connection or understanding ?

What are you thinking that creates that feeling?
(This shows you the exact thoughts you can intentionally practice when you sit down to write or market.)

Now when you go to create content, what are you thinking about yourself?
(This is where the shift needs to happen. Not in your strategy, but in your self-concept in that moment.) When you catch those thoughts redirect your self back to curiosity, connection.

If you were fully booked, in demand, with clients signing up consistently… how would you think about your marketing? If you had a line of people engaging what would you be thinking?

What would feel urgent or important to say?
What would you 
want
 people to understand?

Because that version of you isn’t performing. She’s not wondering if she’s good enough. She’s thinking something more like:
“They need to hear this.”
“I know this will help someone.”
“I’m getting this out there.”

That’s the energy of service. You don’t have to hold it perfectly all the time but you can practice coming back to it. Over and over.

This is identity work. Not fixing yourself just noticing which thoughts put you in service, and choosing them more often.

You’re a lot closer to this than you think.

title: Day 18 / 30 – what if it doesn’t work?
question:
I like how you frame it here, that “readiness” is no longer necessary if you can feel anxiety and move anyway. I can see how that’s true. One of the things that gets kicked up in response to that is the question, “what if it isn’t working even though I’m putting myself out there and I can’t figure out why?”

Obviously if it’s working, I’ll know it. But how will I know what to do if it’s not? Like I’m putting myself out there, I’m talking about what I do, I’m posting, I’m making offers, etc. but still nothing changes? That feels a lot like a 10th step fear rather than a next step fear. & I can also recognize that, if I am believing I can handle whatever comes next then I am also believing I can handle that circumstance.

During the most courageous time of my life I used to affirm constantly, “when the fear passes will there be joy?” That was what I used to say when I was afraid to take the next scary step & it helped me take a lot of courageous action. That’s what this conversation is reminding me of.

I think I would see anxiety as part of the process rather than a sign to take pause. & becase of that I would continue moving forward, even if it was uncomfortable. & when I am avoiding showing up and posting through anxiety – I think I’m avoiding success. Because I don’t want to mishandle it like I did before.

I do want to note, yesterday I recorded and posted a Tiktok because of our conversation. I felt really clunky doing it, which is interesting because I haven’t felt clunky recording videos in months now. But I did it anyway and posted it. & I made an offer at the end of the video as well. I know there is a lot of room for improvement still but I’m glad that I did it anyway, and I plan to make another today and to continue doing that as well.

I don’t know if I mentioned this in previous messages but I also made free coaching offers to 3 past clients so I could practice a new technique I plan to use in my new long term packages. I start the first of those sessions today and I’m looking forward to it. I am taking action even though I am uncomfortable. The next uncomfortable thing I can feel myself avoiding is meeting new people.
answer:
Hi Coach!

I’m so excited to hear that you took action and recorded a TikTok even though it felt “clunky”! That is amazing. Over time I have no doubt it will begin to feel more “second nature.”

Something I remind myself about anxiety is that it’s just “energy” that needs to move. It’s anticipation of something… and wanting to control it. When we just allow that energy to “move” (by noticing it and then moving through it with action – like posting a TikTok), we don’t let the anxiety stay bottled up inside of us. We allow the true ebb and flow of human emotion without being controlled by it. And each time we do this, we build trust in our emotional capacity – so you’re doing amazing work here!

It’s also great that you made free coaching offers to 3 past clients and get to begin that today! Taking action through discomfort is the “game” of entrepreneurship. Even at Stacey’s level, she still has to do it too. Sometimes there can be comfort in knowing that every entrepreneur is out there doing this work – we aren’t alone in feeling the feelings.

You said, 
“The next uncomfortable thing I can feel myself avoiding is meeting new people.”

Not sure if this is helpful but when I think of “meeting new people” I think about 
all of the ways
 that is possible.

For example, each time you post a TikTok, you’re “meeting” new people. They may not make themselves known to you, but you’re reaching new people when you show up and post. This is true for every platform you may use. 
It’s kind of like, they meet you – you just don’t always get to meet them.

You also “meet” new people when you do podcasts (even as a guest) or market yourself on social media, or have past clients or friends refer you. Again, the people becoming aware of you may not make themselves known to you, but trust — they are watching, even silently, and getting to know you/your work. This is why our consistency matters and why we must show up… even when it feels clunky, uncomfortable, or “doesn’t seem to be working”.

This helps take off some of the “pressure” I think. Sometimes meeting people is just 
showing up where you can
 and consistently offering value, or sharing what you do. When you show up online, you’re meeting people (it’s just passively).

So then the next question becomes,
 “How do I want to meet people more actively? Do I want to? In what ways could I do that?”

And try not to overthink it. It may be sitting at a coffee shop working on your laptop, attending free meet ups or events locally, conferences, finding hobbies that cost little to nothing and allow you to connect, saying yes to opportunities to get out of the house just in case random conversations happen, a friend inviting you to meet another friend, etc.,

And as Stacey says, when meeting people it’s not with the intent to 
“get”.
 It’s with the intent to 
build genuine connection
 and to expand your network. When out in the world meeting people myself, I don’t put pressure on myself to tell them what I do in that conversation… I instead get to know them (even if it’s just 5 minutes) and make it a goal to try to 
stay connected
. For example, if I meet a stranger, I show up genuinely interested in them – even if we never talk about me or what I do for work.

At the end of the conversation
 (whether at an airport, a party, a restaurant bar, coffee shop, etc.,)
 I may ask if they have social media and would like to connect real quick before we part ways. Most say “yes”. Not always of course… there isn’t 
always
 the opportunity but that’s my goal. Then once connected on socials I engage with their posts so I stay visible in their feed and let them naturally get to know me over time on their own.

It’s really me asking myself, 
how can I expand my network with low pressure and trust that the value I offer will naturally bring people in?

My job once connections are made is to give them something to look at. That’s why we post and show up even when its “clunky”.

And here’s something big I hold on to. When you meet people, you’re not just meeting “them”. You are meeting them 
and their network.
 Because the reality is, each person you meet probably knows
 at least
 200 people 
or more
. When you meet them, you actually become connected to their network. They themselves may NEVER hire you for coaching – but they may know someone in their network of 200, 2000, or 20,000 that you’d be perfect for. This is why you build
 genuine connection with everyone
 (without “get” energy). Trust that even if they aren’t your person, they may know someone who is. And when you’ve been showing up as who you are in a clean, unattached way just providing value (that they are probably silently watching), you will be someone they can easily refer – especially if they never felt pressure to be your client just because you met them.

Thoughts? Hope this is helpful. Feel free to come back with any further coaching you may need!

Keep going coach, you’re doing amazing!

title: Plans for maternity leave
question:
Hi there, thanks for all your good coaching in the past! Something else I’m hoping to get some support on…

As I’ve shared, I’m pregnant, due in July, and taking off about 3 months from the business. I’ve got a plan for my current clients and how I’ll handle my time away with them, and something else I’m starting to consider is handling new clients who sign between now and the start of my leave (I’ve got a goal of 7 clients before July, I’m ITC’ing this all month!).

The plan: my coaching is a year long, helping moms write novels, and based on past experience, I believe my clients need at least 2 months of working with me before they get into the groove of writing. For consults in May/June, my plan is to delay their start until October (maternity leave July/Aug/Sept), because we wouldn’t have enough time to set them up for success with coaching/writing their novel without us meeting.

Why would they be willing to wait?

– people wait for editors and therapists, so it’s not unheard of

– they’ll understand my reasons for waiting (they are moms, and me having a baby and taking maternity leave would make sense)

– I would totally wait to start working 1:1 with Stacey, so it’s possible my potential clients view me in the same way and would be willing to wait

One area I’m a little stuck is whether I want to give them anything while I’m away on leave – not necessarily worksheets, but a few things to essentially tide them over. On the one hand, I don’t necessarily need to give them anything – some people would be fine waiting until October – but also, I want to help the clients who have signed up and are eager to make progress on their novel. I want to get them started, I want to help them believe in their novel, and I want to build excitement for us to work together. (There’s a little bit of fear that someone would lose belief/excitement over the summer and change their mind by October)

Some thoughts of what I could give them:

– questions to ask about their story foundation (work I normally do in the first couple sessions)

– story assessment questions, which gets them thinking more critically about their novel, which is a powerful skill for writers

– scheduled emails for voice notes from me to maintain connection

I’m wondering if this is too much to expect of me (since I’m 7 months pregnant and it’s a lot of prep) or if I’m coming from desperate energy – or if this would be a pleasant surprise and worth doing. Would love another perspective!
answer:
Hi Coach,

Glad the coaching has been helpful and congrats on baby coming soon!

Here is what I would ask:

1. Does adding some “pre-work” additions before the official October start date feel good to me?

2. Do I love the reasons I would add them?

3. Does it feel super supportive of the clients who would enroll and does it feel doable for me prior to maternity leave?

4. Does it feel like an energetic drain to create some extras? Does it feel like a healthy entrepreneurial “push” to create some added support for these clients waiting? Or does it absolutely feel like a buzzkill and desperate?

Just based on everything you shared, it could be a great “bonus” for them in their excitement AND it also isn’t necessary for the right clients. Both of those can be true – so I’d come back to how it feels. You also don’t have to create all of your ideas, you could choose 1-2 that feel most fun, aligned, and supportive of your clients.

You could ask,
 
“when I do begin with them in October, is there anything I might have wished they had done prior to our coaching to be the most ideal, prepared clients AND hit the ground running powerfully? What serves their success most and the outcomes I want for them?

If one or many of your ideas feels aligned with that question, it may be worth exploring and creating whatever comes from that answer!

Feel free to come back if you would like more coaching or need anything else, we would be happy to help!

title: Identity trouble
question:
Hi,

For the past year, I’ve been earning just enough month after month to pay my bills, and it’s very tiring. Most of my clients come through renewals and a little bit of communication.

Right now, I’m in a moment where I’m listening to my heart whispering to take my artistic practice more seriously again, and because of that, my identity as a coach feels more fragile, so I don’t communicate as much as I used to.

It has been very hard for me to reconcile the identity of the artist with the identity of the coach. They feel like two opposite identities that I’m trying hard to bring together. At the same time, I can see that in reality I’m a better coach when I’m also an artist, and I’m a better artist because I’m also a coach. But somehow, I still don’t find it “sexy” as an artist to also be a coach, haha. I don’t know if that makes sense?!

The context is that I have been an artist from my 3th to my 32, young, everybody was saying that I would be THE great actress you know, and it was soooo tight on my identity. Then I had such terrible life experienced that made me loose my instinct and confidence and so I didn’t had the carrier excpetcted and had a 12 years of depression. Life coaching helped me go out of that, and then I became a passionate coach. But my 3 years old inside child, that was all about art of dancing, playing, singing, all of this came back with force last years in my dreams, waking me up in tears, and I am sooo happy to listen to it and discover that everything is still there. But it’s hard to accept that I still have to be a coach, that I love that too, that it’s ok to do both.

I would love for you to challenge this way of thinking, because I see myself very reluctant to post on Instagram and make better money again, and to imagine a brilliant future while doing both.
answer:
Hello Coach,

Happy to help you out here! Let’s dig in.

I’m curious why your brain keeps positioning these identities as “opposites” when your own lived experience seems to suggest otherwise.

You said yourself that you are a better coach when you’re connected to your artistry, and a better artist because of your coaching. So what if the tension isn’t actually coming from doing both… but from the meaning your brain has attached to what each identity 
represents
?

I also want to lovingly challenge the sentence
 “it’s hard to accept that I still have to be a coach.”

Let’s dig deeper here. Reflect on each of the questions and see what comes up naturally for you.

Do you still 
“have”
 
to be a coach? If so, why? Do you even want to?

What makes coaching feel like the identity that lowers the value of the artist?

Why does one feel more “sexy” or emotionally significant than the other?

From the outside, it sounds less like you’re confused about who you are and more like there may still be grief, attachment, or expectation tied to what your life in art was “supposed” to look like.

I’m curious if staying in this identity conflict also protects you from fully showing up in either direction. Because if the problem is 
“I haven’t figured out who I am yet,”
 then there’s always a reason to hesitate with visibility, communication, or bigger moves forward.

What if you stopped trying to make the identities perfectly reconcile and instead allowed yourself to be a multifaceted human who genuinely loves both? Would you want that?

Take some time with these questions and then bring your answers back here so we can continue to help you! Thanks Coach!

title: Somatic life coaching outcomes
question:
I’m having issues connecting ting tangible outcomes to working with me. I’m a somatic life coach who focuses on working moms over 40 dealing with burnout & exhaustion.

I come up with things like, start believing in a life you stopped believing was available to you. She’s given up on herself in the quietest ways possible. She buried the version of herself that got to rest. That got to be loved well. That got to have a body that didn’t hurt. That got to make money without sacrifice. Somewhere around 38, or 43, or 51, she decided that certain things just weren’t for her. Consistent sleep. A body that doesn’t hurt. A relationship that feels safe. Joy, peace. Rest that doesn’t require earning. Receiving without earning or efforting. She decided those were for other women.

I’m telling her she decided wrong.

But I don’t know how to sell the outcome in a way she wants to pay $5k for.
answer:
Hi Coach!

I actually think you’re much closer than you realize! The issue is not that you don’t understand your client because you actually understand her deeply. I can feel that immediately in your writing. I think the issue may be that while you’re describing her emotional pain beautifully, almost like poetry, you’re speaking more in emotional truth than in “tangible transformation.” It feels like you may be selling the “ache” more than the result. So let’s coach on this a bit because I think your so close 
(with a few simple tweaks)!

A woman will absolutely pay $5k to stop feeling exhausted, resentful, disconnected from herself, emotionally fried, physically tense, and stuck in survival mode. She will pay to sleep better, stop snapping at her kids, feel safe in her own body again, stop carrying invisible pressure all day, and experience joy, rest, intimacy, and emotional steadiness again. Those are tangible outcomes.

The woman reading your work 
needs help picturing herself on the other side of this.

How does her body feel six months later? 

How does she move through her mornings because of the somatic work she’s done? 

What changes in her relationships, energy, boundaries, and nervous system because she is no longer living in constant depletion?

Somatic work creates incredibly real outcomes when you say them more plainly.

Some examples that come to mind are:

“My clients stop living like their body is constantly bracing for impact.”

“They learn how to rest without guilt.”

“They stop abandoning themselves to care for everyone else.”

“Their relationships improve because they are no longer functioning from chronic exhaustion and survival mode.”

What do you think? Does this help a bit?
 
Feel free to come back if you could use some further coaching support!

title: 05/21/2026 | just for today….
question:
Thank you for this coaching around fear of losing it all.

My biggest takeaways from this conversation are 1. focus on the smallest next step to let go of ruminating over fear of the future, and 2. stop trying to solve for discomfort and instead let it exist and move anyway.

Just for today I can start compiling a list of people I want to invite to my networking event, I can research how to host a networking event on zoom, I can start collecting emails, I can choose a date I want to host the event, and I can do all of this in leader energy.

Just for today I can block off time in my calendar where I will meet my 12 year-long clients, I can spend 2-3 hours today performing “client generating” tasks, and I can do all of this in excited expectation that those slots will fully sell out.

Just for today I can be present with the fear I feel in performing these tasks and I can feel the fear and complete these tasks anyway 🤍
answer:
Yes Coach! Exactly these two things you took from the coaching:

1. Focus on the smallest next step to let go of ruminating over fear of the future.

The next smallest step often feels mundane, small, or even insignificant, but taking it keeps you in motion. And that matters so much as entrepreneurs. 
What tends to hurt us most is not always the fear itself, but getting so caught in the rumination of our minds that we stop taking action altogether. 
Not to mention, we create so much of our future through our thoughts, emotions, and actions. So when we get stuck in cycles of fear and stop showing up, we often begin creating the very results we were afraid of in the first place.

2. Stop trying to solve for discomfort and instead let it exist and move anyway.

Yes, much like above we just have to allow ourselves to feel the feelings and move anyways. Feeling fear? 
Keep taking action
.
 Feeling uncertainty? 
Keep taking action.
 
Feel scared something may not work? Let that fear be present and try anyway because at the end of the day, you’ll learn from trying and learn how to tweak it, or do it better with more trials.

Great work here, coach!

title: Restarting 11
question:
I am in the valley of despair. My plan of creating 10k over 8 months is not working. Or I am not making it work. I know it is me. I only have 7 months left and I am not making any offers. Nothing. Not even one. Not for privates, not for workshops.

I am coaching a lot at work (career coaching) and in my private business (mental performance for competitive athletes) – I still have two free coachees that I am working with.

I believe that behind my inaction lies fear that I dont have the capacity. The same stuff as in the last ask a coach question.

That I dont have the capacity to even take on one workshop or one client next to my job, kids, career coaching at work (part of my job but somehow creating even more work) and two practice clients in sports.

Moreover, when Im done with my practice clients, I dont want to coach anymore like I do now- in my lunch break, in the evenings after a full time job and a long commute, on weekends when I am supposed to be and want to be with my kids.

So actually, I am not willing to do this for a year or two to build my business, I also cannot. I am too tired. I have a job with almost 50 hours with the commute, 3 kids, house I am renovating, husband that I spent way too little time with.

But my dream of living my job and only coaching comes at a very high financial price and though we can afford it, we can do so only for half a year or so. They I would need to go back to my real job (which will be in another town if I take a break)

But I simply cannot coach like this. I am too tired. Any thoughts?
answer:
Hello Coach ,

I want to start by acknowledging you and really seeing you where you are. This takes courage and honesty and a willingness to look at your life, your goals, where you are compared to where you want to be, and what you thought this would feel like compared to what you are actually experiencing now.

You mention here that you are onto yourself. You are fully aware that you are not taking action, not making offers, not showing up to the capacity you think it is going to require because you are afraid you can’t handle the capacity.

First, notice your brain is on a negative spiral and it is draining your energy at double speed. Instead of interrupting the spiral, your brain is using all your energy proving why this won’t work, why you can’t handle it, why it costs too much all adding the energy drain and despair.  How is it true you are handling more than you thought possible now too?

And I think this matters more than you realize because the way you speak about something directly impacts your energy and your capacity.

Right now, coaching in your mind is attached to exhaustion.

Lunch breaks.

Evenings after a full-time job.

Weekends when you want to be with your kids.

More work.

More depletion.

So it makes sense your brain is resisting making offers because you believe coaching is the thing taking away your energy instead of the thing creating more freedom and alignment long term.

And this is important too it becomes very hard to sell coaching when your belief about coaching is that it drains you. That energy comes through.

I think before strategy, there needs to be a decision.

Are you going to create this business right now?

And if you are, what has to become different about how you approach it? 
Not just your offers, but your thoughts, your schedule, your expectations, and your relationship with capacity.

Because without making a clean decision, you stay stuck in the negative loop of wanting it, fearing it, questioning yourself, then using the questioning as evidence not to move.

This is normal and human. The brain wants to keep you safe in what it knows.

But as coaches, we have to go first.

And I also want to offer this:

If you decide you do not want the ambition of growing your business right now, that is very different than believing you can’t. 
There is no shame in putting other ambitions first in this season of life.

But it becomes painful when you keep setting goals while simultaneously letting your brain convince you you are incapable. That loop erodes trust with yourself.

I would get very honest with yourself here.

What do you actually want right now?

Not from pressure.

Not from fear.

Not from proving something.

What do you truly want?

And I would also ask:

What do you know about the tools you teach that would help when the brain goes into a negative spiral?

How would you coach an athlete through this exact mental pattern?

Because right now your brain is rehearsing exhaustion and limitation over and over. Awareness matters here. Interrupting the spiral matters.

I also think there’s a difference between “I have no capacity” and “the way I am trying to do this is not working.” 
That is a very different problem.

Because maybe the issue is not coaching.

Maybe the issue is trying to fit a 10-pound bag of potatoes into a 5-pound bag.

When you look honestly at your schedule, does the math work?

Or are you trying to force more into your life than your current structure can hold?

And if that’s true, what needs to change?

What could become simpler?

What support do you need?

What would building this in a sustainable way actually look like?

I also would look from this future vantage point:

How would you show up if you knew you couldn’t fail?

If you knew you would eventually create the business and life you want, what would change about how you are thinking right now?

What would happen in your schedule?

How would you use your time differently?

What pressure would drop?

From that belief from already having done it  what could you offer yourself about your capacity and about feeling better in the messy middle?

Because when we are trying to believe new things, it feels hard. Holding two beliefs at once is uncomfortable.

Part of you believes you have capacity.

Part of you deeply believes you don’t.

That is the exact place growth happens.

And if you choose to commit to this goal, I would get very curious about what you believe about growing capacity. 
Not proving you already have unlimited capacity.

What does growing it, stretching it and how do you talk about your life , your time and your business when you have become the version of you that made the choice and is living it? 

What are your thoughts about this perspective?

title: Follow up 3: Help me work through my feelings of disappointment and discouragement 051826
question:
I’ve written and responded to all the questions that 500K me does, thinks, and feels, and have noticed the biggest difference in how I feel. And now I’m practicing holding that energy….

There is one line that you wrote that really stuck with me.

“Because identity work is repetition. You become her by practicing her. And one of the fastest ways to create a new result is to stop rehearsing the identity that created the old one.”

Help me understand this better… is it really that simple? I feel resistant.
answer:
Hi Coach,

It can really be that simple, yes. Let me try to give a visual if it may help. Think of it this way:

In entrepreneurship, we are kind of in a tug-o-war with ourselves.

We have one version of ourselves that fights to keep our current or old identity. It’s all the stories we hold that keep up safe. It’s the thoughts and beliefs we have tons of evidence for. It’s the version of us feels most comfortable.

Then there is the identity we want for ourselves. In your case, your 500k self.
