She requires different thoughts and beliefs and stories. And she’s also pulling the opposite end of the rope.

Both versions of you exist and both versions are strong… but the version we’ve been the longest tends to be the “most” strong because we’ve shown up as “her” longer. So your 500k self isn’t impossible or out of reach, she just has to apply more strength and effort to win the “tug-o-war” against your current/old self.

Does that make sense? It’s simple, but not always easy.

The repetition of really getting clear on how your 500k self operates in the world is ultimately like “building muscle” so she can win the game of tug-o-war. That repetition is what makes you strong over time. There will come a day (if you don’t quit on yourself or give up) where you can absolutely be her. Right now, you’re building her strength.

Let me know if this visual helps. It’s a bit silly, but I find it helpful when coaching clients on reaching their next big milestones. You’re up against your old self, old stories, old thoughts, old evidence – but you can do it. You want to 
embody your 500k self and what SHE would do
, more than what the “cozy, comfortable” version of you “today” would do.

Let us know if that visual helps clarify a bit and paint the picture of why this work is so important! Thanks, Coach!

title: Strategic Doubt or Exhaustion? Part 2
question:
What do you actually believe makes someone effective at coaching couples? Is it their current relationship status, or their ability to see patterns, hold space, and guide people through dynamics they may not be able to see themselves?

This is what I believe makes me an effective couples coach. I do believe it is unique to me, and really quite different to other couples coaches and therapists… being able to witness and hold space for both people, being able to guide them back into their body, their breath, back to a sacredness beyond words. Slowing down. Holding the truth of their experiences, and also inviting them to create a new truth that feels like love and devotion. That feels hot, fresh, playful, and silly.

I believe what especially makes me effective as a couples coach is my ability to draw out grace for the imperfect. The imperfect is where it all begins for me. The dropping of the ego. The willingness to be the fool. I believe this is where the sacred comes in. I get so excited just writing these words.

So no, it does now seem like a gross simplification to think that “I can’t be an effective couple’s coach without a romantic partner.” As I stated in my previous question.

What do you need right now to feel even slightly more supported?

Where can you give yourself a little more space, a little more care, without abandoning your business?

I think I can give myself support by going to my GP and prioritising my struggle with perimenopause . By not expecting perfection from myself. And yes, I love the idea of leaving evaluations until a set time—focusing on the doing and action-taking. Focusing on encouraging myself and marking off every action taken as a win.

I will take care of myself, but I will not use self-care against myself. There will be times when I don’t take exquisite care of myself, and that’s okay. I can work in the wellness space and not always feel 100% perfectly well. I am human. I am allowed to struggle and be out of balance.

This doesn’t have to be “all or nothing.” You can build something meaningful AND honor where you are. The goal isn’t perfect consistency, but honest, sustainable movement forward. What do you think?

Yes, I think this is spot on. I will not make any changes or do any evaluation until the end of this year. I will just trust that I am on the right track for now. I can adjust at the end of the year if I want. For now, I will take action and not overthink.

I would appreciate your thoughts on my response.
answer:
Hi Coach,

You’ve done something really important here you didn’t just answer the question, you actually let your answers change how you see yourself. When you chose to focus on your unique strengths and effectiveness you create the identity of a confident coach and your ability to show up from that self concept shows.

When you ask whether effectiveness comes from relationship status or your ability to see patterns and hold space, what I notice is that your belief shifted as you explored it. That matters, because the way you see yourself will directly shape how you show up. Clients don’t just respond to your tools they respond to your certainty. Believing you are effective is part of what makes you effective, in the same way you believe in their capacity to grow impact their results.

When you see your relationship status as neutral, not a limitation what changes in how you think, speak, and lead? I’m asking because this is where your power is. The circumstance didn’t change, but your relationship to it did. And that’s what your clients will feel. What is different when you see your relationship status as a neutral circumstance?  You may have believed it gave you confidence before and so now you expect it to be the thing that is missing now.  What if they just want to know you can help and you have tools and skills that they need?

What stands out most is how clearly you see your unique approach. The way you describe drawing out grace for the imperfect, the dropping of ego, that’s not just beautiful language, that’s a coaching skill.  Most people are trying to fix or polish relationships. You’re inviting people into something much deeper.

“The imperfect is where it all begins for me.” I got excited when you shared this too!  This is so great, you need to share this energy!

So I want you to really look at that. What specifically do you do that creates that experience for your clients? The more specific you get, the more usable and visible your “superpower” becomes—not just for you, but for them. What you look for, you strengthen. When you keep finding evidence of what makes you effective, you naturally start embodying it more.

And I also want to reflect something back to you your excitement when you wrote that part, notice the charge in you ? That’s alignment. That’s usually a clue you’re onto something true for you. The question then becomes: what does that make you want to go create, share, or offer? And who needs that perspective because they don’t yet see it the way you do?

You said you want to care for yourself without using self-care against yourself. That’s a powerful distinction. So let me ask you this: what does it look like to offer yourself the same grace for the imperfect that you bring into your coaching?

I’m asking because there’s an opportunity here. Not in spite of what you’re going through but because of it. If your work is about meeting people in the imperfect, what does it mean for you to practice that in real time, in your own body, with your own energy fluctuations?

You don’t need to be perfectly well to do this work. In fact, your willingness to stay present through discomfort may deepen your capacity to hold others there too.

So instead of trying to remove the struggle, what if the question becomes: how can I support myself inside of this, without making it mean something has gone wrong?

You also mentioned committing to action without evaluation until the end of the year.  If you notice overthinking coming up, you might ask yourself: what am I trying not to feel right now? That question matters because often the mental spinning is just a way to avoid emotional discomfort. And your growth will come from your willingness to feel that discomfort without letting it stop you.

So as you move forward, I’d anchor you in this: Who are you becoming as you continue without needing it to be perfect, certain, or easy? And why is that version of you worth showing up for now?

You’re not building this from a place of having it all figured out. You’re building it from a place of being willing to stay, to see clearly, and to keep going. I’m really glad you shared this it’s thoughtful, honest, and you’re much closer to your own clarity than you think. Great job coach, keep going, you going through this is going to help your people.

title: 2 of 30 days of coaching
question: Yes, my thought is that people don’t want to buy packages because they don’t want to make the commitment. I might not be a good fit or they won’t like how I work. I might not want to work with them either. I have historically been a person who likes an “out” and I don’t want to trap people and I don’t want to be trapped. But, they aren’t really trapped, they can always quit?? I’m ok with refunding for unused meetings too. Therapy is a one-on-one thing, so I feel like people are free to come and stop coming when they want too. I am back to I don’t want to trap them. It’s also not all about the money, I can feel something else about not wanting force them to be accountable or something…I am not quite putting my finger on it yet. Trapped is the word of the day though.
answer:
Hey Coach!

Let’s approach this from compassion because I can feel how real “trapped” feels for you. I’m not trying to talk you out of that. I just want to understand it with you. What you shared actually shows me that something shifts the moment coaching shifts from “single sessions” to calling it a “package.” That’s the part I want to understand more.

Right now, it sounds like session-by-session feels open and flexible, like you still have choice.

And “a package” suddenly feels like you’re locked in, like you owe something in a heavier way, or like you’ve lost your “out.”

What comes to mind first for coaching is – we don’t even know what a package is in your mind yet.

4 sessions? 8 sessions? 3-months? Is it flexible?
 Is 
there an exit?

There are so many ways you could structure this to support you & the client in an empowering way.

1. Does it matter to you that clients show up consistent
 and/or
 committed to the results they want from coaching? Do you want clients who only show a few times and give themselves an “out” when it feels challenging or hard? Or do you prefer to explore that with them and show them the benefit of moving through challenges, resistance, etc.,?

I also want to offer this.

When we build our business around having an out, it doesn’t just remove the pressure or discomfort of being “locked in”. It can also remove the depth available for ourselves and for our clients. What I mean is, the moments where things feel uncomfortable, where a client doesn’t like something, where you’re stretched as a coach, where you have to navigate something challenging instead of “opt out” – those are usually the moments where the real transformation happens.

If there’s always an easy exit, you 
may never
 actually have to stay long enough to meet those parts of yourself (or your client). It’s not because you can’t, but because you’ve designed your coaching containers in a way where you don’t have to and they don’t have to.

Having a package isn’t about trapping anyone 
(and I know you know that since you acknowledged it previously).
 It’s about noticing that your brain is simply labeling something as “trapping” yet it hasn’t even been clearly defined. And also, creating a package (if you choose to do so) might actually be asking you for a deeper level of commitment, skill, and self trust. I’d stay with this for a moment and reflect.

How many sessions would you include in a “package” and why?

What might you learn about yourself as a coach if you trusted yourself to stay (when you feel challenged, or the client feels challenged), even when it’s not as easy to do so?

How might it serve you, and your client, to commit to several sessions without an easy “out”? What might you learn in that process?

Take some time to reflect and bring your answers back here when you’re ready!

title: moving into selling courses 5
question:
I know the version of me who knows I can reach more people with less of my time and make more money – She remembers you know things. Who trusts that even your “not best” is still valuable. Who feels taken care of, powerful, heard, and connected to yourself – What’s pulling you out of her? And why? I think the biggest thing is I’m using my current evidence of it’s not working to “prove” that I can’t do it/that I’m failing. Sometimes it feels easier to believe I’m just not capable than to work on believing that I can if that makes sense. It feels easier or more comfortable to hide. It feels hard to step into her – but I love the thought that my “not best” is still valuable. That doesn’t feel like a battle to access her that way. I think I’m also thinking it’ll take a lot of effort to create what I want or I have a lot of value I need to add to my value bank before I can get there – and I’m tired from the rest of my life so I’m avoiding the efforting.

When you hit that naptime moment and you go to consume what are you actually needing right then? Not what you’re doing, but what you’re hoping to feel. I think I’m definitely looking for relief. To turn my brain off. To not be needed by anyone – which is another reason I feel like I’m chafing up against my coaching practice – because it feels like just one more thing that needs me or my clients need me. I’m looking to be entertained. inspired. I’m looking for education too – I watch a lot of parenting content, codependency content (healing from my childhood) and a lot of fashion content (fun, challenging my brain to be creative with something that doesn’t really matter but feels good).

How do you want to take care of yourself as the asset in your life and business, even inside a full life? I think I want to prioritize the way I look – doing my hair/makeup more often. I’m playing with my own wardrobe and that feels good. I also could do more self-care type stuff – like my nails and I have a scalp massage gift card – I should just schedule that. I have tuesday nights to myself now but I struggle with what to do with them – because I often feel tapped out beforehand that doing something feels like too much. But I probably should leave the house and make myself do something I want to do. I just don’t always know what that is.
answer:
Hi Coach,

I want to start with how the thought “it’s not working” pulls you out of the version of you that feels trusting, powerful, and connected.  It changes how you show up, what you see, and what you’re willing to do.

When you tell yourself “it’s not working,”  What does that actually mean to you?  it’s a very broad conclusion. What specifically isn’t working? And just as important what 
is
 working that you might be filtering out? Take your time here.

Right now, it makes sense that believing “maybe I’m just not capable” feels easier because it is familiar. That thought lets you stop trying. It conserves energy. But it also keeps you disconnected from the version of you you described. So another way to approach this is: if you were operating from “this is working,” even just 10%, how would you move differently? What would you do next from that place? Is it true that is is easier, it doesn’t sound that way now.

I also want to connect this to what you shared about those naptime moments. You said you’re looking for relief, to turn your brain off, to not be needed.  But notice what’s actually happening you go to consume, and instead of relief, you’re giving your brain more input, more,  more stimulation. You’re trying to solve for relief in a way that doesn’t seem to actually create it.

So I want to ask you: what do you actually need in that moment relief, or rest? . Relief might look like a clean mental break, quiet, space, nothing required of you. Rest that might actually restore your energy. Consumption often does neither. It also can provide more proof “it’s not working” . Is that happening here?

If you decided ahead of time, “when I feel this, I will give myself real rest,” how might that change the experience? And on the other side of that, if you decided, “this is a work block,” and followed a simple plan what would shift about your trust in yourself?

Because right now, the pattern isn’t the problem the lack of interruption is. Patterns don’t break by hoping they change; they break when you consciously choose something different and are willing to feel the discomfort of that.

I also hear the thought that your business feels like “one more thing that needs you.”  So I want you to consider: who do you want to be in those moments? The version of you who grows this how does she think about being needed? Does she experience it as pressure, or as something she’s choosing? This is identity work, choice and desire will change this experience.

And this ties into treating yourself as the asset. You mentioned wanting to take care of yourself but there’s some indecision there. When decisions aren’t made ahead of time, the default becomes doing nothing or doing what’s easiest in the moment, that is not working currently.

So I’m curious: what would it look like to decide in advance how you take care of yourself, Let’s map one of these moments out so you can really see it clearly:

C – Naptime / feeling tired / business plans
T – “It’s not working” or “I can’t do this” or “This is too much effort”
F – Defeated, resistant, drained
A – Avoid work, consume content, don’t follow through on plan, disconnect from business
R – Reinforces “it’s not working,” builds more evidence that you’re not capable, and keeps you out of the version of you you want to be

So if nothing changes in the thought line, you can keep changing actions and still get pulled back into the same result.

So I want you to play with this what would the model look like for the version of you you described?

C – Same life, same naptime, same level of tired
T – “Even my not best is valuable” or “This is working”
F – Willing, grounded, open
A – Takes a real break or follows a simple plan, shows up in a small way, stays connected to business
R – Builds trust, creates evidence of capability, strengthens that version of you

You don’t have to fully believe the new thought yet but you do have to be willing to practice thinking it and acting from it.

You don’t become her by waiting to feel like her. You become her by thinking and acting in alignment with her especially in the small, ordinary moments like naptime, like a Tuesday night, like the thought “this isn’t working.”

There’s a lot of awareness here already. Stay with it Coach, and be willing to see what’s actually happening without immediately making it mean something about your capability. That’s where things start to shift.

title: Drama around money, impact, and restarting
question:
Hi Coaches,

I will try to keep this simple and short.

My coaching business is in its 3rd year. In 2024 I made $38,000, In 2025 I made $40,000. In 2025 I experienced a lot of change: Ended a relationship of 14yrs, moved into my own place (first time living on my own), and found out I have iron deficiency anemia so have been trying to get well. When my health came to a head I really put business on the back burner and if I am honest, I am somewhat surprised I maintained that coaching income in 2025. I also took on a part time job during this time to help pay my rent. Anyway, I have a few things going on that I would like some coaching on… I want to grow my business, but I am not believing that I have the capacity to do more, even though I think I know I can. I am just very afraid of burning out & have a lot of health anxiety right now. The other thing that is running through my head are thoughts like ” I don’t even know who I’m coaching anymore” “I don’t know how to promote myself when I don’t even get what I do” – I feel lost in recognizing my impact even though my clients are getting great results and most of them have stayed with me since I started. They have results like landing million dollar contracts and buying office space in Manhattan, while I am struggling financially. I have a lot of debit, I messed up my taxes the first year so I am on a payment plan with the IRS and currently feel like I don’t have it in me to do what it takes to succeed. A terrible thought, but there it is. I appreciate your coaching and if you have any tips for 2K resources to review to help me reset & get clear on how to sell/start making more money that would be appreciated too.
answer:
Hey there Coach!

The sentence, 
“I don’t even know what I do anymore”
 is worth slowing down and getting curious about because your clients’ results tell a very different story. Sometimes when coaching becomes very natural to us, we stop recognizing the value of what we’re actually providing because we’re inside of it every day. But women landing million-dollar contracts, buying office space, and continuing to stay in your world tells me there 
is
 impact here, even if your brain is currently disconnected from seeing it clearly.

I also wonder if you’re putting some pressure on yourself to build a business in a way that no longer fits the season of life and health you’re currently in. Your business does not have to be built around exhaustion, over-capacity, or proving. You get to decide what your work hours, client load, energy output, and pace look like. There are many ways to grow a business, and I’d be careful about believing the only path available is one that burns you out. 
What feels good to you when you think about building your business? What are some of your goals?

I think 
Offer Week
 inside the Bonuses section of the 2K portal could really support you right now. Not necessarily to “restart,” but to reconnect to who you help, what transformation you provide, and how to communicate that in a cleaner, simpler way without this feeling heavy in your mind.

What do you think?
 Feel free to come back for more coaching on anything you may need!

title: Pressure
question:
Hi Coach,

I’m so grateful for this resource! Here’s what I’m struggling with. I’ve had two corporate layoffs in a two-year period. For the past six or seven years, I’ve been the primary breadwinner. My deepest desire (or so I thought) was to finally get to a point where I had mental bandwidth to focus on building my coaching business, rather than having it be a part-part time side hustle, as it has been. But now that I’m in this place, with no steady income, I’m feeling so triggered and activated. My partner keeps encouraging me to lean in and really go for it, but a part of me is TERRIFIED. I’ve continued to send out resumes but so far nothing has born fruit. I’m a parent and still have kids at home. I find myself feeling just awful. Here it is, the moment and the permission slip I’ve waited for, and now I’m freezing. Any help would be appreciated!
answer:
Hi Coach,

We are so happy you are leaning into the support available and allowing yourself to be honest about where you are right now. We can help you.

What stands out to me most is it sounds like you expected that when the permission slip was finally granted, when you finally had the time and space to go after your truest desire  you wouldn’t feel terrified.

Is that true?

Did you expect to feel different? And why?

I ask because I think our brains play tricks on us sometimes. We imagine the grass is greener. We think finally going after the thing we truly want will automatically feel freeing, exciting, peaceful. And there will absolutely be things that are better. But there will also be things that are harder while you build new skills and learn new ways to move through fear, uncertainty, and discomfort.

Your brain is trying to scare you back toward what is known and familiar, even if it’s no longer your deepest desire.

What if nothing has gone wrong here?

What if terror is simply your body’s response to change?

Not danger. Not failure. Just change.

What if you allowed the fear to be there instead of making it mean you shouldn’t move forward?

You shared that you have a deep desire to build your coaching business now that you finally have the time and mental bandwidth. I would spend some real time there.

Why do you want to build this business?

Why is it important to you?

What does this possibility look like for you?

I’m asking because your “why” matters. A strong why helps override the brain’s attempt to pull you back toward the path of least resistance the known path. Even when that known path is no longer aligned.

And I would also ask yourself:

What would you regret more?

Working through the fear and giving yourself permission to try…

or never really giving yourself the chance because it felt terrifying?

Almost everything meaningful requires courage and discomfort first. 
I also want you to get curious about the fear itself.

What are you terrified about specifically? 
Can you clarify it?

And then ask:

How can you create safety while still moving toward what you want?

Because safety does not always mean certainty. Are there some criteria you could make around creating criteria for decisions that feel good?

You already know how to be successful. You’ve built a corporate career. You’ve been the breadwinner. You’ve had the mental capacity to build a side business while raising a family and managing life.

That tells me you already have so much to offer. 
How would you get started if you knew you couldn’t fail?

What’s the worst-case scenario?

What’s the best-case scenario?

And are you willing to give yourself permission to go for the best case instead of only preparing for the worst one?

Are you willing to feel uncomfortable,
 to learn and
 to let it be messy while you figure it out. 
You do not need to have it all figured out right now. 
You just have to stop making fear mean you shouldn’t begin.

You’ve got this. Keep sharing your thoughts. We can help you take the next steps.

title: Day 6 of 30 days of coaching
question:
Why am I doing this? I have never been coached or coached myself on why I am transitioning from therapy to coaching. Way back when I started…like 2017-ish….it was to make more money and to escape clinical work. I do not like clinically intense clients. I call myself a “therapist-light” and am so impressed by therapists who do the hard shit. I like helping my clients feel better and get places. But-do I need to be a coach to do so?? For the most part I have amazing clients. I have a higher than average fee. I do hate all of the “rules” of therapy, but that is because I hate to break rules (it makes me nervous) and I definitely bend them as a therapist. While my fee is higher, I still feel limited by the 1:1 work and it seems like there is a cap on my income if I continue with only 1:1 work. So it seems it does have a lot to do with the money and having a little more freedom in my schedule (fewer clients, courses, programs, etc). My work is deep and coachy/my coaching is deep and therapy-like.

I have been doing this for nearly NINE years. Not always full on but for a decent chunk of it. I have quit and come back with new offers. I’ve also invested a lot in being coached to get this thing going. So I wonder-am I supposed to stay a therapist?? I mean I could easily transition my financial coaching into financial therapy and just sell by the session (per my other questions). I could still run a group a couple of times per year. I have other ideas too but I’m trying to keep it simple and stay focused. I’ve been in process with this offer for two years this summer and it’s slow going. No other offers and I really love helping women with money.

Again, I wonder if the universe is trying to tell me something.

I feel like I need to get clear on this as I step into trusting myself and being a leader.
answer:
Hey Coach,

I’m really glad you brought this here, because what you’re actually asking isn’t just “Should I be a therapist or a coach?” It’s: “Can I trust myself to choose and back that choice?”

And right now, the biggest thing I see isn’t confusion… it’s 
indecision
.

Indecision will keep you in a loop where you never actually find out what works because you never fully go all in on anything long enough to let it work. You shared your thought “So I wonder-am I supposed to stay a therapist??” Supposed to according to who? Answer this deliberatley or your brain will do to default answers.  Start deliberately directing it on purpose.

You’ve been in this for nearly nine years, and what stands out is not a lack of experience or capability it’s that you’re still holding the decision loosely. So of course it still feels unclear.  Time doesn’t give you anything her other than more time unclear and less knowing. What do you think you expected from nine years? What creates results is skill, and value and belief.

Why do you think you haven’t just decided?

I’m not asking that to challenge you I’m asking because the answer to that question will tell us everything. When we don’t decide, it’s usually not because we don’t know… it’s because of what we think the decision will cost us. What would be the benefit of deciding ?  What would be the benefit of deciding now for your clients?

If you couldn’t use “I don’t know” as an answer what would be the real reason it feels hard to choose?

Is it that you don’t trust which one will be successful?
Is it that you don’t want to choose “wrong”?
Is it that choosing one feels like losing the other?

Is it that you are worried about what others think?

I’m asking this because clarity doesn’t usually come before the decision. It comes 
after you decide and start moving
. What feeling do you need to be willing to feel to make this choice?

Right now, you’re trying to think your way into certainty but this is one of those places where certainty is created through commitment, not found through more consideration.

You also mentioned wondering if the universe is trying to tell you something.

I want to offer a different perspective:
What if this isn’t the universe trying to tell you something…
What if it’s you not fully backing yourself yet and waiting for a sign keeps you safe.

Because when you fully decide, you stop looking for signs and you start creating results.

Let’s look at your pattern for a moment so you you can understand what is happening.  You’ve started, stopped, created new offers, invested, come back again. That tells me you’re not lacking desire. You’re not lacking capability either.

So the more useful question becomes: What has caused you to stop or pivot in the past?  I’m asking this because if you don’t understand that pattern, you’ll recreate it whether you choose therapy or coaching.

Was it that it wasn’t working fast enough?
Was it doubt creeping in?
Was it hitting the edge of growth and then pulling back?

Because if quitting or pivoting is still on the table, then no path will feel “right” for very long.

And this is where I want to offer something that might shift things for you:

What if the goal isn’t to pick the right path? 
What if the goal is to pick a path and become the person who makes it right?

So this might not actually be a which one decision.

“How do I want to build this in a way that reflects me and supports the life and income I want?”

You’re also clear you love helping women with money. That matters. So instead of asking: “Should I be a therapist or a coach?” What if you asked: “What model best supports the client create results in a way I love, the way I want to work, and the life I want to live?”

That’s a very different question and it puts you back in the position of leadership. Because right now, you’re waiting to feel clear before you lead. But leadership looks like deciding even when it feels uncertain and then leading yourself through the follow-through.

You don’t need to make a choice  to help people feel better and get results. You’re already doing that. The real work here is trusting yourself enough to choose and then removing quitting as an option when it gets uncomfortable.  If you trusted yourself fully to make a choice  What would you choose right now—and why?

And just as important, once you choose, how will you make sure you don’t revisit the decision every time it feels hard or unclear ?

Feel free to come back if you need anything further or coaching on anything else!

title: 06/05/2026 – breakthrough
question:
Hi coaches,

This is a follow-up on the coaching you gave around how I show up on my podcast.

Here is some insight I gained from a couple models I was doing on my results:

Action – I show up on the podcast but not from a place of “inspiring or storytelling” (even thought this is what I want to be doing) but rather from a place of teaching.

What is driving that action? Shame.

& the thoughts creating shame are: “I’m not a good representation of the work and if people figure that out they will stop listening to me, then I won’t get clients, I’ll have no audience, I’ll lose my current audiences’ respect.”

& in order to try and solve for the shame and discomfort I feel, my brain has decided that I need to avoid inspiring / storytelling and instead just teach. I need to hide.

& the result is what we’ve been talking about: no consults from the podcast, little engagement, and even deeper I can see that these thoughts are impacting the way I show up as an entrepreneur, a leader, and a coach in general.

My brain is always holding onto the thought “once we sign clients or our circumstances change THEN we’ll show up again.”

& I think the biggest fear that my brain is trying to protect me from is fear that I’ll lose respect from my community / audience.

I wouldn’t say I’m actively creating this result in the R column, but I’m always living in the belief that this WIILL be the result if I start showing up before my circumstances change.

Or maybe my brain is even using the result of no consults / no new clients / still living at my brothers, etc. as proof that I’m not seen as valuable or respectable within my current circumstances.

I can see the loop. This feels like the most significant model I’ve ever done. Shame is in the driver’s seat and my results (having or not having clients) hasn’t changed in years because I’m constantly stuck looping, trying to “solve” for shame while unintentionally being driven by it.

What I’m also realizing is that I’ve had a lot of experiences with coaches who weren’t good representations of the work. “Coaches” who weren’t actually coaching at all. Who definitely weren’t self-coaching. Who lost my respect. & I think a lot of this stems from the fear that I’ll turn out like them. Most of them gave up eventually and got corporate jobs or just fell off the side of the planet. & frankly I think I had become them.

Now I’m wondering, how do I believe I’m the exception in the coaching industry – like Stacey, like all of you.
answer:
Hey Coach,

Such great work here. I’m so glad you’re taking the coaching, the questions, and using them to create this level of awareness for yourself. As coaches, especially coaches who want to coach at the highest level, we all have opportunities to look honestly at ourselves and decide who we want to be in any given circumstance.

What I see is someone who deeply cares about serving people well. It sounds like you want to show up at your best, and that’s a beautiful thing. But now that you have this awareness, the work isn’t finding another strategy. The work is learning to look at yourself with compassion, perspective, and then making a choice.

When you want to create a new outcome that is beyond your current results, beyond your current skill level, beyond your current emotional capacity, beyond what your current strategies have produced, eventually all that’s left is belief.

Not, “What do I need to do differently?”

But, “What would I have to believe?”

I think that’s the question I’d spend some time with.

Your brain keeps wanting to solve for the discomfort by changing the circumstances first. More clients. More consults. Different results. Then I’ll show up. Then I’ll feel confident. Then I’ll believe in myself.

But in my experience, it almost always works the other way around.

It isn’t the circumstances that create the belief. It’s the belief that creates different actions, and those actions create different circumstances.

You asked how to believe you’re the exception.

I’m not sure that’s the most useful question.

What if the question is: Who do I want to be regardless of the circumstances?

Because every coach gets to decide their standards. Every coach gets to stay in their own lane. Every coach gets to decide how they will show up when things are working and when they aren’t.

You don’t become a great coach because your circumstances prove you’re a great coach. You become a great coach because you continue to practice the work, live the work, and show up aligned with your values regardless of what the circumstances are telling you.

So I would get very curious about this:

What is the thought that would create the result you want?

What would you have to believe to show up on your podcast the way you want to show up today?

Maybe it’s, “I have so much to offer.”

Maybe it’s, “My circumstances don’t determine my value.”

Maybe it’s, “I can serve people while I’m still growing.”

Then practice believing it.

Find evidence for it.

Create evidence for it.

Because right now your brain is filtering life through the belief that you’re not enough and gathering evidence for that. What would happen if you intentionally practiced filtering through a belief that supports the leader, entrepreneur, and coach you want to become?

From everything you’ve written, I don’t think your problem is a lack of awareness anymore. I think you’ve already uncovered what’s driving the loop.

You get to decide you are whatever you want to be in the coaching industry. You get to think anything you want. If that is true what do you decide? How can you make that true, How can you focus on believing that? It is an opportunity to create your own standards.

Now the work is choosing what you want to believe and practicing that belief long before your circumstances give you permission to.

Keep going Coach! You got this.  Thank you for seeing us and Stacey and the entire team here as exceptional, we all receive that, THANK YOU!

title: Energy Struggle – Active/Get vs Passive/serve
question:
I am evaluating my last few months of applying the 2k process.

I started in January and have not gotten any consults yet.

I have been enjoying creating content on Facebook and I have been actively doing this – 4-5 posts per week.

I’m questioning whether my “active” energy here is really get energy.

When I tell myself I need to focus more on serving my brain interprets this as a passive approach.

Right now my active approach in the last 5 months:

4-5 facebook posts a week

3 workshops

4 short videos for each workshop

When I think of servicing, my brain wants to:

Create YouTube videos with more depth than Facebook posts

Host YouTube lives once a month

Invite inquiries for these lives

I had low attendance on the workshops so YouTube seems safer. I put the content out there and those who are interested will find it as opposed to sharing my workshops on facebook when only a small % are interested.

My struggle that my brain is telling me I have given up on the “active” strategy and that YouTube is slow, safe and passive and not what I need to do to make 2k today

I am looking forward to your coaching on this!
answer:
Hey there Coach!

I actually think your brain may be unintentionally turning this into a black-or-white, “all or nothing” situation:

ACTIVE = “get” energy

PASSIVE = “serve” energy

What if there’s a gray area here?

What if almost every action you take in your business can be active 
or
 passive 
AND
 done from a place of service?

I don’t think “get” energy is automatically about posting often, inviting people, hosting workshops, or actively selling. Based on what Stacey teaches, “get” energy is more about when our energy becomes attached, urgent, grasping, or emotionally dependent on the outcome we receive back. Whereas service energy feels cleaner, more grounded, and more focused on genuinely helping, offering, inviting, and creating value 
(regardless of whether the action itself is active or passive).

For example, you could post 5 times a week from
 incredibly clean
 service energy. You could also make YouTube videos from 
avoidance, hiding, or fear
 of direct rejection. And vice versa.

I’d actually get curious less about “which strategy is right?” and more about 
“How am I energetically relating to the strategy while I’m doing it?”

YouTube doesn’t have to automatically mean passive, slow, or “wrong.”

Remember that depth builds trust + clients 
too. 

Long-form content builds trust + clients
 too.

Lives and workshops build trust + clients
 too.

The bigger question may simply be:

Can you continue showing up consistently, inviting people in, and creating from a clean space no matter the strategy while also believing the actions you take can create “2k today”?

title: No Clients – Feeling Low – 2
question:

Coaches doing well are smarter, organized, speak well, vulnerable. Some have jobs, successful partner, no children. Enjoy people, network, socialize, go to network events w/ a mission. More passionate re what they do, think & act quickly.

My expectations are high. Last biz did well w/o much time/effort. I’m knowledgeable & have great IP. My clients get incredible results in life & biz.

A-Interact more w/ people I know online?

THOUGHTS

I spoke for 3 weeks, then stopped. I now realize it was all or nothing. Didn’t leave time for much else. Didn’t take time to eval WWDD.

Likely bc feel like failure when dont live up to my sched, feel like a slow person at times, get disorganized when behind, feel overwhelmed. Soothe myself by slowing down, back to old ways bc more organic & natural pace. Old ways lead to feeling down, stressed. Search for outside work that I’m extremely particular about, & wonder how going to make ends meet.

Comes down to enough $ to live, meet dreams/desires/expectations.

I COACH established women entreprs

I have a 6-month, 1:1, life/biz coaching container for $10K. We meet 12X online for 45-90 min, depend where they are in my 3 step program. Focus on identity.

ENERGIZED COVERSATIONS

Answer nuanced marketing questions w/ my mentor.

answer:
Hi Coach!

Thanks for bringing all of this back. One thing that stood out to me immediately was this:

“I spoke for 3 weeks, then stopped.”

As I read through your post, I noticed that many of the qualities your brain associates with successful coaches seem to point toward
 consistency, organization, and following through
 on things
 over time.

I’m curious what you think your brain was making those 3 weeks of speaking mean.

What was it hoping to see, feel, experience, or prove during that time? I’m also curious what your brain made it mean when those things didn’t happen quickly enough, or in the way it expected.

Three weeks is such a short amount of time in business. It seems like your brain wants to use years of evidence against itself instead of giving a new experiment enough time to produce evidence for itself.

Another thing that caught my attention is that you shared feeling energized when you follow a schedule, but when you fall behind, your brain tends to interpret that as failure. Then it returns to a more organic pace, even though you’ve noticed that approach often leaves you feeling stressed, discouraged, and worried about money. I’d love to know what you make of that.

What do you think your brain is trying to protect you from when it steps away from the very things that seem to create momentum, energy, and structure for you?

I’m wondering if the next opportunity is less about finding the perfect strategy and more about developing a deeper understanding of what happens between deciding to do something and continuing to do it long enough to see what it creates.

What might happen if you chose a handful of income-producing activities that genuinely fit you 
(whether that’s videos, networking, speaking, podcasting, guest appearances, webinars, posting content, or something else entirely)
 and committed to doing them consistently for 
90 days before evaluating
 whether they’re working?

And, what if part of your coaching commitment was to catch anytime your brain gets stuck in “all-or-nothing” so it can be redirected?

What might become possible if the goal for the next 90 days wasn’t to prove whether you’re capable of success, but to gather 
clean data
 about what happens when you stay with something longer than your brain normally wants to?

Feel free to come back with any of your thoughts or continued coaching you may need. Happy to help!

title: Coaching on 200k Mastermind enrollment goal
question:
Hi there, I have set a goal to enroll in the 200k mastermind in June and would love some support with some of my thoughts/beliefs around that goal. I’m hoping to come back here throughout May and June as I work towards this goal!

Currently, I would need to sign about 2-3 clients in the next 6ish weeks to meet the income requirement. I’ve been ITC’ing on the enrollment for a couple of weeks, here’s why I want to do it: I’ve signed about a handful of clients so far and see the mastermind as a great way to further refine my skills, get more support for my business, get clearer on how I’m speaking to my ideal client, and be in community with coaches striving for bigger goals. Enrolling scares me a little too, but I think it’s the right move for me and my business, especially with pushing me outside of my comfort zone and driving my ambition.

Some thoughts knocking me out of belief: I have a tendency to need proof to get into belief; Stacey coached me on this recently and called out that looking for proof builds a system that requires proof, and then you don’t allow for all the possibility in the world. She encouraged me to focus on what I can control, and also know that there’s more possibility out there than I can see. I resonated with that coaching, yet still find my brain going towards when my last sales call was, when the next one is, when the next person will say yes, etc.

Right now, I believe it’s inevitable that I’ll get 2 sales calls in May, but part of that belief is because I got 2 recently and it’s the beginning of the month, and so it feels like “of course it’ll happen.” But I know as the month goes on and if the calls don’t come, I’ll get out of belief. And 3 calls in May feels possible but not inevitable. One piece of proof: my 2 recent sales calls were right at the end of April, and I kept up my belief/ITC work throughout April, so I can see how my belief created those calls.

I’m interested in your thoughts around how to focus more on belief vs proof (keep up with ITC? Embody my 100k self? All of the above!), plus some coaching on moving from “it’s possible” to “it’s inevitable” without needing proof. As I’m typing all of this out, I think my first step is to go back to the first Creating New Beliefs call and listen again! But I’d love additional input as well. Thank you!
answer:
Hi Coach,

I love where your brain is already going, because you can see it: the work here isn’t getting more proof, it’s becoming someone who no longer requires it.

Your brain reaching for timelines, last calls, next yes that’s not a problem, that’s just your human brain trying to create certainty. It thinks proof will make you safer. But what you’re actually building right now is the ability to create without proof first. That’s the work you’ll teach your clients later so you getting to go first here matters.

You mentioned Stacey’s coaching about focusing on what’s in your control.  
When you truly anchor into “this is inevitable,” what does that change about your plan? Not the result the plan.
 What do you do differently, specifically, that would make signing those 2–3 clients a natural outcome of how you’re showing up?

And along those lines, when you’re in the belief that this is done, how do you show up on calls, in conversations, in your invitations? What’s different about your energy, your certainty, your willingness to lead? That difference is often what creates the result, not the waiting for the result to confirm the belief.

You already have evidence that your belief created calls in April. Notice what your brain is doing now it’s saying, “that worked but will it work again?”  You already know your belief drops when the numbers aren’t there yet. So instead of reacting to that, what if you plan for it?

What does it look like to decide ahead of time: “When my brain goes to doubt, here’s exactly how I will lead myself back”? This is where your ITC work becomes less reactive and more directive.

And I want to offer this too, when you create something you haven’t created before, your brain will offer resistance. Not because anything is wrong, but because it’s unfamiliar. It will try to pull you back to what feels known and proven. The question becomes are you willing to feel that uncertainty and keep moving anyway?

Why would it be worth it for you to keep showing up, inviting, serving, offering value even if the evidence isn’t there yet?
 Sometimes when you decide to want the process, the growth with or without the goal as the only measure of success you far surpass the goal, we see it all the time.  What is the benefit of doing this with uncertainty?

You asked about embodying your 100k self, so let’s make that real. Who do you need to become to make this inevitable? Not in a future sense but today What would you need to be doing  to make this  happen?

What does she think about when she wakes up?
How does she carry herself in conversations?
How does she invite people to calls?
What does she do in the hours where nothing is happening yet?

And from there, I’d get very practical. When you’re in belief, what is your actual action plan? Is it robust enough that you never run out of ways to serve, connect, and invite? Because belief paired with vague action will always feel shaky. Belief paired with clear, consistent action becomes self-reinforcing.

Then the other side of that when belief dips (because it will), what’s your plan? Not if, but when. How do you redirect your thinking and keep your actions moving so you don’t stall waiting to feel better first?

Where can you offer more value today? Who can you help today? If this goal were truly inevitable, what would you be doing right now that you might be holding back from?

If you were already a 200k coach in the room, what would you tell yourself today?

There’s something really powerful in what you’re doing you’re not just trying to hit a number, you’re learning how to lead your mind in the absence of evidence. That’s the skill.

I’m genuinely excited for you to join us in the 200K room coach!  You can feel that you’re close not because of the numbers yet, but because of the awareness you’re building. How will will you celebrate? Another great ITC!

Let’s create your success model from this place and then go execute.

What are your thoughts?

title: Day 28 / 30 – Consult evalutions
question:
Hi coaches,

So in one of my last messages I told you that I had gotten 2 consults in a week – so exciting! 1 of those calls turned out to be a no show. This was the person I met on Reddit, I’m not feeling all that concerned about it, some people just don’t show and that’s okay.

The second call I am just getting off now, it was a call that was booked after meeting in a virtual networking event. It was a really wonderful conversation, she left the call feeling inspired and better than when she came to the call, but was a no because she didn’t have the money to invest. She didn’t have a negative reaction but she did say “that’s a good price you’ve got there to keep your load light.” Something like that, I can find the exact words she used if you want to know, I recorded the call so I could do my own evaluation of it.

Anyway, she was a no because of the price because she is currently not making much money and is looking for work but said that she thinks she will be back in a few months when she is doing better financially. There was a part of me that wanted to ask what price would have made her a yes but I felt a bigger pull to stand in my commitment to the offer as it stands, I could even sense that I would cheapen the offer’s energetic value if I lowered the price for her, or I’d be signing someone from a state of compromise rather than empowerment and holding strong to my desire to sell at my current price point.

I notice thoughts coming up like:

“Why do I always attract people who are low on money?” but I followed that up with:

“Maybe that was true in the past but it doesn’t have to be true anymore.”

I used to lower my price until this specific type of person was able to pay comfortably, given their circumstances, & I didn’t do that today so I’m really proud of myself for that – even if that means I didn’t convert.

I also noticed that as the call was ending I was feeling really good, despite her not signing. I was thinking things like:

“That was such a good call, I helped her feel better and like her goals are possible, I invited her to network in the future when I create a group and she said yes, she may come back eventually, I could get another consult today, this was really fun, I felt really confident on that call, I really believed I could help her, it’s okay that some people are a no,….” and those are all really good thoughts and I feel empowered and excited to keep doing this!
answer:
Hey Coach,

Yes! First, great job celebrating the consults. In the beginning especially, just getting consults matters. When they book and don’t show, celebrate that too. This is part of the 8 phases of building a coaching business process and one of the phases of building.  Phases 1-7 are all no’s then you start getting yes’ . When you remind yourself, “this is a phase,” what do you notice happens in your brain?

Because even this, one person books and no-shows, another comes to the consult and says no… this is still movement. This is still evidence you’re getting in the room, practicing, refining, learning. So many people quit before they ever even get to this phase.  I also love how aware you were during the call and after it how you were thinking and feeling.

You said: “She was a no because she didn’t have the money to invest.” This is where I’d invite you to get really curious and put your coaching hat on for a minute. How do you know that’s actually why she said no? Does that mean she has the money just not to invest in coaching? I wonder why not to invest?

People often say “money,” but money is usually attached to a thought. It’s rarely just numbers. People buy things all the time they technically “don’t have the money” for when they deeply believe the value, trust themselves, trust the process, or believe the result is possible.

And this doesn’t mean she was lying or manipulating. She may genuinely not have the money right now. But there’s still value in exploring what’s underneath the objection because that’s where clarity lives.

One way you could explore it gently is something like:

“I completely understand, and honestly I hear that a lot. Would you be open to exploring something with me for a minute? If money wasn’t the issue, do you think there might still be a part of you that’s unsure? Maybe because you don’t know me well yet, or you’re unsure coaching works, or maybe you’re not fully convinced you’d follow through or get the result? Do any of those resonate?” Not to pressure her or try to convince her. But to help uncover what’s actually true for her. Fear can sound practical in her mind, deciding not invest if she is uncertain and unclear.

Sometimes “I don’t have the money” is really:

“What if this doesn’t work?”

“What if I fail again?”

“What if I invest and still don’t change?”

“What if I disappoint myself?”

I also really love the question you considered asking:

“What price would have made this a yes?” That’s actually a powerful question  not because you should change your price, but because it helps you understand what value she had in mind and what meaning she attached to the investment. It gives you insight into her thinking.

I’d also encourage you to revisit the Objections Module inside 2k The Client/Coach Models  and place her response into the model. Not so we can “be in her model” or assume we know exactly what she thinks, but because it helps train your brain to see beyond surface actions.

C — Offer

T — ?

F — ?

A — “I don’t have the money to invest.”

R — ?

What thought may have created that action? What feeling was driving it? Fear? Doubt? Scarcity? Uncertainty? Distrust in herself? That awareness helps you coach more deeply on future calls because you stop taking objections at face value and start listening for what’s underneath them.

And honestly, you have SO much to celebrate here. Especially not changing your offer the moment discomfort showed up. That’s huge growth. Before, you noticed you would lower your price to relieve your own discomfort and help the other person feel more comfortable. This time, you stayed grounded in the value of your work without collapsing into compromise. That’s a completely different energy.

Also notice how healthy your brain sounded after the consult ended. You weren’t spiraling into: “I failed.” “I’m bad at sales.” “No one will buy. Instead, you noticed:

“That was a great call.” “I helped her.” “I believed in what I offered.” “This was fun.”

“I can do this again. That shift is massive. That will create teh right energy to go again.

As you think about future consults, I’d get curious about this:

What might the client need to see, feel, or believe in order to trust the value of the work and trust themselves enough to say yes? Because often people are not just buying coaching. They are buying belief in a new future they cannot fully see yet.

And I really love how intentionally you kept directing your brain back toward growth, possibility, and evidence of progress instead of letting it run back to old stories. That is such important work.

title: Taking My Goal Seriously / Selling Intangibles
question:
I have a goal to support myself financially through my business. Currently I am able to pay for my personal bills, business bills, and discretionary spending (eating out, travel, shopping). This is a big step up from 2025 when I made $1200 total for the year. I am at about $9400 for 2026 so far.

The next step in achieving this goal is to be able to afford my own apartment and pay all of the costs associated with living on my own. Right now I live with my parents and don’t pay for housing or meals (unless I decide to go out to eat, but my parents are providing food).

And finally after that it will be contributing to my retirement, which I stopped doing when I left corporate in 2023.

So the stages are clear and I see myself making progress.

Yet, last year when my income went down and I only made $1200 the whole year I got scared and told my parents I would go to school to become a therapist so that I could have a more stable income. This was not actually what I wanted to do but I was so scared and I felt like I had no choice because I spent many months with $0 in my account and it was very scary.

They are incredibly on board with that plan, but have started encouraging me to stop working on my business altogether in order to give myself the best chance of success with preparing for and applying for school, plus completing the program and doing the licensing hours, etc.

The thing is, I know myself and no matter what I am going to show up for my business because it is the high point of my life. Even when I was making no money last year I showed up week after week to market and evaluate and get coached until I figured it out. I can’t imagine a world where I don’t work on my business and so since this is always going to be a part of my life I’m realizing I need to recommit to my plan of supporting myself with my business full time.

I’m crying even as I write this because I feel crazy. I have so much drama in my head telling me it’s impossible for me to support myself with my business despite the fact that I have actually made progress towards that point. I’m closer than I have ever been.

I don’t NEED to go to school, I just told mu parents I would, and now I’m realizing I’m scared they will be disappointed and possibly stop letting me live here if I tell them I am instead going to actually focus exclusively on supporting myself with my business, which was my plan before the $1200 year freaked me out.
answer:
Hi Coach,

Thank you for bringing this here. First let’s just pause to celebrate the fact that in 2025 you brought in $1200 but this year you’re already at $9400!!! Have you slowed down to get clear on what has created that? What thoughts, feelings, and actions? What you have been doing consistently to create those results?

If you haven’t already, spend some time doing that. If you can create $9400, you can create even more… especially once you know what is helping to create that.

What you desire sounds so clear – to be able to fully support your life with your business. Notice how the biggest “fear” holding you back is disappointing your parents and if they will be supportive of your choice. And of course that is there, because you’re human and I’m sure you are deeply grateful to your parents for their support (especially during the challenging times).

What may be super helpful here is getting clear on just how much you would need to bring in in order to support yourself at your own place. Seek out spots you are interested in, gather the financial information, and then start setting your business goals to support what you want to do. Almost as if you will “reverse engineer” the process.

Get coaching each time your mind starts to waiver in belief that it is possible.

Your goals are clear, now it’s asking “WHO do I need to be (or continue being) in order to create the results I am looking to achieve? You’re already doing this based on where you were in 2025 and what you have already accomplished so far in 2026…

And lastly, much of what you shared you’re feeling is absolutely normal as an entrepreneur. We operate a bit differently than those who clock in each day for a traditional job because we have a deep burning desire for what we do. In loving it so much and what it requires of us, we may often feel a little “crazy” and experience mind-drama as we work on our belief that we can do it. And you can, you can absolutely, undoubtedly do this if it’s what you really want.

So my suggestion is get clear on what
 is
 
working and how you’ve created the $9400 this year so far.

Then also get clear on the financials you’d also need to support yourself the way you desire and come to AAC for any coaching you need as it relates to the 2k process and you showing up in your business to get the results you want. Anywhere you feel stuck – we are happy to help you!

title: “Signing 3 clients in May is inevitable”
question:
Hey there! We’re heading into the last week of the month, and I’d love some support around this belief I’ve been building all month, and my overall goal of trying to qualify for the 200k mastermind.

My belief about 3 clients this month is definitely shifting down to a 3 from a 4 (on a scale of 1-5), mainly because there’s one week left of the month. And I’ve never had 3 sales calls in one week. But also! I had 2 sales calls in 1 week at the end of April – so actually, the possibility is still there.

I’m also improving with my sales calls (with some great coaching from you) and getting more comfortable with helping people explore their willingness to get uncomfortable with their finances in pursuit of their dreams. So if the sales calls appear on my calendar, my confidence in closing them has increased.

I’m continuing to take big action and daily work on my belief, especially around the value of writing a novel for moms and why it’s worth investing in help. I’d love some coaching on ways to maintain belief heading into the last week of the month, as well as some ideas for coming up with additional ideas to end the month.

I’ve also started to manage the potential disappointment – not assuming I’ll experience disappointment with the goal, but just responding to my brain with how I’ll treat myself and what I’ll do next if I miss the goal.

Thank you!
answer:
Hey Coach,

So glad you brought this to AAC. This is such important work because you’re not just trying to create 3 clients  you’re learning how to hold belief when the result isn’t here yet. That’s the real skill being built. That is valuable not just for this goal but everything you want in your life and when your clients struggle you have the road map!

And first, I want you to notice something really important: your awareness is increasing. At the start of the month your belief felt higher, and now you can feel it dipping as the month comes to an end and the results aren’t fully where you want them yet. That awareness matters because now you can actually work with it instead of unconsciously reacting to it.

Notice how your brain wants to use time and past evidence together:

“There’s only one week left.”

“I’ve never had 3 sales calls in one week.”

That sounds factual, but look at what it does to your energy and how you show up. Even micro shifts downward in belief change the way you think, market, invite, sell, and lead yourself.

It’s kind of like a car shifting down gears. The engine still works, but the output changes. The speed changes. The way the car moves changes.

So I would get very curious here:

What is different about you when your belief starts shifting down?

How do you show up differently in your actions, your energy, your willingness, your urgency?

Because often the actions matter less than the belief behind them. When your brain thinks, “There’s not enough time,” it makes sense that it subtly pulls back. It thinks it’s protecting you from disappointment.

But this is where coaching becomes so powerful.

As coaches, one of the greatest skills we can develop is believing in something before there’s evidence for it yet. That is the work. Creating belief instead of waiting for proof is where so much of your power is.

And I want you to notice — you already are stretching into new belief. You even caught yourself saying:

“I’ve never had 3 sales calls in one week… but I did have 2 at the end of April.”

That right there is your brain opening the door to possibility. That’s a good sign. It means you’re no longer fully anchored to your past.

Because the version of you that creates this result is not found in your past evidence. She exists in the decisions, thoughts, and actions you are practicing now.

I also love that you’re noticing your confidence on sales calls increasing. That matters. You’re not the same person you were a month ago. You’ve practiced. You’ve refined your skill. You’re becoming more willing to help people face financial discomfort in pursuit of their dreams instead of rescuing them from it. That changes everything.

I’d also play with this model a little:

C — Goal: Qualify for 200K Mastermind

T — What would you genuinely be thinking if you knew you qualified?

F — How would you feel?

A — What actions would that version of you take? What would she stop doing? Would she shift down… or double down? Would she brace for disappointment… or allow disappointment to be possible without making herself smaller?

R — What would that create?

And your question about maintaining belief at the end of the month is such a good one.

I’d ask yourself:

What thoughts do I already have access to that genuinely strengthen my belief?

What do I already know about myself that supports the possibility of this goal?

Why is this goal worth going all in for?

When I feel connected to my mission and the people I help, what ideas naturally come to mind?

What else is working and why?

What else do I know about creating clients today the 2k way?

Because belief isn’t always created by forcing yourself to think positively. Sometimes it’s created by reconnecting to your vision, your purpose, your growth, and the woman you are becoming through the process.

And I also want to offer this: stop treating disappointment like danger as something to brace for.

You mentioned managing potential disappointment, and I actually think that’s healthy if you’re doing it from acceptance instead of self-protection. There’s a difference between:

“I can handle disappointment if it comes,”

versus

“Let me emotionally prepare now by pulling my belief down ahead of time.”

One creates emotional resilience. The other weakens your power before the month is even over.

You still have time.

You still have possibility.

And regardless of the exact outcome this month, you are actively becoming the woman capable of creating bigger results. Don’t miss that part while measuring the calendar.

Keep going all in. We Can’t wait to have you join us int the 200k room!  This is just the beginning! Thank you coach, we love supporting you.

title: 05/28/2026 | sharing a win & A Day in 200K
question:
Hi coaches,

I came in here a few days ago asking for coaching on whether or not I should join A Day in 200K.

After sitting with it for a couple days I got honest with myself – the only reason I wouldn’t sign up is because “I don’t think I can afford it.”

So I decided to coach myself through that objection and what I saw was really interesting.

I boiled it down to asking myself this question: which story about myself am I verifying by the action I choose to take next?

1. If I don’t buy a seat then I’m verifying that I can’t afford this & I’m also backhandedly telling myself that I don’t believe I can sign a client in the next 2 weeks, the next month, the next however long my brain is telling me I will need to make it back by.

2. & if I do buy a seat then I am verifying that I believe in myself, that I believe in my ability to sign a client and soon, I’m verifying the belief that there are people out there that want to work with me and that I can find them.

Then the decision felt simple – even if I am making a semi “risky” financial choice by purchasing this ticket, I am still moving in the direction of belief in myself. & more than anything I centered into this thought: “I belong in this room.”

I belong in this room with people who are forward thinkers, who are already succeeding, some of them past where I am succeeding now, I belong in the room because I am one of them even if I can’t see it physically around me yet. I belong in the room because I know these women are all desiring and attempting to accomplish what I am – exponential growth.

I see how close I am to being accepted into the 200k room, it would really only take me signing 2 or 3 clients to meet the requirements. Wouldn’t be amazing and exciting if I did that in the next 2 weeks? I believe that’s possible. I believe that I know what I’m doing, that I’m getting better everyday, that the courage to take bold action is coursing through me and my capacity to hold it and maintain it is growing.

I know I have something truly valuable to offer, more than I ever have before, I know that the right people will spend a year with me and be truly transformed, I know that my offer is a no-brainer. Of course I can make the money back, I can make EVEN MORE back.

All things to say, the decision was obvious once I saw all of this & I will see you in A Day in 200K 🤍, and soon I will be back to celebrate signing a client!
answer:
Hey Coach! I just want to celebrate this with you. What stands out isn’t that you bought the ticket. It’s the quality of the conversation you had with yourself before you did! You slowed down long enough to see what story each option was reinforcing, and then you made a decision from the version of yourself you want to become rather than the fear that initially showed up. That’s so powerful – kudos to you!

I especially love hearing, “I belong in this room.” YES! The self-concept and self-trust you practiced in arriving at that conclusion is amazing. Thank you for sharing this win with us. We can’t wait to hear what happens next, and love seeing you intentionally choose thoughts and actions that align with the future you’re building.

See you at A Day in 200K, Coach!

title: No Clients – Feeling Low
question:
I have been feeling up and down lately with my business…. which is a testament to how well I can pull myself back together. But the pattern has been more like a roller coaster vs just every once in a while.

I have not had any consults since October 2025, where I signed a client for my six-month, 1:1 program.

I also have years of not getting consults. And that thought seems to come up in the back of my mind during these down times.

I tend to ask myself what is wrong with me? And I look at others in the various programs I’m in of Stacey’s, and start telling myself they are doing well for this reason or that reason, and I’m just not like that. I only think these things when I’m feeling down, though.

I post consistently on different social media sites. And this month I created 3 free offers, 1/wk, where one person reached out for the free coaching. She’s also a friend and won’t be someone I work with. I was expecting more engagement overall. The thought enters my mind, ‘I can’t even give it away.’

I got my last client because I knew her from 2k, and she was local to me, so we became friends. She heard more specifically about what I do from a networking event and pulled me aside, saying she thought she needed to work with me. I thought she was joking at first.

But my last few clients over the years have been friends also.

Which leads me to think I need to go to more networking events, or do things socially, etc, but it takes so much time from my schedule and having a form of social anxiety, I loathe going. I loathe get-togethers most of the time.

There’s so much more, but we can start here.
answer:
Hi Coach!

Thanks for bringing this here. Happy to help you dig in.

It’s quite easy for our brain to start pulling old evidence forward when things feel quieter in the business again, especially after going a stretch without consults. At the same time, I’d like to celebrate how aware you are of your own patterns and how actively you try to pull yourself back together when you dip – great work in doing that.

I’m curious what meaning your brain attaches to consults not happening right now. For example, you mentioned that during lower moments, your brain starts telling you that other people are doing well 
“for this reason or that reason”
 and that you’re 
“just not like that.”

Can you share more specifically what your brain means by that?
 What qualities, traits, abilities, lifestyles, personalities, strategies, etc., does your brain think other coaches have that are helping them succeed… that you don’t feel connected to or believe you possess yourself? I’d love some specific examples so we can slow those thoughts down and look at them more closely.

I’m also curious about the way your brain is interpreting the clients who 
have
 come to you through friendships or more personal connection. 
Could there be something meaningful there about the environments where you naturally shine, build trust, or feel safest being yourself?
 Of course it doesn’t mean that you “can only” get clients that way, but it could be some feedback worth paying attention to in order to figure out creative ways to make those connections.

Lastly, here is what I’d be curious to know:

Who do you coach and what is your offer (ideal client/package/pricing/what they get, etc.,)?

What conversations make you feel energized afterward? What do people naturally come to you for already?

What are some of your goals for your business that you’re working toward? Be specific.

It feels like there’s an opportunity to get curious about the stories that become loud during slower seasons, while also re-connecting to the kind of coach and business owner you genuinely want to be! Let’s start here. Bring back your answers and we will continue to help you. Thanks Coach!

title: Stepping Up and Making a Plan
question:
Hello, I know that this is for the 2K process. I want to share a bit about me, I joined $2K in November, Behind the Scenes in December and Entrepreneur Coach in January. To say that there was a firehose of information coming in is an understatement..lol. I currently am working through the 2K process for the second time. I’m feeling stable and sure footed and ready to launch my coaching business.

I truly believe that I have all that I need to become a successful life coach and to create a thriving business.

title: Feeling stuck
question: I’ve been making less money the last few months and it’s really starting to get to me. I think I was triggered by my highest month of all time in December ($7,000) and it scared me. I think because I’m not “supposed” to make money like that. So I started focusing on other things. I created multiple offers, I ran a retreat, I’m planning another one and have a new offer in addition to that. I have a million ideas, I show up every day, I love what I do, I believe in myself and also I made $1,600 last month. What is going on? Can you help me through this block?
answer:
Hey there coach!

Happy to help. Let’s dig into that $7,000 month. First, big congrats! Celebrating that – it’s amazing!

Now let’s address feeling triggered by it.

1. 
What are the thoughts you noticed arising once you hit that 7k month?

2.
 You said, “I am not suppose to make money like that.”

How come?
 Let’s dig into some of the underlying, sneaky thoughts there.

Why aren’t you “supposed” to make money like that? 

What does it mean about you when you do?

3. You shared that you made $1600 last month, what are you making that mean about you and/or your business?

 You say you have a million ideas and things you’re executing:
