It sounds like after hitting that high of a month and it feeling unfamiliar to your body, you (possibly) began doing things differently than you had been… even if that meant your mindset shifted, belief shifted, or your actions changed… This makes sense as your brain didn’t know how to “be with” the results you created. What is important to mention though is that the shift in income doesn’t 
necessarily
 mean anything has “gone wrong”. Still, let’s explore it together and see!

Take some time to answer the questions above and then come back with your answers so we can keep coaching!

Thanks coach!

title: 36/44 Sign 1 more client by 3/31
question:
So far, I’ve signed 2 clients! I’m so close. I have 8 days & I have some thoughts.

Those 2 clients came from my podcast & had been following me for a while. I don’t feel like my IG marketing did anything to create those clients. It felt like I “waited” for those clients to come. This makes me feel like in the 8 days, nothing I do will actually create clients because I’ve been creating content, sending emails, etc. and that doesn’t seem to be converting. Also, I get intimidated by the thought of creating $4k of value (price of program) in every post, thought, value I share. And that feels daunting. To think of a piece of content to have $4k worth of value. My thought is: “My brain can’t do that. It can’t think that valuable. That’s a stretch.” I’m not very cerebral or book smart. My brother did soo good at the ACT/SAT but I didn’t. I excelled in having a high GPA & being super involved. I believe I’m smart but idk, there’s levels. Level 1: “street smart Level 2: Tenacity smart Level 3: Delayed Gratification Smart, Level 4: Create New Ideas Smart, Level 5: Offer Unique “Unheard Of” Perspectives Smart

I’m at Level 3 and I don’t know if I “have what it takes” to get to level 4 & 5. I know I can create some value (I’ve hit $100k in 2024 and $50k in 2025). So I know I’m creating some value and that’s why I get some results. But Level 4 & 5I feel like is the place where I have to take my brain to actually hit bigger goals.

Unintentional Model:

C: 8 days left to sign 1 more clients so I can hit my goal by my deadline

T: Creating that much value is going to be hard

T: I’m not sure I can creat that much value in such a short amount of time

F: discouraged, dumb, sad

A: silently give up, keep posting but then decide “they’ll come when they come,” maybe put out 2 podcast/week to “try harder,” procrastinate, wait for “new month” to come to have a ssense of “reset”, tell myself “I can extend the deadline to Apr 8”

R: I make it so that I for sure don’t create that much value

Intentional Model:

T: I know how to bring in sales, I’ve created momentum before, I know what energy I need to be in

F: relief, less pressure, curious

A: Go back to rewatch that one time I made an offer out of excitement and someone booked, remember that feeling/thought, get curious at my best guess of $4k for each post, keep taking actions & evaluating

R: Create my best attempt of $4k of value for the next 8 days
answer:
Hi Coach!

First, let’s slow down just a bit and celebrate that you’ve already signed 2 clients! Don’t bypass how amazing that is… that means things are working! Before we make anything else mean something negative, I want you to slow down and really look at where you are. 
What 
has
 been working? What 
energy
 have you been in this month? What 
have you been thinking and believing
 when those clients said yes?
 Because that didn’t happen by accident. You created that – even if they have been following a while and have been listeners of the podcast.

The same way they found you, so can others. Instead of trying to become a completely different version of you in the next 8 days, what if your only job was to 
keep being her?

Right now your brain is trying to move the finish line by making this about whether you’re “smart enough” or capable of creating $4k value in a post. That’s not actually the problem to solve. You’ve already proven you can create value. You’ve made $100k before and you’ve signed clients. This is about 
staying in the energy that creates movement,
 not overcomplicating what value has to look like.

What if you dropped the idea that every post needs to be worth $4k? Only keep it if it feels exciting and fun these next 8 days… not from pressure to perform. That’s a lot of pressure for something that isn’t even true. People don’t buy because of one perfectly crafted, genius-level piece of content, they buy because over time, they feel something from you. They trust you and see themselves in what you say. 
What if your only job for the next 8 days was to show up consistently, speak clearly, make offers, and let that be enough?

Think about this like a foot race. You started running at the beginning of the month with a goal to cross the finish line. You’re in the last stretch now, and of course fatigue and doubt are showing up. That’s when it always happens. But the only way you don’t cross the finish line is if you stop running before you reach it. If you step off the track. If you decide ahead of time it’s not going to work and pull your effort back. Do your best not to do that. This is where your emotional capacity has to stretch – you’ve got this.

Instead of focusing on whether you’ll “win” or not, I want you to focus on 
how you want to feel about yourself when these 8 days are over.
 Imagine finishing the race knowing you never stopped and that you kept going even when it felt uncomfortable, even when your brain was loud, and even when you weren’t sure of the outcome.

What would THAT version of you do over the next 8 days? Would she hold the vision while releasing the fear of it not working? Would she keep making offers? Would she stay connected to the people already in her world instead of waiting for new ones? Would she trust that momentum is already in motion and she just has to keep doing what she has been?

What do you think?

title: #3/30 days I am in control of 10k months
question:
10K a month me plans ahead and follows through, redirects her brain to what’s valuable and not what’s comfortable; and is skilled at not only redirecting her brain when needed but being fully present and in service on consults. from that knowing, my answers to your last coaching is this:

I can plan better for myself by deciding when I’ll sit down and calendar for the following week (Friday). I’ll create a list of projects that need to be completed and also a ‘white space’ list of things I can do when I find myself with extra time but don’t want to buffer. I am also going to ensure that my off-time is scheduled as well. I will follow through on these things and get coached on what’s not working.

To follow through, I’ll need to believe “I can have it all. I DO have it all and there’s plenty of time to do it all; 10 women are watching me closely, talking themselves into working with me; I have the solution to her problem and need to get it out. I’d feel focused ,compelled, empowered and creative/not boxed in.

Money objection -if I believe it wasn’t about the money, I’d be more curious and lean in with questioning to create a space where they tell me what’s coming up. I’d expect money to come up as an objection because my clients live in survival and lack. I’d create a better space to discuss this BEFORE we get to money. because they are hesitant at moving forward the same as they are hesitant to show up for their goals, take action despite what people think.

As far as the big wins my. clients are gaining, I’m not sure why I’m disconnected to it. there’s a block of some sort that keeps me from connecting to the power of coaching. the power of the space I help my clients with. it’s like that’s not even me doing it or helping them. it doesn’t feel massive.it doesn’t feel compelling at times. I do have small moments where I”m in theenrgy of wow I am really shifting womens lives but for the most part it feels meh when I’m alone thinking about it.
answer:
Hey coach!

When I read your last paragraph, the line that stood out most was when you said 
“I’m not sure why I’m disconnected to it… it’s like that’s not even me doing it or helping them.”
 That’s a very honest observation 
(thanks for sharing)
, and it’s a useful place to look at your thinking.

One thing I want you to consider is the meaning your brain might be giving to the 
feeling
 itself. You mentioned that when you’re alone thinking about your clients’ wins, it sometimes doesn’t feel “massive” or “compelling” and can feel a little “meh.” But the emotional intensity we feel about something isn’t always the measure of the impact it’s actually having.

Here’s what I mean:

Think about professions like surgeons, therapists, or teachers. They can help someone in a life-changing way, and yet on a random evening at home they may not be sitting there feeling a huge emotional surge about it. The work they are doing still matters and the impact is still very real, it’s just that the feeling isn’t always loud in every moment. Can that be okay?

I’d love for you to sit with this question for a bit:

When you say you feel disconnected from your clients’ results, what are you expecting that experience to feel like instead?

You also wrote that sometimes it feels like it’s not even you doing it or helping them. That’s a really fascinating thought for a coach to have, because it opens up an important distinction about coaching itself. Remember, coaching works because 
the client’s brain changes. 
Not because we as coaches force any sort of result. Our role as coaches is to create the space, ask the questions, challenge the thinking, and guide them back to their own authority. The transformation happens in them because 
they
 engage with that work. So when a client creates a breakthrough, the result really comes from both you and the client. You created the environment where it became possible, and they chose to step into it.

So another question to explore is this:
 when your clients create results, what part of that process do you see as yours? 
Was it holding space? Asking powerful questions? Showing them their mind? What would your answer be?

And the last place I’d get curious is simply noticing what your brain does in those moments when you reflect on their wins and the “meh” feeling shows up. 
What are the exact thoughts you notice yourself thinking in those moments?

Just getting curious about the meaning your brain is giving the experience will likely show you a lot. Take some time to reflect and answer these questions and then bring back whatever you may still want some coaching on. Thanks coach!

title: day 2 / 30 – how do I overcome the thought that I’m no longer an expert?
question:
I saw a lot of success in my first year of coaching (2022), I had multiple clients (4 or 5 one on one), I was connecting with new people constantly, I had a mastermind that ran for 4 months (6 women), & I was doing so well that I felt confident to start traveling abroad while working. I made about $25k that first year, my prices were VERY low but I was VERY confident that I could guide transformation. Anyone who wanted to work with me was welcome, & I would lower my price if they needed me to until they were a yes. Once I got to Bali, I stalled out. I relied on my current clients and stopped talking about my work with new people, I tried posting to social media but got scared and would delete everything, I deleted nearly 50 podcast episodes I’d recorded the year before, I signed no new clients. Eventually I ran out of money and had to move home.

I have maintained working with at least 2 clients monthly since then. Usually repeat clients who have been with me for years or referrals. When people leave it’s because they can’t afford to stay on. I live with my brother now and he is housing me while I work on my business and in the last year I have started posting to socials every day, to my podcast weekly, I make offers in every post and episode. I have had 2 new clients sign and have 1 client who has been on for years. I’ve made less than $12k in the last 12 months.

I just watched the video about positioning yourself as the expert and came up with this model:

C – Living with my brother, no car, 2 paying clients, less than $1k/month income

T – “I can no longer position myself as an expert as I used to because I lost my original results that made me FEEL like an expert.” “I care about my clients and don’t want to fuck up their lives like I fucked up mine.”

F – Dejected, ashamed

A – Hesitate to sell / don’t make clear/confident offers, undercharge, don’t position myself as someone worth buying from, change niche and messaging often

R – I’m not seen as an expert / no one buys

Preferred model

C – Living with my brother, no car, 2 paying clients, less than $1k/month income

T – “I am grateful for the safety of where I am, it is possible for me to gain success again, I can learn from my mistakes, I can do better, I am willing to let go of the past, it is possible for me to become the person who has a successful business.”

F – hopeful

A – show up and make offers with confidence

R – it becomes possible for me to gain success in my business again
answer:
Hey there, coach!

First, let’s acknowledge something big. You picked action back up, you’re posting daily, you’re making offers, and you signed two new clients….That is not the behavior of someone “unqualified.” That is the behavior of someone rebuilding momentum! Don’t forget to take a step back and really celebrate that. It may not be where you want to be in your business, but you have pulled yourself back up – that’s a big deal, so kudos to you.

Now let’s address what is really happening. In looking at your unintentional model, you’re equating 
positioning
 with your current income and lifestyle. You wrote, 
“I can no longer position myself as an expert because I lost the results that made me FEEL like an expert.”

Notice what happened there: 
You didn’t say you “lost your skill”, or that you “don’t know how to coach.”

You said you lost the feeling and feelings are fluid. They aren’t permanent. They are present based on our thoughts.

You can separate your positioning from what you’re feeling – what I mean is: You are not “an expert” because of your current address. It’s not where you live that makes you an expert. It’s not your bank account that makes you an expert. It’s the skills you’re equipped with that help clients. When you started in 2022, you had made zero dollars, and yet you positioned yourself as a coach. 
Why?
 
Because you were steps ahead of the people you were helping. 
That hasn’t changed at all. No one can take your skills away from you.

Your clients are not hiring you to ask about your living situation or to peer into your bank account. They are hiring you to coach 
their thinking
. Your qualification lives in your ability to see their brain, interrupt their patterns, hold the standards they have for themselves, and guide their transformation. None of that disappeared when your income dropped. The only thing that changed was your self-perception.

When you make your current circumstances mean you “fucked up your life,” you unconsciously protect your clients from you by shrinking. That creates shame. You don’t need to convince yourself 
(or anyone else)
 you’re successful again. You need to separate your current season from your 
capacity as a coach
. Those are different things. And the amazing news is, you’re already proving this!

Two new clients signed. Your long-term clients stay. You sign referrals (which means people are talking about how amazing you are). That is market feedback. The work now is simple: stop making your “positioning” about your current season of life. Positioning is about 
who you can help and how,
 not about where you live. You were qualified before you made $25k. You’re STILL qualified now. The only shift required is selling from your skill instead of from self-image. And you’re already taking the actions that support that. Keep going!

What are your thoughts? Feel free to come back with anything you may still want coaching on! We are happy to help.

title: Is it possible that my price is too low?
question:
Dear Ask a Coach, is this what is happening? I’m from Croatia (Europe), I charge 1.000 EUR (1.150 USD) for 3 months 1:1 coaching (stress and burnout for women in corporate). I made 15.000 EUR in the last 9 months (have 15 clients so far). Is it possible that I’m charging too little, and when people hear that I charge 1000 EUR for this kind of work, they flake – like: in their mind, the value doesn’t match the price.

I’m already at a level where I believe that 2.000 EUR is a perfect price for what I’m offering, and yet I am not raising the price until I’m full (12 – 15 clients regularly + 3 – 5 consults ahead). Love to hear your guidance on this.
answer:
Hello Coach,

Welcome from Croatia!

Before we can know whether you’re charging “too little”, I’d want to understand why you’ve concluded that price is what’s causing people to “flake.”

What specifically is happening that makes you think, “The value doesn’t match the price in their mind”?

The reason I’m asking is because our brains are very good at filling in the blanks
. Someone doesn’t buy, and we immediately create a story about why. But if we’re solving a problem, we want to make sure we’re solving the actual problem not the one we’ve imagined.

Right now, here are the facts:

You offer 3 months of 1:1 coaching for burnout and stress for women in corporate.

You charge 1,000 EUR.

You’ve enrolled 15 clients and generated 15,000 EUR in the last 9 months.

So if 1,000 EUR is automatically signaling “low value,” how did 15 people decide to work with you at that price?

That’s why I’d be curious to explore what has changed.

When you first started selling this offer at 1,000 EUR, what were you thinking about it? What are you thinking about it now?

Sometimes the offer hasn’t changed. The price hasn’t changed. But the coach’s relationship with the price has changed. All normal it’s going to change that is good we can change the way we think on purpose about the price.

You shared that you already believe 2,000 EUR is a more appropriate price for the work you do. That stood out to me.

When you think, “This should really be 2,000 EUR, but I’m selling it for 1,000 EUR,” how do you feel?

Do you feel fully convicted?

Do you feel generous?

Do you feel resentful?

Do you feel like you’re underselling yourself?

Because how we feel about our pricing often shows up in how we present it. Clients can feel our certainty just as much as they can feel our doubt.

It’s a little like selling a house. The house may be exactly the same, but if the seller keeps apologizing for the price, buyers start wondering what they’re missing.

I’m also curious why you’re waiting until you’re full to raise your rates.

Do you genuinely like that reason?

Or are you borrowing someone else’s pricing strategy while your own thinking has already evolved?

There’s nothing wrong with following the guidance Stacey offers of raising prices once you’re fully booked. That strategy works for many coaches. But it only works when it aligns with your beliefs.

If part of you already believes the offer is worth 2,000 EUR, and another part of you is telling yourself you aren’t allowed to charge that yet, there may be some internal friction worth looking at.

I’d also challenge the assumption that people are not converting because they think the price is too low. 
Have you asked people why they decided not to move forward?

What evidence do you have that  pricing is the reason?

If price wasn’t the explanation, what else might be?

Maybe they aren’t convinced they need help yet.

Maybe they aren’t prioritizing the problem.

Maybe they’re afraid of change.

Maybe your sales process has shifted.

Maybe your messaging has shifted.

Maybe nothing has changed at all, and you’re simply noticing normal sales variability through a different lens.

The goal isn’t to convince yourself the price is right or wrong. The goal is to understand what’s actually happening. 
And then decide intentionally.

What are your thoughts about raising your price now?

What reasons do you have for doing it?

What reasons do you have for not doing it?

Most importantly, do you like those reasons?

Bring your answers back here to Ask a Coach, and we can coach more deeply on what’s underneath this.

title: How to overcome resistance to being a coach because I am worried I would not be effective at getting people to make changes
question: I realise I am avoiding attracting coaching clients (I haven’t done this yet!) because I fear that if I made a promise and signed a client I would not be able to get them results and I fear this. How can I offer coaching to people, promising to help them get results, with integrity when I am not sure this is true? Do I need to find a way to start where I offer something for free and get results? But when you offer things for free, my fear is the people won’t be committed and so I definitely wont’ get results. Change is hard and people resist change – and I am not good at helping them overcome resistance so they get change. How can I give myself evidence that I can get results and can therefore offer coaching with integrity? Thanks for coaching on this 🙂
answer:
Hi Coach!

Let’s start simple with this:

When you’ve felt resistant to change, how did coaching help you? What did you gain by being coached? What did you learn?

It sounds like you are very aware that sometimes people resist change (and yes this is true), but something else that is true is that when people are suffering or unhappy with something, change is very much welcomed. The resistance comes from some of the hard work of changing beliefs or patterns we’ve held onto.

When people seek out a coach, they
 typically
 want something in their life to be different than it currently is.

So in knowing this, how do coaches help someone get there?

We can’t force them, or do it for them… but we can coach their brain. We can help them see their own mind. We can ask powerful questions that make them reflect. Part of how we help clients get results is by showing them how they have co-created their current situation… and helping them create new thoughts, feelings, habits/behaviors/actions, that change their results.

What has a coach maybe done for you? How would you say they helped you?

And how confident do you feel doing the same for your client when you think about what 
really
 
helped you?

Take some time to reflect on these questions and then bring back your answers/any thoughts or coaching you may still need. We are happy to help. Think about the results you want your clients to get and what you think it’ll take to help them get there. Anywhere you may be feeling stuck after reflecting, bring back here for more coaching. Thanks coach!

title: Restarting 10
question:
What immediately comes up when you think about making 10k net?

It is too much, how can I earn 10 k from April to December 2026 (I believe that the approval of my external activity next to my current job will come by the end of March). This is too many clients?!

This leads me to the second question (and your answer) on capacity – I currently have 2 practice clients next to my job. Do I have capacity to have more? I have a three months package, meaning that I need to have like 20 clients by December 2026. This is not possible next to my job, family and kids, regardless how I extend my capacity.

What is the extended capacity that I am capable of holding?

Id say 3 clients at the same time, this is with the time I have left, 9 clients.

10k net with 9 clients and occasional team workshops?

My package is priced at 490 EUR, so 10k net wont happen with 9 clients.

I need to redraft my plan and believe in it.

Selling 3 packages after my approval gets in. I am not allowed to presell, I can loose my job and benefits I have gathered over the years.

Selling 3 packages twice more by the end of the year. So 9 clients.

and then the workshops: if I sell 10, I have 290 per workshop. 2900 plus clients contracts c 4000

So im not at 10k

But can this also be enough proof to actually go fully in? (I work 45 hours per week plus commute time, so it is a lot and this will of course be then dedicated either to my business or family)

I have to say, I am a bit confused at the moment as to how to make 10 k in 9 months (actually 8 months, since I have one months project in the summer where I wont be able to do anything extra)
answer:
Hi Coach, Let’s slow this down and look at what’s actually happening in your thinking. There is a lot of awareness here.

The original coaching asked you to identify the thoughts you have about the result you want to create so you can begin building belief around the 10K goal. And you did exactly that, you showed us the thoughts that come up.

Your circumstance is simple: you want to create 
10K between April and December.

But notice the thoughts that immediately attach to that:

“It’s too much.”
“This is too many clients.”

Then when you look at capacity:

“This is not possible next to my job, family, and kids.”
“Regardless of how I extend my capacity, it’s not possible.”

Before we solve the strategy, it’s important to see what your brain has already concluded. Your brain has already decided the result is 
too big and not possible
. When the brain believes that, the emotion that usually follows is confusion or overwhelm  and from that place, clear planning becomes very difficult.

So the first step is simply noticing that this is thinking, not fact.

And at the same time, I agree with something important you pointed out: 
the current math may not be working.
Sometimes confusion happens because our brain senses that the numbers and the structure of the plan don’t actually line up yet. So there are really two parts of the work here:

Find math that works.

Build belief that you can execute that math within the life you have.

Right now your brain is trying to jump straight to 
how
 while believing it’s impossible. That’s a very hard place to plan from.

You want to create 10K in about eight months. When the brain cannot see a path, confusion is a very natural reaction. The work now is to turn the result into a plan, and then the coaching becomes about who you need to become to execute that plan.

This is where the idea of 
who before how
 becomes very useful. Check out the module in the portal.

First: 
If the result is 10K, what actions would have to happen?
When we map actions first, the result becomes less abstract and more tangible.

Next: 
What do you already know about your capacity right now? 
You mentioned you believe you could hold three clients at a time. That’s important data. It helps define the boundaries you’re working inside.

Then the question becomes: 
Given that capacity, what would the math of 10K need to look like?

This might involve:

a certain number of packages

a different price point

workshops or group offers

or a combination

Sometimes the insight we discover is that the offer structure needs to evolve, not that the goal is impossible.

If 10K cannot be created with the current offer and time available, what would need to change for the math to work?

Maybe it’s pricing.
Maybe it’s the type of offer.
Maybe it’s how time is allocated.

If you didn’t allow yourself to stay in confusion, what answer would start to appear?

Confusion often feels very real, but it can also become a place we sit in instead of experimenting with possible solutions. Clarity usually comes from testing ideas, adjusting the math, and seeing what’s actually possible. Right now the thoughts driving your planning are:

“I don’t have the capacity.”
“This is not possible.”

But planning becomes much more powerful when the thought shifts slightly to something like: “Let me figure out what would make this possible.”You also asked a really thoughtful question at the end: whether creating something like 9 clients plus workshops could be enough proof to go all in later.

That’s a very powerful way to think about this year not only as a revenue goal, but also as evidence building. Evidence that you can create clients, deliver value, and grow something alongside your current job.

Look again at the 10K result over eight months and ask yourself:

What version of this plan would I actually believe in?

What would the math need to look like for that belief to grow?

What kind of value would I need to create in the world for 10K to be a natural result?

Because at the end of the day, money follows value. And the real work is becoming the version of you who 
c
reates that value consistently.

That’s where the plan and the mindset begin to meet. Please take your time to answer and feel free to bring it back here for further coaching .

title: Follow up: Help me work through my feelings of disappointment and discouragement 051826
question:
Thank you for your compassion. I feel so heard. I appreciate you reminding me that this work, coaching, my clients, and my business matter deeply to me.

I notice I worry that I won’t sign clients if I feel bad (disappointed, dejected, discouraged). Ouch – this perspective isn’t helpful.

My habit is to push those feelings of discouragement and sadness away – to resist feeling them because I worry that it means I won’t ever be a success.

I also have a habit of isolating, so I’m pleased that I reached out to you – I am evolving.

Pushing away looks like staying very busy, working on another project, and avoiding the feelings of disappointment/discouragement. I can see this doesn’t help, and in fact, suppressing, denying, and should-ing all over myself leaves me feeling ashamed and inferior.

A couple of models

C My biz

T I’ve done so much and it’s not working

F Discouraged

A Rush to find another “to do” to stay busy. Don’t sit with the feeling, avoid the feeling. tense up, and get tunnel vision. Tighten my neck and back muscles (defensively). Lots of pressure, forcing, rushing. Don’t notice the physical sensation of the emotion. Don’t acknowledge how I’m feeling and don’t give myself grace. I forget that everyone experiences ups and downs. I forget to deeply acknowledge the joy of seeing the clients I do have grow. Forget that it’s a process.

R I don’t do much in the present, so “it doesn’t work, or rather I don’t work, (even though I tell myself I’ve done so much in the past)

Also,

C My biz

T I’ve done so much, and it’s not working

F Entitled

A Tell myself it should be working seamlessly now 100% of the time- feeling very spoiled and entitled. Act frustrated and close down – do this by tightening my face and clenching my jaw. Stay stuck and don’t try anything new. Don’t evaluate and see what has actually worked, what hasn’t, and what’s changed/shifted. Forget that I want this business and that I’m blessed to have found something I love to do. Forget that I have clients. Forget that people pay me to do this work (instead of telling myself “it’s not enough”). Don’t create a long list of things that could work. Don’t dig into the 2k consult process and get good at it. Don’t decide that lots/if not all ways can work – and remind myself my thoughts create my outcome.

R: It doesn’t work, not because it won’t or can’t but because I’m so stuck on myself and feeling entitled that it should be easier than it currently is.

Thanks
answer:
Hi Coach,

I am so glad you received so much from the coaching. You’ve done such a beautiful job with these models, and the specificity matters here because it shows you are really seeing what these thoughts and patterns create in real time. That awareness is powerful.

What stands out to me most is that the discouragement itself is not actually the problem. The resistance to feeling discouraged is what seems to create the spiral. You described it so clearly the rushing, tightening, avoiding, tunnel vision, overworking, searching for the next thing to do. It makes sense why you feel exhausted inside of that.

And I also want you to notice something important: you reached out instead of isolating. That matters. That is evolution that is interrupting the pattern.

I think it could be really useful now to start shifting from studying the problem to intentionally studying the version of you you are becoming. If you take yourself to where you ultimately want to go, what does the model of success actually look like? What does the coach who creates the business she wants think when things are temporarily slow or uncomfortable?

Not because she never feels discouraged, but because she no longer makes discouragement mean the dream is failing and that it will never work, learning in the process what works and what doesn’t work willing to test and iterate.

Right now, it sounds like the thought “it’s not working” immediately narrows your focus so much that you stop seeing evidence that things 
are
 working. You stop seeing your clients, your growth, your skills, your evolution, your ability to connect, your willingness to keep learning. It’s almost like the brain starts scanning only for what is missing instead of what is already being built.

So instead of asking, “Why isn’t this working yet?” maybe the more useful question is:

“What does success require from me today?” 
That question opens possibility instead of pressure.

Maybe success today looks like meeting one new person.

Maybe it looks like adding value somewhere instead of evaluating yourself all day.

Maybe it looks like practicing your 2K energy before the evidence arrives.

Because the energy of someone building a successful business is very different from the energy of someone waiting to feel certain first.

I also think your awareness around entitlement is insightful and honest. There’s a difference between wanting ease and believing growth should feel seamless 100% of the time. Businesses require refinement. Adjustments. Repetition. Evaluation. Not because you’re failing, but because mastery is created through willingness to keep engaging with the process.

What if instead of making discomfort mean “this isn’t working,” you allowed it to mean: 
“I’m in the middle of becoming someone who can hold more.”

Higher-value thoughts could sound like:

“I’m learning what works and what doesn’t, and I can adjust.”

“I’m capable of creating results one step at a time.”

“I know how to reconnect instead of retreat.”

“I can feel discouraged and still move forward.”

“I am building this.”

And when hopelessness or discouragement starts creeping in, that’s the moment to intentionally direct your mind again. A podcast, a 2K call, coaching, revisiting process work not to escape your feelings, but to help you access thoughts that create movement instead of paralysis.

Then use that energy to take action. Even small actions compound over time.

You do not need to become someone who never feels discouraged.

You are becoming someone who no longer abandons herself when she does.

Great work coach.  What do you notice in your models and what do you want the Intentional model to look like when you aer in high value thinking?

title: $ Objections
question: I have a potential client who’s been following my work. She approached me this week about my services, I explained I have a 5 Day cleanse, a 30 day, 6 month and a year program. We talked about what her pain points are and how I can help her. She left, what seemed to me excited and eager to get started. She then texted me and said: Ty for taking the time to explain everything to me. I really appreciate it. I had a chance to go through your website again today and I’m honestly so excited and would love to start your program. This is something I’ve had in mind for such a long time. Unfortunately, financially it’s just not the right moment. I recently signed my daughter up for 5wk camp and officially broke LOL. just need to postpone for now, but I truly hope I can join in the near future. Thank you. My thoughts- it’s not a $ objection, it’s other things (as is usually the case). I have multiple offers at multiple different prices from $97- to 25K so it’s not a $ objection. I’m finding myself in a dilemma, do I release and focus on clients who are ready now, or do I coach her through the price objection. I was thinking I can ask her which program she was looking at and explain she can get started with a lower priced program for now and experience what it’s like to work with me and get the results. Can you help me navigate these $ objections I keep hearing and help coach me to step into the coach who’s no longer attracting these types of clients. What am I thinking and not seeing that’s prob so obvious to you as an outside coach. Ty
answer:
Hey coach!

First, let’s slow down a moment to celebrate. This woman reached out to you, told you she’s been following your work, said she’s excited about your programs, and shared that this is something she’s been wanting to do for a long time. What a compliment of the work you’re doing! A lot of times when we “almost” signed the client but didn’t, we immediately jump into trying to solve the objection and forget to celebrate what 
has been
 working. Clearly who you are, and how you show up is working. Women are watching and they are coming to you – we just need to figure out why they “almost” sign up.

Right now all we actually know is what she told you: “financially it’s not the right moment for her.” You mentioned that you think it’s not really a money objection. Maybe it is, maybe it isn’t. We don’t actually know yet, so your job is 
simply to decide how you want to lead from here.

One thing I love that you already hinted towards is what you would focus on if you were thinking about other clients who are ready.

I like to ask the question of, 
“how would you respond if you had ten clients ready to pay you right now?”
 
That’s a really powerful place to lead from. When coaches are in that position 
(where they believe there are other clients ready to buy right now without objection),
 they usually respond to “almosts” with warmth and respect, but don’t spend a lot of energy on those who just said no. They leave the door open and keep their energy with the people who are ready.

That said, there’s absolutely nothing wrong with gathering more information if you want to. This is a personal choice. You could simply ask which program she had in mind when she was looking through your site. Just make sure you can do it from a clean place where it’s coming from genuine curiosity. The energy in which you approach it can be felt by the client and that’s what you want to keep in mind. If you do ask, it’ll help you understand what she was actually considering instead of you guessing 
(if she is willing to share).

You also mentioned that you have offers ranging from $97 all the way to $25k. If you genuinely believe one of your lower priced offers could be a meaningful place for her to start, you’re welcome to mention that. Again, just keep the energy clean. You’re offering a pathway, not trying to convince someone who already told you it’s not the right time.

The bigger coaching I want to offer you is around the part where you said you want to become the coach who no longer attracts these types of clients. Every coach, even very successful ones, has people who are interested but not ready right now. It’s not always a thinking error, but rather a natural part of selling. However, something to keep in mind is what you notice yourself thinking or believing when someone books a consult.

Do you believe they are ready to buy, or have you developed a subconscious thought that they will object?

Sometimes our brain uses past experiences and then latches on to those results. Unchecked, it can be easy for our brain to “assume” that how it happened in the past is going to be how it “always” happens moving forward. This is what you may want to get clear on and see if your brain believes there is a client ready to say yes today. 
If you believed this, what actions would you take in your business right now knowing that person is coming?

Another powerful question to ask yourself: 
when someone tells you they’re excited but it’s not the right moment financially, how do you want to show up as the leader of your business in that moment? 
You might thank her and leave the door open. You might ask what program she had in mind. You might mention a smaller offer. All of those are completely reasonable options. What matters most is that you don’t let your energy get stuck trying to solve the people who aren’t ready, when there are other people out there who are.

What are your thoughts?
 Feel free to reflect over some of this and bring back any coaching questions you may still have. We are happy to help you.
