question:
Hi Coach,

First things first, I just signed my 2 paying clientes for the first time. I am so grateful for all the coaching.

But, now I am having so much drama with the payment methods. I need help.

I just can’t figure it out.

here is what is going on. I’m dealing with two payment issues.

A client from the U.S. sent me a wire transfer to my virtual USD account. The transaction appears but has been under review for almost 48 hours. I’m not sure if this is normal for wires or if there might be a problem with the transfer.

Another client made a transfer on Sunday. It showed as pending for several days. After I contacted support and sent them the receipt, they changed the status to “completed,” but the funds still don’t appear in transit or in my balance (it still shows $0).

Since I’m based in Ecuador and options like Stripe, Wise, or linking local banks to PayPal are limited, I rely on other platforms to receive international payments. I’m trying to understand whether these delays are normal or if there might be an issue with how the payments were sent.

I feel like this is too much and cannot be solved.
answer:
Hey coach!

First, I just want to say congratulations on signing your first two paying clients. That’s a big moment, and it’s worth pausing to acknowledge that you did that! The logistics can feel messy sometimes, but the fact that two people said yes to working with you is a really meaningful step.

As far as the payment questions, the 2k platform unfortunately isn’t the best place for troubleshooting payment systems, especially when it involves different countries and financial platforms. Because of that, the best next step may be to email 
support@staceyboehman.com
 and share the questions you included here. They’ll be in a much better position to offer some insight for those specific concerns.

I will say that delays like the ones you’re describing can happen with international transfers and wires, especially when transactions are under review or moving between different systems. It doesn’t necessarily mean something has gone wrong, but the support team will be the right people to off some additional insight.

In the meantime, see if you can gently notice the thought you shared at the end: 
“I feel like this is too much and cannot be solved.”
 Getting your payment systems set up when you’re coaching internationally can take a little trial and error. It’s very normal for this stage of business to involve some figuring things out. The good news is you already did the hardest part coach, you signed the clients! The logistics can be solved step by step.

If you would like coaching on the thought, “
“I feel like this is too much and cannot be solved” 
we can help you with that here in AAC.

Tell us what feels like “too much” and why? Be specific.

2. And also, why do you think your brain is offering that “it cannot be solved?” Is that true? How do you feel when you think that thought? 

If you’d like, answer those questions above and then bring back your answers for more coaching.

For the concerns you have with the wires, 
email support@staceyboehmancoaching.com
 and the team should be able to guide you.

title: Being All In
question: I listened to Stacey’s podcast where she talked about being “all in” and it really hit. I discovered throughout the years it’s been hard at many points to fight for myself, which makes me sad because looking back I was so much better than what I thought at the time. I noticed that because I didn’t think anything was ever enough at the time, I would give up along the process or half ass things. If I didn’t get good results fast, I didn’t see a reason to keep trying. At this point I’ve grown from not thinking things are good enough but still have to work on being all in. I want to get really good at it this year, I really believe it’s my next growth opportunity. I know to do that I have to have thoughts that are “all in” but I also don’t want to have rush or need energy with them. But maybe me not wanting rush energy is just an excuse my brain gives to procrastinate! If you could offer any other insights or exercises for “all in” energy I would appreciate it.
answer:
Hi Coach!

I love that you’re seeing this as your next growth opportunity because it really is. This is such a powerful shift to focus on.

Here may be a helpful way to think about this… When it comes to going
 all in
 as an entrepreneur, it can be grounded in the understanding that there will be highs and lows and many emotions to navigate along the way. Even still, the goal becomes feeling like you gave as much as you could in every action you take.

Another visual I find helpful to share and use myself is imagining being in a foot race. The finish line is your goal for the year. When you’re at the starting line, you decide in that moment you’re going to go 
all in.
 Then the race starts, and from there it’s about continuing to run. At certain points in the race, you may feel tired. Your leg might cramp. You might need to slow down a bit to catch your breath. The same is true in business. But if you’re
 all in
, the goal is 
still to finish the race.

Many times when things get uncomfortable, the brain tries to get you to quit the race if you aren’t going to be in “first place” (aka hit your goals). But what if it wasn’t about “first place”? What if it’s just about finishing strong, even if it doesn’t play out exactly how you had hoped or trained for?

So let’s play around with this:

1. If you were to show up to your business this year, not perfectly, but with the mindset of crossing the finish line, how would you make decisions?

2. How would you show up in the harder seasons?

3. What would you keep doing even when it’s not giving you immediate results?

What if being 
all in
 isn’t about doing it perfectly the entire year, but about crossing the finish line proud that you didn’t let anything take you out of the race or stop you before you were done?

Take some time to reflect on this and then bring back your answers if you would like more coaching! We would love to help you!

title: Follow up to is entrepreneurship for me
question:
Coming back to answer some questions:

What would it look like to create stability for yourself, instead of waiting for the business to provide it?

On the surface, I suppose I have some “stability.” I have $68,00 in my personal savings account. I currently have $24,000 in my business account. Technically, if I made zero dollars I would have 11 months of money to cover my expenses. So I do have a financial buffer, and yet I still don’t feel “stable.” What felt stable to me before entrepreneurship was knowing I would get a certain amount of money a year and exactly how much I would get each month. So I’m still struggling with what it would actually look like to create stability.

So when you say you need $250K, What do you believe is actually in the way between where you are and where you want to go?

Not “there’s not enough time,” but specifically Is it volume? Pricing? Offers? Capacity? Support, mindset, Time blocking and follow through work?

I need the mindset that it is possible for me to take steps to create 250k AND prioritize healing my nervous system. Right now, if a client cancels a call, I feel sheer relief. And that is my body saying, thank goodness, we get a little more spaciousness and a break. So I can’t override that need. With that said it looks like I definitely need more capacity.

I also need to get more clients at a higher price and launch a group. Right now, many of my clients come from coaching organizations that I subcontract with. If I could secure some of my own clients, I would be making more money. Even with that, launching a group seems to be the thing that needs to happen.

Which goes to needing to create an offer.

So essentially, it looks like there’s a combo platter of things in the way.

What are you telling yourself throughout your day—especially in the moments you feel fried?

I tell myself I have the capacity to get things done. And that everything is working together for my good. And that even tiny actions will create movement. However, I can’t override the truth of my body being depleted, which is what I often feel like I’m attempting to do. On the days that I don’t have many client calls, when I allow myself to take a break and rest I come back the next day on fire in a good way. However, I’m also not meeting new people, telling them I’m a coach, and making offers. ON the comeback days I’m meeting with clients.

All of this is starting to feel brain swirly to me.
answer:
Hey coach,

I’m really glad you wrote all of this out. There’s actually a lot more clarity here than it feels like. Let’s just slow it down.

You shared the facts  $68K in savings, $24K in your business, 11 months covered. And then the thought: 
“I don’t feel stable.”
 That tells us right away,  stability isn’t coming from the money. It’s coming from how you’re thinking about it.

When you tell yourself “I’m not stable,” what does that have you do or not do? 
this is where we see what’s really driving your results,  hesitation, holding back, overthinking, not fully going all in.

What feeling are you trying to avoid by tying stability to money?
Because before, a paycheck created a sense of certainty. Now your brain is trying to recreate that same feeling through numbers but it’s not working the same way.

Money is neutral. It doesn’t create stability  your thoughts about it do. So even with 11 months covered, your brain can still say “not enough.”

That’s actually good news. It means stability is something you can create on purpose.

Before it was: 
“I know exactly what I’ll make.”
Now it can become: 
“I know I can create money.”

Just notice the shift there.

Then when we look at the $250K goal  you listed a lot of things: capacity, more clients, higher prices, a group offer. That might all be part of it. But underneath, there’s a belief running the show:

“I can’t grow to $250K and take care of myself at the same time.”

So I want to ask you directly: 
Is that actually true? Or is that just what it feels like right now? Why ?

Because your body is giving you useful information. When a client cancels and you feel relief, that’s not a problem   that’s awareness. It’s showing you that the way you’re currently working doesn’t feel sustainable yet. So instead of pushing past that, we clean it up.

What would it look like to create capacity on purpose?
Not wait for it create it.

You already see the pattern   you rest, you come back energized. But on those days, you’re not selling or meeting new people. Then on the days you feel good, you’re full with client work. So of course it feels inconsistent.

What would it look like to design your week where both exist  energy and creation? 
Not all client work. Not all rest. Both.

That’s where stability actually starts  in how you structure your time and how you think while you’re doing it.

And then let’s simplify this so it doesn’t keep feeling like “everything at once.”

Come back to this:

What is the offer you’re willing to sell right now?
Not perfect. Not final. Just clear.

Because everything builds from there.

And as you think about growing…
Who is the version of you making $250K?
How does she think about her time? Her energy? Her clients?
Is she waiting to feel ready… or is she creating structure that supports her?

You don’t need to do everything. You just need to start thinking and deciding like her in small ways.

So instead of letting it swirl, just come back to this:

What am I offering?
How am I planning my time?
What am I choosing to believe about my ability to create money?

You’re not as far off as it feels. This is just you learning how to create stability from you not from a paycheck.

If we were to clean up one thing first, what feels most helpful right now your thinking about stability, or how your days are currently structured?

title: Overcoming my Objections in my coaching career
question:
I started coaching in June 2019 and officially started my coaching business in August 2019. I recently looked back at my very first video and realized how vulnerable I was from the beginning.

For most of my coaching journey, my focus was on motherhood and helping moms manage stress based on my own personal experiences and what I was able to overcome. I’m also a social worker, and when my clients are not in crisis, I naturally shift into coaching and supporting personal growth.

Throughout this journey coaching programs, offers, content, and all the things I have not made any money from coaching. I’ve coached for free many times because I genuinely wanted more experience and wanted to become better at coaching. I’ve made low-ticket offers, high-ticket offers, and there was even a time when I struggled to get people to sign up for free coaching.

I’ve followed Stacey and her programs for a while now, but I still haven’t made money in my coaching business.

Recently, I pivoted my niche to helping women who keep everyone else happy and comfortable except themselves reconnect with who they are and learn to choose themselves again. But I still have so many mental objections around it.

Part of me keeps thinking:

* What if this becomes another 7 years of making no money?

* What would make this different?

* Coaching feels so saturated now. How do I even get seen?

* If I couldn’t get people to buy when I was deeply passionate before, what would make people buy now?

* Should I quit?

I never really thought about quitting before. I’ve taken pauses, but lately I’ve honestly been on the verge of giving up.

I truly just want to coach, but sometimes it feels like the hardest thing in the world to make work.

Right now, my mind feels filled with objections, fear, doubt, and overthinking, and it’s making it hard to move forward.
answer:
Hey Coach,

First, I want to acknowledge how vulnerable and honest this was. I can feel the discouragement you’ve felt after putting so much time, energy, heart, and hope into coaching without seeing the financial results you wanted 
yet.

Something I noticed immediately is how quickly your brain is using the last 7 years to predict the next 7.

“What if this becomes another 7 years?”
 feels less like a factual prediction and more like your brain trying to protect you from disappointment, failure, uncertainty, and uncomfortable emotions. If your brain can convince you the future is already decided, then you never fully have to risk “hoping” again. So of course it would go there – very human response to protect you from potential pain.

I’m also really curious about something…..

If coaching 
did
 start working the way you wanted it to and clients consistently started coming in, is this still what you would want to do? When you imagine yourself coaching women, creating content, building offers, serving clients, and growing this business, does something inside of you still light up? Or does the idea of fully walking away actually feel relieving? Sad? Heavy? Expansive?

I think your emotional response holds to those questions some powerful insight. Keep in mind (and I know you know this) every career path in the world has hard parts. Traditional jobs do. Entrepreneurship does. Coaching does.

The question becomes: 
what kind of hard feels worth it to you? And there’s no wrong answer.

I also want to lovingly challenge the “coaching is saturated” thought because honestly, almost every industry could be viewed that way if we wanted to play that game in our brain. There are countless doctors, therapists, nurses, grocery stores, restaurants, gas stations, and social workers. And still, people have preferences. They connect differently to different people. Even with ten grocery stores nearby, you probably have one or two you naturally prefer. Same with hair stylists… there might be hundreds of them in one city but we often choose one particular person for our hair….. Why?

The same is true for coaching. Clients are not only buying information. They are connecting to the person, the energy, the approach, the experience of being understood. So I wonder if some of the “stuckness” here is more about if you fully believe there is room for 
you
 inside of this coaching market…. and there is, coach – if you want it. Your uniqueness is perfect for certain individuals out in the world that only your voice/style/coaching methods can reach – it’s a matter of you finding them and them finding you.

You absolutely can quit if you want to. But I would really encourage you to explore your reasons carefully. 
Would you LOVE your reasons for walking away?
 Or would quitting mostly come from fear, discouragement, comparison, exhaustion, or trying to protect yourself from the vulnerability of continuing? I don’t think there’s a right or wrong answer there. I just think it’s important to know the difference!

Feel free to come back here with any follow up thoughts, questions, or coaching requests. We are happy to continue helping you. Thanks coach!

title: Day 10 / 30 – it goes full circle
question:
Thank you for the coaching on “how do I start implementing the work?”

Yes, I do see how I am not really stuck. I think I’ve been feeling frustrated with my obvious procrastination on doing things that will call in new clients. I do see, however, how asking the question “what is my problem” isn’t useful or serving me.

I think the emotion that my brain is trying to avoid is embarrassment or incompetence. If I go out and meet new people, will they think I’m incompetent? Will they find my content useless? Will they see that I have low engagement? I guess I hadn’t explored that before but it definitely relates back to something else I was coached on in my message “day 10 / 30 – shame and embarrassment.”

I feel a lot of embarrassment about my current circumstances and I’m not entirely sure how to get to a place where I believe that the clients that I want will also want me. That stops me from meeting new people. It feels like I need to change my situation first, then the clients will see me as valuable (like I need to have results in my own life before they’ll see me as valuable), but there’s also a belief that I need to have clients in order for my situation to change.

To answer your questions:

I have no evidence that people are confused by my content, it’s just a mind story.

& I like the idea of giving myself certain tasks to complete before I continue consuming content. I think you are absolutely correct about me consuming as a distraction tactic.

I think I’m avoiding that piece before, feeling like “what’s the point of meeting new people? The clients I want won’t want to work with me so it’ll be all for nothing.” I’m not believing that the clients that will want me offer will want me offering it to them because of my current circumstances and because of my history and “failures.”
answer:
Hi Coach!

When you say,
 “I think the emotion that my brain is trying to avoid is embarrassment or incompetence.”

What might it be like if you practiced these emotions more?

What good might come from it?

Would you be willing to?

Many times the emotions we avoid are the ones that are capping our potential most.

If there’s nothing we are unwilling to feel, there is nothing we are unable to accomplish.

I was recently listening to a reel on social media by a billionaire – the one who started Poppi sodas.

She said, 
“
I think embarrassment is the most underexplored emotion when it comes to success. I embarrassed myself repeatedly until I gained confidence.”

Something that may be helpful is remembering that emotions are fluid. They simply come and go. Some linger longer than others, but we have a range of emotions throughout the day. We can feel happy one moment, sad the next, angry the next, then embarrassed, then back to joyful. When embarrassment or incompetence happens, they “sting” in the moment, but they are temporary as long as we don’t make them apart of our identity. As long as we don’t attach meaning to them. We as humans are capable of allowing an emotion to surge through our body and then exit.

What would you do/try in your business more often if feeling embarrassment or incompetence wasn’t a problem?

P.S. You’re doing great work coach.You’re very dedicated. We can’t wait to see you win at your goals. Keep going!

title: am I confusing my audience?
question:
I’m navigating something in my business and would love your coaching.

I know you teach that we don’t need a niche, and that we can sell from our brain and our skill.

At the same time, I’ve worked with a money coach (also trained under Brooke Castillo) who said she made the most money when she niched down and spoke directly to one person.

Here’s where I feel stuck:

I can help my clients in multiple areas, food obsession and binge eating, money trauma, identity and nervous system work, and overall self-leadership. I’ve created workshops and webinars across all of these because they’re all deeply connected to my story and my work.

Could I be confusing my audience?

When this coach said this to me, I immediately thought of binge eating and how easily I can coach on this. I’ve lived it for 48 years. It feels the most natural and powerful in my body right now.

At the same time, I feel resistance to focusing only on that day to day. And my brain tells me:

“Everyone is already teaching this.”

“People aren’t showing up when you do this.”

“What makes you different?”

So my questions are:

I’ve helped clients with binge eating, but it was really all mindset. When they came to me, they knew what to do, they just weren’t doing it.

Would you recommend choosing one core topic and repeating it consistently, even if I can help in many areas as a general life coach?

I’ve done food noise webinars, selling webinars, and meant for more webinars. Could I be confusing my audience?

How do I decide between what feels most aligned?
answer:
Hi Coach,

This may not feel the most helpful but the truth is, there isn’t a right or wrong answer here. You simply get to decide what you want to do. If you love coaching on multiple things as a general life coach and have a business you love showing up to, that may be a reason to keep doing what you’re doing. If you feel pulled to niche down because there is a specific set of ideal clients you want to target in your marketing, messaging, and programs – you can do that as well.

I think what is important is to know that you can be successful no matter your choice. There have been wildly successful general life coaches who make a lot of money and also wildly successful coaches who niche down…

1. If you believed you would meet all of your goals and the make the money you want to be making no matter your choice, what would feel most aligned?

Remember you’re also never stuck. If you wanted to do general life coaching a few more years and then one day wake up and know the niche you want to pursue, that is always available to you as well.

1. What makes you come alive in coaching? 

2. What excites you to wake up and get to work in your business?

3. What clients and/or topics do you love so much it drives you to show up, even on the days business feels hard?

Having a niche doesn’t always make business run more smoothly, guarantee more money, or change our results.

It’s about WHO we are being in the process (no matter what we have chosen).

Take some time to reflect on these answers. Bring them back here if you would like to continue coaching through this! And feel free to come back with any thoughts you may also want some help with. That’s what we are here for. Thanks Coach!

title: 04/19/2026 | lasting, stable change pt. 2
question:
Thank you so much for this gentle reminder. I very much see how I get caught in a thought loop that says “I’m right on the edge of a breakthrough.” I created a model to show myself just how unhelpful this thought is – which truthfully masquerades as helpful in the moment it’s occurring.

C – low income, few clients

T – “I’m right on the edge of a breakthrough. Something is still missing. Once I find that thing THEN things will finally start moving.”

F – confusion, seeking, yearning

A – waiting, intellectualizing, learning without implementing

R – low income, few clients

As I read your response I feel motivated, I believe what you shared, that lasting change comes from our SKILLS that we keep practicing over and over again until they materialize as physical results, that I don’t need anything other than that to have success, and that my job is to show that to my clients too.

When I ruminate on not having the answer yet, it serves as validation in losing momentum, in doing nothing other than learning or focusing heavily on thought work rather than continuing to practice generating consults.

One of the things I can feel myself avoiding is creating my own networking event. I had this idea while feeling really lit up by a networking event I went to & thinking “I could do this, and I could expand my existing network by doing this, I have a much bigger network than I give myself credit for, they would benefit too, I could create a facebook group too, etc.” A long stream of very productive thoughts. I even asked a few people in my closest network and they were all excited by the idea.

& yet I haven’t done anything about it.

Model:

C – desire to create virtual networking event

T – “what if I can’t find a time that everyone can make, what if people get on the call and then feel like I just created this to sell my offer, I’m not sure how to setup a networking event on Zoom, what if there aren’t enough people for breakout rooms, what if there are so many people and I don’t know how to handle it, etc.”

F – fear

A – do nothing, sit on the idea, take no action

R – networking event isn’t created
answer:
Hi Coach,

This is such a great “model” to lay out because you can clearly see how your brain keeps fighting to protect you every time it thinks “something is still missing.” The moment it believes there is still one more answer, breakthrough, or thing you need first, it pulls you out of action and into confusion, seeking, yearning, learning, and waiting. And yet your own awareness here is so important: “rather than continuing to practice generating consults.” I would really stay with that. Your brain already knows the focus. It’s not to find the missing thing. 
It’s to practice the skill of generating consults consistently and often enough 
for the results to compound over time.

I also want you to notice how quickly your brain got itself “stuck” again with this networking event you want to host. You went from feeling lit up, expansive, and excited to immediately trying to account for 
every possible outcome
 and 
accommodate everyone
 
before you’ve even hosted the first one.

What if some people can’t come?

What if the breakout rooms aren’t perfect?

What if there are too many people?

What if there aren’t enough?

I’d get curious whether your brain is approaching this from
 leader energy
 or “accommodate-everyone” energy. Those are very different energies… which one do you think serves you and your audience best? You pick the date, the time, and send the invite… then you learn through it and change anything post-event that didn’t work. Just as you would do an eval for consults, you do an eval for stuff like that…

“What worked, what didn’t work, what am I going to do differently next time?”

If you want to host the networking event, definitely host it. Focus on value, on connection, on practicing visibility. At the end – whether ONE person shows up or 10, all you have to do is offer consultations at the end. Have your booking link ready to drop in the consults.

“If you enjoyed this event and learned something, I’d love to invite you to a free consult. I’m going to drop my link here in the comments just in case you want to book a free call to see if coaching is something that could help you.”

That doesn’t make the event “just to sell” someone. It makes you a coach that becomes visible, someone who provided free value, and a business owner with an offer that may support the women there. And this is the best part….if the first one is awkward, imperfect, too small, too big, or not what you hoped? You can host another one 2–4 weeks later. There are no rules saying you have to get it right the first time. You can host as many networking events as you want. What if one woman came, but that one woman was an easy yes to your 8k offer? Think about this as you create it. Even if no one came, you would still learn a lot and you could still choose to be the entrepreneur that keeps going!

What I’m noticing is just how hard your brain fights to “stall” you on every decision you make… and honestly I think the deeper reason is because you are a force to be reckoned with when you get out of your own way. Sometimes our brain tells us to stall because we fear failure, but really…. we fear success more. I wonder if somewhere deep inside, your subconscious knows the power inside of yourself and there’s one half of you that itching to let it come out, while another part fights to hide it away. Don’t let yourself stall and hide it away coach. It’s in there, I can feel it.

What do you think? Feel free to come back with any further coaching you may need on this.

title: Day 8 / 30 – limitations around new offer
question:
I had told you in my previous message that I have officially decided on my new offer and price. I felt really good about that when sending the message and now I am hoping for some coaching on the thoughts that are coming up.

I listened to Stacey’s podcast episode #49 “determining your prices” & offer week. Both made me tighten when she talked about raising your prices only once you’ve reached a certain demand. I know I have been coaching for years at lower price points, but I wouldn’t say that I have “high demand,” and now I’m second guessing. Am I trying to raise my price prematurely? She said for 2k for 2k she charged based on undercharging and overdelivering and encouraged that we do the same thing with our coaching practices until we’ve reached a certain demand, and with $200k she chose what to charge as a way to filter her best clients because she had such high demand. So am I trying to filter for better clients without the demand? If so, how do I solve for the issue of resentment I feel towards “the business model that isn’t working for me?”

I also briefly noticed my brain wanting to “convince” my potential clients that my new offer is worth the price by drawing comparisons to things like therapy or hiring a personal trainer. I caught it right away and recognized that it was born from a lack of belief that says “they won’t be ready to invest so we need to convince them that it’s not a lot of money compared to other things they buy in a year.” I am sure this is coming from my old clientele, which mostly were made up of people who were struggling financially and were barely scraping by. They DID need to overcome financial objections, honestly they mostly ONLY had financial objections. Strangely enough, I have rarely had someone get on a consult with me and have any objection to working with me other than price.

But with the clientele I desire to call in now, these are people who won’t be worried about the price as much as they are about the offer overall. Before, I was always able to get my new clients to sign because I offered the price they felt most comfortable with (if they had objected to the price I originally offered). It sounds like moving forward I will have to either turn those people away or coach them to paying the higher price which will definitely be a new challenge for me, but a challenge I’m excited to face. If it’s in my best interest to be charging more at all.
answer:
Hi coach!

I think it’s important to start this coaching by grounding you back in your decision. You chose an $8k offer because the previous model created resentment and wasn’t working for you. If you go back to undercharging just to match where you think you “should” be, you will recreate the exact problem you just identified. I think instead of, 
“am I allowed to charge this yet?”
 the better question for now is, 
“am I willing to stand behind this decision and build demand for it?”

Your brain is looking for certainty (which is understandable as you’re human and that’s what is most comfortable). But remember, demand is something you create, not something you wait for before you decide your price. So I want you to consider, what if 
this price i
s the standard you are now building demand for?

When you mentioned, 
“wanting to “convince” my potential clients that my new offer is worth the price” – 
great awareness.

You were able to spot that it’s coming from doubt, not strategy. Anytime you believe you need to justify the price, you will attract people who need convincing. When you believe the offer stands on its own, you will attract people evaluating whether it’s right for them, not whether it’s affordable.

What if instead of 
“how do I get them to see it’s worth it?”
 you asked, 
“do I fully believe this is worth it for the woman I WANT to work with?”

You’re also exactly right that this will require a different standard on your consults. You won’t be adjusting your price to meet people where they are. That means some people will not be a fit anymore and that’s okay. That is the “filter” for who you want to work with showing it’s working. What to keep an eye on within yourself is if you start making that mean something has gone wrong.

So here are the bigger questions:

Are you willing to let some people walk away who fully object to the price you’ve landed on?

Are you willing to hold your price confidently even when it feels uncomfortable?

Are you willing to believe that the right clients exist, even if you haven’t been surrounded by them 
yet
?

Take some time to answer these questions and bring back your answers for additional coaching! Thanks coach!

title: Day 10 / 30 – shame, embarrassment, and grief
question:
I just want to tell you how excited I am when I wake up and see that I have received responses in AAC. It feels like Christmas morning! I feel so held and supported in your responses. That is exactly what I strive to give as a coach, thank you for acting as a good “model” of the work!

One of the things I am really noticing is how much the models I’m creating haven’t been serving me like the thought that “I am a mess,” as you mentioned. I have been spinning that belief for nearly 3 years.

For contexts sake, here are the facts:

In 2020 I quit my desk job to pursue life coaching full time. Over the next 3-4 years I traveled for 4 months, moved to a different state where I lived for 1 ½ years, moved to Bali where I lived for a year, & was then running so low on money that I moved back home (late 2023). Then in mid-2024 I entered into a relationship for 1 year, which was later labeled psychologically abusive by my therapist. I am now living with my brother with no car and am making about $500/month.

Some of the most painful thoughts I have about these circumstances:

“I used to be so inspiring and now I am just a mess,” “I peaked between 2020-2023 and now my life is embarrassing in comparison,” “how could I let this happen,” “I have no idea how to get back to where I was before.”

The one that hurts the most is probably: “I just want to go back.” It makes me feel deep grief and sadness when I think about it. When imagining potential clients knowing these things about me I feel shame and embarrassment.

I think it’s really interesting all of the circumstances you pointed out vs. the ones that I did. Because nowhere did I feel the need to add in context about me showing up in my work. My thoughts related to that are, “I was never consistent, I always disappeared after showing up for a while, I deleted a lot of content, I always changed my offers, and really only became consistent with social media presence and my podcast in the last year.”

But it’s true, I’ve never had a lull in clients, I’ve always had at least 2, they’ve always been paying me, and I am STILL HERE.

I do agree, this is just a season for me, but I’ve also felt stuck in it for so long & though I feel things shifting, I am still believing and ruminating on the thought that I’m a mess, “I am a failure” is coming up now as well, & I’m not sure what to do about that loop. I have been stuck on the past.
answer:
Hey again coach!

First, I’m so glad you get excited for the responses and feel held/supported! That is always the goal here inside of AAC.

Okay – let me just share with you what stood out to me of everything I read in this response…

It blew my mind and my hope is that this lands for you as well.

You said something pretty profound that I think is contributing to “the loop” you feel stuck in…

Here it is:

“I PEAKED between 2020-2023″

Just sit with that for a moment…

A peak is the “best of the best.” It’s reaching “the TOP.”

Online if you Google “I hit my peak”, this is literally what it says verbatim:

“
I hit my peak
 means
 reaching 
the highest point of capacity, success, development, or happiness.
 It signifies that a person or process has 
achieved its strongest or best possible state
, often 
implying that subsequent performance may remain at a plateau or decline.”

Think on this….. Do you really believe you PEAKED in 2020-2023?

As in you reached the BEST parts of you? The BEST accolades in business? Your BEST skills? THE BEST?!

And I don’t mean 
“compared to where you are now”
, I mean in general….

Think about how profound this is for the brain to believe you already hit YOUR PEAK!

Why would it be motivated to keep going, keep trying, keep showing up, and keep building if it truly believes your BEST DAYS are “behind you” ?

And also, because your brain is believing that, it’s using your energy to try to solve for going “back” to that ….vs. using energy thinking about how you want to move forward.

What if 2020-2023 was not at all your “peak”?

What if that was a “baby mountain peak” compared to what you are actually capable of and meant for?

What if you haven’t even 
discovered
 the base of the mountain for what your peak TRULY is in this life?

Coach, remember you are capable of so much!! Get really clear on your vision for yourself. What you want for yourself. The money you want to make, the lifestyle you want to live, the business you want to have, the clients you want to work with, the things you want to do!

Reaching THAT VISION over time will be YOUR PEAK. It’s not where you were in 2020-2023. You have so much in front of you to look forward to. The “mountain” your climbing right now is the one where you get to access the truest potential of your peak. 
The journey is the reward
 in the meantime.

What if you stopped believing that your “best, most inspirational days” are behind you?

Can you imagine what would change if you believed your “best, most inspirational days” are in front of you?

What are your thoughts?

title: day 6 / 30 – an addition to “stuck between pricing & capacity)
question:
I noticed something after submitting that last question:

I feel a lot of resentment when I think about charging at my current level of belief.

But I also have a belief that I attract people who can’t afford a price point that would keep me out of resentment.

I’ve sold 6 month packages for $10k where clients didn’t even flinch, maybe they even noticeably relaxed when I said it out loud.. My current package is listed for 3 months of work together for $2k which I have very little, to no drama around selling.

I would much prefer to make it a 12 month package. If I extended it at the same price point that would be $8k for the year. I love that price on paper, but the thought of actually selling it to someone? It immediately feels difficult because I assume people can’t afford it. Not even that it’s not worth that amount of money – I think it’s worth more. But for some reason I have a belief that people are generally struggling financially, they’ll WANT to say yes to the offer, but they WON’T BE ABLE TO because of financial struggles. That’s been a common theme for my clients through the years.

It just seems like I have combatting thoughts. One says my future clients are all struggling financially and I need to sell low for them, the other says if I don’t charge more I’ll be trapped in resentment or will burnout trying to survive on the little I’m making from them. What do you suggest I do with this?
answer:
Hi Coach,

This is a powerful place to be because you’re able to see what your own mind is doing. Right now, what you’re experiencing isn’t really about pricing or capacity. It’s about two different versions of who you believe your clients are, and you’re trying to build one business while holding both of them as true at the same time.

For example based on what you’ve shared, one version of your client is capable, resourced, and ready. She hears $8-10k and relaxes because she understands the value and has already decided she’s someone who invests in herself at that level. The other version of your client is struggling, limited, and wants the work but can’t afford it. She needs you to keep your prices lower in order to say yes. When both of those beliefs are active, it creates tension because your pricing is no longer just about the number, it’s about 
which client you are deciding to build your business for.

When you lower your price to accommodate the client you believe can’t afford more, you are also choosing the experience that comes with that. That can often bring more emotional labor, more pressure to make the investment feel worth it for them, and more attachment to their outcomes. Over time, that’s where resentment starts to build. You’ve likely already felt that, which is important. It means your current model is giving you really clear feedback.

You’ve also already had the experience of selling at $10k to clients who didn’t flinch. That is really valuable insight because that is real evidence that there are people who not only can afford your work, but feel relieved to find it at that level. So the work isn’t so much figuring out the perfect price point, it’s deciding which client you want to be available for.

There are people who cannot afford $8k, and there are people who can. Your brain is almost trying to to solve for both which you do not have to do. When you say 
“I attract people who can’t afford it,”
 what I hear is that maybe there have been moments you’ve made yourself available for people who can’t afford it. Your pricing, your messaging, your energy, and the way you sell all signal who you are for. Right now, there is still a part of you trying to be for everyone, and that’s likely what’s creating the internal conflict.

I also want to offer that the resentment you’re feeling isn’t coming from your clients. It’s coming from you saying yes to a business model that doesn’t actually work for you. Lowering your price to avoid the discomfort of someone not being able to afford it will cost you in a different way. It will cost you your energy, your enjoyment of the work, and eventually your desire to keep showing up. You’re already starting to feel that tradeoff.

If you were to move forward with a 12 month offer at $8k, the real work would be becoming the coach who fully believes she is available for clients who are ready for that level of investment. That is a different identity than the one who is trying to make coaching feel more accessible for those who “cannot afford it”. Neither is wrong, but they create very different businesses.

What would it look like to make a clean decision about who you want to build for based on your offer? The woman who needs you to stay at $2k so she can say yes, or the woman who is ready for $8k and is looking for someone to meet her at that level? Once you decide that, your pricing decision becomes much simpler. Your job becomes learning how to hold that decision, even when your brain offers you all the reasons someone might not be able to afford it.

What do you think?

Feel free to come back with anything you might want some additional coaching on as it pertains to this! Thanks coach!

title: Who do I need to be to make it work ?
question:
Dear coach,

That was exactly the coaching I needed. I came to the same conclusions and I was exploring the «who». Who do I need to be to make this work ?

When I am not in the « who », the quantity and consistency of work that is required to make this work seems completely unreachable for my adhd self.

When I slip into to my coach identity, it feels very different.

Q : How can you keep bringing yourself back to the thought, “I make it work”?

A : the thought you offered “My business is producing results that reflect the actions I’m taking” is working quite well because it is taking me out of the drama.

It makes it doable. But if I am not in good shape, I could feel pressure and slip into dispair. The thought « I am a born coach » and everything close to it could work too. It’s what I am practicing right now. The important thing is to get me out of drama.

Q : Who do I need to be to make this work?

A : I need to be my real self, the playful one, the one who is curious, the one who is in aw, (it’s a sort of child energy) the one who is open to any emotion and very compassionate. The one who is fiercely loving. The fool and the poet.

Q : What are your thoughts?

A : My thought is that « making it work » is very abstract. I don’t even know what it means. I notice some resistance when I read « I am ready to make money » or « I follow through » (brain is saying No we don’t!)

I can easily fall back into the how with the thought I make it work.

And I make it work isn’t the opposite of it’s not working.

I make it work but it’s still not working

grrrr My brain is so stubborn !

I want to go into the feeling instead, because I am tired to try to convince this brain.

I want to feel openness and curiosity. And compassion.

Of course I don’t know. Of course it seems impossible.

Let’s try anyway.
answer:
Hey Coach,

You’ve done a beautiful job answering these questions and allowing the awareness to sink in. One thing I want to offer is that you can come back to these questions anytime you notice your brain trying to tug at your belief and pull you back into doubt, drama, or confusion. Not to convince yourself of something, but to reconnect with what you already know.

As I read your answers, I notice your brain still wants to make this about finding the perfect thought. But businesses aren’t built by finding the perfect thought. They’re built by making decisions, creating value, testing things, learning from the results, adjusting, and continuing. When you say, “I can easily fall back into the how,” I think that’s because “make it work” is still a little abstract for you. Your brain hears it and immediately wants evidence, guarantees, and certainty.

Instead of asking, “How do I make it work?” I would get much more practical.

What would working look like this week?

What are the actions you believe create value?

What are the things you can do that put that value in front of people?

The reason I ask those questions is because they bring you out of the philosophy of the business and back into the practice of 2K today. You don’t have to know exactly how you’ll get from where you are to where you want to go. Nobody does. What you need is a theory, a plan, and a willingness to test it. Then reality gives you feedback. Some things work do more of those. Some things don’t adjust and keep going.

I also noticed you wrote, “I make it work, but it’s still not working.” My question would be, what does “not working” actually mean? If revenue isn’t where you want it to be yet, that doesn’t automatically mean it’s not working. It may simply mean you haven’t yet created the right value, delivered at the right frequency, to the right people, enough times for them to buy. That’s a very different problem than  “something is wrong with adhd me.” One is a business problem that can be solved. The other keeps you stuck in self-doubt and drama.

Your brain will often want to make the results mean something personal about you, but business is much more practical than that. Money is a result of value. So when you notice yourself spinning, come back to questions that move the business forward: 
What value can I create? How can I communicate it? How can I get it in front of more people?
 Those questions create movement. Wallowing, getting mad, or arguing with reality might be understandable, but they don’t create results.

What I love most is where you landed: openness, curiosity, compassion, playfulness, awe, the fool, and the poet! Bring all of those with you. The who is the one who makes a decision, creates a plan, follows through, learns from the outcome, and keeps going. Of course you don’t know exactly how to do it yet. Of course it feels impossible sometimes. That’s not evidence that you can’t do it. That’s often what it feels like when you’re building something you’ve never built before.

And when your brain wants certainty before action, remind yourself that your job isn’t to know exactly how it will unfold. Your job is to make a decision, work the plan, and stay in the process long enough to discover what works. Yes! “let’s try anyway”

title: Irresistible Offer thoughts
question:
Hi – I’d like to discuss my offer simple result and guarantee (per the “irresistible offer”). I’m a PR and media management coach. My audience is: High stakes decision makers, founders, entrepreneurs. I love the simple results of “mastery and perfection.” As measured by improvements on the wheel. I LOVE this and feels so elegant to me! … BUT I’m concerned that my audience will feel the same. That’s my T. My F is indecisive.

I think my audience will think it’s too vague or intangible. So I’m thinking of adding the word “positioning”: “master and perfect your positioning”/“mastery and positioning perfection”

Why I think this is because: Previous clients have come to me for: to be sought after, to sell to high-end clients who want a luxury experience, or to sell a new offer/pivot. None of them say “mastery and perfection” I have pro bono clients now. I see them as “perfecting;” they are perfecting their positioning. But when I do organic marketing online by writing posts and connect calls, I feel like my offer – mastery and perfection – is too vague. Please coach me to keep this offer and sell myself on it or change the offer. I can’t decide if I just want to sell myself/make the offer right (perfection) OR change the offer to “prefect their positioning”
answer:
HI Coach,

You’re asking a really good question here and I think the bigger thing to look at is not just “should I keep the offer or change it?” but what problem are you actually trying to solve underneath that question.

First, well done putting your offer through the irresistible offer protocol. Let’s dig into your model a little because I think there is awareness here that can help you make the decision instead of spinning in indecision trying to find the “right” wording.

What I hear is:

C — Offer: “mastery and perfection”
T — it’s too vague
F — indecisive / uncertain
A — questioning it, reworking it, trying to solve for certainty
R — more confusion about the offer

Then:

C — Offer: “perfect their positioning”
T — they think this is vague / intangible
F — ?
A — wanting to shift the language, what are you not doing ? What do you do when you think its not tangible? how do you solve for this when you think this? 
R — I don’t get clear and tangible less clear myself

What I notice is you say you LOVE “mastery and perfection.” It feels elegant to you. Refined. Elevated. And I think that matters because when we love our work and our messaging we naturally sell it stronger. But loving it and it being clear to your audience are two different things.

And I think that is the part your brain is trying to sort through.

One thing I notice is when you describe your clients and what they come to you for, they are not using the words “mastery and perfection.” They are saying:

“I want to be sought after.”

“I want luxury clients.”

“I want to pivot.”

“I want to elevate how I’m perceived.”

Not because your offer is wrong, but because clients usually buy in the language of their current problem and desired result, not always the language of our philosophy behind the work.

I also think there’s a difference between:

having the wrong offer vs not yet having messaging that translates clearly yet.

Those are very different problems.

Because honestly, “mastery and perfection” sounds valuable but also somewhat intangible unless you anchor it into how that actually shows up in their life or business.  And it’s not the audience’s job to make intangible work tangible.

That’s our job. Especially online it can be harder to perfect the messaging . Stacey coached here about in person less necessary to be impeccable with message and perfect place to test and improve.

People that know you in person may not need perfectly tangible language because they can feel your conviction and understand what you mean. But colder audiences online don’t have access to your energy in the same way, so clarity matters more.

And I wonder if part of what is happening is your brain is trying to solve uncertainty by finding the “perfect” wording instead of being willing to test and refine messaging over and over.

Sometimes we think we need the right message when really we need willingness to say the same thing 100 different ways until we find what lands for our people.

What feedback are you actually getting?

What are people saying back to you?

What posts or conversations make people lean in more?

What language creates connection fastest?

Those questions matter because messaging is data collection.

And I also want to point out something important around belief. You asked:

“Do I sell myself on the offer or change the offer?”

I think belief work matters a lot here because if your belief in the value of your offer changes daily, your messaging will feel inconsistent too. Belief has to become practiced.

You build belief intentionally.

You repeat it.

You collect evidence for it.

You train your brain to hold it longer.

Otherwise every day your brain wakes up renegotiating the value of your work and then your marketing starts sounding uncertain too. But belief work also does not mean ignoring feedback from your audience.

If your people are clearly telling you they resonate more with “positioning” than “mastery,” that is useful information. Not because your original offer is bad, but because clearer language helps people immediately understand the value.

What I would explore is:

Do you actually want to change the offer?

Or do you want to dial in the messaging around the offer?

For example:

What does “mastery and perfection” actually create for them tangibly?

Does it help them:

become more sought after?

get invited to speak?

land premium clients?

increase influence?

be seen as the obvious expert?

elevate perception in their industry?

That is where the tangible value lives.

Clients often don’t buy “mastery.”

They buy what mastery gets them.

And I think this question could help bring clarity:

If you fully believed your current offer was working and clients were buying easily, would you still want to change the offer? Or would you just refine how you communicate it?

And lastly, I would play with this:

How would you describe what your clients are achieving in 20 different ways to founders and entrepreneurs in your niche? Their language.

Because somewhere in there is probably the bridge between the elegance you love and the clarity your audience needs. Great work Coach!

title: Believing They Are Ready Now Pt 3
question:
I’m responding to the following coaching from my recent question entitled “Believing They Are Ready Now”:

Why do you want to feel safe believing people are ready before you know their name or face? That question matters because it points us to what you’re protecting. What does this keep you from doing?

My response:

When I sit with this question, the thing that comes up is…I want to know that my business is happening “behind the scenes.” kind of like…at any given moment someone could be watching a YouTube video or listening to my podcast or reading an email or watching the replay of an Instagram live and getting to the point where they are ready to buy/ready to book a consult. I don’t need to micro-manage their journey.

I also want to feel safe believing this because whenever I set an income goal my brain offers me the idea that unless I can name a person who is engaging, and unless I’ve interacted with them recently, I don’t get to believe in my income goal. Kind of like, believing in my income goal depends on the belief that someone is ready to buy, and if I don’t believe someone is ready to buy unless I known their name/face I don’t believe in my income goal. And when I don’t believe I can meet my income goal I show up differently. I don’t try as hard, I don’t make as many offers, I don’t troubleshoot or problem solve. Belief that I can meet my income goal is what has me showing up in ways that actually cause me to meet my income goal, but it feels right now like I can’t access that belief consistently until I can also consistently believe someone is ready to buy even if I don’t know who they are.
answer:
Hey coach,

I can really see how much you slowed down and actually sat with the question and what you uncovered is important. You didn’t just answer it, you exposed the mechanism that’s running your business.

The part I want to gently but clearly highlight is this: you’re currently choosing to believe that you need evidence of someone being there engaged, ready, real in order to let yourself show up fully.

And I want you to really look at that choice.

Because you already showed yourself the cost of it.

You said: “And when I don’t believe I can meet my income goal I show up differently.”

Let’s just make that really clean so you can see it working:

C: Income goal
T: I don’t get to believe (unless I see someone ready)
F: (likely doubt / hesitation / maybe even pressure)
A: You hold back
You don’t try as hard
You don’t make as many offers
You don’t troubleshoot or problem solve
You wait to feel certain

You tell yourself ” I can’t access the belief consistently

You don’t create belief on purpose

R: You don’t create the opportunities that would generate the income / withhold income from myself

So the result isn’t just “I don’t feel belief.”
The result is: I withhold the very behaviors that would create the income I want.

What would be different if you decided that, at any given moment, someone is engaging, is listening, is getting ready even if you don’t know who they are?

I’m asking this because your brain is currently treating visibility as a prerequisite for belief. But your business actually requires the opposite: belief first, visibility later.

Think of it like planting seeds. Right now, your brain is saying: “I’ll keep watering once I see something growing.” But the work is: you water because you trust something is growing underground.

So if you believed even 10% more that people are there…

How would you show up?

Would you make more offers?
Would you speak more directly?
Would you solve problems instead of questioning if it’s worth it?

What would you be willing to do for your income goals even if you don’t see who is there?

That version of you the one who believes people are there is the one creating the results.

Who do you need to become in order to show up consistently without needing to see engagement first?

Not hypothetically get as clear and specific as possible. Because right now, you’ve tied your consistency to proof.
And that will always keep your business reactive instead of deliberate.

You mentioned this idea of your business happening “behind the scenes” people listening, reading, watching, deciding.

What if that’s not something you need to prove… but something you choose to operate from? And then build evidence for it. Not by checking metrics but by watching yourself:

“I showed up today.”
“I made the offer.”
“I solved for my client or myself.”
“I created an opportunity.”

That is evidence.

So instead of asking, “Are they there?”
I’d invite you to shift to: “Am I showing up like they are?” 
Because that’s the only part you actually control and it’s the part that creates everything else.

You don’t need to access perfect belief to start.
You need to be willing to practice thinking in a way that allows you to act. That’s how belief becomes available.

And just to anchor this back to what you already said you already know this is true: “Belief that I can meet my income goal is what has me showing up”

It’s deciding on purpose to think in a way that lets you become the version of you who creates them.

You got this Coach!

title: Staying Busy Instead of Signing Clients 05192026
question:
Hi I’m back today to talk about why I’m not signing clients. After your coaching yesterday, I sat with my discouragement, and over time, my emotions shifted. So I asked myself…

Why do I think I’m not fully booked…. here’s some of what I came up with

1. I didn’t like selling, so I wasn’t making offers. I held back, hesitated, didn’t actually invite people. Hoped and wished people would put up their hands.

2. I stepped back and stayed hidden

3. Stayed busy instead of focusing on signing clients.

4. I didn’t ask for what I want.

I’ve definitely worked through the “I don’t like selling” mindset, and now I realize it is a very unhelpful perspective. I clearly see now that every single person who has worked with me says…”this has been so helpful. I get amazing results. Every session makes a big difference.”

So that meant the best way for me to help others (and myself) is to work with more clients…and this makes selling with integrity an act of generosity.

Now, what I’d like coaching on is #3: “staying busy instead of focusing on signing clients”.

Here’s my model:

C My business

Ts I must be missing something. I need to try X now, maybe it will work. ( I know this isn’t a clean model but it’s the gist)

F Frustrated/Anxious

A: Jump into a new approach and rush around. Get excited about doing something. Think “this will solve my problem”. Perk up. Work. Stay busy. Jump tactics and hop around instead of sticking with one approach. Don’t meet people/tell them I’m a coach/make offers (MTM). Forget that my T+F creates the results. Forget that I already have ways that do work. Think I’m missing something. Look outside my self and my brain for someone else’s solution.

R I’m busy, but I’m not building a business. And I think I am missing something (1 that I already have ways that do work and I’m not sticking with them 2. So busy in the doing that I’m not doing the basics MTM)
answer:
Hi Coach!

I think the biggest thing I’d slow down and get curious about is the thought: 
“I must be missing something.”
 Because that thought subtly keeps the brain in searching mode and “staying busy”. It keeps you in incompleteness. It creates the feeling that the answer is “out there” somewhere in the next tactic, strategy, approach, or idea. When the brain believes something major is missing, it becomes very easy to overlook or abandon the quieter things that actually compound over time.

From your own submission, it doesn’t sound like you’re missing proof that your coaching helps people. It also doesn’t sound like you’re completely lacking ways to sign clients. So I’d get curious what happens when your brain labels the problem as “I’m missing something” versus 
“I need to consistently practice the basics long enough to let them work.”
 Those create very different energy and actions. One keeps you scanning for the breakthrough thing “that will change everything”. 
The other asks you to tolerate repetition, consistency, visibility, thought work, and simple actions over and over again without needing them to feel exciting in order to keep doing them.

What do you think?
 Feel free to come back with any further coaching you may need. We are happy to help!

title: Day 30 / 30 – how do I create lasting, stable change?
question:
I’ve been feeling deeply contemplative the last few days; about my offer, my price, the name of my package, the results it gets people, & the service that I provide.

The bones of my offer feels stable, $8k, 1 year, weekly calls

I contemplated naming my package EVOLUTION because “making our brain do uncomfortable things that help us grow and succeed is literally conscious evolution.” But now I’m contemplating changing it to something that frames the result rather than the process of transformation.

I know the result I want to get people is that moment where they look around & think to themselves, “wow, this is it, this is what I’ve been asking for.” Taking them from a life they are tolerating to a life they feel like they chose & are satisfied with.

But I get caught up wondering if I really believe I am capable, at this stage in my life and business, to get people those results. I don’t even have those results personally and I fear I don’t know how to get them.

I occasionally find myself spinning in this place, wondering if I need to hire a coach, go back to university and pursue a graduate degree, get a coaching certificate – & wondering why I’m ruminating there. I think it’s because I’m struggling to answer the question “why haven’t I figured out how to create real, lasting change in my life?” & that thought makes me feel frustrated but determined. Like I’m right on the edge of figuring it out, or like the answer is hovering above my head just waiting for an entry point.

I feel like it’s my life’s purpose to almost clinically answer the question, “how does a professional like me facilitate sustainable change in others?” I seek to find the answer for myself but I also seek the answer because I genuinely want to help people get to the life they would choose to live if they felt it was possible. I just feel like I can’t confidently answer the damn question!

I know I’m getting really philosophical about it but, I want more than anything to get out of my own way and to change my life so I’m not existing within circumstances I didn’t choose. I want to feel empowered and productive and like I’m moving in the right direction – & I think I am, but that question is still eating away at me. I feel like I’m staring at a math equation that has never been solved before and I’m on the edge of solving it, like the moment before the eureka. & also like, until I do it myself and prove that it’s possible for me, I’ll feel like I could be doing better for my clients.
answer:
Coach,

I want to offer something lovingly because I think this is the very place your brain wants to keep cycling to:

You keep relating to lasting change as though there is still 
one final answer
 you haven’t uncovered yet. Like there is something important hovering just outside your awareness that, once found, will finally make you feel fully confident in yourself, your work, and your ability to help people transform.

It’s important to know that the brain does something counterproductive when it believes something is “still missing.” It uses up all its energy to keep seeking, scanning, and searching for the next insight, credential, framework, realization, or breakthrough that will finally make things feel “certain enough.” I think that can quietly become its own form of stuckness because the mind stays focused on 
what it believes it lacks
 
instead of
 
fully trusting, practicing, refining, and participating in the life and business already in front of it.

You said you feel “right on the edge” of figuring it out, and I’m curious how long you’ve felt 
“almost there.” 
Without realizing it, that belief keeps you in a cycle of thinking you need something more – something else than what you are equipped with right now
. You have everything you need inside of you right now to help others… it just hasn’t materialized yet. 
And part of why it may not have materialized into clients is because your brain’s “winning energy” is focused more of what it’s missing, or what it lacks in order to get the result.

I don’t know that “lasting change” comes from finally solving yourself or solving humanity. I think a lot of meaningful change is built through lived experience, repetition, emotional resilience, self-awareness, and continuing to lead yourself even while still evolving.

I’m curious if there’s something vulnerable about fully trusting what you already know right now….

Because if the answer still exists somewhere “out there,” then there is 
always another place to seek
 – instead of –
 having to stand fully in your work as it currently is.

I’d spend more time with this thought you shared:

“I think I am moving in the right direction.” 
Because I believe you are as well. What if you’re not actually “missing” anything more?

What if lasting change actually comes from THE SKILLS we foster within ourselves (like emotional resilience, thought work, belief, embodying who we desire to be, etc) and we keep doing it over, and over, and OVER until we have materialized everything we could ever want?

What if “change” is created and actually LASTS because of the skills in our brain that no one can
 ever
 rob or take away from us — no matter what challenges life brings our way? If we change at our core, and on the inside… no one can ever take it. It lasts forever. That’s what you’re helping your clients do who come to you… Change what isn’t working and equipping them with skills that no one can rob.

What do you think, coach?

You’re doing amazing by the way – keep going!

title: Energy of 2k Today – separating the value I give from when the results arrive Pt 1
question:
I recently wrote in and asked for help understanding the energy of 2k today, given that I have had a YT video that I posted in 2024 produce consultations in 2026. I am working on separating the idea of giving daily value from the idea of getting immediate results, without removing the possibility of being paid today.

Here, I’m responding to the question from Ask a Coach: How might it also be true that the value you share daily/weekly can be found and acted upon quickly?

Ok so the first thing coming up is that it can’t, or I can’t expect it to…because nurturing people takes time and it’s rare for someone to find a post and immediately become a client. However, I will say that one of my recent YouTube videos did produce a consult (and that person converted and ended up referring someone else who also converted), within less than a month of me posting it. That person found that one video and watched it even though it only had 7 views, then did a deep dive into my other content, then came to the consult already knowing a lot about me and my perspectives as a coach. This could definitely happen again. So someone could find something shortly after it’s posted, and even if they need more nurturing they could quickly consume my other content (I have hundreds of pieces of content), and then they could decide to book a consult. And I know that one way I support this happening is to continue building out my value bank by putting out several pieces of content each week.

Another thing coming up for me is that someone I met at an in person networking event booked a consult that same day without even seeing any of my content. That person didn’t end up becoming a client, but I do at least have evidence that consultations can come quickly and even within the same day as long as I’m taking marketing actions.
answer:
Hi Coach,

You did a really nice job actually doing the exercise and staying in it long enough to see more than your first answer. That stood out to me.

I do want to slow this down for a second because I’m not totally clear what you want coaching on.

You said you’re working on separating giving daily value from expecting immediate results, without removing the possibility of being paid today. Are you wanting help detaching from the expectation of being paid today? Or are you trying to understand how to hold both giving value and being available for it to convert quickly without creating pressure?

I’m asking because those are two different things, and right now they feel a little blended together.

Your first response to the second question ( value can be found and acted upon quickly)  was essentially, “it can’t” or “it’s rare.” But when you stayed with it, your brain immediately showed you evidence that it 
can and has
 happened. That’s important to see.

So now the question becomes what do you do with that? Not just as an answer to the exercise, but in how you actually show up.

How do you approach sharing value when you allow that it could be acted on quickly?

Your energy is different depending on what you believe. If you’re in “this takes time,” you’ll show up one way. If you’re in “this could land for someone today,” you’ll show up another way.

Neither is wrong, but they create different experiences.

Giving value because that’s what you do.
And also being available for someone to act on it quickly.

Like planting and harvesting can both exist… you’re just not gripping either one. You already have evidence of this you shared in your answer, someone found one video, went all in, and booked.
someone met you and booked same day. So it’s not a question of “can it happen?”

When you believe it 
can’t
 happen quickly, what shifts for you?
Sometimes we call that being realistic, but it can subtly close us off.

What’s different about you when you believe someone could find this today and move?

How do you speak?
How do you invite?
How ready are you?

So I’d love to know, what’s the actual friction point for you right now?
Is it the attachment to wanting to be paid today?
Or is it trusting that your work can land both quickly and over time?Once we separate that, this gets really clean.

And just to reflect back to you you are creating consults, you are converting, and you are taking consistent marketing action. This is working!

Now it’s just about cleaning up the thinking so it supports what’s already happening, instead of quietly working against it.

title: avatar
question:
I have a question about messaging for something like a food noise or binge eating webinar.

How do I know exactly who I’m talking to?

Am I speaking to someone who doesn’t know what their problem is yet?

Someone who knows what to do but isn’t doing it?

Someone who thinks they’re missing information?

Someone who knows it’s mindset?

Or someone who feels like they’ve tried everything and is ready to give up?

I feel like I can help all of these people, but I don’t know how to decide who to speak to in my marketing.

How do I figure out who to focus on, and how do I know I’m choosing the right person?

Thank you.
answer:
Hi Coach!

It could be all of these actually! Many times our clients do not always know what their “problem” is, they just know they aren’t getting the results they want. If you target all of these in your marketing (different posts speaking to different problems that arise), you are likely to have posts or emails resonate with the women who “see themselves” in that particular situation you are marketing. So you can choose if there is a specific problem you want to target every time, or if you want to address each problem that sometimes arises with food noise/binge eating.

There could be some women who don’t even know what “food noise” is… you can speak to that.

There may be women that do binge eat but don’t know why they do it.

There could be the women who want to stop – but don’t know how because it doesn’t feel simple.

And there could be the woman who has tried and failed over and over… and she doesn’t understand why she can’t just change it.

In all of these you have the opportunity to raise awareness to what these women may be feeling. For them to feel “seen” in your marketing and build trust that you know how to help them. Does that make sense? Feel free to come back with anything else you may still need as it relates to this!

title: moving into selling courses 4
question:
T- “I can reach more people with less of my time and make more money.” – What allows that version of me to exist more often? Why? Get specific to deepen the who before how. When I remember i know things – and that even my not best can be helpful. Like a lot of people don’t know even the basics – and that’s a good thing – I can help them. What does selling actually look like for you when you’re in your best energy?
