title: Fear of making offers
question:
I think I’m afraid of making offers. I really want to coach more clients and I know I can help people. I feel confused about how to make offers and I think it’s because I’m afraid of doing it. My thought is something like I’m afraid people will say no, or it could be that they will think I’m too forward or arrogant for making the offer.

How can I make offers even when I’m afraid?
answer:
Hi Coach,

Thanks for sharing where you are. Of course it feels scary to share your offer. When our brain is afraid people will say no, or that we may seem too forward or arrogant, it tries to use various methods to protect us. Confusion is one of them. In reality, you aren’t really confused. Sharing our offer can be as simple as meeting people, telling people you’re a coach, and making offers to help them. And also, if you need more clarity beyond that, that is what the 2k for 2k modules are for, right? To help teach any skills we lack. I share all of this just so you can see where the brain uses confusion or fear to stall what we may inherently know how to do.

The work here is actually in allowing yourself to 
feel the feelings and take action
 despite and in spite of it.

Your brain simply wants to avoid the 
potential
 
emotions it may feel if someone says “no” or if someone gives feedback that doesn’t feel pleasant. It helps to remind our brain that it’s normal to feel a wide range of emotions, especially as an entrepreneur.

Take some time to reflect and answers these:

1. What would it take for you to take action, even while you feel afraid? Can you do that? Why or why not?

2. What might you learn by allowing yourself to feel fear but take action anyways? How might doing so strengthen who you are as an entrepreneur? 

3. When in your life have you felt afraid but taking action anyways has led to good things? What did you learn?

Take time to answer these questions and then bring back your answers here if you’d like more coaching.

title: OVERPREPARED PEOPLE #30DAYSCHALLENGEMYOWN86.
question:
People look for me. When they see me, when they hear me… they want to have what I have.

My issue is that they (we) are all overprepared people. And, as it happened to me in the past, we want to solve it all with more: another certification, another learning, a deeper understanding of his business, we think more preparation is the secret clue!

That is how I got involved in a Masters degree, then a PhD, then a Post-PhD; I always thought “with this other certification I will have it all” (and it was never enough).

There was a moment in my life when I realized all the people I worked with, including myself, missed a skill: Mindset. (I never used this word. I described differently, but after years of over preparation I suddenly realized something was wrong. I did not get any different results and there were no more levels for me to get)

Now, working on overcoming obstacles, I know those clients who “want what I have” frequently have the obstacle : “I only need this ONE OTHER certification, which requires time, and money, and THEN I can hire you”.

They think their missing part is MORE KNOWLEDGE.

I am having problems trying to manage this obstacle.

How do I guide them to the Mindset world when all they appreciate is getting some higher knowledge?

(I know I do not have to convince them. They know they need help. And they want my help. I just need to have it clear in order to make sense for them)
answer:
You want to help your clients overcome this thought that they need another certification/more education before they can hire you and before they can reach their goals.

And you get it. You know how they are thinking because you used to think this too. You thought more knowledge was the answer.

How can we help these people shift what they are thinking so they can get out of this pattern and create results? Let’s get curious about it.

They think they need more knowledge. Maybe they DO need more knowledge – but not the knowledge they think they need. Maybe they need some knowledge around mindset (probably you’d use other words instead of mindset.) Maybe they need more knowledge around how to implement. What do you think of taking an approach like that with them? What helped you eventually see that more certifications wasn’t helping and that you needed something else?

title: #70 consults evaluation objection coaching 2
question:
Look at and answer Part 1 of this first. Then you can read what I’ll add here too.

You were thinking that she doesn’t put herself first and that’s why the money objection came up.

That could be. It could also be that she doesn’t really have the money.

Or that the other things she’s paying for and looking at moving around are important too. They might be necessities or necessities to her. Like a gym membership or paying for kids dance classes. etc.

It sounded like from Part 1 that she wants to make more money. Is that part of what she wants with you? Or was it something else? It felt like part of her result might be becoming the person who knows how to bring in enough money for what she wants – so that she’s not having to move things around. There just actually is extra money. Could part of your work be either helping her make money or figuring out her money mindset/habits so that she is that person who does have “extra” money for things like coaching?

I wasn’t on the consult so I don’t know this client like you do. What do you think?

OMG… YAY… So, as you can see, I kind of hit on that in our follow-up. I wasn’t as clear as you, but I see now that I was trying to help her solve her problem of not having money for coaching… by creating more clients.

I did not see this clearly on the consult or that clear on the f/u today.

she didn’t specifically want to focus on making more money with me, but she did want to be more confident and believe in herself so she can go all in on her business…which means, she’d be making more money. I didn’t realize that connection.

I struggle to know that first part, and I guess the answer is asking questions like this?

Can you technically afford it but it would be a stretch with your funds?

Are you saying you don’t have $500/month to invest in coaching?

if she says yes, I don’t have the money.

what I would say, is ok… bye. basically.

But you are saying that the coaching would be to offer to help her be the person that creates more money (by saving/spending less/creating more money), but how do I do that on consultation? especially since I am usually close to time.
answer:
I don’t “know” what the right coaching is.

That’s something that’s happening for you is you think there is a right answer.

But the right answer is arrived at WITH the client. I can’t just know the right answer for someone else. I don’t know her. And it’s not my place to impose my values on her.

For example, I can’t tell her that what she wants is to make more money. But it sure sounds like she does. That’s what I was hearing. And I can believe for her that if she wants that, it’s possible.

I’m going to say that back to her and see what she ways. “You want to be confident in your business. You want to know how to bring in clients. You want to know how to make more money so you have money for things.”

Maybe she tells me – “No the money isn’t important. What I want is impact. I already have lots of money.” (But then why is she objecting about budget? She probably won’t say this. And if she does – then you get curious. There is some other hesitation she’s having.)

Or maybe she says: “Yes. I would like to have extra money to invest in my business. To be able to grow it. And for my life.”

Then you say “This is going to be part of the work we do …… etc.”

title: Consult eval
question:
WW – did a good intake and got a sense of the problem early on – he’s not connecting what he does to his best buyers and giving them a simple next step.

WDW – it felt messy at the beginning – he was on a masterclass with me the day before and I assumed he knew what the consult was for but he said at the beginning ‘this is to see how we can support each other’ so I explained the purpose of the consult but it felt messy to me. Didn’t set the agenda clearly.

He went into a lot of stories about his business and why he thinks it hasn’t worked. At some points it felt like an argument because I was saying why I thought it hadn’t worked and he was disagreeing with the points I made. The bridging the gap was also messy – I think I was so keen to ‘get my point across’ on what would work that I brought in convincing energy. He asked me to send the process over on email and then responded with ‘The process is pretty clear, but not revolutionary or innovative. It contains no guarantees. I am not willing to do this high investment – and I do not see the ROI.’

My thought on this was ‘of course it’s not innovative, but if you do it it works’ and I felt a lot of frustration when I read that. He cancelled the follow up call.

WDD Stay out of specific solving on the call. I fell into this trap of solving for what wasn’t working specifically instead of walking through the top 3 problems and how that would look when we work together – which created the back and forth and almost argumentative energy (for example he told me one coach has said to him he needs to smile more and bring in more personality, that’s why he’s not selling’ and I disagreed and told him why. Instead of being curious and on his side about it – do you agree? What do you think?

Stay rooted in the value of my work and get better at explaining what happens when you do the fundamentals well – this comes down to doing a better job of bridging the gap. I’m still seeing this area as my biggest shift – going into more detail so they can see how it looks step by step, but staying out of specifics.

I would love if you can see anything else that I can coach my brain on with this one, thank you
answer:
We want to celebrate that you are creating consults. That’s huge. You are showing up in a way that is having people reach out to you.

Let’s see what we can fine tune and learn from this consult. You noticed you got into convincing energy a bit. Let’s work through what you said for bridging the gap, and then what he disagreed with. We want to find a way to get curious about what he’s disagreeing with so we can better understand him and where he is at. Why did he think that your solution wasn’t what he needed? What did he think he did need? Why wouldn’t what he thought he needed work?

Bring this back for coaching and we can work through it. This will help you get really clear on what you do and how you help.

title: Consult Eval 4
question:
WWW: we really connected on the call, she had just found me on IG and directly reached out to me and had binged my podcast so my marketing had really resonated, felt I was able to “go there” with what I was seeing and she said that my diagnosis & BTG really resonated with her, she initially said she wouldn’t be able to afford it but we coached through that & booked a follow up & she came to the follow up call having decided she was a yes, definitely the best consult I’d done so far

WDW: I could have painted the vision a bit more, but otherwise I think it went really well

WDD: spend a bit more time on painting the vision
answer:
This was consult 4/5 this week, and you have shown so much growth each consult.

On this consult you coached through that objection she had.

What was different on this call where you were able to coach on that objection vs. the previous calls? We want to see that so you can repeat it.

title: Anticipating objectives
question: Hey there. I’m moving right along in terms of figuring out my signature offer. When I look at the list of 20 people I want to buy the offer, part of me doesn’t believe that they will buy. Is my work now to to break down every single objective that I anticipate them having and model it so I can get to a place of really believing in integrity of the offer? That also gives me the opportunity to think more deeply about the offer and whether it makes sense, as perhaps I’ll want to make some changes to it. Thank you.
answer:
Yes – you want to look at why your mind is telling you they won’t buy. That helps you see what their objections might be, and it also helps you see your own objections. It helps you see where you might have gaps in your belief.

When you think about those 20 people, it’s not about getting or convincing them to buy. What you want to do is know that there are SO many people in the world just like those 20 people. You want to understand those 20 people and why they would or wouldn’t buy so you can talk to the 1000’s of other people just like them.

What are some of those reasons you think someone might not buy?

And what are some reasons someone will buy?

title: Why is it so hard for me to coach around a client’s decision?
question:
In my last consultation the client said she didn’t think she could afford the program, and I just accepted her “no” without exploring it at all. I didn’t ask any follow-up questions, didn’t coach her on her thinking, and didn’t hold space for her to reflect on the decision.

What I noticed in myself was a mix of discomfort and fear — I didn’t want to pressure her, and I didn’t know how to stay present without feeling salesy or pushy. I defaulted to people-pleasing and trying to be “nice” instead of helping her make a clean and empowered decision. It felt like I completely froze.

Can you help me understand what I might be missing here? What skills or mindset do I need to develop to be able to coach through indecision or objections, especially when I start to feel that internal panic?
answer:
You noticed that you started to feel some internal panic. Let’s explore that more so you can understand better what’s happening. That will help you see what you want to do to help yourself in those moments.

C Client says “I don’t think I can afford it.”

T What did you think in that moment?

F internal panic

A You freeze for a moment. You don’t ask anymore questions. You end the call. What else did you do or not do?

R What result does this create? It often relates to the initial thought.

Let’s step away from that for a minute.

Imagine you and I are sitting together. I’m thinking about going to Mexico this winter. I’d really like to go with my friend but I’m not sure if I can afford it. What might you say or ask me to help me decide if I want to go or not?

title: Consult eval 6
question:
Hi AAC,

I had another consult last week, yay! 🙂

WWW: I had connected with this person on IG and they resonated with my messaging and the talk I had done, created a safe space for him to talk about his struggles in a way he hadn’t before

WDW: I felt disconnected before the call but I dismissed it as “hormonal” lol, and I did do my pre-consultation writing to get me more connected but afterwards on reflecting I realised I was feeling a bit overwhelmed with the clients I have as it is the most I’ve had so far & many of my systems are not great so I have addressed that and really gotten back to a place where I genuinely want more clients & am connected again, on the call he said his main concern was anxiety, depression and burnout & he’d landed in hospital a few times over the last few years and he is doing better & is seeing a psychiatrist. I didn’t feel completely sure that he needed therapy instead but also felt a little hesitant and unsure whether I should be taking him on as a client; as a result of these thoughts I didn’t bridge the gap powerfully on his main concern, also had a thought like “I don’t want to be focusing on mental health struggles in my coaching”; when he said he’d need to check his finances I didn’t ask more questions about it like I normally do from some thought like “he has to decide whether this is right for him” which was part of my hesitation on whether I could definitely help him, but also I think from not quite being connected I was less attuned to his subtle shifts in emotional state and thought he was very sure on the coaching but just wanted to make sure on the finances, we did schedule a follow up but he messaged me before that to let me know that he was a ‘no’ which hasn’t happened in a long time & tells me I didn’t quite create the safety for him to talk through his objections on the call

WDD: even if I only feel a little disconnection I want to explore it with myself more before the call, I also have gotten much clearer now on what my philosophy is on when therapy is appropriate and how I would actually address this better on the call and bridge the gap more powerfully but I think building that even more going forward so I’m clearer and more confident rather than hesitant, without missing the red flags that no really is the right answer; I also want to always ask more questions when someone brings up an objection and coach on it like I usually do which I think will happen naturally with different thoughts
answer:
Yes! Great work showing up and creating all these consults!

Good work noticing you were feeling overwhelmed a bit and addressing it. That’s what helps you look after yourself and show up how you want to show up.

Let’s talk about your hesitations around coaching him – you weren’t sure if he needed therapy or if you want to take him on as a client. It’s totally okay to talk about that on the consult call. The consul call isn’t about getting a yes – it’s really about figuring out if this is the right fit. In cases like this, you can talk about what you do and what you don’t do. That helps you and him make the best decision about if you want to work together or not and how that coaching relationship might look. For example, you don’t offer emergency care like the hospital would. You might talk to him about coaching vs. therapy to help him know the difference too so he can better understand what you do and don’t do as a coach. What might that conversation have looked like if you had asked him more about the mental health and wanted to figure out together if coaching was a fit for him?

title: Consult ended early
question:
I had a consult call this week where ended up cutting it off early, which I’ve never done before, and I want support making sure I get all my learning from it.

The potential client was an executive coach with 25 years in the healing arts. Booked the call originally looking

for support around business expansion — moving from one-on-one work into group coaching. But her

priorities had shifted since she booked it; she’d decided to prioritize finding a romantic partnership, and the business growth could wait.

I opened with my usual consult format, including the life wheel. And it landed badly. She told me directly: “I don’t think about my life that way, with numbers.” She also said the process felt “really intimate really fast” and that it was making her “kinda dissociate a little bit.” She described the experience as trying to “fit into a structure that I don’t actually fit that well into.”

I felt her not liking the structure, so I named that and asked her about it. Then I dropped it entirely. We switched to audio-only when she said video felt “very inorganic.” I gave her lots of permission to just know it wasn’t what she wanted it, but still offered her reflection on what I saw and questions about what her next steps might be. She landed in a new level of clarity, so that felt good, but I wonder what I could have improved.

What worked?

Offering meaningful reflection

Naming what I sensed about her not being into the structure

Switching to voice only

Staying unattached

Getting a clear No

What didn’t work?

I think she got turned off immediately by me asking to bring my recorder in the room; she decided we weren’t a good fit right then (she didn’t like AI tools). We also talked about the weird Colorado weather at the start and it felt kind of awkward.

I never felt very connected to her

Even as I led us into the drop-in moment I do at the beginning, I felt nervous and like I had something to prove to her, like I wasn’t going to be good enough

We ended early and I never even gave her the offer or bridged the gap

I didn’t prep for the consult very well, was dealing with personal life stuff at the last minute

She felt like I came on too strong and she didn’t seem to want to share so deeply with someone she just met

What will I do differently?

Name it even earlier if I sense an energy disconnect?

On the one hand, I think I did fine here, but it’s also never happened to me to end so early, curious if you have any advice.
answer:
Hey there, coach!

First I’d like to say that you did a really beautiful job staying present and responsive here. You noticed the disconnect, named it, adjusted your approach, and stayed unattached even while it was uncomfortable. That’s not always easy to do in real time. Also, the fact that she still left with clarity says a lot about how you held the space. So great job there.

I also love the honesty around what you noticed about yourself 
(the feeling of having something to prove and not feeling fully connected).
 That level of self-awareness is exactly what makes you a strong coach.

A few things I’d invite you to reflect on:

When you think back to the very beginning of the call, where do you notice the energy shift first happened? Was it when she shared her goals had changed? Or the life wheel?

If you were to meet a client like this again, how would you want to open the conversation differently, 
if at all?

What would it look like to stay fully grounded in your own style, while also allowing space for someone who may need a different pace or entry point?

When you say you might, “Name it even earlier if I sense an energy disconnect?” what might this look/sound like if the opportunity presented itself again?

If you’d like, take some time to reflect and answer the coaching questions. You can bring back your answers and any further coaching you may want to ask. We are happy to help out! Thanks coach!

title: Consult evaluation
question:
I just did a consult I would like a review on my evaluation.

What worked:

Did the whole five step process went smoothly and great. I uncovered her real objection behind her money objection – which was that she didn’t trust herself to do the work and we coached on it. She said her husband would say yes and he would give her the money. That she was a yes.

What didn’t work:

She messaged me after I sent her the invoice a screenshot of the pediatric orthodontist call that they called her during our consultation and a screen shot of the voice message they left her about payments for her son’s braces.

She messaged me this message:

“thank you for your time and experience. This was very helpful and a much needed conversation for me to have. Just before I had consultation with you I was reading up on reliance on God. The meaning of it to have reliance upon God while taking the means. Which is why I decided to schedule a meeting with you. As we where having our consult, my sons orthodontist called me. (I am attaching a photo so that you can see), Requesting payment for his braces. Which is a little pricey. I am truly sorry, but at the moment I am not able to commit to the coaching due to the fact that financially it is a little high for me to pay for right now. This is something I need but I can not commit right now. I know I need the help

To get out of this imprisonment within me but, I can’t feel good when I know I there are other priorities right now.

I am so sorry. I value your work tremendously and I appreciate your help.”

I replied back saying You don’t have to apologize to me or send me pictures.

You have to ask yourself

Am I resourceful?

Am I the type that when I need something for me I can figure it out? In the same way, energy and dedication that I would figure it out for my children?

And I wished her the best on her journey.

So all in all is what didn’t work is that she didn’t become a client.

What would I do differently:

I would say honestly nothing. I did a great consult. Uncovered her objections and coached her. Even in this message I did not believe her story I gave her some coaching there. I grew from this consult in that now with her I didn’t even offer a payment plan only pay in full. I had a client sign up and pay in full recently and it’s just a better dynamic and commitment for me and my client.

Would love your feedback and thoughts.
answer:
Sometimes no is the best answer for a client. Sometimes there really are other priorities and their goals that they want to work on with you aren’t as important as those other priorities.

You want to get them to that place if it’s a no. Where they are saying like she did her that the results they want to create with you just isn’t a priority for them right now. Not from thinking they can’t do it, or couldn’t make more money if they truly wanted to, or that it might not work, etc.

You did a great job coaching her through her objections and having conversations around it. We can take a look more at what she said, and what you said in response on the call, in order to see if there is anything you would shift around it, or if you would do the exact same thing again.

title: I need to see if I can afford it – Pt. 2
question:
Assuming you can see my last question on this?

You asked if there are any thoughts I’m having when they say they can’t afford it.

I’m thinking,

“I don’t know what to say next”

Which is probably – “I don’t know what to say to continue the conversation to a yes.”

Or “I bet they have some objections but I don’t know how to get them to tell me.”

Would appreciate any coaching on this.

And you suggested a few ways forward –

The first would be affirming them – and then probing to see if there are any other thoughts lurking… right?

“Yah, you don’t want to sign up for the gym membership if it’s going to cause more stress due to finances. Do you think you could afford it and there are maybe some other hesitations coming up about going? Or is it really just the money?”

The second approach would be reminding them of their ultimate goal – and asking them – what would happen if you did do it? What would happen if you didn’t? To invite them to fully see it through in their minds – what would be like if they did? and to fully see – what would happen if they didn’t?

Let me know if that feels right?
answer:
YES! That’s exactly what you want to do. Affirm and hear them. And then explore it more. Which is exactly what you did here. We truly don’t want them to be a yes if it really isn’t a good fit. That would put so much stress on them and you if you knew that they were going without food in order to pay for coaching. That’s not a good situation for anyone. But a lot of the time, that’s not what’s happening. A lot of the time it’s more that there aren’t sure they can create results, or they aren’t sure it will work or maybe they do have to adjust priorities a bit. Maybe they pay for coaching and decide that’s more important than getting their hair done that month. The goal is to explore it more with them.

And yes we can see all of your past questions.

title: I got stuck at “I’ll be away for 2 weeks and I wont’ be able to start coaching for 2 weeks anyway”
question: I had a consult with a client who I knew I could help. What went well was that she was on board with everything I was saying and then she asked the price ( A good sign) some objections that I didn’t know how to handle were: “I have to check my budget” I said ok and let’s say you check your budget and it checks out then would you be ready to move forward? Her body language was saying no. So I asked her “What’s your belief you can get the result?” She said a 5. I asked “What would it take to be a 10?” She said “I’d have to see it happen first” I said “Ok so then you’re plan is to wait for it to happen to believe it?” She said “well no I can’t just do that” Then I said ok so then what do you think is stopping you from believing you can?. She said “Well we’re going on a trip, I’ll be away for 2 weeks and I wont’ be able to start coaching for 2 weeks anyway” AND I still have to check my budget. Then I didn’t know what to say from there. Maybe I believed that story, now I’m thinking I could have said “Great we can schedule the first call for 2 weeks from now so we can get in on the calendar” but I didn’t say that. I don’t think she was ready, I missed something. I need help figuring it out.
answer:
What we want to look at first is what you were thinking and feeling when you were in the overcoming objections part of the consult. What was going on for you?

C noticing her body language is looking hesitant, she says she has to check her budget

T What did you think?

F How were you feeling?

A You responded by asking her if she was ready to move forward. Asking her to rate her belief. Asking if she was going to wait for it to happen to believe it.

R You and her don’t get clear on the thoughts/feelings/situations keeping her from signing up with you.

Did it feel to you like you were trying to get her to be a yes vs being open to what was going on for her? If you think back, what do you think her hesitations were? What was keeping her from believing she could create the result?

title: Fear of going all in
question:
Hi Coaches!

I realized something last night that’s been sitting under the surface for me.

I noticed I have a real fear around going all in on my offer.

It sounds irrational when I say it out loud, but it feels very real: I’m afraid that if I step into coaching hosts on getting better guests and having more control, something will backfire in my own business. Almost like I’ll suddenly start attracting bad guests or have situations that contradict what I’m teaching.

I can see that it’s probably not actually about guests, but more about stepping into being visible and claiming that level of expertise. It feels like once I do that, I’ll be “tested” or exposed in some way.

I don’t want to let this hold me back, because I know it’s exactly the kind of thinking that keeps me playing small.

I’d love your help unpacking this and shifting how I’m thinking about it so I can move forward cleanly. Thank you s much for your help!
answer:
Hi Coach,

Great work catching this thought! Let’s get down to the root of it.

You said it comes down to: 
“Claiming that level of expertise. It feels like once I do that, I’ll be “tested” or exposed in some way.”

If we dig into this more, just notice what your brain is doing. It’s anticipating being “tested” or “exposed” –
 and THAT is what it is resistant to have happen. Your brain is simply saying, “I don’t want to be tested or exposed.”

So what would it mean if you were?

What feelings or emotions do you anticipate would arise if you were to show up as the expert and then be tested?

The core of what is coming up is 
what your system is resistant to feeling
 
“IF”
 it were to happen. And the interesting thing is, it may not even happen – maybe ever! But what this visceral feedback gives you is insight into what you may need to strengthen as far as your emotional capacity and your self-concept.

You 
are
 an expert. You are fully capable of owning it and stepping into it.

If somehow that expertise were tested,
 who do you want to be in the face of it?

How do you want to respond?

How do you want to treat yourself if or when those uncomfortable emotions follow?

Your brain is simply doing it’s job right now – protecting you 
ahead of time
. The sneaky part is that it’s wants to avoid you stepping into what is possible because it isn’t certain you could emotionally handle “backfire” — 
but what if you can, coach
?

With a willingness to use thought work, practice capacity work, and take advantage of the resources (2k, AAC, Live Coaching, etc.),

“IF” this were to happen – can you trust yourself to navigate it knowing you have the support & tools? 
(inwardly and outwardly)

That’s what you want to ask yourself.

And if you can trust yourself to navigate it, there is nothing to truly resist or fear by embodying who you are as an entrepreneur and coach.

What do you think?

Feel free to come back with anything coming up and we will gladly help!

title: Restarting 8a
question:
I am bringing back the model as you suggested

C: 1200 EUR for a package.

T: “I don’t know if they will pay.”

F: I feel powerless and I feel scared of being without money

A: I do still make offers, but from the place of despair and need, as well as weakness

R: No one wants to work with this kind of energy

C: 1200 EUR for a package.

T: My ideal clients are waiting to pay for it

F: Uau, I feel like I am doing the right thing, that I am really helping them, that is why they are waiting in line for it

A: I talk about my offer everywhere but without being pushy

R: Clients

But the question is, how can I really believe the thought that my clients are just waiting to work with me and pay for it? That they really really want to work with me regardless of the price.

Thank you!
answer:
Hi Coach,

Thanks for bringing back your models. Let’s dig in some more.

Based on your models, you want to believe that clients are willing to pay – but – you’re not certain they will.

You shared that you feel powerless and scared of being without money. That you do still make offers, but from the place of despair and need, as well as weakness.

Let’s start with that.

In 2k, Stacey teaches the importance of selling from sufficiency vs. scarcity. Notice how you feel when you make offers from despair and need vs. how you show up when you believe clients will pay the 1200 EUR. Another thing Stacey mentions in 2k is being able to sell without being attached.

In saying this,

How can you create sufficiency in your business vs. operating from scarcity?

What are all of the ways you create money?

Also, let’s do a scale rating 1-5.

1 is very low belief.

5 is very high belief.

On a scale of 1-5, what is your belief in:

1. Belief there are clients ready to work with you right now.

2. Belief clients will pay $1200 EUR.

3. Belief in the value of your offer.

After you rate each one on a scale of 1-5, explain why it’s the rating you gave it and 
(if it applies)
 what is keeping you from a 5.

title: 5-15-25 Objections
question:
It definitely comes from the belief that they don’t want this anymore. They did when they signed up and now we’re here and they don’t.

And instead of making it about me (I failed, etc.), what if I put the focus on them. This consult is supposed to be for them, not me. I’m trying to get passed an uncomfortable emotion when this whole hour is supposed to be for them. I think that’s going to be the driver… reminding myself this isn’t about me and I wonder if it’s jut pushing myself to “gag and go” like olivia says and ask the questions until I get comfortable with it.
answer:
How we get past this and change how you are thinking about it is by exploring it more. It is facing those feelings and asking the questions anyway – and it’s also figuring out why you are having this uncomfortable response and shifting that.

What do you make it mean when you think they don’t want this? What does that mean about you or your coaching?

Let’s also look at that model that happens.

C They have an objection.

T They wanted this when they signed up but now they don’t. (Is there another thought here too? It might be the thought above that you are making it mean.)

F How does that feel?

A What do you do or not do? You don’t ask more questions. You might think it’s you and focus on you vs. them. You have more thoughts that create more uncomfortable feelings. What else?

R What result does this create?

title: Consultation Evaluation
question:
Please coach me on the evaluation.

What worked:

Did the whole process and showed her the bridging the gap and created the vision etc.

What didn’t work:

She never asked for the price so I asked her if she wants to work together on this and she said she does but she doesn’t have the access to her money.

She mentioned she had money when we did the wheel but her father watched her spending and accounts even though it’s her personal money from previous work.

So she never found out the price of the coaching to begin with.

I did coach her on her having the money and not feeling like she can use it to get the help she really needs and how she’s allowing that to stop her in her life.

Then our time for the consult started to wrap up.

Knowing she had the money and that she didn’t even ask for the price she had already decided she can’t access her money at all. Because she mentioned her dad scolded her for using $30 of it last month. I left with her if she wants this to be where she wants to be. He would scold her on spending on coaching but she would get the help she needs and it’s still her own money. So it’s about who she wants to be and how she shows up for herself or does she choose to be trapped by her parents when in reality it’s her trapping herself. Him scolding her doesn’t necessarily stop her. But she’s letting it stop her.

What would I do differently:

I coached her enough on her thoughts and everything. I don’t see how doing more would have changed her in where she was. Even though the time wrapped up, she was a no because she didn’t ask for the price. I didn’t see her needing a follow up or anything because she was adamant on leaving the session with what she got and not wanting to pay for coaching.
answer:
Whenever there are objections, we want to get curious. What is happening for them? Why it it happening?

Not to get them to sign up necessarily, but to better understand them.

She knew about this situation with her money before she got on the consult call.  The next time that happens – you want to get curious about it. You want to ask them so you can better understand them – what were you hoping to take away from the call today? Or what made you sign up for this call today?

It could be she didn’t know it was a consult for paid coaching. If you look back at how you are making offers, do you think that could be what happened? That’s so useful for you to know if something like that happens. It can help you adjust how you are making offers.

It could be she really just wanted the free coaching on the call. That’s okay if she truly is in a place where that’s all she can do right now – you could even ask her about how she could start to implement anything she learned today. (Which also might lead to her becoming a future client or referring other people to you!)

Or maybe she has some other hesitations happening. Maybe she’s not sure enough about it in order to take that risk of what her father will say.

You can also look at your bridge the gap too when this happens. Did you share how you’d work together with her to create the goals? Or did you more just give her a plan that she might think she can now do on her own? You want to check in with that just to make sure there isn’t something happening there.

title: Language for asking them if they have questions/objections
question:
I’ve gone through the process and after vision, ask them if they have any questions or anything that feels intangible and that’s when they ask question or two.

Then they ask the price and I tell them and they often say OK. I’m gonna go think about this. Thanks.

I’m looking for language to try to help me open up a space to find out what objections they have. Could you give me a few suggestions?
answer:
There are two parts on the consult when you can create a space for them to look at their objections.

1. Before you talk about the price. This is Step 4: Figuring Out Objections. You can watch the video in the Consults module. After you paint the vision, you’ll ask them some questions around how they are feeling. For example: On a scale of 1-10, how committed would you be to this process? What makes it that number? This helps get out some of their objections. There are a few questions listed there – choose questions that make the most sense for you and your clients. This is about checking in with how they are feeling so they can see how they are feeling. Sometimes when we really think about signing up – that’s when all of our objections come up.

2. After the price. You want to open up conversation with them. “I totally get thinking about it and you can take that time if you need it. Tell me, what are some of the thoughts you are having about it right now?” From really wanting to know and understand this human in front of you. That normalizes them wanting to think about it – but it also opens up that conversation. You want to give them that space to think about it with you – with having a coach with them – instead of on their own like they have been doing it so far.

How have you been responding so far when objections like this come up?

title: objections
question:
I am noticing from my many consults that I am not tapping into curiosity.

I am asking either directive questions or asking either or questions.

I notice this also on my coaching calls too… not every time ,but I notice it.

So, when it’s offered… “like you do on a coaching call you get curious and ask this or that’ it does’t resonate because I am struggling with curiosity, connection, and confidence on coaching and consult calls.

So, I’d like to explore the curiosity on a consult.

I am struggling to see how I can ask curiosity questions to certain responses …

I can’t afford that

I don’t have that kind of money

to me, those responses are straight forward and there is no other question to ask.

I know this isn’t true though, and it’s just my thinking about it, because I’ve gotten coached and see that other people find ways to create conversations past those responses.

I’ve had someone say, No, I literally dont have $500 to pay. Where do I go from there?

I think I am struggling with knowing how to handle these statements because they seem done, finite, and anything after that is me pushing for a yes?
answer:
There is a difference between pushing for a yes and wanting to really know.

When someone says “I can’t afford it” it can mean lots of different things. Sometimes on the call you have context. You might know enough already about them to know that when they say they can’t afford it they mean they are choosing between coaching or paying rent. Or they literally don’t have room on their credit card. Those examples fall under the video When No Is The Best Decision. A no can be really empowering for someone too. If they really can’t do the coaching because they are in some of those examples from the video then no really is the best answer. And what’s next for them? You can guide them to their next steps.

And sometimes people say they can’t afford it when really they would rather spend the money on something else. They don’t fully see the value or the impact or they lack belief they can do it, etc.

On the call, you want to figure that out. Is this a case where No Is The Best Decision or is it more that they are missing a belief? If it’s a No Is The Best Decision case, then we don’t keep asking and getting curious. We respect that and we help them figure out what’s next for them.

title: #86 consult intake, BTG, and her response
question:
WDW:

1 hour over, here’s why:

-I had a new process and wasn’t great at streamlining my questions. they were a bit all of over the place and then I’d jump back to something we’d already talked about .I also am new to asking questions that were specific to my process but in the moment what I was doing was looking at BTG process and seeing if I asked about everything

-BTG was clunky. I know my 3 core steps but struggled to remember examples from intake so it was still more surface level than I like.

WDD: shortening my intake will give me less to have to remember- my take was over an hour long.

her réponse to the BTG was it was scary – she was afraid of how people will feel with this new version of her; who she would hurt; who she’d lose’ and what that life is like. I noticed I didn’t know what to say then… instead of convincing which is where I went, I want to work through and have a better idea for next time.

truth is… we dont know what they life is going to be like, but we know what right now is like. is that what I’d say? It seems like my clients are needing something from me in the moment. they feel safe enough to be honest, but then I am not powerful in my response. 1)maybe I think that will scare them from moving forward (attached) 2) I’m thinking of solutions instead of creating curiousity and a safe space for them to work it out in the moment?

I dont know if this is making sense, please let me know. I’d like to really pull apart this consult so I know exactly what I’ll do next time these things come up.
answer:
Hi Coach!

This does make sense. Let’s coach on it.

You shared that this consult-client said,
 “she was afraid of how people will feel with this new version of her; who she would hurt; who she’d lose’ and what that life is like. I noticed I didn’t know what to say then… instead of convincing which is where I went, I want to work through and have a better idea for next time.”

Let’s jump into her shoes for a moment pretending to be her.

You’re on a consult with a coach and tell them you’re afraid of doing coaching because you’re concerned how people will feel when you become a new version of yourself… You’re afraid of who you may hurt. You fear that coaching means you’ll lose people and worry about what that is like….

What questions would be helpful next? I’ll share some and you can see if anymore come up for you:

“How do you think people will feel when you become a new version of yourself?”

“Why do you think that?”

“Who are you afraid of hurting or losing? How would changing hurt them / make you lose them?”

“What else could be true about you becoming a new version of yourself? Let’s explore together.”

“What are some best case scenarios you think coaching could help with?”

“Who do you think you’d be in the world if coaching helped you feel less afraid?”

Notice how each of these questions help us get more curious with the client’s brain. Her answers would allow you to gather more information as to her true objections and what is truly keeping her from being a “yes.” What she is having trouble seeing is how becoming a different version of herself is beneficial vs. meaning she will “disappoint/lose/upset” people. In bridging the gap, she may need awareness help in how it feels to be living her life knowing she has potential, but fearing she will lose everything/everyone if she steps into it. This is her brain offering thoughts to protect her and keep her safe.

What are your thoughts?

Anything more with this consult-eval you’d like coaching on?

If so, be specific and we can continue to help!

title: Consult Evaluation from 9/11/25
question:
Consult Eval: Had a consult yesterday that led to a follow-up call next week. Appreciate your coaching and feedback!

Biggest thing that went well was coming from an energy of service and commitment, setting an intention to be super honest and sharing that with her at the beginning, helping her paint a vision she was excited and lit up by (10/10 urgent and important). When objections came up, I was calm and believed nothing had gone wrong. I called them out honestly and helped her see what was underneath the surface. Tried to ask questions to guide her back to the value and impact of coaching and show her what her brain was doing and how it was completely normal to be afraid.

What didn’t work was I don’t think I helped her see the value of coaching clearly enough. I could have bridged the gap in a more powerful way, sharing more clearly how my specific process would help the things she mentioned and what exactly we’d do in our time together. She had both time and money objections (once a week felt like a lot for her). She’s never experienced coaching before so it was clear to me I didn’t do a good enough job helping her see the value.

Do differently: we have a follow up call next Wednesday. We talked about what she’d explore between now and then (her goals, finances, what’s coming up in the next couple months, as well as ROI reflection questions I sent her). On the call, I want to be ready to speak more clearly to how we could bridge the gap in our work together, and help her talk through her reflections on ROI and how she could make the most of this investment.

My thoughts / fears: I missed an opportunity to serve her. I absolutely believe I could serve her and I want to more powerfully help her see the value and overcome the fears of what’s getting in her way to invest in herself and my brain is telling me I don’t know how.
answer:
Let’s look more at what happened during the overcoming objections part of the consult.

She had both money and time objections – once a week seemed like a lot for her.

You said that: when objections came up, I was calm and believed nothing had gone wrong. I called them out honestly and helped her see what was underneath the surface. Tried to ask questions to guide her back to the value and impact of coaching and show her what her brain was doing and how it was completely normal to be afraid.

Tell me more about this part of the consult. What did she say exactly? What exactly did you say in response?

Often time and money objections are surface level – and not really the true objection. So let’s look a bit more at that part too. Is once a week what she needs in order to create results? Why or why not? Why did she feel like once a week was a lot?

We can use this consult to help you get really good at dealing with objections so you can feel confident that you’ve helped the client make the decision that’s best for them.

title: Follow-up on 2 conversations
question:
First I want to say this service is absolutely amazing. Thank you.

There was a lot to unpack in the last two conversations. In the follow-up about the coffee chats. Based on what was said I believe I just need to do some thought downloads on meeting people and making offers and figure out where or what my fear is coming from. I believe that I do the bakery version of making offers. I just listened to a recorded Live coaching call and it adjusted my view of what an offer really is. I think I’m good on that.

The feedback on the evaluation was deep and amazing. There was a lot to consider and unpack there. That idea of slowing down is something I hear a lot especially from my family so I know I have some work to do there. I also need to work on the skill of hard listening. Let be break down where I have more questions.

when we don’t yet know which lever needs to be pulled. Do you think you needed to get more information or it felt unclear how you would help her? I think it was a little of both. When I heard what she said it was a combination of things boundaries, emotional responsibility and lack of recovery time. That’s a lot to process at once.

It was suggested to have a foundational way to bridge the gap to plug into any problem and then adapt. Can I get an example of what that means? I understand the part of have tools that I teach but I’m not clear how that can get plugged into any problem.

About the money question: I think I need to have more questions available to me to probe more as to what is meant when someone says “I need to think about it”.

When it comes to the skill of hard listening I think where my growth needs to expand is after I hear something that is important how to dig deeper on the topic and/or how to determine what’s most important from what they said.

Real opportunity – yes I am taking notes on what people are saying to use it my marketing.
answer:
Hi coach,  we’re really happy to help.

There’s a lot here, and I want to start by saying this: when you’re open to feedback like this, you open yourself up to real growth. You’re not just learning what to do , you’re learning where to place your skills, and that’s empowering. Developing the skill of hard listening will serve you in your business and in every consult going forward.

You asked: “When we don’t yet know which lever needs to be pulled — do you think you needed more information, or did it feel unclear how you would help her?” You noticed it was probably both, and I agree with you. What’s important here is that you identified three things, boundaries, emotional responsibility, and lack of recovery time and that’s a great start.

If you had the opportunity to go back into that conversation with all the time you needed, what would you want to know about each of those areas? The answers help you decide how you would help. What information would bring clarity for you? What would you need to hear to know where to start?

For example, with boundaries, you might ask for a specific example of when a boundary isn’t honored. Or you might ask what she thinks should happen when she sets one. With recovery time, what actually isn’t getting replenished? These questions matter because they move you from “there are many issues” to “this is the one we can work on first.”

You also asked about having a foundational way to bridge into any problem and then adapt. This is a great question. Think of foundations less as tools and more as structure. Whether someone comes in with relationship issues, money stress, health challenges, or time overwhelm, there are often a few core things they need to learn: how to take responsibility so they can create change, how to make decisions ahead of time instead of reacting, how to evaluate what’s working without beating themselves up, and how to get back on track when they fall off.

Those foundations can plug into almost any problem the topic changes, but the structure stays the same. Early on, this takes more thought. Over time, you’ll naturally know how to talk about how you help, no matter what someone brings you.

About the money question, you said you want more questions available when someone says, “I need to think about it.” I hear that. Rather than thinking about the right question, notice what happens if you stay in curiosity. If you didn’t make that sentence mean they don’t want to work with you, what would you want to know? What feels natural to ask when you’re genuinely curious?

One of the best default questions when you’re unsure is simply, “Tell me more.” It’s open, it keeps you connected, and it gives them space to clarify what they’re actually thinking through. What comes up for you when you imagine asking that instead of moving on or filling the space? You can validate that response and say something like, i understand I hear that all the time, what do you think you need to think about? You can show them it is normal and you cna help them think through together. What if you didn’t think you didn’t have the questions to walk them through that?

When it comes to hard listening, your awareness here is really strong. The growth edge is often not hearing what’s important, but knowing how to go deeper once you hear it. One simple way to do that is to let the client help you prioritize. You can ask, “Based on everything you’ve shared, what feels most important for me to understand so I can help you?” That question matters because it keeps you from guessing and brings focus to the conversation.

And yes taking notes on what people say and using that in your marketing is a real opportunity. You’re extracting gold from real conversations, learning by doing, and letting your work evolve as you go. That’s a skill in itself.

You already have a solid plan here. Each consult will get clearer as you practice, and you’ll feel more confident in the flow the more you do it. Bring what you notice back, and we can continue to support you as this sharpens.

title: #86 consult – responding to her fear
question:
You shared that this consult-client said, “she was afraid of how people will feel with this new version of her; who she would hurt; who she’d lose’ and what that life is like. I noticed I didn’t know what to say then… instead of convincing which is where I went, I want to work through and have a better idea for next time.”

Let’s jump into her shoes for a moment pretending to be her.

What questions would be helpful next?

“How do you think people will feel when you become a new version of yourself?”

“Why do you think that?”

“Who are you afraid of hurting or losing? How would changing hurt them / make you lose them?”

“What else could be true about you becoming a new version of yourself? Let’s explore together.”

“What are some best case scenarios you think coaching could help with?”

“Who do you think you’d be in the world if coaching helped you feel less afraid?”

What are your thoughts?

GREAT questions. Straight to curiosity! She told me it would be scary and mention an example with her Husband/Mom saying “I’ve literally been this way my entire life, will be a drastic change. will be difficult for alot of people to accept. It’s hard but I’m ready for it.” I asked how she knows it will be hard, she said because it just will, I don’t want to do any of that stuff, I don’t want to say no, hurt anyone’s feelings, none of that, I’m an empath.

I then went into EXPLAINING how her brain is working right then vs. me tapping into curiosity. The question I did ask was, “what do you think the difference might be, you valuing yourself more than….” She said great, but the “journey is the hard part” people might fall off, etc.

What do you think worse case scenario is? People I love get distant….she got emotional and shared a big moment in her life where she had a medical emergency and felt that nobody cared. And that’s what led her to want to change the way she was with people that she gives herself of everything but only a few people cared. – she said, hurt, disappointed. When she really needed ppl for the first time, nobody was there. made me think of where I spend my time, energy, and out of obligation. pt 2

“In bridging the gap, she may need awareness help in how it feels to be living her life knowing she has potential, but fearing she will lose everything/everyone if she steps into it.”- what do you mean here? My BTG may need to answer that fear ahead of time about what it will be like (the impact) of doing this work WHILE being afraid? the benefit of that?
answer:
Hi Coach,

AAC said, “In bridging the gap, she may need awareness help in how it feels to be living her life knowing she has potential, but fearing she will lose everything/everyone if she steps into it.”

You asked: “what do you mean here? My BTG may need to answer that fear ahead of time about what it will be like (the impact) of doing this work WHILE being afraid? the benefit of that?”

Yes. Based on what you shared about this particular client, it sounds like she has a good amount of awareness that things need to change in her life 
(and it sounds like she wants those changes)
. However, she hasn’t actively made those changes 
(yet)
 due to fear of what she thinks she will lose in the process (close relationships). It sounds like although she is ready for change, she also believes making changes will be drastic. Her undertone comes off as if she knows the potential of who she 
could
 be (or what is possible for her life) but has fears what could go wrong if she “goes for it.”

How can/could you help her bridge the gap of where she currently is, and how she currently feels, and then paint the picture of where she could be with coaching support based on the results 
she wants
 for her life? How might you help her see the impact of doing the work while letting fear be present/feeling afraid? 
(As you also said).

Does this help clarify a bit more? You’re on the right track! Great work, Coach.

answer: You said that from a clean space you helped her see the options and think through this. That’s exactly what you want to do.
